papers.title: On the Nash equilibrium for a model of traffic flow
papers.abstract:
The paper consider a conservation law model of traffic flow on a highway, where each driver chooses an optimal departure time $\tau^d$, based on a departure cost $\varphi(\tau^d)$ and an arrival cost $\psi(\tau^a)$. Nash equilibria are studied, where no driver can reduce his own cost by changing his departure time.
  The first results provide continuity estimates on the arrival time, depending on the distribution of departures. In terms of the ${\bf L}^1$ distance, we show that the corresponding map is H\"older continuous with exponent $1/2$ in Lagrangian variables (labelling individual drivers), and Lipschitz continuous in Eulerian space variables.
  Concerning the regularity of the a Nash equilibrium, our results show that, when the total number of drivers is sufficiently large, a queue alway forms at the entrance of the highway and the corresponding traffic density contains a shock. Moreover, for any number of drivers (possibly small), we prove that for generic $\mathcal C^2$ cost functions $\varphi, \psi$ the Nash equilibrium solution still contains a shock.
  In the last section of the paper, assuming that the initial departure rate is not a Nash equilibrium, we consider an evolution equation for the departure rate, where each driver keeps changing his daily departure time in order to reduce his own cost. It is proved that this nonlocal integro-differential evolution equation admits a unique solution, globally in time. This provides some theoretical support to earlier numerical simulations, which indicated the dynamic instability of the Nash equilibrium and the possible existence of a chaotic attractor.

papers.title: Online Covariance Estimation for Averaged Stochastic Gradient Descent on Riemannian Manifolds
papers.abstract: We study online inference for averaged Riemannian stochastic gradient descent (RSGD) when the unknown parameter lies on a manifold. Although the averaged RSGD iterate is asymptotically normal, practical inference requires estimating the unknown covariance operator in its limiting distribution. Existing online batch-means methods cannot be applied directly because a general Riemannian manifold lacks an addition operation, and the tangent space containing the Riemannian gradient varies across iterations. Through vector transport, we construct overlapping and non-overlapping covariance estimators that adaptively combine information from successive batches while accounting for the changing tangent spaces. The proposed estimators are online, require neither Riemannian Hessian computations nor a prespecified terminal sample size, and attain the same convergence rates as their Euclidean counterparts (Zhu et al., 2023). Together with asymptotic normality, these estimators enable online statistical inference for RSGD on manifolds. We illustrate the proposed framework through a detailed study of streaming principal component analysis on Grassmann manifolds.

authors.name: Sen Na
authors.institution: Swiss Centre for Applied Human Toxicology

papers.title: Floor Friction Assessment from Robot Tire-Surface Interaction
papers.abstract: Floor traction influences wheel-slip behavior, dead-reckoning accuracy, and the navigation performance of wheeled mobile robots that rely on wheel odometry. As these robots become increasingly common in GNSS-denied indoor environments, including automated manufacturing and retail facilities, their onboard measurements could also be used to characterize floor conditions and improve localization. In this study, a skid-steer robot was driven over five floor surfaces with distinct traction characteristics using commanded velocity profiles designed to induce wheel slip through repeated acceleration and direction reversal. Differences between the body velocity estimated from inertial sensing and the velocity obtained from wheel odometry were evaluated using the integrated relative-velocity error, phase-derived wheel-to-body response delay, and velocity-reversal response delay. Welch power spectral density analysis was additionally applied to characterize the frequency distribution of the velocity mismatch during positive and negative acceleration. Band-integrated spectral power, spectral centroid, and spectral decay rate were extracted from each recording and evaluated using linear discriminant analysis and multiclass classification. The response-delay measurements produced consistent surface-dependent trends, with the longest delays observed on soap and the shortest delays observed on carpet. The spectral features also provided clear separation among the tested surfaces, achieving a balanced classification accuracy of 97.1% under recording-level cross-validation. These results demonstrate that both the magnitude and frequency domain characteristics of wheel-to-body velocity mismatch contain useful information about tire-surface interactions. Such information could support surface recognition and the development of slip-aware wheel-odometry weighting within robot state-estimation frameworks.

papers.title: Counting Integral Matrices with Given Cubic Characteristic Polynomial
papers.abstract: We show that the number of $3\times 3$ matrices with given characteristic polynomial and entries in $\mathbb{Z}\cap [-H,H]$ is at most $c H^{3}(\log H)^{6}$ for all $H\ge 2$, where $c>0$ is an absolute constant.

papers.title: Plasma and light: Shaping High Harmonic Generation in Time-Varying Media
papers.abstract: High harmonic generation in solids is typically described under the assumption of a stationary medium. This assumption is rarely questioned because the electronic properties of most media evolve on timescales much slower than the harmonic emission process itself. However, in strongly driven time-varying transparent conductive oxides the plasma frequency, carrier density, and effective mass can evolve on the same femtosecond timescale as harmonic generation. Under these conditions, harmonic generation and material evolution are no longer independent processes. Within this context, we consider a two-field pumping scheme in which a strong field generates a comb of high-order harmonics across a broad spectral window, while a weaker field simultaneously reshapes its own individual spectral lines. Distinct from geometry-dependent wave-mixing processes, the evolving electron plasma reshapes multiple collinear harmonic channels simultaneously. A fully self-consistent hydrodynamic-Maxwell framework reveals that even- and odd-order harmonics naturally emerge from free- and bound-electron dynamics without the typical need to invoke phenomenological nonlinearities. Our model captures the full spectral evolution on an ultra-broad bandwidth, while experiments performed on ITO confirm the distinct behavior of bulk-driven odd harmonics and interface-driven even harmonics under strong pumping. These results establish time-dependent plasma dynamics as a powerful new tool for broadband hyperspectral shaping of multiple harmonic channels beyond the framework of four-wave-mixing processes. Our findings are of particular relevance to ultrafast science, with potential applications in ultrafast pulse manipulation and the generation and control of tailored multi harmonic waveforms.

papers.title: Traveling Waves for Mixed Nonlocal-Local Systems of Conservation Laws on $\mathbb{S}^1$
papers.abstract: Non trivial traveling waves in genuinely nonlinear conservation laws hardly appear and, in some cases, scalar nonlocal conservation laws inherit this feature. Here, we show that mixed nonlocal-local systems of conservation laws display a far richer scenario. A variety of traveling waves may exist, different components may travel with different speeds and traveling waves can appear as time-asymptotic limits. Technically, these results need a significant extension of Dafermos' "trend to steady state" theory, exploiting properties of Hamiltonian systems solved by generalized characteristics.

papers.title: Evaluating Visual Language Models on Visual Grounding for Visually Impaired People
papers.abstract: Visual grounding (VG) in visual question answering (VQA) is a fundamental capability of Vision-Language Models (VLMs), enabling the detection of the most relevant region in an image to answer the question. This reflects the model's capability of multimodal comprehension, which is crucial when interacting with visually impaired people (VIP). Indeed, visual grounding, when applied to assistive scenarios, is not merely a technical feature, but rather a trust and safety requirement. In this work, we study visual grounding in VLMs for visually impaired people. To this end, we assess open-source VLMs on visual grounding using the VizWiz-VQA-Grounding dataset and challenge, which contains real-life images taken by VIP. We propose VG-SHAP, which extends an existing explainability framework to provide visual grounding explanations, allowing the evaluation of black-box VLMs. Our results on the VizWiz-VQA-Grounding challenge show that despite generating correct answers, VLMs struggle to ground in the proper region in the image. However, these results are constrained by the quality of the segmentation model of our explainability framework and further research is necessary.

affiliations.raw: University of Malta, Msida, Malta

papers.intro:
Grounding, the collaborative process by which speakers establish and maintain mutual understanding, is crucial in human communication (Clark and Schaefer, 1989). Visual grounding (Nagaraja et al., 2016; Yu et al., 2016; Mao et al., 2016) in VQA describes a model’s ability to localize the relevant region in the image to answer the question. Despite its importance, recent VLMs tend to answer with self-confidence(Shaikh et al., 2024) rather than grounding their responses. When it comes to assisting visually impaired people (VIP), visual grounding is essential to clearly communicate uncertainties and to correct misunderstandings. Particularly, in critical assistive scenarios, such as verifying the name of a medication, the dosage on a label, or the expiration date on a food package, where the VIP must be able to trust that the VLM’s answer is derived from the correct part of the image and whenever the model is uncertain, it should explicitly convey it.

VLMs have recently achieved remarkable progress across a wide range of multimodal tasks, particularly in VQA, where models generate natural language responses conditioned on both image and textual inputs (Ribeiro et al., 2016; Antol et al., 2015). These advances have enabled practical applications such as assistive systems for visually impaired people (VIPs), where users rely on visual models in their day-to-day tasks (Liu et al., 2024a). One of the most important aspects of this use-case is visual grounding, which will ensure safety and reliability for the VIPs. However, most modern large-scale VLMs are evaluated primarily on textual correctness, and their grounding capabilities on images taken by VIPs remain largely underexplored. Furthermore, many state-of-the-art models operate as black boxes and do not expose internal attention maps, making it difficult to directly assess their visual reasoning processes.

In this work, our contribution is two-fold. First, we extend an existing explainability framework (Cafagna et al., 2023) to generate visual grounding explanations, and we integrate recent state-of-the-art segmentation models into it. Second, we assess the visual grounding capabilities of open-source VLMs on the VizWiz-VQA-Grounding dataset and compare them to the baselines reported in the challenge of the same name (Chen et al., 2022). Our preliminary results show that although VLMs tend to generate the correct answer, they do not correctly ground in the proper region in the image, suggesting they lack visual grounding. However, because our evaluation relies on external segmentation models, the results are subject to uncertainty and require further investigation before drawing definitive conclusions about the reliability and trustworthiness of VLMs.

papers.title: BAARC: Uncertainty-Driven Adaptive Partial Spectral Measurement to Full Reconstruction for Material Classification
papers.abstract: Spectroscopic instruments with limited wavenumber coverage require accurate scan positioning or multiple measurements to complete the material analysis. This often requires prerequisite knowledge about the material under diagnosis to measure the spectral regions with distinguishing peaks. In our study, we simulate a Bayesian Adaptive Acquisition with Reconstruction-driven Classification (BAARC) framework for Raman spectral measurements, using masked training to learn spectral features that dynamically drive laser channel selection until the material is identified. We present a jointly trained two-level framework that takes progressive partial measurements of small wavenumber patches across the complete spectral range and, at each step, first attempts to reconstruct the full spectra until the model uncertainty is low. Secondly, material classification is performed at each reconstruction step until stoppage. Uncertainty quantification during reconstruction steps helps determine the measurement position of our next patch, while combining it with classification uncertainty determines measurement termination. By closing the loop between hardware acquisition and deep probabilistic modeling, the proposed system minimizes physical measurement steps while maintaining both spectral fidelity and diagnostic accuracy. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our framework achieves high-accuracy sample identification using only a fraction of full-spectrum channels, offering a scalable solution for real-time, high-throughput spectroscopic instruments.

papers.intro:
Raman spectroscopy is a powerful analytical technique for characterizing materials through their intrinsic molecular vibrational signatures (Raman, 1928b; Raman, 1928a). When coupled with microscopy, it enables non-destructive, label-free chemical imaging of spatially inhomogeneous specimens. However, spontaneous Raman scattering suffers from inherently weak signal intensity, requiring long integration times that severely limit its applicability to dynamic biological processes (Krafft et al., 2016; Hou et al., 2011). Coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering (CARS) microscopy was developed to overcome this bottleneck by enhancing signal intensity through coherent nonlinear excitation (Cheng and Xie, 2003; Müller and Zumbusch, 2007; Maker and Terhune, 1965). However, CARS suffers from non-resonant background contributions that distort its spectral shape compared to spontaneous Raman (Polli et al., 2018). Stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy resolves this limitation by delivering background-free, quantitative spectra identical to spontaneous Raman (Shen, 1975; Mohn et al., 2025; Ranjan and Sirleto, 2024).

Despite these advancements, SRS microscopy faces a fundamental trade-off between spectral coverage, acquisition speed, and sample viability. Acquiring a full spectrum across a wide wavenumber range requires continuous laser tuning, prolonging total measurement times, increasing hardware complexity, and elevating the risk of phototoxicity in biological samples (Yu et al., 2024; Pence et al., 2021; Mohn et al., 2025; Lin et al., 2017). As a result, practical constraints often force experimentalists to acquire only partial or sparse spectral bands. Similar limitations arise across many spectroscopic modalities, such as hyperspectral imaging (Gao and Smith, 2014), near-infrared spectroscopy, and diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (Andries and Martin, 2013), where only a fraction of the available spectral information can be acquired within a given measurement budget.

Rather than relying on uniform, exhaustive scanning, recent advances in machine learning enable a transition toward information-driven, adaptive acquisition (Luo et al., 2022; Denzler and Brown, 2002; Denzler et al., 2003). While real-time uncertainty propagation and active sensing have been successfully applied in dynamic tracking and active vision tasks (Trummer et al., 2010; Trummer et al., 2009), existing Raman spectroscopy methods predominantly rely on static acquisition grids. Instead of measuring every wavenumber directly, a physical system can dynamically select high-information spectral coordinates based on real-time feedback from prior measurements (Gehm and Kinast, 2008). In chemical and biological applications, reconstructing the full spectrum from partial observations is vital as it preserves physical interpretability, allowing domain experts to perform standard peak assignments and compare spectra against established reference libraries.

To the best of our knowledge, this work introduces the first uncertainty-based, closed-loop adaptive sensing approach that uses spectral reconstruction for target classification. We call this the Bayesian Adaptive Acquisition with Reconstruction-driven Classification (BAARC) framework. From partial scans of a spectrum, a completely reconstructed spectrum with its prediction uncertainty is obtained. It has been shown previously that sensing in a high-uncertainty region optimally increases information gain (Krause et al., 2008; Houlsby et al., 2011). Our autonomous measurement control follows this by measuring the next high uncertainty region at each measurement step, as shown in Figure 1. The reconstruction of each step is used for classification along with its uncertainty. Both uncertainties are used as stoppage conditions in our framework, automatically halting physical measurement the moment confidence in sample identification stabilizes. Bayesian uncertainty quantification offers a principled criterion for both guiding laser selection toward ambiguous spectral regions and determining when measurement can be safely halted.

We evaluate BAARC using experimentally acquired Raman benchmark datasets (RRUFF (Lafuente et al., 2015), COVID-19 (Yin et al., 2021), Marine Pathology (Yu et al., 2021), and Bacteria (Ho et al., 2019)) to simulate hardware-in-the-loop constrained acquisition. This setting provides a controlled environment for investigating adaptive sensing strategies using various baselines (Monte Carlo Dropout (MCD) (Gal and Ghahramani, 2016), Neural Process (NP) (Garnelo et al., 2018b; Garnelo et al., 2018a), and Deep Gaussian Process (DGP) (Tran et al., 2015; Wilson et al., 2016)) while retaining realistic spectral complexity. Our results demonstrate that the proposed framework often requires only about 50% of the spectrum in effect to achieve the performance of a classifier trained on the full spectrum. The effectiveness of our adaptive sensing methodology is benchmarked against budget-matched random scans over the spectrum.

papers.title: The chromatic number of a random graph with $o(n^{3/2})$ edges
papers.abstract: Let $G(n,m)$ be the Erdos-Renyi random graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges and let $\delta>0$. Alon and Krivelevich [Combinatorica 1997] proved that for any sequence $m\leq n^{3/2-\delta}$ there \emph{exists} an integer sequence $q=q(n)$ such that the chromatic number of $G(n,m)$ equals either $q$ or $q+1$ with probability tending to one as $n\to\infty$. In this paper, we give an explicit formula for this sequence $q(n)$ and confirm their result under a less restrictive assumption that $m=o(n^{3/2})$. Furthermore, we show that for all but a vanishing proportion of the admissible values of $m$, the chromatic number of $G(n,m)$ equals $q$ with high probability.

papers.title: Cross numbers and the characterization of finite abelian groups by length sets
Data-driven segmentation of solar filaments based on ground-based instrument data
papers.abstract: The dynamic behavior of solar prominences and filaments is a precursor to coronal mass ejections (CMEs), which can disrupt Earth's magnetosphere and affect satellite communications. Systematic ground-based solar observations, conducted with high temporal resolution, are instrumental in monitoring these structures. Analysis of the morphological changes and destabilization processes of filaments and prominences captured in datasets can help identify early warning signs of potential eruptions. This capability is vital for developing reliable space weather forecasting systems, thereby mitigating the adverse effects of solar disturbances on Earth's technological infrastructure. Previously, we introduced hybrid algorithmic-data driven method which performance was shown on a set of Solar Dynamic Observatory (SDO) Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) instrument data performing segmentation of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) and shock waves. In this work, we extend certain aspects of this approach to image segmentation of solar features -- filaments and prominences using H-alpha Kanzelhohe Observatory data. We describe a leakage-aware, sparse multi-year sampling strategy. We present image segmentation models pre-trained on synoptic and normalized image data, followed by a discussion of how model performance depends on training-set engineering, data preprocessing techniques, and the choice of loss metrics. We perform a limited study, both analytically and numerically, of the effect of external, fixed normalization versus native input for compact U-Net-based segmentation of solar H-alpha filaments, also contributing to ongoing research on normalization in deep networks in general and compact models in particular.

papers.title: Context-dependent Runtime Construction of Safe Regions of Attraction from Design-Time Identification for Multi-Candidate Simplex Architectures
papers.abstract: Deploying safety-critical cyber-physical systems requires control strategies that reconcile high performance and adaptability with rigorous safety guarantees. Classical control strategies offer stability proofs but are conservative, while advanced optimization- and learning-based controllers achieve high performance but lack formal verification. Runtime Assurance (RTA) architectures bridge this gap by introducing their own (dis-)advantages. Safety filters use online optimization and introduce chattering, while Simplex permissiveness is bounded by the tightness of the certified Region of Attraction (RoA) of its High-Assurance (HA) controller. Targeting this conservatism, we present a two-stage RoA certification procedure leveraging contraction-based stability to establish a target set for Taylor-model-based reachability analysis. We then treat the closed-loop system under HA control as a switched system, enabling: (a) runtime construction of context-dependent safe RoA and (b) safe switching between HA candidates to optimize recovery and maximize the operating envelope of the uncertified High-Performance (HP) controller. We validate this framework on a robotic path-tracking task using a three-stage evaluation: Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE) simulation for theoretical verification, high-fidelity Gazebo simulation under unmodeled dynamics, and experiments on physical hardware. Results show that the Simplex architecture maintains safety under fault injection and successfully shields a behavioral-cloning-trained HP controller. Crucially, the decision module introduces negligible overhead (0.028 ms average, 4.13 ms worst-case), consuming under 10 % of the control period.

papers.title: Properties C and D fail for $C_n^r$ whenever $n \equiv 2 \bmod 4, n\geq 6$ and $r\geq 4$
papers.abstract: Let $s(C_n^r)$ be the Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv constant (zero-sums of length exactly $n$) and $\eta(C_n^r)$ the short zero-sum constant. Properties C and D of Gao et al.\ assert that every sequence of the extremal length without the relevant zero-sums has the form $T^{n-1}$. For even $n$ they imply $s(C_n^r)=2^r(n-1)+1$ and $\eta(C_n^r)=(2^r-1)(n-1)+1$. G.~Wang recently disproved both for $C_6^r$, $r\ge4$. We prove that both fail for $C_n^r$ for every $n\equiv2\pmod4$ with $n\ge6$ and every $r\ge4$. More precisely, for these $n$ we have: $s(C_n^r)\ge2^r(n-1)+2^{r-2}+1$.

papers.title: EKT-Router: Expert-Evidence Alignment for Embodied Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Embodied vision-language models must answer questions from partial, evolving observations. Their success depends on both the reasoning capability selected and the evidence available to it. Expert routers adapt internal computation, while tool-augmented systems acquire external evidence; choosing these independently can leave a suitable expert without the evidence it needs. We introduce EKT-Router, a bounded framework that jointly selects a capability expert, optional knowledge, and perceptual tools. Outcome-derived signatures represent the overlapping strengths of General, Spatial Reasoning, and Spatiotemporal experts. A joint utility scores complete expert-evidence routes under a call budget. After acquisition, a packet verifier admits valid evidence with positive predicted expert-conditioned gain. The selected expert then answers once, reverting to the unchanged observation if all packets are rejected. Across 6 embodied QA benchmarks, EKT-Router achieves a mean score of 61.4, the highest among the compared systems, and averages 74.7 on 10 general vision-language benchmarks. With all external evidence disabled, question-conditioned expert selection alone improves over the best fixed expert by 1.75 points. Ablations show that learned routing is the dominant component and that knowledge and perception are complementary.

papers.title: Rethinking Video Storage for AI Training: Breaking Cross-Frame Dependencies for Efficient Random Access
papers.abstract: Large-scale AI training increasingly relies on massive video datasets with random temporal sampling patterns. However, existing video storage paradigms are optimized for sequential playback and employ sophisticated inter-frame reference structures to maximize compression efficiency. When applied to the random-sampling workloads of AI training, these paradigms face substantial decoding-efficiency bottlenecks. Workarounds such as independent JPEG frames and short groups of pictures (GOPs) reduce decoding work at the cost of larger storage and transfer volumes. In this paper, we identify two sources of decode amplification: sequential reconstruction of unrelated frames and reconstruction of the reference chains required by sampled targets. We address both sources by co-designing the decoding schedule and video reference structure. Dependency-aware sparse decoding reconstructs only requested frames and their required references, skipping unrelated reconstruction without transcoding the source videos. Optional offline Dependency-Decoupled Random Access (DDRA) encoding further reduces reference reconstruction by restricting each interior frame to two bounding intra-coded anchors. Together, sparse decoding and DDRA retain inter-frame prediction while bounding reconstruction to at most three frames per requested target, independent of the intra period. Experiments on a large-scale robotics corpus show that, at comparable reconstruction quality, our method achieves $1.45\times$ the loading throughput of LeRobot v3 with 58.7% less media payload.

papers.title: PRISMA: Differentially Private Synthetic In-Car Telemetry via Differentiable Simulation
papers.abstract: Differentially private synthesis of in-car energy consumption data is challenging because the output is high-dimensional, and known lower bounds show that the privacy-utility trade-off degrades with the square root of the number of output dimensions. However, we observe that the intrinsic dimensionality of in-car energy consumption is much lower than that of the raw trace: given a small set of contextual personal variables-such as start point, end point, the car model, and the driving behavior-the consumption profile can be largely explained by publicly available map data (including elevation) combined with a physical model of vehicle energy use. We exploit this low intrinsic dimensionality in PRISMA, a Privacy-preserving In-car Synthesis and Modelling Algorithm. PRISMA involves three stages: (i) energy consumption traces are encoded into a low-dimensional latent space; (ii) the distribution of latent vectors is synthesized using the differentially private tabular data synthesis algorithm AIM, and (iii) samples drawn from this distribution are decoded back into full energy consumption traces via a differentiable physics-based simulation, a step that consumes no additional privacy budget since it uses only public information. By using a compact, physically-grounded latent representation of the traces, PRISMA significantly reduces the effective output dimension. Our experimental results show that PRISMA achieves for a competitive $\varepsilon = 0.5$ a better data synthesis performance than prior tabular and marginal-based DP synthesis baselines by preserving the diversity of the original power consumption profiles without collapsing to a small set of modes.

papers.title: Prescribed spectral configurations under rank-one perturbations
papers.abstract:
A spectral configuration specifies the Fredholm set, the Fredholm index on each of its components, and, on zero-index components, either the whole component or a locally finite set of discrete eigenvalues with prescribed algebraic multiplicities. We show that any two spectral configurations with the same Fredholm set and index can be realized by a suitable closed operator \(A\) and a rank-one perturbation \(A+K\). This remains true even when the rank-one operator \(K\), acting on a given separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space, is prescribed in advance. In particular, for any such prescribed \(K\), one can choose \(A\) such that the discrete eigenvalues of \(A+K\) accumulate at the common essential spectrum at any prescribed rate.
  The proof is inspired by classical linearization theory. The main tool is the fact that arbitrary holomorphic functions can be represented as rank-one perturbation determinants.

papers.title: A unified and composable framework for modeling packed-bed liquid chromatography
papers.abstract: Packed-bed chromatography is a cornerstone of bioseparation, yet its modeling landscape remains fragmented by numerous model variants, inconsistent terminology, and limited structural clarity. While prior work has categorized and contrasted individual variants, our approach shifts the focus to unification. We present a unified, modular, and composable framework that integrates diverse mechanistic packed-bed chromatography models into a coherent structure. Starting from a high-resolution three-dimensional model, the framework systematically derives a hierarchy of reduced-order models through formal model order reduction. It encompasses a broad range of bulk transport phenomena, intraparticle mass transfer processes, binding mechanisms, and chemical reactions. Formulated orthogonally, these modules are independently meaningful and can be systematically combined into mathematically consistent models tailored to specific applications. The framework recovers and generalizes existing models, establishes a consistent taxonomy, and enables novel model combinations and extensions, including alternative column and particle geometries, particle-size and particle-type distributions, component-specific pore accessibility, rapid-equilibrium binding and reaction formulations, and size-exclusion with simultaneous binding. The framework is accessible through CADET-Equations, an interactive web application for model assembly and automatic generation of governing equations in LaTeX, promoting standardization and transparency. Its design principles are increasingly reflected throughout the CADET ecosystem, whose modular architecture supports the majority of the proposed model family. The generality and composable design of the framework provide a foundation for extending chromatography modeling software toward integrated bioseparation processes and advanced computational biotechnology applications.

papers.title: Bidirectional Cross-frequency Domain Interaction Network for UHD Low-Light Image Enhancement
papers.abstract: Existing Ultra-High-Definition (UHD) low-light image enhancement (LLIE) methods typically rely on either spatial- or frequency-domain modeling, or independently process different frequency components for efficient restoration. However, they often fail to jointly exploit complementary spatial--frequency information and the inherent relationship between illumination and structural information across frequencies, leading to inconsistent illumination, residual noise, and detail artifacts. In this paper, we propose a novel Bidirectional Cross-frequency Domain Interaction Network (BiFreqNet) for UHD LLIE. Specifically, BiFreqNet incorporates a Dual-domain Feature Interaction (DFI) module into the multi-scale representations of a pretrained variational autoencoder (VAE) to perform reciprocal enhancement between low- and high-frequency features. DFI consists of a Spatial and Spectral-Aware Low-Frequency Enhancement (S$^2$LFE) block and a Cross-Frequency Enhancement (CFE) block. S$^2$LFE exploits high-frequency structural cues to guide low-frequency restoration and jointly models spatial and spectral information to recover global exposure and spatially varying illumination while suppressing sensor noise. CFE further leverages the enhanced low-frequency contextual information to guide adaptive high-frequency refinement, enabling faithful reconstruction of structures and fine details. Extensive experiments on four general and UHD LLIE benchmarks demonstrate that BiFreqNet achieves competitive or superior performance compared with state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: Interfacial Orbital Rashba Edelstein Effect Identified in CoO/Cu/Pt Trilayers
papers.abstract: We investigate the generation of orbital angular momentum currents at engineered Cu-oxide interfaces using CoO/Cu/Pt thin-film trilayers. Angular-dependent magnetoresistance measurements on samples with varying Cu interlayer thickness reveal systematic changes in both longitudinal and transverse resistance components, including a sign inversion of the signal. By systematically varying the Cu interlayer thicknesses, we disentangle the spin and orbital contributions to the magnetoresistive response. Our results show that large orbital currents originate from the interfacial orbital Rashba-Edelstein effect due to the presence of the Cu-O bonds at the CoO/Cu interface. Unlike previously studied CoO/Cu bilayers that rely on uncontrolled natural oxidation, our trilayer geometry enables reproducible and stable orbital-current generation at ambient conditions. Our results identify Cu-oxide interfaces as efficient sources of orbital angular momentum and clarify the microscopic mechanism underlying orbital current generation. Consequently, this work establishes a well-defined materials platform for all-orbitronic devices that does not require relativistic spin-orbit coupling or orbital-spin interconversion processes.

papers.title: MANTA: Unlocking DAG Flexibility in Asynchronous BFT
papers.abstract:
DAG-based BFT protocols marked a shift in consensus design by replacing single-leader proposal paths with concurrent block proposals linked through a shared graph, where references encode consensus evidence. However, under heterogeneous wide-area networks (WANs), existing designs suffer from prolonged rounds and degraded performance due to straggler effects. The root cause is rigid round advancement: replicas move in synchronized rounds, waiting for enough references from the previous round before advancing.
  We propose a flexible DAG growth framework for asynchronous BFT consensus. Our key observation is that while reference quorums are necessary for safety and liveness, they need not block every round advancement. Instead, the connectivity required for commitment can be accumulated across rounds. Within the framework, we instantiate MANTA, which combines flexible DAG growth to advance by relaxing round synchronization and flexible coin to trigger leader election and finality earlier. Experiments on heterogeneous WAN deployments show that MANTA reduces latency by approximately 30%-70% in our evaluation.

papers.title: Finiteness of algebraic Weil-Petersson totally geodesic curves in pointed moduli spaces
papers.abstract:
For every pair $(g,n)$ with $2g-2+n>0$, we prove that $\mathcal M_{g,n}$ contains only finitely many closed algebraic curves that are totally geodesic for the Weil-Petersson metric. We show that every such curve is an arithmetic quadratic Teichm\"uller curve and has equal heights for all marked maximal cylinders in every periodic direction. Although there are infinitely many arithmetic Teichm\"uller curves, we can bound the degree of the associated torus covering by the crucial equal-height property. This leads to the desired finiteness statement.
  We also prove that quadratic Teichm\"uller curves are characterized by the existence of a holomorphic splitting of the logarithmic cotangent Kodaira-Spencer map. This result is the analogue of M\"oller and Viehweg's characterization of Kobayashi geodesics in $\mathcal A_g$.

papers.title: A living catalog of stream interaction regions in the Parker Solar Probe era
papers.abstract: Stream interaction regions (SIRs) and corotating interaction regions (CIRs) are important phenomena in heliospheric physics. These large-scale structures vary temporally and spatially, both in latitude and with radial distance. The additions of Parker Solar Probe (PSP) and Solar Orbiter have allowed for investigations into the radial evolution of these structures over a wide range of heliocentric distances for the first time since the Helios era. To better enable investigations of SIRs and CIRs within the inner heliosphere, we have developed a living catalog of SIR and CIR observations by Parker Solar Probe with corresponding observations by STEREO-A as well as ACE and Wind at 1 au. The methodology used for the identification of events and the generation of this catalog, the initial catalog of PSP observations spanning orbits one through five along with corresponding 1 au observations, and information on accessing the living catalog for future studies is described. This list of SIR and CIR events from PSP and corresponding observations from other heliophysics missions will enable case studies utilizing unique orbital arrangements, as well as aid in future statistical studies to further understand the properties and evolution of these structures.

papers.title: Hyperbolic complex tangencies on a four-sphere
papers.abstract: We construct a smooth embedding of $S^4$ into $\mathbb C^4$ whose CR-singular locus is a connected surface of genus two consisting entirely of nondegenerate hyperbolic points. Its image is locally polynomially convex and admits a basis of smoothly bounded, strongly pseudoconvex Stein tubular neighbourhoods.

papers.title: Dark Matter and MOND successes and degeneracies in reproducing SPARC rotation curves and weak lensing data
papers.abstract: The observed rotation velocities of spiral galaxies at large scales exceed those predicted by their baryonic components, motivating the need for dark matter (DM) or Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND). We fit the rotation curves of 147 late-type galaxies from the SPARC database, using a suite of models including Cold Dark Matter (CDM) models with and without baryonic feedback, Warm DM, Fuzzy DM, and MOND. We also combine SPARC kinematics with weak-lensing data to extend the mean rotation curves to ~1 Mpc. On a galaxy-by-galaxy basis, the inner SPARC rotation curves marginally favour CDM models with baryonic feedback, although accounting for the uncertainties in distances and inclinations increases the degeneracy among DM-based models and MOND. All DM models predict host halo masses larger than abundance-matching expectations, with only the CDM model with baryonic feedback reducing the scatter around the mean luminosity-halo mass relation. MOND is able to reproduce the flatness of the mean galactic rotation curves on scales up to 1 Mpc, providing stellar mass-to-light ratios within observational uncertainties. In contrast, all DM models, without the contribution of mass external to the bound halo, struggle to explain the flat rotation curves. The inclusion of the current weak-lensing data tends to favour MOND over DM models, at least at the largest scales. Future observations from BIG-SPARC, the Square Kilometre Array, and most importantly, upcoming weak-lensing surveys such as EUCLID and Rubin will provide more stringent and independent tests of these competing frameworks

papers.title: The Thermodynamic Complexity of Circuits
papers.abstract:
When any physical system executes a logically irreversible (non-injective) step of a computation, the excess heat released over the Landauer limit is an energetic cost that cannot be recovered. In modern computers this cost vastly dwarfs the Landauer cost. Modern stochastic thermodynamics refers to this cost as the ``entropy production'' and has derived fundamental lower bounds on its value. Here we introduce a thermodynamic model of circuits using heat functions and investigate its entropy production, deriving new results on the thermodynamic complexity of circuits.
  We first show that computing the optimal heat functions for gates in a given circuit (minimizing the entropy production) is PP-complete and multiplicative approximation of those heat functions is NP-hard, but additive approximation admits a polynomial-time randomized algorithm. We give tight bounds for entropy production for certain specific families of circuits (on uniformly distributed inputs): an $n$-ary AND tree of depth $O(\log n)$ requires $\Omega(n)$ entropy production, while a serial chain achieves $O(1)$ in an idealized model, showing an energy-depth tradeoff. The Batcher odd-even mergesort network on $n$ bits has $\Theta(n)$ entropy production, asymptotically less than its $\Theta(n \log^2 n)$ gate count. On random permutations of distinct integers its entropy production is $\Theta(n \log^2 n)$, asymptotically exceeding the Landauer cost of sorting; but preceding it with Leighton and Plaxton's almost-sorting network reduces the total heat released to $O(n \log n)$. Finally, we show how to sort $n$ values with zero circuit entropy production over any exchangeable input distribution. Our framework also yields streamlined proofs of known results in stochastic thermodynamics on mismatch cost and modularity cost.

papers.title: Distributional statistics of nonequilibrium
papers.abstract: We establish a reference modeling framework for random probability distributions subject to constraints. Generalizing the hyperensemble approach of Crooks, we formulate Jaynesian priors of maximal uncertainty over the unit simplex of categorical distributions. This framework is entirely general, but we primarily investigate models with constraints on physically relevant quantities, namely, average energy and Shannon entropy. A constraint on the exact value of average energy uniquely determines a Boltzmann-Gibbs equilibrium, but also defines a hyperplanar subset of the probability simplex consisting of all distributions with that value of average energy. The associated hyperensemble has a uniform probability density across all such distributions, regardless of distance to equilibrium. Such reference models make predictions of generic nonequilibrium properties such as the mean and modal microstate distributions and the expected free energy of a random distribution, which we examine analytically and via exact sampling algorithms. Moreover, introducing constraints on Shannon entropy permits parametric access to tunably nonequilibrium regimes. The approach follows conventional Jaynesian modeling logic and is compatible with standard Bayesian inference, and reduces to Boltzmann-Gibbs statistics when Shannon entropy is maximized. We examine the physical predictions of this scheme, and demonstrate its wide compatibility with other approaches to nonequilibrium modeling. We illustrate the framework in three scenarios: (i) comparison to superstatistics quasi-equilibrium modeling, (ii) generation of random nonequilibrium steady states, and (iii) Bayesian inference under a prior hyperensemble. We highlight numerous prospects for theoretical extensions and empirical application.

papers.title: O2D-MedNet: An Optimization-Aware Dual-Domain Framework for Robust Medical Image Segmentation
papers.abstract: Medical image segmentation (MIS) remains challenging due to composite degradations and multi-scale geometric variations, which jointly impair lesion-background separability, structural consistency, and optimization stability. Existing single-stream frameworks entangle heterogeneous cues within a single representation pathway, while hybrid-stream approaches often rely on generic or static fusion, limiting effective coordination across domains and failing to explicitly address optimization instability. To overcome these limitations, we propose a new optimization-aware dual-domain framework for MIS (O2D-MedNet). First, a degradation-aware dualdomain interaction (DDI) module integrates Fourier - and Wavelet-domain features to suppress degradation-sensitive responses while preserving structural and fine-detail information. Second, a cross-backbone contour-guided fusion (CGF) module enables selective interaction between CNN-based local detail modeling and visual state-space-based global structure modeling, improving boundary accuracy and representation consistency. Third, a gradient-context optimization (GCO) strategy stabilizes training by adaptively adjusting learning dynamics based on loss trends and gradient statistics, mitigating instability caused by class imbalance and heterogeneous sample difficulty. Extensive experiments on six benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art MIS methods across multiple imaging modalities. Further analyses confirm enhanced sensitivity, structural consistency, and optimization stability, validating the effectiveness of the proposed O2D-MedNet for robust MIS under heterogeneous conditions.

papers.title: Symmetry-resolved quasilocal entanglement as a key to Mott and pseudogap physics in plaquette CDMFT
papers.abstract: In order to identify intrinsic quantum resources in strongly interacting fermionic systems, we introduce a symmetry resolution of the parity-superselected two-site entanglement, as measured by both the fermionic negativity and the relative entropy of entanglement. We discuss how the symmetry resolution can be extended also to the full entanglement in pure and mixed two-site states. We apply our recipe to the Hubbard model, first for a dimer, and then for a plaquette cluster dynamical mean-field theory, an established method tailored to accurately capture short-range correlations. Following the evolution of the model through the interaction- and density-driven Mott transitions at zero temperature, we highlight how the three symmetry-resolved components of the two-site entanglement probe different key aspects of Mott and pseudogap physics.

papers.title: Assessing the detectability of a realistic massive black hole binary population in LSST
papers.abstract: Electromagnetic signatures of massive black hole binaries (MBHB) are expected to be found in quasar light curves. Specifically, MBHB light curves are expected to show periodic modulations which may originate from different physical processes. The detection of such periodicities requires algorithms suitable to model modulations with arbitrary shapes embedded in quasar red noise, in massive datasets. With the advent of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), such sources may finally be within reach in the next decade. In this work, we assess the performance of a recently proposed flexible detection algorithm for periodicities of arbitrary shapes with simulated LSST-like data that span its 10-year baseline. For the first time, we examine a physically motivated population of binaries and assess the effect of assumed priors on the period on the periodicity search. We study two methods to set the detection threshold: the first based on the posterior odds ratio, which assumes knowledge of the expected fraction of binaries in quasar light curves, and the second, which limits the detection of false positives. We find that the expected distribution of detected periods shows a clear peak between 5 and 10 years, depending on the specific LSST band considered. We recover a detected binary fraction ranging from ~ 20% to ~ 3% depending on the detection threshold assumed and the band analysed, with the peak of the observed period distribution depending on the underlying binary period distribution. Therefore, the detection of a population of binaries in LSST can constrain the binary population and shed light on their evolution.

papers.intro:
Massive black hole binaries (MBHBs) are expected to form as a consequence of the hierarchical growth of galaxies (Begelman et al., 1980, e.g.). Depending on their masses and orbital separations, these systems are expected to emit gravitational waves (GWs) in the frequency ranges probed by ongoing Pulsar Timing Array (PTA) experiments (Verbiest et al., 2016, see e.g.), by future space-based interferometers such as the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (Amaro-Seoane et al., 2017; Amaro-Seoane et al., 2023, LISA), and by Moon-based GW interferometers such as the Lunar Gravitational Wave Antenna (Ajith et al., 2025, LGWA, see).

Massive black hole binaries (MBHBs) are expected to form as a consequence of the hierarchical growth of galaxies (Begelman et al., 1980, e.g.). Depending on their masses and orbital separations, these systems are expected to emit gravitational waves (GWs) in the frequency ranges probed by ongoing Pulsar Timing Array (PTA) experiments (Verbiest et al., 2016, see e.g.), by future space-based interferometers such as the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (Amaro-Seoane et al., 2017; Amaro-Seoane et al., 2023, LISA), and by Moon-based GW interferometers such as the Lunar Gravitational Wave Antenna (Ajith et al., 2025, LGWA, see).

The GW detection rate from MBHBs remains highly uncertain. This is due to the wide range of physical scales involved in their evolution11 1 From ∼>10\mathrel{\hbox to0.0pt{\lower 3.0pt\hbox{$\sim$}\hss}\raise 2.0pt\hbox{$>$}}10 kpc to ∼<10−3\mathrel{\hbox to0.0pt{\lower 3.0pt\hbox{$\sim$}\hss}\raise 2.0pt\hbox{$<$}}10^{-3} pc, with the exact range depending on the massive black hole (MBH) and host galaxy properties. towards coalescence and the complex interaction between MBHs and their environment (see e.g. Singh et al., 2026; Izquierdo-Villalba et al., 2026, and references therein). The detection of MBHBs through electromagnetic observations can constrain the MBHB evolutionary path, the expected rate of GW mergers, and shed light on the PTA stochastic GW background (EPTA Collaboration et al., 2023; Agazie et al., 2023; Reardon et al., 2023; Xu et al., 2023, see). This task is highly non-trivial, as only MBH pairs at separations from kiloparsecs (e.g. Scialpi et al. 2024, see De Rosa et al. 2019 for a review) down to a few parsecs (Rodriguez et al., 2006, e.g.) can be directly resolved with current or upcoming facilities (Severgnini et al., 2026, e.g.,). The same is not feasible for smaller-separation binaries, for which a plethora of indirect methods have been proposed (see Bogdanovic et al., 2021; D’Orazio and Charisi, 2023, for recent reviews).

The same is not feasible for smaller-separation binaries, for which a plethora of indirect methods have been proposed (see Bogdanovic et al., 2021; D’Orazio and Charisi, 2023, for recent reviews).

Upcoming time-domain surveys, like the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory (Ivezić et al., 2019, see) and the High Latitude Time Domain Survey at the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope (Haiman et al., 2023, see) will provide unprecedented sky coverage, cadence, and multi-band photometry. In this context, one of the most promising signatures for the presence of a small-scale (Charisi et al., 2022, ≲10−2\lesssim 10^{-2} pc; e.g.) MBHB is the detection of a periodic modulation in AGN light curves. Such modulations are expected to originate from various physical processes. First, the interaction between a small-scale binary and the surrounding gas can drive periodic accretion, resulting in periodic modulations of the observed emission (MacFadyen and Milosavljević, 2008; Hayasaki et al., 2008, see). Second, when the binary separation is small enough, relativistic effects become important: Doppler boosting beams the emission along the direction of motion, producing a lighthouse-like effect (D’Orazio et al., 2015; Charisi et al., 2018, see). Third, if the MBHB is observed nearly edge-on, gravitational lensing can periodically magnify the emission from the minidiscs around each black hole (D’Orazio and Di Stefano, 2018; Kelley et al., 2021, see). The shapes of the periodic modulations due to such processes are expected to be very different: gravitational self-lensing produces narrow, spike-like features in the light curve (Hu et al., 2020, see) while periodic accretion generally yields asymmetric and irregular profiles (Duffell et al., 2020; Zrake et al., 2021; Westernacher-Schneider et al., 2022; Cocchiararo et al., 2024, see). Only Doppler boosting from nearly circular binaries is expected to produce approximately sinusoidal modulations (D’Orazio et al., 2015, see).

Only Doppler boosting from nearly circular binaries is expected to produce approximately sinusoidal modulations (D’Orazio et al., 2015, see).

Detecting such modulations is complicated by the intrinsic variability of AGN (Ulrich et al., 1997, see). Such variability is well described as red noise (see Paolillo and Papadakis, 2025, for a recent overview), a stochastic process with a power spectral density decreasing with increasing frequency. Such intrinsic noise introduces long-term correlation in the observed light curve, mimicking periodic signals when the observational baseline spans only a few apparent cycles of the underlying modulation (Vaughan et al., 2016; Witt et al., 2022; Robnik et al., 2024, see).

Such intrinsic noise introduces long-term correlation in the observed light curve, mimicking periodic signals when the observational baseline spans only a few apparent cycles of the underlying modulation (Vaughan et al., 2016; Witt et al., 2022; Robnik et al., 2024, see).

Standard periodicity identification methods, such as the Lomb-Scargle periodogram analysis (see VanderPlas, 2018, for a review), have been shown to struggle when the shape deviates from being sinusoidal and in the presence of red noise (Lin et al., 2026, see). For this reason, more robust algorithms, leveraging, for example, Gaussian processes (Covino et al., 2022; Rigamonti et al., 2025; Foustoul et al., 2025, GPs, e.g.), matched filtering (Park et al., 2026, e.g.) and coherence-based searches (Kovačević et al., 2026, e.g.) have been proposed. Such methods rely either on the assumption of dealing with a sinusoidal modulation or on knowledge of the specific shape of the modulation (e.g. the matched filtering algorithms). Recently, Bertassi et al. (2026, henceforth referred to as Paper 1) proposed a pipeline that allows the detection of periodicities with arbitrary shapes, expanding on previous GP-based algorithms. This is particularly important as periodic signals from MBHBs are rarely expected to be sinusoidal (D’Orazio and Di Stefano, 2018; Cocchiararo et al., 2024, e.g.).

The goal of this work is to determine the expected fraction of detectable MBHBs by LSST assuming a realistic underlying population of binaries through the application of the analysis proposed in Paper 1. The effect of a realistic binary population has been neglected in previous studies, which assumed broad and uninformative distributions of the binary periods (Vaughan et al., 2016; Witt et al., 2022; Banaszak et al., 2026, e.g.). Incorporating the effects of realistic period distribution is necessary, as previous studies (see, e.g. Witt et al., 2022; Lin et al., 2026, and Paper 1) found higher detection rates for shorter-period binaries, whereas the population is expected to be dominated by longer-period binaries.

papers.title: VulDec: Vulnerability Detection in Binaries via Neural Decompilation
papers.abstract: Automated vulnerability detection in binary executables is challenging due to the lack of source code and the limited semantic information available at the assembly level. Despite significant progress in machine-learning-based code analysis, the field still lacks methodologies and large, high-quality datasets that provide vulnerable code jointly at assembly- and source-level with precise vulnerability labels. To address this gap, we introduce VulDec, consisting of (i) a new large-scale, carefully curated dataset aligning real-world Assembly-C function pairs with detailed CWE annotations across multiple architectures, and (ii) the first end-to-end framework that leverages neural decompilation for binary vulnerability detection. Tuned LLM-based neural decompilers trained on our dataset achieve strong source-level recovery across architectures (Edit Similarity of approximately 56%, BLEU-4 of approximately 43%), while our tuned LLM-based detectors reach a macro F1-score of 0.61 on an in-distribution realistic test set (3% vulnerability rate). Our findings provide evidence that neural decompilation offers a powerful alternative to conventional low-level binary representations, facilitating robust binary vulnerability detection.

papers.title: Enhancing LLM-Based Vulnerability Detection via Representation-Aware Logical Ensemble
papers.abstract: Automated vulnerability detection in C source code is a long-standing challenge, as traditional static analysis tools often trade precision for scalability and struggle with complex vulnerability patterns. Recently, large language models (LLMs) have shown promising results; yet, most approaches rely on a single code representation, implicitly assuming uniform suitability across vulnerability types. In this work, we systematically study LLM-based vulnerability detection under multiple code representations, including raw source code, Abstract Syntax Trees (AST), and Control Flow Graphs (CFG). Through extensive empirical analysis, we show that different representations exhibit complementary strengths, with specific views being more effective for particular classes of vulnerabilities. Building on these findings, we propose a Representation-Aware Logical Ensemble (RALE) that integrates LLMs trained on different code representations through explicit logical rules and majority voting. While single-representation models achieve up to 73% F1-score, our integrated approach reaches 78% F1-score, with commensurate gains in accuracy, precision, and recall, consistently outperforming individual models. These results highlight the importance of explicitly leveraging complementary code representations when combining LLMs for effective vulnerability detection.

papers.title: Inverse problems with fractional operators: an analytical study and its numerical linear algebra treatment via the GLT theory
papers.abstract: Fractional derivatives model memory effects and nonlocal interactions beyond classical integer-order models. Fractional differential equations (FDEs) thus describe anomalous diffusion, transport in heterogeneous media, and hereditary dynamics. Their nonlocality, however, makes inverse problems challenging: unknown sources, coefficients, or initial conditions must be recovered from indirect and noisy data. Inverse problems for FDEs are usually ill-posed in the Hadamard sense, so regularization, such as the quasi-boundary value method, is required for stable reconstruction. Discretization produces large linear systems whose matrices inherit the nonlocal structure of fractional operators. Understanding the asymptotic spectral properties of these matrix sequences is essential for efficient solvers and preconditioners. Generalized Locally Toeplitz (GLT) theory provides a unified framework for the spectral distribution of large structured matrices and for preconditioner design. This thesis uses GLT theory to analyze matrix sequences from inverse problems for FDEs, construct structure-preserving preconditioners, and study nonlinear operations in the GLT algebra. In particular, it proves maximal distribution results for geometric means of GLT sequences: when the symbols commute, the geometric mean sequence remains GLT without symbol invertibility. This resolves a long-standing conjecture and shows maximality in the noncommuting degenerate case. Overall, the thesis integrates regularization, spectral analysis, and preconditioning into a coherent computational framework for inverse problems in nonlocal fractional dynamics, while enriching structured matrix analysis.

papers.title: Dancing circles
papers.abstract: Recent results on diffeomorphisms of $4$-manifolds make essential use of families of embeddings of $1$-manifolds into $4$-manifolds. We survey what is currently known about such families.

papers.title: RIDE-Splat: Reflection Removal for In-the-Wild Driving Environments
papers.abstract: Driving video captured through a windshield violates the world-space consistency assumed by 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS): the road scene exhibits parallax while cabin reflections remain attached to the camera, causing standard 3DGS to embed reflected content into the reconstructed scene. We introduce RIDE-Splat, a pipeline for reflection-free 3D reconstruction from posed driving video without clean images, reflection masks, or pretrained networks. RIDE-Splat assigns world-consistent transmission through the windshield to a 3DGS scene and the dominant camera-attached reflection to one shared, signed RGB image. It builds the clean reconstruction in two passes. First, it learns the 3D geometry and the signed reflection image, representing both added radiance and transmission attenuation. Then, it uses the reflection-removed training images to fit a clean 3DGS model. At inference, the reflection image is discarded, preserving the standard 3DGS rendering path. We also introduce the RIDE-Splat Dataset, the first 3D reconstruction benchmark for reflection removal from driving video -- with real driving scenes, physical windshield reflections in training views, and separately captured non-reflective evaluation images. Across the RIDE-Splat Dataset, XLD, and Wayve, RIDE-Splat outperforms 3DGS, DC-Gaussian, and RobustSplat on all nine aggregate metrics, improving PSNR by up to 3.59 dB and reducing LPIPS by up to 0.0876. We achieve the highest metrics in 38 out of 42 per-scene comparisons and removes windshield reflections that remain visible in the baselines while preserving the transmitted scene.

authors.name: Alex Hanson
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: Unbelievably Complex
papers.abstract: We present the directed simplicial complex: this is an extension of a simplicial complex with a direction on its faces. This enables us to model a local notion of belief in a three-valued semantics, in which formulas may be true, false, or undefined. Of particular interest is a class of directed simplicial complexes called cups, in which any maximal set of vertices of different colors is a facet. Cups permit a more concise relational representation. We give examples and applications of our logical semantics. We then provide a sound and complete axiomatization for the class of directed simplicial complexes and extend it to an axiomatization for the class of cups. We include a detailed technical comparison with other works on belief on complexes. Our work generalizes a prior axiomatization for knowledge on (undirected) impure simplicial complexes.

authors.name: Hans van Ditmarsch
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Investigating supernova-remnant X-ray maps with dendrogram-based techniques
papers.abstract: X-ray images of supernova remnants provide important information regarding the spatial distribution of the physical and chemical parameters of the shocked plasma. Our objective is to provide a comprehensive and quantitative assessment of the similarities observed across narrow-band images and equivalent-width maps of a given supernova remnant. We also aim to perform comparative analyses between distinct remnants. We adopted two dendrogram-based techniques, namely a multivariate analysis and a deep-learning, graph-based approach (by exploring different metrics) for the study of Chandra X-ray maps of Cassiopeia A, G292.0+1.8, Tycho's SNR, Kepler's SNR, and W49B. We also tested the reliability of our results on synthetic X-ray maps produced from a 3D hydrodynamic simulation of Cassiopeia A. We identify clusters of narrow-band images (and equivalent-width maps) corresponding to emission lines of chemical elements that are expected to be synthesized in the same layers of the exploding star and/or that originate from plasma at similar temperatures. By comparing different objects, we clearly observe strong similarities among Type Ia remnants (namely Tycho's SNR and Kepler's SNR) and core-collapse remnants (Cassiopeia A and G292.0+1.8), with W49B being more similar to the latter objects. The methodology developed in this work provides a robust tool to measure the analogies and differences between narrow-band images and equivalent-width maps of a supernova remnant, offering clues on the distribution of the different chemical species and on the plasma temperature. Although tested on a limited sample of objects, the adoption of this tool for the classification of supernova remnants (Type Ia vs. core-collapse) yields promising results.

authors.name: E. Greco
authors.institution: Saint Camillus International University of Health and Medical Sciences

papers.title: Simplified Parisi Ansatz III: Constructive Cavity Method and Ultrametricity
papers.abstract: We present a physical explaination of the Constructive Cavity Method (CCM) for the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model, which identifies the decomposition of the cavity variables into layers with the random overlap structure of Aizenman--Sims--Starr. We describe the low-temperature excitations through a dilute gas of defects relative to the ground state. The sharing of these defects among the descendants and the renewal of the fluctuations along new branches produce the GREM structure and the ultrametricity of the overlaps. This mechanism is developed first with a finite number of defects and then extended to exponential populations of states. At fixed kernel, the Gaussian covariances of the fresh fields connect the complete cavity variables, including their common components, to the same hierarchy that determines the Gibbs masses. We also correct some ambiguities of earlier formulations.

papers.title: Global $\mathcal{O}\left(k^{-2}\right)$ Convergence of Multilevel Gradient-Regularized Newton Methods
papers.abstract: We develop and analyze multilevel gradient-regularized Newton methods for unconstrained convex optimization with Lipschitz-continuous Hessians. By computing Newton corrections in lower-dimensional subspaces, the proposed methods aim to reduce computational costs while preserving the global $\mathcal{O}\left(k^{-2}\right)$ convergence rate in function values of the full-space method. To establish this rate for multilevel methods, we introduce a class of row-nested restriction operators that ensures monotonicity of the reduced-gradient norms across levels. Numerical experiments with row-nested operators demonstrate convergence behavior comparable to full-space gradient-regularized Newton, while offering substantial computational savings on large-scale instances.

papers.title: Geoeconomic Stress and European Defence Readiness
papers.abstract: This study develops a country-level measure of the economic-industrial capacity of European NATO Allies to mobilise, replenish, maintain, and sustain military capability under strategic stress. The measure comprises four components: macroeconomic capacity, sectoral resilience, defence-industrial capability, and logistics and sustainment. The analysis covers 28 European Allies and evaluates a balanced baseline against five geoeconomic stress scenarios. The results distinguish baseline capacity from stress vulnerability and provide an assessment framework for identifying the economic-industrial bottlenecks that can constrain sustained military readiness. Baseline scores vary materially across countries, with a sample mean of 0.610 and a range from 0.471 to 0.759. The calibrated geoeconomic shocks reduce effective capacity in every scenario, though the effects are highly heterogeneous. The combined-stress scenario has the largest average effect, lowering the sample mean to 0.491, a decline of 19.5 per cent relative to baseline. TRS and PR operate mainly through defence-industrial and replenishment constraints; supply-chain fragmentation is driven primarily by sectoral exposure and substitutability; and external-support reduction operates through allied access and sustainment. Our results suggest shifting attention from expenditure targets alone towards the capacity to convert resources into usable military capability: the key issue is not only how much is spent, but also which bottlenecks limit the conversion of resources into capability.

papers.title: The biases caused by interpolated table models and their impact on X-ray spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Models for X-ray spectroscopy involving complex relativistic or plasma physics are commonly pre-computed on a grid, In this paper, we aim to quantify the potential biases and distortions introduced by the computational error and propagated into parameter inference by interpolating linearly these complex, non-linear models. We analyse the performance of Bayesian sampling algorithms on mock inference problems. Then, we model real observations of an accreting black hole X-ray binary in both the soft and hard states. We find that linear interpolation can a) greatly bias the posterior distribution of model parameters and b) distort the likelihood space to such a degree that posterior distributions become artificially multimodal. This multi-modality causes a noticeable loss in computational efficiency in both sampling and fitting techniques. As a result, exploring a given parameter space until convergence requires an extremely large computational cost. These findings call for improving the computational techniques used when fitting modern X-ray data, for example through better sampling algorithms and/or more sophisticated interpolation schemes

papers.title: Regularized Sequential Reconstructions of Dynamic Nonsmooth Sources from Sparse Boundary Flux Data
papers.abstract: We consider an inverse source problem for the heat equation on the unit disk $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ with flux measurements at finitely many boundary points. The source is piecewise constant in time on prescribed intervals and, on each interval, is the characteristic function of an unknown region with Lipschitz boundary. The measurements on each interval split into the contribution of the current source and a history term from earlier sources; subtracting the latter leaves a linear inverse problem for a forward operator $F_\tau$ that is densely defined and unbounded on $L^2(\Omega)$. We prove that $F_\tau$ is not closable, so the classical regularization theory for closed unbounded operators does not apply. We regularize instead with a Hilbert-scale penalty that compactifies it. The resulting Galerkin--Tikhonov reconstruction is sequential: each source is recovered from the flux observed up to the end of its interval and from the previously reconstructed sources. We prove its convergence and uniqueness, show that earlier reconstruction errors propagate into later data with exponential decay in time, and establish stability estimates with respect to the number of sensors. A numerical experiment on noisy measurements shows the feasibility of the sequential approximations, refined by Fourier approximation and boundary correction by a neural network.

papers.title: Smoothing splines with some discontinuities
papers.abstract: We generalize cubic smoothing splines to signals with a finite number of discontinuities at unknown positions. Rather than changing the roughness penalty, we deform the domain over which it is computed: every interval between consecutive observations can be stretched by a non-negative warp, subject to a total budget, and the optimizer spends the budget only where a jump makes stretching cheaper than bending. The estimator inherits the state-space form of smoothing splines, so it can be fitted by maximum likelihood with the Kalman filter, and it also admits a fast alternating algorithm that solves a banded linear system and takes a projected-gradient step on the warps. The budget is selected by an extended Bayesian information criterion whose constant is calibrated by simulation. In a Monte Carlo comparison the new estimators reconstruct a piecewise-smooth signal more accurately than the cubic smoothing spline with discontinuities of Storath and Weinmann, at the cost of more false alarms. Two energy applications illustrate the method: the temperature response of electricity demand in Northern Italy, and retail fuel prices, whose discontinuities, changes in excise duties, are dated by public record. The three supplements follow the references.

papers.title: Complete Cancer Prevalence Predictions via LASSO Regularization and Flexible Parametric Survival Cure Models
papers.abstract: Cancer prevalence is a key measure of disease burden, and accurate projections are essential for healthcare planning and resource allocation. The Prevalence Incidence Analysis Model (PIAMOD) is widely used to estimate and project cancer prevalence in population-based studies by combining incidence rates and net survival within a forward calculation framework. We propose an improved approach to projecting cancer prevalence by using regularization techniques to select the optimal incidence model and flexible parametric survival cure models to improve the estimation of net survival. The proposed and conventional approaches were compared through a simulation study and an application to population-based data on patients diagnosed with colon cancer in Sweden between 1958 and 2019. Applying the proposed methodology, colon cancer prevalence in Sweden was projected through 2030. The number of individuals living with a previous diagnosis of colon cancer is projected to continue increasing, reaching approximately 550 per 100\,000 males and 500 per 100\,000 females by 2030. Careful model selection is essential when estimating measures of disease burden such as cancer prevalence. The projected increase in colon cancer prevalence in Sweden reflects continued improvements in survival for both sexes and highlights the growing number of individuals living with colon cancer.

papers.title: RAGing Against Misogyny: Improving Implicit Misogyny Explanations
papers.abstract: Implicit misogyny often requires background knowledge to be understood. To address this challenge, we propose a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework for detecting and explaining implicit misogyny in English and Italian, leveraging encyclopedic, slang and feminist knowledge sources. Using the ImplicIT-Mis and SBIC+ datasets, we evaluate the contribution of each knowledge source to detection and explanation quality, investigating also whether RAG addresses known LLM failure modes in implicit misogyny. Results show that RAG improves recall on ImplicIT-Mis, but does not improve detection performance on SBIC+. However, human evaluation shows that RAG-based explanations are preferred over no-RAG explanations in both languages. Feminist literature emerges as the most consistently useful source for detection and explanation.

papers.title: Strongly Adaptive Online Learning with Time-Varying Movement Costs
papers.abstract: We study strongly adaptive regret for Online Convex Optimization (OCO) with time-varying movement costs, a setting that evaluates a learner's performance over arbitrary sub-intervals. This framework captures complex sequential decision-making problems where both the environment and the cost of switching decisions fluctuate over time. We propose a novel algorithm which, for any interval $[a,b] \subseteq [T]$, achieves a data-dependent regret bound of $ \widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\left( \sqrt{(D^2+DP_{[a,b]})\sum_{t \in [a,b]}(\|g_t\|^2+\lambda_t\|g_t\|)} \right) $, where $D$ is the diameter of the decision domain, $P_{[a,b]}$ is the path length of the comparator sequence over $[a,b]$, $g_t$ is the gradient of the loss, and $\lambda_t$ is the movement-cost coefficient at round $t$. Key to our approach is a novel reduction to sleeping experts with movement costs, a previously unexplored variant that is of independent interest. As a result of this development, we further establish the first strongly-adaptive guarantees under delayed feedback. Our approach also naturally extends to OCO with time-varying memory, where we obtain strongly-adaptive guarantees which improve the best-known bounds.

papers.intro:
Online convex optimization (OCO) (Cesa-Bianchi and Lugosi, 2006; Hazan, 2016; Orabona, 2019) is a fundamental framework for sequential decision making under uncertainty. At each round, a learner selects a decision wtw_{t} in a convex decision set 𝒲\mathcal{W} before observing the current loss function ft:𝒲→ℝf_{t}:\mathcal{W}\to\mathbb{R}, and then incurring the corresponding loss ft​(wt)f_{t}(w_{t}). The objective is to design algorithms whose cumulative loss is close to that of a benchmark comparator sequence chosen in hindsight. Classic (static) regret guarantees compare the learner’s performance against a single fixed comparator over the entire time horizon, and are therefore most appropriate in stationary environments. However, many modern applications are inherently non-stationary: the best decision may evolve over time, the environment may undergo abrupt shifts, and the performance on short or intermediate time intervals can be just as important as performance over the full horizon.

Several regret notions have been developed to capture such non-stationarity settings. Dynamic regret (Zinkevich, 2003; Zhang et al., 2018) takes a global perspective by comparing the learner against a time-varying comparator sequence over the entire horizon, RT(u1:T)≜∑t=1Tft(wt)−ft(ut).R_{T}(u_{1:T})\triangleq\sum_{t=1}^{T}f_{t}(w_{t})-f_{t}(u_{t}). By contrast, strongly-adaptive regret (Daniely et al., 2015) requires the learner to achieve low static regret simultaneously on every contiguous time interval. In this paper, we answer this question affirmatively by developing the first strongly-adaptive algorithms for OCO with time-varying movement costs. Our main technical ingredient is a reduction that decomposes the regret of a mixture predictor into two components: the movement-cost regret of a base expert and the movement-cost regret of a meta-algorithm for the sleeping experts problem.
