papers.title: Vector space embeddings of modal logic formulas: theory and application
papers.abstract: Reasoning tasks over modal logics are notoriously difficult, comprising problems which are often semi-decidable. Hence, it is not rare for applications leveraging such tasks to exploit heuristic approaches able to give results in an acceptable amount of time, at the cost of some inaccuracies. Some approaches may benefit from vector embeddings, allowing for instance to involve neural networks and machine learning models in the reasoning process. This work aims at providing a new way to provide such embeddings specifically for the modal case, aiming for faster reasoning through both mathematical and learning techniques.

papers.title: Second order N-Electron Valence state Perturbation Theory for polaritonic systems
papers.abstract: Molecules strongly coupled to optical cavities often show multi-configurational character, which the cavity can enhance by mixing electronic states. Describing them accurately requires a complete treatment of correlation between all the involved quantum particles. The available QED ab-initio methods do not treat it in its completeness except for QED-FCI. We extend second-order N-electron valence state perturbation theory (NEVPT2) to polaritonic chemistry, in its state-specific (QED-NEVPT2) and quasi degenerate (QED-QD-NEVPT2) forms. Here, the correlation due to the interaction of more degenerate configurations comes from a QED-CASSCF reference, while that associated with instantaneous interactions between the particles is added by second-order perturbation theory. Application of the methods to ammonia, ethylene and formaldimine revealed that this approach represents the perfect alternative to the well established QED-Coupled Cluster approach when the molecular system is described by more degenerate configurations. The approaches developed in this work have the potential to become state-of-the-art methodologies for the description of reactivity and photochemistry in polaritonic systems.

papers.title: A low-volume cold-atom microwave clock with an additively manufactured cavity
papers.abstract: We present the performance of a compact microwave interrogated atomic clock based on laser cooled $^{87}$$\rm{Rb}$ atoms. The clock utilizes a micro-fabricated grating magneto-optical trap (gMOT) to cool and trap atoms, and an additively manufactured microwave cavity for microwave interrogation. We demonstrate a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of $370$ at a 1 Hz bandwidth and mid-term instability of $6.7\times10^{-14}$ at an averaging time of $\tau=3 \times 10^{4}$ s. In addition, a low cost mu-metal foil has been implemented on the vacuum chamber to reduce the quadratic Zeeman shift which was previously limiting stability beyond $\tau = 10$ s.

authors.name: Sean Dyer
authors.institution: John H. Stroger, Jr. Hospital of Cook County

papers.title: Zeeman-field-induced three-spin interactions and relativistic coupling to the scalar spin chirality
papers.abstract: Magnetic fields are commonly incorporated in atomistic spin models through the Zeeman energy of individual magnetic moments. Starting from a microscopic electronic Hamiltonian, we show that the Zeeman coupling of conduction electrons also generates field-linear three-spin interactions, the lowest-order corrections allowed by time-reversal symmetry. Using a Green-function expansion of the grand potential, we identify two classes of interactions. Isotropic terms of the form $(\mathbf S_i\cdot\mathbf S_j)(\mathbf S_k\cdot\mathbf B)$ exist without spin-orbit coupling, and their total strength obeys a sum rule involving the three-site electronic loop at the Fermi energy. Relativistic terms require spin-orbit coupling and include $\mathbf K_{ijk}\cdot\mathbf B,\chi_{ijk}$, where $\chi_{ijk}=\mathbf S_i\cdot(\mathbf S_j\times\mathbf S_k)$ is the scalar spin chirality. We show that this coupling is forbidden in the spin channel without spin-orbit coupling, whereas the orbital channel recovers the orbital-flux mechanism of Mott insulators. Exact diagonalization of the Hubbard trimer confirms the independence and additivity of both channels. For magnetic trimers in Rashba electron gases, we derive analytical expressions showing that $\mathbf K_{ijk}$ lies in-plane at first order in spin-orbit coupling but vanishes for $C_{3v}$-symmetric trimers, where an out-of-plane component emerges at second order. These interactions can shift magnetization-step fields and modify field-induced noncoplanarity. In the continuum limit, the chirality coupling splits skyrmions from antiskyrmions, while the relativistic terms generate a field-dependent Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction.

papers.title: Curvature-induced fracture mode coupling in doubly curved shells
papers.abstract: Classical shell fracture theories predominantly consider cracks aligned with principal curvature directions in cylindrical and spherical shells under tensile mode or pressure loading, leaving the fracture behavior of arbitrarily oriented cracks in doubly curved shells under general loading poorly understood. Here, we introduce a semi-analytical framework based on Reissner shallow-shell theory to investigate isotropic shells with positive, zero, and negative Gaussian curvature. The formulation computes stress intensity factors, energy release rates, and crack-lip displacements for arbitrarily inclined through-thickness cracks in spheres, ellipsoids, cylinders, hyperboloids, and minimal surfaces under general mechanical loading. We show that shell curvature couples opening, sliding, and tearing, allowing a single loading component to activate multiple fracture modes, unlike in flat plates. This coupling depends strongly on crack orientation and the normal, parallel, and torsional components of the shell curvature. Ellipsoids exhibit weak coupling, hyperboloids generally exhibit the strongest coupling, and cylinders display the most complex orientation-dependent responses. Moreover, in-plane shear can induce crack closure in hyperboloidal shells, suggesting a potential geometric mechanism for enhanced damage resistance. These findings elucidate the role of local curvature in fracture-mode coupling and provide a mechanistic foundation for the analysis of shellular (meta-)structures with engineered curvature distributions.

papers.title: VPR-Space: A Benchmark for Visual Place Recognition in Space Analog Domains
papers.abstract: Visual Place Recognition (VPR) is an important means for loop closure detection in visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM). While state-of-the-art VPR and SLAM approaches excel in urban and feature-rich natural environments, the vast and feature-poor environments of extraterrestrial surfaces like on the Moon or Mars pose severe challenges for existing approaches. This paper presents a novel benchmark, VPR-Space, to evaluate VPR capabilities on extraterrestrial surfaces. There are three contributions: (1) We collected sixteen VPR database-query datasets based on existing data from Space Analog Domains (SAD), terrestrial environments that resemble properties of the Moon or Mars. The collection includes a range of challenges regarding environment, viewpoint change, and illumination conditions. (2) To address the ill-posed nature of VPR, we propose a novel approach to generate the ground-truth information in VPR benchmarks. Instead of defining that a query and datbase image show the same place if and only if their camera poses are within fixed position and viewing direction thresholds, we propose to make the decision dependent on whether the match would be valuable in the downstream SLAM task. To avoid the overhead and restrictions of evaluating VPR in-the-loop within SLAM systems, we provide VPR ground-truth (GT) matrices based on the performance of an ensemble of state-of-the-art Relative Pose Estimators (RPE). Under this GT we require a VPR method to identify exactly those image pairs for which a subsequently applied RPE is expected to provide a valuable pose estimate in a SLAM context. (3) We evaluated nine state-of-the-art VPR approaches. The results show considerable room for improvement and indicate directions for future research. We provide a pre-release version of the dataset on github: $\texttt{https://github.com/rfechner/VPR-Space}$

papers.title: The Intermediate Silicon Tracker Detector for sPHENIX
papers.abstract: A new barrel-type silicon detector has been constructed in the central rapidity region of the sPHENIX experiment as part of its charged-particle tracking system. The detector, referred to as the intermediate silicon tracker (INTT), provides single-event timing capability and contributes to charged-particle tracking in combination with the silicon-pixel vertex detector and the time-projection chamber. The INTT consists of two cylindrical barrels with full azimuthal coverage. The inner and outer barrels comprise 24 and 32 silicon strip ladders, respectively. Each ladder consists of four silicon strip sensors, covering the pseudorapidity range $|\eta| < 1.07$ for collision vertices within $\pm~10$ cm along the beam axis, at radial distances between 72 and 103 mm. The INTT has been fully integrated into the sPHENIX data acquisition system, with detector signals processed by eight FELIX servers. Continuous data taking is enabled by a streaming readout mode, in which detector data are accumulated without hardware triggers, while a conventional trigger-based mode is also supported. The detector achieves stable operation, small inactive area, and high efficiency, providing precise timing, tracking, and vertexing performance during the collection of beam-beam collision data.

papers.title: XL MIMO Extreme Learning Machines: Wave-Domain Inference with Stacked Metasurfaces
papers.abstract: The recently envisioned goal-oriented communications paradigm requires machine learning inference to be performed directly on wirelessly transferred data, by splitting neural network computations between the transmitter, the Receiver (RX), and the wireless channel. Such approaches aim to offload large portions of the computation onto the channel itself, which is often controlled by reconfigurable MetaSurfaces (MSs). Typical MS-parametrized systems, however, enable only limited computation offloading in the wave domain, usually corresponding to a single neural network layer, due to adverse channel fading effects and the almost linear operation of the channel and conventional MS models. In this paper, we demonstrate that an eXtremely Large (XL) Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) system equipped with Stacked Intelligent MSs (SIM) at the RX side, together with a single antenna and its accompanying radio-frequency chain, may act as a two-layer neural network operating exclusively over the air. The first (uncontrollable) network layer corresponds to the transformations offered by wireless fading, while the second (controllable) layer is implemented via SIM operations. In particular, only the first, front-end MS layer needs to exhibit nonlinear response to serve as an activation function. Leveraging the Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) framework, the proposed XL MIMO system architecture is shown to be a universal approximator, and the optimal linear-SIM-based combining is derived in closed form, allowing for fast training even and partial signal observability. Numerical evaluations across diverse datasets showcase that the proposed XL-MIMO-ELM framework achieves classification accuracy comparable to idealized digital models, thereby, proving the viability of low complexity, wave-domain neural computations.

papers.title: The LALA Benchmark: Evaluating Literary and Linguistic Analysis in LLMs
papers.abstract: We introduce the Literature and Linguistics Analysis Benchmark (LALA), comprising 236 open-ended questions written by experts in linguistics and literary studies, together with expert-provided ideal answers. By comparing models within families and at similar training scales using human and LLM judges, LALA identifies differences in linguistic competence associated with post-training, offering a framework for evaluating future models and guiding targeted improvements. We administered questions to 17 language models and evaluated their responses using both human expert assessment and two LLM evaluators, Sol and Qwen. Base models displayed little of the linguistic competence assessed by the benchmark, whereas their post-trained versions performed markedly better, suggesting that post-training plays a central role in making linguistic knowledge accessible and usable. Parameter count, by contrast, showed no statistically significant association with partial-credit performance, and competencies remained unevenly distributed across linguistic domains. We interpret this pattern as evidence that post-training adds linguistic competencies piecemeal, without producing a general linguistic intelligence capable of extending them beyond the learned policies that support them. Models performed best on logical relations between statements and selected discourse-level tasks, while even the strongest post-trained models continued to struggle with ambiguity, literary style, reference, and misleading assumptions. Human and Sol evaluations produced nearly identical model rankings in both the original and ReliableEval runs, supporting the replicability of the comparative results.

papers.title: From Parameter Rebasin to Functional Transfer Across Heterogeneous Transformers
papers.abstract: Adapting pretrained Transformers to downstream tasks produces task-specific updates that are expensive to reproduce for every model variant. Reusing these updates across different depths and widths is challenging because their parameters have incompatible shapes and do not share a canonical coordinate system. We introduce Ariadne, a training-free method that transfers task-specific behavior across heterogeneous Transformers without resizing the source model or transporting its parameters. Rather than treating the source task vector, i.e. the difference in parameter space between the fine-tuned and the base models, as the object to move, Ariadne characterizes fine-tuning by the activation changes it induces at matched blocks. First, it aligns these effects to a target base through local Procrustes maps. Then, it directly synthesizes a native target update by closed-form ridge regression. Across Transformer expansion, reduction and language-model transfer, Ariadne improves target-model performance while substantially reducing the time and memory required to construct an update relative to previous cross-architecture rebasin approaches. These results show that local functional effects provide an efficient alternative to parameter transport.

A single pretrained checkpoint can give rise to many fine-tuned task variants, represented as task vectors (Ilharco et al., 2023), each defined in the parameterization of its source architecture. This coupling is limiting in practice. For example, a practitioner may have an instruction-tuned assistant at one Transformer depth and width, but later need to deploy the same instruction-following behavior in a smaller model under a tighter serving budget, or in a newer and larger backbone. Similarly, reducing depth can lower latency and memory use, while expansion can make an existing model family compatible with a larger target architecture. Retraining every task-specific model in the new architecture may be unavailable or prohibitively expensive; it also repeats substantial training compute and its associated energy use. The practical goal is therefore to reuse task-specific behavior across heterogeneous Transformer architectures without repeating fine-tuning.

This typically entails assumptions on the backbone and relative depth of the models, together with architectural resampling operations such as block copying, interpolation, or deletion to match their depths. To reach these goals, Ariadne adopts a different transfer paradigm. Rather than transporting the source task vector, it transfers the observable effect of source fine-tuning, that is the change in the transformer block activation induced by fine-tuning. For each matched pair of Transformer blocks, Ariadne aligns source and target base residual-stream states with a local Procrustes map and uses it to express the source fine-tuning activation displacement in target coordinates. Then, a closed-form ridge regression computes an additive update to one residual-writing target component that matches this desired effect. The base-model relation is therefore only a local coordinate bridge, not the optimization target. The resulting update is native to the target backbone and requires neither a target fine-tuned checkpoint, source resizing, parameter transport, nor inference-time interventions. The name of the method recalls Ariadne’s thread: the activation displacement guides construction of an update through a differently structured target model. papers.title: Large spin large deviations for interacting particle systems
papers.abstract:
We propose a novel framework for analyzing the sample-path large deviations of interacting particle systems directly on a lattice by considering a large-spin limit ($s \to \infty$). Through an appropriate scaling of variables, the process concentrates around its deterministic trajectory, governed by the lattice diffusion equation. We quantify the exponential cost of observing atypical trajectories by explicitly computing the path-space large deviation rate function from the scaled microscopic generator, based on a theory due to Feng and Kurtz. The rate function is described in terms of a Hamiltonian on a lattice in terms of classical spin variables. Notably, for our main model, the symmetric harmonic process, the corresponding Hamiltonian is identified with the classical integrable non-compact Ishimori spin chain.
  Furthermore, we show that our large spin large deviation theory is fully consistent with traditional Macroscopic Fluctuation Theory (MFT), smoothly recovering the standard MFT Hamiltonian in the spatial continuous limit. We also perform a Poisson-noise Martin--Siggia--Rose (MSR) computation to derive the non-linear lattice Hamiltonian directly from microscopic dynamics, use a relative entropy argument to obtain the density-current action, and establish the lattice fluctuation theorem alongside its symmetry origin. Overall, our framework provides a naturally regularized, lattice analogue of MFT that circumvents spatial ultraviolet singularities and possible continuous density blow-ups.
  We also apply our new scheme to partial symmetric exclusion process, symmetric inclusion processes, Brownian energy process and integrable heat conduction model, showing how their large-deviation Hamiltonians relate to classical compact and non-compact spin chains.

papers.title: Path space large deviation on a lattice for interacting particle systems
papers.abstract:
We investigate the path space large deviation principle (LDP) for a class of interacting particle systems on a fixed finite discrete torus. As an illustrative example, we use the partial exclusion process with maximal occupation of $s$ particles. We first verify the standard Kurtz-type law of large numbers for the original and tilted processes, thereby identifying the deterministic flows around which the large deviations are formulated. We then establish the path space LDP, with speed $s$, and identify the associated rate function in variational form as the Legendre transform of a nonlinear Hamiltonian. The proof relies on martingale techniques, exponential tightness, and a change-of-measure argument based on exponential tilting, which renders atypical trajectories typical under a modified dynamics.
  We also explain how the same strategy extends to further interacting particle systems. The inclusion process illustrates the conservative non-compact finite-jump case. The harmonic process is qualitatively different: a single transition may move a variable number of particles, and the limiting Hamiltonian is logarithmic with a non-trivial domain. This places the harmonic process outside the usual finite-reaction framework for density-dependent Markov jump processes. Finally, we discuss continuous-state energy-exchange models, such as the Brownian energy process and an integrable heat-conduction model, to indicate how the same Hamiltonian large-deviation formalism appears beyond discrete-state particle systems.

papers.title: A MAGNHIFFIC cold-gas filament fuelling the nuclear activity of NGC 3100
papers.abstract: MAGNHIFFIC (MeerKAT AGN HI Feeding & Feedback Investigation close-by) leverages on sensitive MeerKAT 21-cm and VLT Survey Telescope (VST) observations of nearby Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) to study feeding and feedback from the circum-nuclear ($\lesssim 1$ kpc) to the circum-galactic scales ($\gtrsim 10$ kpc). In nearby ($D\sim38$~Mpc) radio galaxy NGC 3100, these observations reveal, for the very first time, a starless filament of neutral atomic hydrogen ($M_{\rm H {\hskip 0.02cm \tt I}}\sim 3.4\times 10^8 {\rm M}_\odot$) extending from its outskirts ($\sim 340$ kpc) down to its innermost kiloparsecs. The kinematical properties of the filament show it likely formed by gas stripped from dwarf galaxy MKT095931-312323, flying by NGC 3100 $\gtrsim 0.5$ Gyr ago. The filament appears to replenish the cold-gas reservoir of NGC 3100's circum-nuclear disk traced by archival $^{12}$CO images as well as by HI absorption. The kinematics of the HI absorption and of the $^{12}$CO(3--2) show that, in the very centre, the jets are currently stirring the multi-phase gas while dense clouds may still fall into the SMBH. The coexistence of a surviving cold reservoir, compact inner atomic/molecular clouds, and localised jet-driven heating indicates that AGN feeding and feedback operate simultaneously rather than as separate evolutionary phases.

papers.title: O VI Emission in Starbursting BCGs: An HST-COS Extension of "Reigniting the FUSE"
papers.abstract: In this extension of our "Reigniting the FUSE" series, we have obtained new far-ultraviolet spectroscopy of 3 starbursting brightest cluster galaxies with the Cosmic Origins Spectrograph (COS) aboard HST. With these new data, in combination with archival COS data of 2 additional systems, we measure star formation rates (SFRs) from the young stellar continuum and cooling rates through $10^{5.5}$ K gas with the O VI $1032,1038\,\mathring{\rm A}$ doublet ($\dot{M}_{\rm O\,VI}$). We use these measurements to increase the size of the "Reigniting the FUSE" sample, which itself contains high resolution far UV spectroscopy for 29 nearby massive elliptical galaxies from FUSE, and extend it 1 dex upwards in SFR and cooling rate. Our derived SFRs agree well with photometric GALEX$+$WISE SFRs from the literature. The new data also reinforce the previously observed trend in cooling efficiency ($\dot{M}_{\rm O\,VI}/\dot{M}_{\rm max}$; where $\dot{M}_{\rm max}$ is the X-ray luminosity-based cooling rate) versus mass, with groups cooling more efficiently than clusters by a factor of $\sim$4-5. When we isolate a sample of the most star-forming central galaxies, we find that the star formation rates, X-ray spectroscopic cooling rates, and UV spectroscopic cooling rates are all consistent with one another, on average, while retaining substantial system-to-system scatter, reflecting time-depenent multiphase condensation and cold gas reservoir evolution. The remainder of the sample, in contrast, overwhelmingly shows ratios of ${\rm SFR}/\dot{M}_{\rm O\,VI} \sim {\rm SFR}/\dot{M}_{\rm X,spec} \sim 10\%$.

papers.title: Maximal curves with trivial automorphism group
papers.abstract:
We construct algebraic curves with trivial geometric automorphism group by taking cyclic scalar quotients of curves of the form \[
  y^r-y=xR(x),\qquad r=p^e. \] We give a condition on the genus under which the quotient has no nontrivial automorphism. The proof uses the ramification of a degree-$r$ morphism to the projective line, Castelnuovo--Severi, and explicit automorphisms of the covering curve. The quotient also has gonality $r$, with a unique morphism of degree $r$ to the projective line up to an automorphism of the latter. Applying the construction to maximal additive curves gives explicit maximal curves with trivial geometric automorphism group in every positive characteristic, including families defined over the prime field and of unbounded genus. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first examples of maximal curves with trivial geometric automorphism group. Every maximal curve in these families is covered by the Hermitian curve. For every odd prime $p$ and every $n\ge2$, we prove that the curve $\X_{p,n}$, maximal over $\F_{p^{4n+2}}$, is not a Galois subcover of the corresponding Hermitian curve, even over the algebraic closure. Thus every odd characteristic yields an infinite family of curves covered but not Galois covered by the Hermitian curve. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first such infinite families.

papers.title: Recursive Neighbor Pruning: Decentralized Community Detection with Certified Behavior from Saturated Opinion Dynamics
papers.abstract: Detecting communities, i.e., groups of densely connected nodes, usually requires a central entity that knows the whole network. We study Recursive Neighbor Pruning (RNP), a fully decentralized alternative inspired by social learning. Each agent holds a private opinion but only shows its neighbors a coarse public action, namely its opinion amplified and clipped to a fixed range. Agents repeatedly move their opinion toward the actions of their neighbors and, once opinions settle, drop the links with neighbors whose action has the opposite sign. Repeating this procedure on the remaining network splits it into communities, without any agent knowing the network or the number of communities. We use tools from nonlinear control to characterize this behavior. We show that splitting requires the amplification to exceed a threshold set by how strongly the network is bottlenecked. We also show that a group in which every member has enough of its links inside the group can no longer be split once its members agree, and that a single run separates such groups exactly when started from suitable opinions. Finally, we bound the number of runs and messages. On two standard families of synthetic networks, RNP is as accurate as the best centralized method as long as each node has fewer than about forty percent of its links outside its community, and it fails close to the value predicted by our analysis. It is more accurate than two decentralized competitors below this level, but exchanges many more messages.

papers.title: How Steep is your Dust? Direct Measurements of Nebular Attenuation Curves at Cosmic Noon with JWST
papers.abstract: Tracing the shape of the nebular attenuation curve, which is crucial for accurately measuring intrinsic emission-line fluxes, has proven challenging both in the local universe and at high redshift. Here we present nebular dust attenuation curves measured directly for 24 star-forming galaxies ($9.3<\log(\rm M{\star}/M_\odot)<11.1$) at cosmic noon ($1.8<z<3.3$) from the Blue Jay survey. Using deep JWST/NIRSpec spectra, we measure up to eight hydrogen recombination lines from H$\delta$ to Pa$\beta$ per galaxy and find little diversity in the curve shape, with most galaxies agreeing with the \citet{calzetti_dust_2000} attenuation curve. For over $90\%$ of the sample, the nebular reddening from the Balmer lines is consistent with that from the Paschen lines. Using \texttt{Prospector} spectral energy distribution (SED) fits, we obtain the stellar reddening and find that the difference between stellar and nebular reddening increases with stellar mass, and that each reddening measurement is independent of inclination, which disagrees with the two-component dust model. We then measure the impact of using the derived nebular attenuation curve or a literature curve when determining metallicity using the strong-line method, and find that for some diagnostics (e.g., S32, S3, S23, and S3O3), the difference can be as large as $5\sigma$. Caution is needed when using these diagnostics if the nebular attenuation curve cannot be directly measured, since the resulting uncertainty can exceed the measurement uncertainty on the emission-line fluxes even with high signal-to-noise Balmer decrement measurements. These results show that the shape of the nebular attenuation curve is poorly understood and that constraining it is important for reducing systematic uncertainty in galaxy measurements.

papers.intro:
The luminosities and ratios of rest-frame optical emission lines are used to measure many key properties of galaxies, including the star formation rate (Kennicutt et al., 1994, SFR; e.g.,) and gas-phase metallicity (Maiolino and Mannucci, 2019, see review by). The photons producing these emission lines are scattered and absorbed by interstellar dust, a process known as dust attenuation (Salim and Narayanan, 2020, see review by). Accurate modelling of this attenuation is therefore crucial for measuring galaxy properties, such as star-formation rate and gas-phase metallicity via emission-line measurements, and stellar mass and star formation histories (SFH) via spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting.

Accurate modelling of this attenuation is therefore crucial for measuring galaxy properties, such as star-formation rate and gas-phase metallicity via emission-line measurements, and stellar mass and star formation histories (SFH) via spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting.

The variation in dust attenuation with wavelength is known as the dust attenuation curve, and measurements of the dust curve have been made for decades. When measuring the dust attenuation of emission lines in local galaxies, Fanelli et al. (1988) and Calzetti et al. (1994) found that emission lines often have higher dust attenuation than the overall stellar continuum. These observations led to the two-component dust model from Charlot and Fall (2000), wherein all the stars are attenuated by a component of dust in the ISM, and the young stars, typically with ages ≲10​Myr\lesssim 10\rm~Myr (Blitz and Shu, 1980), and the nebular emission lines produced around those stars, are additionally attenuated by the dust in the nascent birth cloud. After ∼10​Myr\sim\rm 10~Myr, these birth clouds disperse. Observations at higher redshifts have also identified elevated nebular reddening compared to that of the stellar continuum (Wuyts et al., 2013; Price et al., 2014; Reddy et al., 2015; Shivaei et al., 2020; Lorenz et al., 2023).

Different geometries and optical depths toward young and old stellar regions also motivate different attenuation curves, since variation in attenuation curves tends to be dominated by geometry (Narayanan et al., 2018; Salim and Narayanan, 2020, e.g.,), with subdominant contributions from extinction curves. It is typical to assume that the dust in the birth clouds can be modelled as a foreground screen of dust with negligible scattering into the line of sight. Since this aligns with how the dust in the Milky Way is modelled (Cardelli et al., 1989), the shape of the Milky Way extinction curve is commonly assumed for the nebular attenuation curve. However, for the stellar continuum, dust scattering into the line of sight by ISM dust is a significant effect. Attenuation curves that model this scattering into the line of sight, such as the Calzetti et al. (2000) law, are commonly assumed for the stellar continuum attenuation curve.

Various methods have been used to measure the shape of the stellar continuum attenuation curve, such as the empirical template method by Calzetti et al. (1994), which stacks the spectra of local galaxies in bins of dust attenuation to infer the shape of the dust attenuation curve. More recently, Reddy et al. (2015) and Shivaei et al. (2020) applied this method to cosmic noon galaxies, and the attenuation curves measured in these three works vary in shape. Many studies have used SED fitting tools to infer the shape of the attenuation curve for local galaxies (Burgarella et al., 2005; Leja et al., 2017; Salim et al., 2018) and for galaxies at cosmic noon (Maheson et al., 2025) and at even higher redshifts (Markov et al., 2025; Shivaei et al., 2025). These works find significant variation in the shape of the stellar continuum attenuation curve, and that the slope and UV-bump strength depend on parameters such as dust content, stellar mass, SFR, and redshift.

These works find significant variation in the shape of the stellar continuum attenuation curve, and that the slope and UV-bump strength depend on parameters such as dust content, stellar mass, SFR, and redshift.

However, the shape of the nebular attenuation curve has not been studied as widely, particularly at high redshift. Recent works using the Balmer emission lines to measure the nebular attenuation curve directly have shed light on its shape (Reddy et al., 2020; Rezaee et al., 2021; Sanders et al., 2024; Reddy et al., 2026a). The Balmer lines are widely used to calculate the optical depth towards nebular regions (Garn and Best, 2010; Shivaei et al., 2015; Maheson et al., 2024; Sandles et al., 2024; Maheson et al., 2025, e.g.,), since the intrinsic ratio of Balmer lines is well predicted theoretically, and varies little with the physical conditions they originate in (Tacchella et al., 2016; Chakraborty et al., 2021, e.g.,). Reddy et al. (2020) introduced a method to measure the nebular attenuation curve directly using several Balmer emission lines. They stacked galaxy spectra to measure the Balmer lines from Hα\alpha to Hϵ\epsilon at z∼1−2z\sim 1-2. The low signal-to-noise of their pre-JWST spectra required stacking to boost the signal of the higher-order lines, allowing them to measure an average attenuation curve across this redshift range. This nebular attenuation curve was similar to the Milky Way extinction curve in the rest-optical. A similar result was reported for a stack of local (z∼0z\sim 0) galaxy spectra using the same methodology (Rezaee et al., 2021), which found no dependence of the nebular attenuation curve on stellar mass, metallicity, or specific star-formation rate (sSFR).

However, the shape of the nebular attenuation curve has not been studied as widely, particularly at high redshift. Recent works using the Balmer emission lines to measure the nebular attenuation curve directly have shed light on its shape (Reddy et al., 2020; Rezaee et al., 2021; Sanders et al., 2024; Reddy et al., 2026a). So far, this has only been achieved using galaxies from the AURORA survey (Shapley et al., 2025), first for an individual galaxy in Sanders et al. (2024), and then in a follow-up paper (Reddy et al., 2026a) for 24 galaxies. Both works find many galaxies with nebular attenuation curves far steeper than the Milky Way, SMC, or Calzetti et al. papers.title: Multi-Agent Retrieval-Augmented Causality Assessment (MARCA) of Individual Case Safety Reports in Pharmacovigilance
papers.abstract:
Introduction: Increasing volumes of individual case safety reports (ICSRs) challenge expert-led causality assessment in pharmacovigilance. We developed MARCA (Multi-Agent Retrieval-Augmented Causality Assessment), a four-agent framework for Naranjo-based assessment, and evaluated agreement with human experts and exploratory differences between non-RAG and RAG-labelled scores.
  Methods: MARCA combined scientific literature retrieval, drug-label assessment, objective-evidence classification, and clinical causality reasoning using Gemini 2.5 Pro and DeepSeek-V3.2. Agent-generated rationales informed human-assisted scoring. A consensus expert reference standard covered 215 ICSRs and 1,562 drug-event combinations (DECs) from FAERS (Q1-Q2 2025). Agreement was measured using percentage agreement and Cohen's kappa.
  Results: Question-level agreement was 96.8% for Naranjo Q2 (kappa = 0.491; 95% CI 0.265-0.663), 85.4% for Q5 (kappa = 0.269; 95% CI 0.180-0.340), and 96.8% for Q10 (kappa = 0.922; 95% CI 0.885-0.951). Final causality classification agreement was 79.4% (95% CI 71.8-85.3; kappa = 0.587, 95% CI 0.450-0.690). In a retrospective subset of 60 DECs, agreement was higher for RAG-labelled than non-RAG scores for Q5 (83.3% vs 65.0%) and Q10 (100.0% vs 18.3%).
  Discussion: MARCA-assisted assessment showed substantial variation in agreement across Naranjo questions, with lower concordance for alternative causes. Retrospective RAG comparisons are exploratory and do not establish prospective effectiveness.

papers.title: Path-Specific Geometric-Stochastic Channel Model for Scattering from ISAC Targets: A Unified Measurement-Based Characterization of Robots, Humans, and Automobiles at 28 GHz
papers.abstract: This paper develops a channel model for scattering from a broad class of integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) targets-robots, humans, and automobiles-based on a unified measurement campaign at 28~GHz. Nine targets are characterized from numerous transmitter--receiver configurations per target, spanning full bistatic and aspect angles and thus covering backward to forward scattering. Repeated acquisitions are collected for each configuration to capture target motion and dynamics, yielding nearly 117\,000 acquisitions in total. Measurements are collected with a 2~GHz-wide channel sounder equipped with a 256-element phased-array antenna, followed by digital beamforming and super-resolution processing for reliable extraction of multiple paths in delay and 2D angle, with average estimation errors of 0.1~ns and 0.2$^\circ$ respectively. From these measurements, we reduce a \emph{path-specific} channel representation in which the scattering is modeled as a cluster of paths whose center is defined by the bistatic specular \emph{geometry}; the cluster shape is described \emph{stochastically}. To ensure physically grounded spatio--temporal consistency, extracted paths are mapped to incident points on the target, each with an associated radar cross section (RCS) that is compatible with the 3GPP TR~38.901 ISAC channel model, and are subsequently mapped back to path properties for channel synthesis. The resulting statistical distributions are well behaved, physically interpretable, and consistent across targets, geometries, and motion. Comparison between measured and synthesized channel realizations demonstrates close agreement in pathloss trends and fluctuation behavior. Together, these results yield a high-fidelity, measurement-derived channel representation suitable for ISAC simulation, target modeling, and system design.

papers.title: NovaFabric: A Black-Box Recorder for AI Agents with Sealed, Replayable, Diffable and Auditable Runs
papers.abstract: An AI agent run is no longer a function call. It is a cascade of prompts, model calls, tool invocations, file and network effects and sub-agents. When such a run misbehaves, or an auditor asks what happened, logs and traces answer poorly: they are mutable, partial and cannot be re-executed. This technical report describes NovaFabric, an open-source (Apache-2.0) black-box recorder for AI agents that turns a run into a sealed, replayable, diffable and auditable evidence capsule. The design rests on two formats only. The Run Capsule is a directory of flat files and the source of truth; every database is a rebuildable index over capsules. The Evidence Bundle is the signed export for an auditor. Everything else follows existing standards: OpenTelemetry GenAI, OpenLineage, W3C PROV, in-toto/DSSE, RFC 3161 and CycloneDX. A single-node run is the smallest case of a distributed one; the schema supports a capsule hierarchy for Slurm arrays and Kubernetes jobs, though automatic parent finalization is library-only today. The report covers the architecture and the engines behind the verb chain capture, seal, replay, diff and audit: fail-closed mocked replay; a diff gate with a stable exit-code contract; DSSE signatures that bind their intent and a capsule root that commits to file names; a capsule treated as untrusted input; signer identity-trust levels with offline TSA and CRL checking; maker-checker promotion against an operator-held trust list; and a deny-by-default authorization table for every dashboard route. It presents no new experiments; the evaluation is in arXiv:2609.12582. Every count except the private ADR tally is generated by a probe script run on the public source at the v0.107.0 tag (150 top-level commands, 84 Python subpackages, 16,721 test functions), every capability carries an explicit maturity label, and honest-limits boxes state where the system stops.

papers.title: On Gill's problem with anomalous diffusion
papers.abstract: The classical formulation of Gill's theorem establishing the linear stability of the buoyant flow in a vertical porous channel subject to transverse diffusion and bounded by impermeable walls is here reconsidered from the perspective of anomalous mass diffusion. Anomalous diffusion is a physical effect implying a more general formulation of the governing equations of mass transfer either in a fluid or in a fluid-saturated porous medium. Anomalous diffusion is mathematically modelled via a diffusion equation with a time-dependent mass diffusivity. In this study, the stationary and parallel buoyant flow in a vertical porous layer saturated by a fluid is investigated. The implications of the anomalous diffusion model for the proof that such a flow is always linearly stable are analysed.

papers.title: The flipping principle for boundedly acyclic covers and colorings
papers.abstract: Based on the theory of multicomplexes and other ideas by Gromov, we describe the flipping principle. This is an easy geometric criterion that forces the vanishing of the Gromov norm of homology classes. We use it to provide proofs based on a common geometric principle of the Vanishing Theorem and the Amenable Reduction Lemma by Gromov in the case of amenable and boundedly acyclic covers and colorings. We also strengthen the conclusion of the Amenable Reduction Lemma by showing that it implies the $\ell^1$-invisibility of the homology classes and not only the vanishing of their Gromov norm.

papers.title: Gevrey Regularity for a Sum of Two Squares in Two Variables
papers.abstract: We study the Gevrey hypoellipticity of a sum of two squares in two variables, satisfying the H\"ormander hypothesis, assuming that the function, $ q $, describing (the space projection of) its characteristic variety vanishes only at a single point, which can be assumed to be the origin. A hypoellipticity result is given in a Gevrey class, depending on $ q $. In some examples the found regularity is known to be optimal.

papers.title: Random-walk scaling without Bernoulli statistics: transport, persistence and resonances in the triangle map
papers.abstract: The triangle map is an area-preserving, piecewise-parabolic map of the torus with vanishing Lyapunov exponent. We study the symbolic process $X_n=\pm1$ given by the two halves of the torus, whose partial sums $S_n$ are the transport of the lifted momentum, with an integrator free of accumulated rounding errors and exact computations on polygonal cylinder sets. We prove that the Koopman operator has no non-constant $H^1$ eigenfunctions, that the symbol is not an $H^1$ coboundary, and that runs of equal symbols are uniformly bounded. For generic parameters the walk is normally diffusive and Gaussian, but its diffusion coefficient is not that of a coin: away from the edges of the parameter square it varies between $0.2$ and $14$ times the Bernoulli value, and for a benchmark pair, with $D=3.09\pm0.01$, the excess is produced by the order of the bounded inter-event intervals, not by their distribution. The first-passage exponent is $1/2$ with a non-Bernoulli amplitude, and worst-case Birkhoff averages decay as for a uniquely ergodic system. For $\beta=0$ the Green-Kubo sum cancels, $D=0$, yet $\mathrm{Var}(S_n)$ keeps growing slowly, sign changes are rare and the correlations of Fourier modes decay as $n^{-0.2}$. We identify the zero-sum words, which become pure twists at $\beta=0$, as resonances that trap orbits with a computable $1/\ell$ law, set the crossover time $\beta^{-1/2}$ at small $\beta$, and, in an asymmetric deformation of the symbol, produce a logarithmic term in the variance whose coefficient we compute exactly. We formulate conjectures on unique ergodicity, mixing, the central limit theorem and the cohomology of the symbol.

papers.title: Semantic burstiness across principal directions of textual variation
papers.abstract: Long-range correlations in written texts extend over scales far beyond local syntax, but their relation to semantic organisation remains incompletely understood. Previous work has linked these correlations to the bursty recurrence of topically relevant words. Here we generalise that construction from individual lexical items to distributed semantic observables. We map a text token by token onto a trajectory of pre-trained word embeddings, use principal component analysis (PCA) to identify text-specific directions of semantic variation, and threshold the projected series to define inter-event times; their coefficients of variation form a component-resolved burstiness spectrum $\{B_k\}$. Across 28 literary and scientific texts and the first 20 components, the originals remain systematically above the geometric inter-event-time baseline and above two complementary controls: a word-shuffled null, which preserves the embedding covariance, the PCA eigensystem and the marginal projected distributions while destroying temporal order, and a fractional-Gaussian-noise surrogate, which preserves the Zipfian frequency structure and matches the detrended fluctuation analysis (DFA) exponent of the original rank sequence. With events defined by the upper 5% tail of each projection, the original exceeds both controls in every text-component pair, while the two controls are statistically indistinguishable from each other. Autocorrelation and detrended fluctuation analysis of the semantic projections separate the originals from both controls in the same way. Global rank-level long-range correlations are therefore insufficient to generate the bursty recurrence observed along semantic directions. The results instead support an interpretation in terms of the ordered recurrence of semantically related material.

papers.title: Model-independent calibration of gamma-ray bursts with Bayesian neural networks
papers.abstract:
Context. Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) extend cosmological distance measurements beyond the range densely sampled by Type Ia supernovae, but their standardization requires reliable calibration and uncertainty estimates.
  Aims. We calibrate the Amati correlation without assuming a background cosmological model, assess its stability, and examine the cosmological reach of current and future GRB Hubble diagrams.
  Methods. We train a Bayesian neural network on Pantheon+ supernovae, assess and recalibrate its predictive uncertainties, and calibrate the correlation for GRBs at $z \leq 1.5$ using the D'Agostini and Reichart likelihoods. We combine the GRB Hubble diagram with supernovae, Hubble-parameter measurements, and DESI baryon acoustic oscillations. Local-regression, covariance, leave-three-out, redshift-evolution, and Efron-Petrosian diagnostics test the standardization assumptions. We also analyse idealized future catalogues of 1500 standardized GRBs.
  Results. The diagram reaches $z \simeq 9.4$. Covariance and leave-three-out diagnostics produce small changes in the cosmological constraints. A parametric evolution coefficient is consistent with zero, whereas the truncation-corrected diagnostic indicates marginal isotropic-energy evolution that can occur along the Amati relation. Dark-energy extensions improve the phenomenological fit relative to flat $\Lambda$CDM: AIC favours the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder parametrization, while BIC favours constant-$w$ dark energy. Forecasts show strong conditional model-discrimination power under the adopted uncertainty model.
  Conclusions. GRBs provide a complementary high-redshift extension of the supernova distance ladder. Present results do not establish an evolving dark-energy equation of state. Larger homogeneous samples are promising, but realistic selection functions and calibration systematics remain essential.

papers.title: Relativistic Cavity Quantum Electrodynamical Algebraic Diagrammatic Construction Method for Strong Light-Matter Coupling
papers.abstract: We present the relativistic four-component implementation of cavity quantum electrodynamical algebraic diagrammatic construction theory at second order (4c-QED-EE-ADC(2)) for the ab initio treatment of light-matter interactions. Starting from the unitary-transformed, origin-invariant Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian, a rigorous four-component Dirac-Hartree-Fock formulation including cavity effects is considered, forming the basis of the 4c-QED-EE-ADC(2) framework. Two variants are implemented, allowing cavity effects to be introduced either at the relativistic mean-field or exclusively at the electron-correlation level. Applications to Hg, AuH, and halogen hydrides demonstrate that cavity coupling significantly modifies relativistic excitation spectra, induces strong state mixing, and enables tunable polaritonic features. Potential energy surface calculations for HBr further reveal cavity-induced qualitative changes in excited-state surfaces. It is also observed that the inclusion of photonic degrees of freedom leads to a moderate computational overhead of approximately three to five times relative to standard 4c-EE-ADC(2).

papers.title: Scattering and Schmid-Bulgadaev Transition in Qubits Based on Josephson Junction Chains
papers.abstract: A Josephson junction subject to an ohmic dissipative environment undergoes a zero-temperature quantum phase transition called Schmid-Bulgadaev transition form an insulating state to a superconducting state upon increasing the impedance of the environment above the resistance quantum. Superconducting qubits based on Josephson junction chains represent a system where it is possible to dynamically explore both sides of this transition by probing the scattering of individual plasma modes of the junction chain on a SQUID at the boundary which was achieved in recent experiments. Here, we provide a theoretical analysis of the scattering in the system paying special attention to the non-perturbative superconducting regime. We find that in this regime, a specific diagrammatic resummation must be performed in order to correctly account for fluctuation renormalization of the SQUID's potential. We find analytic expressions for the modes' frequency shifts and quality factors which together provide a full description of scattering. We argue that the non-perturbative nature of the superconducting phase manifests itself through a power-law dependence of the frequency shifts on the SQUID flux and through non-monotonous dependence of the quality factors on the mode frequency. Our predictions may be readily verified in modern low-temperature experiments.

papers.title: Ambient Chain-Relation Reduction in Contracting Controlled Skew-Product Semiflows
papers.abstract: The qualitative dynamics of nonautonomous differential equations is often studied through cocycles and skew-product semiflows over a driving base. We develop a chain-recurrence reduction principle for systems admitting an equivariant attracting section and uniform asymptotic tracking. The abstract theorem determines the complete chain-attainability relation in the ambient phase space: chains may start off the attracting section, but every attainable target lies on it and is selected solely by the factor semiflow. Applied to contracting controlled skew-product semiflows, this gives exact descriptions of the chain recurrent set, chain components, Conley order, compact strictly invariant sets, attractors, basins, and dual repellers. A weighted-supremum transverse gauge yields a complete Lyapunov function for the full semiflow while preserving the recurrent values of the base. The differential hypotheses are verified through subadditive fiber-derivative growth and averaged moving-metric logarithmic norms, allowing transient expansion and non-unique ergodicity. Quantitative persistence is established for finite-window maps and smooth vector-field perturbations. The results provide a unified framework for chain recurrence, Lyapunov structure, and attractor--repeller geometry in contracting nonautonomous dynamics.

papers.title: PathKGen: Pathology Knowledge Assisted MLLM for Explainable Histopathology
papers.abstract: Whole Slide Image (WSI) analysis serves as the fundamental method for the clinical diagnosis of cancer in digital histopathology. Recent advances in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have enabled state-of-the-art (SOTA) automated histopathology report generation. However, MLLMs reason purely through distributions encoded in their neural parameters, limiting the amount of knowledge and reasoning logic they can contain given the model scale. Their black-box reasoning poses another challenge to the human interpretation of intermediate reasoning. We address these issues by utilizing knowledge graphs to inject external structured knowledge for MLLMs to reason over, while making this reasoning component visible. Knowledge graphs are capable of partially externalizing the containment of medical knowledge, an area that remains underexplored in pathology report generation. We introduce PathKGen, a knowledge graph-assisted MLLM for histopathology report generation. PathKGen has two main branches: (1) a visual path that learns visual token inputs to the MLLM using pathology foundation models, and (2) a knowledge path that learns knowledge token inputs by extracting key morphological features of WSIs through querying a pathology-specific knowledge graph. A comprehensive evaluation on WSI-Bench dataset shows that PathKGen surpasses previous SOTA methods while revealing diagnostic reasoning as visually intuitive graphs. Due to its modular design, the proposed knowledge path is complementary to vision-aligned MLLMs and can be extended to other applications by curating domain-specific knowledge graphs to generate knowledge tokens.

papers.title: Synthetic linguistic data
papers.abstract: Synthetic linguistic data have become increasingly prominent in linguistic research, from the analysis of large collections of AI-generated texts to controlled experiments investigating grammatical and lexical preferences. This glossary entry extends Bresnan's (2016) distinction between the linguistic garden and the bush by introducing an artificial plant nursery as a metaphor for synthetic data. We distinguish between synthetic bush data, consisting primarily of corpus-like collections of model-generated language, and synthetic garden data, in which model outputs are elicited under controlled conditions to investigate specific linguistic hypotheses. We argue that synthetic data constitute a distinct object of linguistic investigation: comparing them with natural language data can reveal both shared patterns and divergences, but their interpretation requires careful consideration of the conditions under which they are generated.

papers.title: PlayerEmbed: Learning Behavioral Fingerprint Representations from Raw Input Sequences
papers.abstract: Raw player input sequences in video games contain fine-grained behavior, but are high-dimensional and noisy, which makes large-scale analytics challenging. To address this, we introduce PlayerEmbed, a framework that learns compact and discriminative player embeddings using deep metric learning. Our approach uses a hybrid CNN-LSTM encoder trained on raw input sequences from 1,000 players. We evaluate the model on held-out sequences from these players and on sequences from 1,000 players entirely unseen during training to assess generalization to unseen identities. For player identification, a nearest-centroid classifier built from reference embeddings achieves strong performance, reaching balanced accuracies of 0.950 for players seen during training and 0.879 for players unseen during training. Systematically increasing the number of training players substantially improves generalization to unseen players, indicating a transition from simple fingerprinting to learning transferable behavioral patterns.

papers.intro:
Video games generate large amounts of player input data, capturing complex patterns of player behavior [1]. While they contain huge amounts of valuable information, important behavioral patterns are mostly hidden behind layers of noise and complexity, making it challenging to extract useful insights without extensive manual and game-specific preprocessing [2]. Extracting compact and meaningful representations from these input sequences offers a promising approach that enables a wide range of downstream player behavior analysis tasks, while reducing or eliminating the need for manual analysis [3]. Efficiently processing and analyzing large amounts of player input data is highly valuable for game development, as manual analysis is time-consuming, limited in scope, and increasingly impractical for games with many players [2].

This becomes increasingly challenging as the number of players grows. Player identification is useful for monitoring account integrity, for example by flagging potential account sharing [4], account hijacking [5], and smurfing [6], where experienced players use fresh novice-rated accounts, undermining matchmaking integrity.

We study player identification using learned representations based on raw input sequences, instead of relying on manual, game-specific feature engineering. We focus on keystroke and mouse dynamics, which are mostly game-agnostic. These fine-grained inputs are diverse, but at the same time contain patterns that are consistent per individual, enabling reliable identification [7]. We propose the framework PlayerEmbed, which leverages deep metric learning to extract discriminative and compact embeddings from raw player input sequences, enabling efficient and scalable analysis of player behavior. By training on a wide range of players with diverse skill levels and playstyles, PlayerEmbed is designed to model the complex patterns and relationships of in-game actions, capturing relevant aspects of temporal dynamics, behavioral style, and skill. Since embeddings are significantly smaller than the input sequences, they reduce storage requirements and improve computational efficiency in further analysis.

DDraceNetwork (DDNet) is a “free and open-source side-scrolling platformer with unique cooperative gameplay” [8]. The game’s core mechanic centers around using a grappling hook, allowing players to maneuver through complex map layouts with the goal of reaching the finish of a map. DDNet is particularly well-suited for this work due to several key factors: The game is free and open-source, allowing self-hosting of game servers and enabling the storage of player input data. Since the game has existed for many years, there is a large variety in player skill, as the community includes everything from complete beginners to veteran players. Also, while the game’s input schema is relatively simple, the resulting physics-based movement is highly dynamic and complex. This is crucial as it introduces sufficient diversity in player behavior that makes distinguishing between players non-trivial, as there are no clear repeating discrete patterns.

papers.title: Neural LoFi with Backward Coupling: A Spectral Theory of Cross-Layer Feature Learning
papers.abstract: During joint training, backpropagation allows later layers to reshape earlier representations, a feedback mechanism absent from purely layer-wise learning. We extend Neural Low-Degree Filtering (Neural LoFi), a recently proposed layer-wise spectral surrogate for feature learning, to capture this interaction. Starting from the exact backpropagation gradients, we derive a local coupling between a neuron's incoming weights and its corresponding next-layer column. In a controlled small-initialization regime with smooth activations and fixed surroundings, these dynamics amplify singular modes of a cross-layer correlation operator. Each growing mode pairs an earlier feature with an upper-layer response through shared neuron coefficients. This motivates a backward-coupling algorithm in which upper-layer sensitivities generate sample-dependent effective labels for earlier spectral steps, while corrected features refine upward transmission. A function-space variational principle characterizes the selected feature-response pairs by maximizing the label correlation of their product under kernel-norm constraints. For three-layer networks, we derive self-consistent continuous-time dynamics for the filtered hidden-layer features, the activation kernels, and the network output under the proposed backward coupling. In a hierarchical multi-index model, we establish a feature-recovery separation: backward coupling recovers lower-layer directions invisible to the original forward label-weighted statistic. The linear specialization recovers residual-dependent singular-mode dynamics, while paired modes provide a dynamical mechanism for linked low-rank covariance components consistent with the rainbow-network picture. Experiments with fully connected and convolutional networks on binary CIFAR-10 show improved accuracy over forward Neural LoFi at matched widths.

papers.intro:
Deep neural networks learn hierarchies of task-adapted representations through backpropagation (Rumelhart et al., 1986; LeCun et al., 2015). Yet a hierarchy in the forward computation does not imply a layer-wise order of learning. During joint training, features emerging in later layers reshape the learning signals received below, while changes in earlier representations alter what the upper layers can learn. Understanding this feedback requires going beyond how features are constructed successively. It raises a central question: How does learning in later layers change which features earlier layers can discover?

Deep neural networks learn hierarchies of task-adapted representations through backpropagation (Rumelhart et al., 1986; LeCun et al., 2015). Yet a hierarchy in the forward computation does not imply a layer-wise order of learning. During joint training, features emerging in later layers reshape the learning signals received below, while changes in earlier representations alter what the upper layers can learn. Understanding this feedback requires going beyond how features are constructed successively. It raises a central question:

How does learning in later layers change which features earlier layers can discover?

This paper builds on Neural Low-Degree Filtering (Neural LoFi), introduced by Dandi et al. (2026b) as an explicit spectral construction for purely layer-wise learning. Given the current representation, each layer selects directions through low-degree correlations with the labels and passes them through a nonlinear random lift. Depth changes the geometry in which subsequent layers search for signal, making structure that is complex in the input accessible through low-degree statistics of intermediate representations. However, this construction proceeds only forward: features learned above cannot refine the directions selected below. A useful upper representation may therefore become available only after the lower feature-selection step that could benefit from it has already been completed.

Existing theories describe complementary aspects of feature learning. Neural-tangent limits characterize training with essentially fixed representations (Jacot et al., 2018; Lee et al., 2019); mean-field and dynamical-field frameworks describe evolving features in shallow and deep nonlinear networks (Mei et al., 2018; Chizat and Bach, 2018; Nguyen and Pham, 2020; Bordelon and Pehlevan, 2022; Hajjar et al., 2024). Feature-space mean-field models and tensor programs further describe feature learning at infinite width (Fang et al., 2021; Yang and Hu, 2021). Deep linear networks admit explicit analyses of coupled singular-mode dynamics (Saxe et al., 2014), while spectral analyses of quadratic and diagonal networks connect learned weight structure to generalization (Defilippis et al., 2026b). Backward feature correction studies how joint training with higher layers can refine lower representations (Allen-Zhu and Li, 2023).

Backward feature correction studies how joint training with higher layers can refine lower representations (Allen-Zhu and Li, 2023).

In this paper, we seek a tractable and interpretable spectral mechanism that identifies how an upper-layer response changes the "earlier" features. We extend Neural LoFi with a tractable and interpretable spectral surrogate that captures backward feature correction and, in addition, identifies a distinct effect of joint training: learning how lower-level cues selectively activate higher-level features. This couples the learning of lower representations to the learning of their transmission upward. Starting from the exact backpropagation gradients, we couple a neuron’s incoming row to the next-layer column that reads its activation. For a jointly trained block at small initialization, with smooth activations and fixed surroundings, we prove that the leading dynamics amplify singular modes of a cross-layer correlation operator. Each mode pairs an earlier feature with an upper response, with the same growing coefficients across intermediate neurons in both weight factors. The paired updates coordinate what a neuron detects with how its activation is transmitted upward: the incoming row acquires the lower feature, while the outgoing column couples it to the selected upper response. A similar mechanism has been seen to spontaneously emerge in the feed-forward blocks of modern LLMs (Geva et al., 2021; Geva et al., 2022) and we note additionally that with linear activations, the residual-driven row–column equations are exact and recover the singular-mode framework of Saxe et al. (2014).

Upper-layer sensitivities define sample-dependent effective labels for earlier spectral steps; the corrected nonlinear activations then determine the corresponding upward transmission. The algorithm uses spectral selection and normalized corrections as a surrogate for the local dynamics. papers.title: A 140.5$\mu$W, 99.8% Accuracy, 96.1dB SNR BioZ IC for Real-Time Cell Analysis with On-Demand Push-Pull Excitation and Continuous-Time $\Delta\Sigma$ T-D Readout
papers.abstract: This paper presents a bioimpedance IC combining an on-demand push-pull driver and continuous-time $\Delta\Sigma$ T-D readout to address the trade-off between SNR, accuracy and power consumption. The driver delivers 200$\mu$App with $\leq$0.14% THD while consuming 80.3$\mu$A. Using a 6MHz clock, the readout achieves 53.6ps effective timing resolution at a 4k$\Omega$ load (0.1-4Hz noise integration). The IC achieves 96.1dB peak SNR, 99.8% magnitude accuracy and 0.13$^{\circ}$ phase error at a maximum power consumption of 140.5$\mu$W.

authors.name: Junzhe Chen
authors.institution: Affiliated Hospital of Zunyi Medical College

papers.title: Extreme proxies for causal identification: deconfounding with outliers
papers.abstract: Causal identification under unobserved confounding typically relies on additional structure, such as a valid instrument or proxy variables. We show that heavy tailed variables offer an alternative route to identification by revealing treatment variation for which confounding becomes asymptotically negligible. Our key assumption is extreme propagation: when an unobserved confounder takes an extreme value, some observed variable in the system (called a safeguard) will become extreme with large probability. This way, selecting extreme treatment observations while safeguards remain non-extreme makes confounding asymptotically negligible relative to the treatment. We call this certification. We derive graphical conditions specifying which latent confounders must be monitored by safeguards and distributional conditions ensuring effective certification. The framework includes valid-instrument and double-proxy structures as special cases, as well as confounded instruments that are invalid in most approaches that do not exploit heavy tails. Geometrically, certification isolates the extremal ray whose slope equals the causal effect. This connects causal identification with multivariate extreme-value geometry and motivates a family of novel simple estimators. Simulations demonstrate performance gains under nonlinear confounding and heavy tails, while revealing limitations in light-tailed regimes (where cancellation can conceal extreme confounding from the safeguards). We validate our methodology in simulation studies and by recovering the ground-truth flow in a river discharge application.

papers.title: Theory of the $1/9$ Magnetization Plateau of the Spin-$1/2$ Kagome Heisenberg Antiferromagnet
papers.abstract: We investigate the $1/9$ magnetization plateau of the spin-$1/2$ kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet using infinite projected entangled-pair states and identify a spin-density-wave state with a $27$-site unit cell and a lower variational energy than previous approaches. In contrast to higher-magnetization plateaus, which are well described by localized magnons on nonoverlapping hexagons and preserve a sixfold rotational symmetry, the $1/9$ plateau only keeps a threefold rotational symmmetry and consists of a tiling by three types of $9$-site clusters related by $\pm2\pi/3$ rotations. These conclusions are supported by a complementary cluster mean-field theory which correctly preserves the symmetry of the higher plateaus but leads to the same spontaneous symmetry breaking for the $1/9$ plateau with a qualitatively similar pattern of nine different local magnetizations.

papers.title: A graded version of the separator theorem for planar graphs
papers.abstract: We prove that every planar graph on $n$ vertices has a vertex ordering $v_1,v_2,\ldots,v_n$ in which each prefix $\{v_1,\ldots,v_i\}$ is joined to at most $C\sqrt{i}$ elements of $\{v_{i+1},\ldots,v_n\}$, where $C$ is an absolute constant. Consequently, every prefix can be separated from its complement by deleting $O\left(\sqrt{i}\right)$ vertices lying entirely in its complement.

authors.name: Nabil H. Mustafa
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Inductive Grounded Arithmetic: Goodstein, the Hydra, and $\Gamma_0$
papers.abstract: What does a recursive definition mean when the logic is grounded, so a sentence is true only if a terminating process makes it so? Kripke's answer for the special case of truth was the least fixed point. This paper takes that answer as a rule. Reflective Grounded Arithmetic (RGA) already writes any recursive definition as one self-referential term, paradoxes included. Inductive Grounded Arithmetic (IGA) adds the elimination rule for every positive one, so that accessibility, the winning positions of a game, and grounded truth itself each come with their own induction principle. The rule is sound for the omega model and the system is consistent, both machine-checked in Isabelle/HOL. With the rule, IGA proves Goodstein's theorem outright, in a logic without implication at an undecided hypothesis, and the Kirby-Paris hydra game for primitive recursive strategies, both with every step of the arithmetic a grounded derivation. It proves the Cantor normal forms well-founded, from which the well-foundedness of the standard $\varepsilon_0$ notation system in HOL follows, and it certifies the Veblen notation as an ordinal below every $\varphi(n,0)$. It defines Kripke truth for RGA's own language as one fixed point that agrees with the omega model exactly. Two equivalences locate what the classical world has and the grounded one does not. IGA proves the whole Veblen notation well-founded exactly when it admits bivalence of accessibility for that order, and bivalence of accessibility for an order is sound exactly when the order is well-founded; so $\Gamma_0$ lies at most one instance of excluded middle away, at the accessibility predicate of the notation, and that instance, the well-foundedness sentence and one membership claim in a primitive-recursive form of Kleene's $\mathcal O$ are interderivable over IGA.

papers.title: SPARTA: A Sparse Ternary LLM Accelerator with Adaptive Attention and Unified Datapath for Long-Context Edge Inference
papers.abstract: LLMs on edge devices are constrained by limited memory and bandwidth. Although 1.58-bit ternary weights greatly reduce model storage, long-context inference is increasingly bottlenecked by KV-cache traffic and attention. Existing accelerators also use separate datapaths for ternary linear layers and attention, incurring hardware and execution overhead. We present SPARTA, a sparse ternary LLM accelerator for efficient long-context edge inference. SPARTA integrates: (1) a phase-aware sparse dataflow exploiting heterogeneous sparsity across compute-bound prefill and memory-bound decode; (2) a unified compute fabric mapping ternary SpMM/SpMV and bit-serial attention onto shared processing elements to exploit zero-weight and zero-bit sparsity; and (3) an adaptive two-stage attention engine combining page-level Top-k selection to reduce K-cache accesses with token-level Top-p pruning to reduce V-cache traffic. SPARTA reduces KV traffic by 4.1-4.8x over full attention and 1.3-1.5x over a state-of-the-art sparse-attention scheme, with task-dependent quality loss. Compared with NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, SPARTA achieves 3.9x higher generation throughput and 8.3x higher end-to-end energy efficiency on average; versus AMD Ryzen 7 9700X, the gains are 5.0x and 81.7x. It also delivers 1.6-12.0x higher throughput, 2.0-4.2x higher energy efficiency, and 1.3-51.4x higher area efficiency than FIGLUT, TeLLMe, and MCBP.
