papers.title: Enabling Motion-Induced WiFi-CSI Sensing in Multi-Robot Systems: A Simulation Framework
papers.abstract: WiFi Channel State Information (CSI) enables fine-grained sensing of spatial relationships between wireless devices. The WiFi Sensor for Robotics (WSR) toolbox demonstrated that WiFi-CSI measurements collected during robot motion, combined with odometry, can be used to synthesize virtual antenna arrays, enabling motion-induced bearing estimation in multi-robot experiments. However, deploying the WSR approach has remained challenging due to its limited integration with standard robotics tools and reliance on deprecated WiFi-CSI acquisition hardware. This work presents an open-source simulation framework that integrates the WSR sensing pipeline within the robotic simulator Gazebo. The framework generates synthetic WiFi-CSI measurements with realistic physical signal properties and leverages realistic robot motion required for motion-induced sensing and downstream localization. It further supports processing both simulated and real WiFi-CSI data for direct comparison and validation. Our aim is to make WSR-style sensing accessible as a modular sensing modality for robotic research. We validate our framework by comparing simulated and real-world experiments using TurtleBot3 robots, and demonstrate its use for bearing estimation and robot localization. This work lowers the barrier to entry for WiFi-CSI-based sensing in multi-robot systems and provides a foundation for integrating WiFi-CSI sensing with multi-modal perception for localization and coordination. All code and experimental details are publicly available at https://github.com/baharhaghighat/DARS_2026_Dijkstra_et_al

papers.title: Lightweight Change Detection for Adaptive Collective Perception in Dynamic Environments
papers.abstract: Swarm robotics enables scalable inspection through collective perception, where robots infer environmental properties from distributed observations. A common benchmark considers robots exploring black-white tiled environments and determining the majority tile type. While most work studies static environments, dynamic environments remain underexplored. We study collective perception in dynamic environments where the tile proportion and the spatial correlation of surface patterns may change over time. To enable implementation on resource-constrained robots, we integrate a lightweight change detection mechanism into a Bayesian collective decision-making framework that resets robot beliefs when distribution shifts are detected. The proposed detector requires constant memory and constant per-sample computation, unlike two recent competitive approaches that store the full sample stream, making it suitable for memory-constrained robots. We further introduce a method that detects spatially correlated sampling and adapts sampling intervals online to mitigate correlation effects. Our simulation results in Webots show competitive change detection delays, more consistent precision across communication settings, and improved decision accuracy under changing spatial correlations.

papers.title: Optimal Linear Filtering of Markov Jump Systems
papers.abstract: This paper deals with the optimal state estimation problem for discrete-time Markov jump linear systems in the sense of linear minimum mean-square error where the noises corrupting the system are mode-dependent and need not be Gaussian. An orthogonal projection extension-based equation (OPEBE) is established, which can decompose a random vector into several parts where the random vector contains conditional expectation of another random vector. Using the OPEBE and some results obtained in this paper, an optimal linear filter for the system under consideration is proposed. The computational and storage load of the proposed filter does not increase with time. Also, the proposed filter is finite-dimensionally computable and has a recursive structure. Computer simulations are provided to verify the effectiveness and performance of the proposed optimal linear filter.

papers.title: Retrospective Comparison of Radiation Oncology Patient Message Responses Generated by Epic and Institutionally Managed LLMs
papers.abstract: We retrospectively compared Epic-generated draft replies with institutionally managed hybrid GPT-4.1 and Gemini 2.5 Pro responses to 51 selected single-turn radiation oncology messages. Six clinicians, blinded to response source, rated overall quality on a five-point scale and perceived editing effort on a four-point scale. Mixed-effects models accounted for repeated ratings by message and clinician. Adjusted overall-quality means were 2.95 for Epic, 4.27 for hybrid GPT-4.1, and 4.39 for hybrid Gemini 2.5 Pro. Corresponding editing-effort means were 2.38, 1.46, and 1.41, with lower scores indicating less perceived effort. Both hybrid models received more favorable ratings than Epic for both outcomes (all Holm-adjusted P < 0.001), without a statistically significant difference between the hybrid models. These findings support prospective evaluation of clinician-supervised draft generation, though editing time and patient outcomes were not measured, and clinical safety was not established.

authors.name: Mark Waddle
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: Number of equations defining the Kummer varieties of hyperelliptic curves
papers.abstract: The Jacobian of an hyperelliptic curve $C$ of genus $g$ over $\mathbb{C}$ is equipped with a symmetric theta divisor $\Theta$ that defines a principal polarization. The line bundle $\mathcal{O}(2\Theta)$ defines an embedding of the Kummer variety $K$ inside the projective space $\mathbb{P}^{2^g-1}$, which factorizes inside a certain orthogonal Grassmannian. We describe a minimal free resolution of $K$ inside this Grassmannian using geometric representation theory. As a consequence, we obtain a formula for the number of quartic equations defining $K$ in the projective space $\mathbb{P}^{2^g-1}$.

authors.name: Nathan Partouche
authors.institution: École Nationale Supérieure d'Architecture et de Paysage de Lille

papers.title: GEAR: Feature-Based Configuration and Code Generation for Agentic Systems
papers.abstract: Engineering multi-agent systems (MAS) requires choosing agents, orchestration strategies, communication mechanisms, reasoning approaches, and memory configurations. These choices depend on framework-specific capabilities and abstractions, requiring developers to learn different APIs when exploring alternative implementations. We present GEAR, an open-source tool for configuring MAS and generating framework-specific implementations from a common specification. GEAR uses a feature-based representation to make configuration options and their constraints explicit, enabling users to validate specifications before code generation. Through connectors for ten agentic frameworks, users generate projects from the same specification and can then inspect reports describing framework-specific adaptations. A preliminary assessment of mapping feasibility identifies translation strategies for 271 of 320 evaluated feature-framework pairs (84.69%). GEAR supports developers prototyping agentic systems and researchers exploring MAS configurations across frameworks. GEAR is available as open-source software at https://github.com/brellsanwouo/gear-framework and a video demo is available at https://youtu.be/iwNi-oC2tCw.

authors.name: Brell Sanwouo
authors.institution: Centre Inria de l'Université de Lille

authors.name: Romain Rouvoy
authors.institution: Centre Inria de l'Université de Lille

papers.title: ARMD-Predict: multi-site machine learning to predict antibiotic resistance before culture results
papers.abstract: Clinicians select empiric antibiotics before culture susceptibility results are available. Electronic health record (EHR) models could inform that choice, but most are developed at a single hospital and transport poorly to others. We developed ARMD-Predict using 7.5 million culture-antibiotic observations from four academic medical centers. One set of models estimates susceptibility to individual antibiotics; a second, hierarchical set predicts the infecting organism and then organism-specific resistance phenotypes. Across 23 pooled susceptibility models evaluated in same-period, patient-grouped test partitions, median area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.77 for inpatient urine and 0.70 for inpatient blood cultures; chronological retraining reduced AUROC by approximately 0.04. At an exploratory threshold with 95% positive predictive value, derived and evaluated on the same test observations, the model identified 55% of ceftriaxone-susceptible inpatient urine observations as suitable for narrower therapy and flagged 60% of ceftriaxone-resistant observations for broader coverage. Organism classifiers achieved top-3 accuracy of 51.3-83.3%; phenotype AUROCs were conditional on the observed organism. Research applications are available at https://armd-predict.stanford.edu. Independent calibration, threshold and end-to-end prospective validation are required before clinical use.

authors.name: Steven M. Asch
authors.institution: The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center

papers.title: MarineSet: Large-Scale Underwater Acoustic Data Curation and evaluation
papers.abstract: The scarcity of labeled underwater acoustic data limits the development of data-driven models for marine acoustic monitoring, motivating the use of self-supervised learning to exploit the abundance of unlabeled recordings. However, large-scale data alone does not guarantee effective representation learning, because model performance is strongly influenced by the distribution of the training data. To facilitate such training data, this study introduces a scalable curation pipeline that curates 3,000 hours from 41 years of raw NOAA hydrophone recordings, producing MarineSet, a large-scale and diverse dataset designed for underwater acoustic learning. A baseline model, MarineNet, trained on MarineSet achieves competitive performance on marine mammal call and ship-type classification, highlighting the value of systematic data curation for developing self-supervised learning models in underwater acoustics.

papers.title: Elasto-Plastocapillarity: Surface-Tension-Driven Flows of Yield-Stress Fluids
papers.abstract: In this perspective article, we introduce elasto-plastocapillarity: surface-tension-driven free-surface flows of yield-stress fluids in which capillary stresses compete with yielding and elastic relaxation. We frame the relevant parameter space, and highlight representative problems (drops, bubbles, jets/filaments, thin films, and porous media) that are central to applications ranging from additive manufacturing and coatings to biological flows. We then outline a set of timely open challenges, including surface-tension measurements, breakdown of scale separation near the microstructures, coupled bulk-interface flow experimental diagnosis, interfacial rheology and surface stresses, history dependence, constitutive models and boundary conditions, reduced theoretical models, and the emerging opportunity provided by artificial intelligence and microgravity; aimed at guiding future experiments, theory, and computation.

papers.title: Bridging Search Intent and Tabular Data in Dataset Search
papers.abstract: Dataset search remains a bottleneck in data analysis workflows, as existing systems largely rely on keyword matching or shallow retrieval that fail to capture user intent. To facilitate intent-driven search, we present two retrieval components to equip multi-faceted dataset search interfaces through natural language. First, we propose Hypothetical Schema Embeddings (HySE) that uses a language model to generate task-aligned hypothetical table schemas which are used for embedding-based retrieval, bridging the gap between intent and table content. We introduce KaggleDS, a corpus comprising 6,503 tables and diverse task-queries derived from Kaggle, and show that HySE consistently improves recall over strong keyword and embedding-based baselines, as well as over a dense table retriever fine-tuned on KaggleDS. We also show that HySE generalizes to end-to-end question answering on, for example, the NQ-Tables dataset, a corpus of 169,898 Wikipedia tables with human-written queries, where HySE improves Recall@10 by +6.0 pp over dense retrieval baselines. Second, we introduce FlexPrune, which translates dataset constraints expressed in natural-language into SQL predicates over a customizable metadata index, enabling filtering across arbitrary metadata attributes. Combined with HySE, FlexPrune increases Recall@10 by +6.0 pp over dense retrieval followed by tag-based filtering. Our results show that natural-language-based retrieval supporting task and metadata queries offers a viable alternative to schema-level keyword search in dataset search.

papers.title: General-position sets and linear hypergraphs
papers.abstract: We prove that every linear hypergraph on $N$ vertices with edge sizes $O(\sqrt N)$ and $O(N^2\log N)$ triples contained in its edges has a subset of size $\Omega(\sqrt N)$ meeting each edge in at most two vertices. As an application, every set of $N$ planar points with at most $\sqrt N$ collinear points contains $\Omega(\sqrt N)$ points in general position. This proves a conjecture of Payne and Wood and gives the optimal quadratic bound for a geometric Ramsey problem posed by Gowers.

authors.name: Le Quang-Ham
authors.institution: The Vietnam National Institute of Educational Sciences

papers.title: Geometric progressions in distance sets in odd dimensions over prime fields
papers.abstract:
For $E\subset\mathbb{F}_p^d$, let $\Delta(E)=\{Q_d(x-y):x,y\in E\}$, where $Q_d(z)=z_1^2+\cdots+z_d^2$. We introduce and study the problem of the existence of nondegenerate three-term geometric progressions in the distance set $\Delta(E)$ when $d$ is odd. If $M_{GP,d}(p)$ denotes the largest size of a set whose distance set contains no such progression, then, for every prime $p\geq7$ and every integer $m\geq0$, \[
  p^mM_{GP,1}(p)\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p)
  \leq4p^mM_{GP,1}(p). \] For all sufficiently large primes $p$, we also prove \[
  p^{m+\frac{7}{26}}\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p)
  \leq Cp^{m+\frac{16}{25}}, \] where $C$ is an absolute positive constant.

papers.title: The Lay of the Land in Idiom-Translation Quality Estimation
papers.abstract: Idioms have long been a challenge for machine translation, and while large language models (LLMs) have proven increasingly adept at handling them, whether quality estimation (QE) systems have kept pace and can reliably score idiomatic renderings of these expressions above faulty literal ones remains unclear. We introduce the first parallel dataset pairing idiom-bearing English sentences with both literal and idiomatic translations across nine target languages, augmented into multi-sentence segments and a graded literality continuum. Using this dataset, we benchmark eleven conventional QE metrics from the COMET and MetricX families and ten LLMs from the Qwen-3, Gemma-4 and OLMo-3 families used as GEMBA-style judges. We find that most systems, especially older metrics and smaller models, display a marked literality bias, rating literal translations of idioms above idiomatic ones. Higher parameter counts and newer training sets appear to reduce this bias to an extent; nevertheless, of all the benchmarked systems, only MetricX-24-Hybrid (XL, XXL) and Gemma-4-31B consistently rate idiomatic translations of idioms above literal ones, and only Gemma-4-31B reliably ranks intermediate degrees of idiomaticity and literality. Our findings caution against deploying standard QE metrics in domains rich in figurative language, where higher scores might be rewarding undesirable literalism.

papers.title: Routing Around the Queue: An Evaluation of Eco-Routing Protocol on different Traffic Scenarios
papers.abstract: We evaluate ErouVe, a vehicular eco-routing protocol in which roadside units (RSUs) collect per-segment travel-time and CO2 reports from passing vehicles and answer route requests with the lowest-cost alternative, across a range of road architectures and traffic scenarios. We conduct the evaluation with a working implementation of the protocol inside Veins, adapted to drive SUMO's own router rather than a hand-rolled shortest-path search, on a network offering a short, signal-controlled route and a longer, signal-free bypass, under two traffic scenarios. This evaluation reveals clear strengths and weaknesses of the protocol. Under light, uncongested traffic, ErouVe's fleet-wide effect is light. Under traffic dense enough to stress the signalized route's throughput and produce a real, growing queue, the same protocol succeeds a medium fleet-wide CO2 reduction, with diverted vehicles individually saving even more fuels. We use these findings to propose three targeted corrective methods; a knowledge-gated cost-acceptance rule, a diversion-locking rule, and a distance-normalized CO2 cost function, that respectively address a cold-start knowledge asymmetry, decision flapping under noisy crowd-sourced data, and a per-second CO2 metric that rewards idling. Each of these weaknesses are generic pitfalls for any crowd-sourced routing signal and all proposed methods measurably restore protocol effectiveness.

papers.title: Higher Spherical Scissors Congruence II: Comodules
papers.abstract: We define the higher Dehn invariant on the Euclidean, hyperbolic, and spherical variants of scissors congruence $K$-theory, and prove that it makes these spectra into comodules over the spectral Sah algebra. This allows us to make the first formulation of the conjecture that the higher volume and Dehn invariants are jointly injective.

papers.title: SVD-Attention: Efficiently Analyzing Attention Blocks in Transformers
papers.abstract: Pretrained transformers spend a large share of their inference compute inside self-attention, yet the per-head query-key interaction is structurally low-rank by construction. We ask a diagnostic question: across layers and architectures, which heads actually use the full rank budget on real data, and which do not? We propose SVD-Attention, a post-hoc method that decomposes the per-head interaction matrix $M_h$ and scores every singular mode by both its spectral magnitude and its activation variance across tokens on a small calibration set. The score keeps the modes the head can amplify and that real data actually activates, and discards the rest; the resulting factorization is exact for the retained modes and needs no finetuning. Across seven pretrained models and five task types, the diagnostic finds a task-dependent pattern: redundancy sits in the early to middle layers for sentiment and image classification and for generation, and in the late layers for dense prediction and extractive question answering. It is also predictive: truncating the layers it flags costs at most $1.75$ F1, while truncating the same number of layers elsewhere in the same model costs up to $50$ F1. SVD-Attention is an analysis tool rather than a compression method: acting on it reduces inference FLOPs by $0.8$-$1.5\%$ on its own and by $8$-$11\%$ when composed with weight pruning, with $0$-$4\%$ change in task quality.

authors.name: Hongjie Chen
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: Towards Adversarially Robust Multigraph Neural Networks for Financial Crime Analysis
papers.abstract: Financial transaction networks are naturally represented as multigraphs, where repeated transactions between the same pair of accounts are modeled as distinct edges. Recently proposed multigraph neural network architectures leverage this structure explicitly to achieve a strong performance on anti-money laundering (AML) tasks. However, their robustness to adversaries that manipulate transaction structures to evade detection remains largely unexplored. We present the first scalable framework for structural attacks and adversarial training of multigraph neural networks using node-edge incidence matrices, adapting projected gradient descent and projected randomized block coordinate descent methods to optimize structural perturbations over such matrices. We further introduce a cycle-based regularizer that penalizes changes in the global counts of directed 2- and 3-cycles, providing a structural measure of attack plausibility. Experiments on synthetic pattern-detection and realistic AML datasets show that our learned attacks substantially outperform non-learnable perturbation baselines in reducing detection performance (PR-AUC), while adversarial training consistently improves robustness against these attacks. These results demonstrate that multigraph neural networks are vulnerable to learned structural attacks and that adversarial training provides an effective defense. Our code is available at https://github.com/denheijmans/robust_multignn.

papers.title: Effect of Size Asymmetry and Zwitterionic Character of Solvent Ions on Impedance Spectra of Ultradilute Colloidal Suspensions
papers.abstract: Buffer chemistry modulates colloidal impedance critically for label-free biosensing and electrokinetic diagnostics, yet classical models neglect buffer-specific interactions. We studied carboxylated polystyrene (PS) microspheres in conductivity-matched zwitterionic 4-(2-hydroxyethyl)-1-piperazineethanesulfonic acid (HEPES) and phosphate-buffered saline (PBS). Two concentration-dependent regimes emerged: oscillatory at ultradilute concentrations (<0.02 w/v%; Region 1) and monotonic at higher concentrations (Region 2). In Region 1, HEPES at pH 6.9 (approximately 80% zwitterionic) produced the largest deviation of delta Z from the O'Brien prediction. The conductivity increment was opposite in sign to classical expectation. We attribute this to zwitterion-driven interfacial ordering that enhances local conductivity and promotes self-limiting particle clustering. Dynamic light scattering detected cluster formation at 0.008 w/v%, well below aggregation thresholds. Changing pH from 6.9 to 8.1 strongly altered impedance amplitude; DLS profiles remained invariant. This indicates zwitterions modulate electrochemical polarization, not physical assembly. Molecular dynamics simulations showed pH-dependent HEPES organization at the PS surface. At pH 6.9, interfacial charge- and number-density profiles showed comparable oscillatory periodicity. At pH 8.1, anionic HEPES produced a more diffuse profile with increased Na+ compensation. These results support interfacial ordering as a contributor to enhanced conductivity but do not establish discrete layers or registry. Zeta potentials distinguished stable HEPES interfaces from PBS, where magnitude increased with ionic strength, contrary to classical screening theory. These nonlinear signatures and mesoscale organization underscore the role of buffer selection in high-sensitivity impedance biosensing.

papers.title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Evidence Misgrounding in Multimodal Knowledge Editing
papers.abstract: Multimodal knowledge editing aims to update visually grounded facts in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) while preserving unrelated text and visual behaviors. However, standard answer-level metrics can hide evidence misgrounding: an edit may produce the target answer on the original image yet remain sensitive to incidental context rather than the intended visual evidence. To examine this issue in a controlled setting, we construct WaterBird-Edit, an analysis set that decouples bird habitat labels from background context and measures whether edited predictions remain stable when the target evidence is preserved but the background changes. Motivated by this diagnosis, we propose VICE (Visual In-Context Editing), a retrieval-based framework that stores edits in external memory and applies them through visual in-context demonstrations designed to expose task-relevant evidence. Experiments on three standard benchmarks show that VICE achieves strong lifelong editing performance, while results on WaterBird-Edit show that it substantially reduces sensitivity to the controlled background shifts. Code and dataset are available in https://github.com/Wang-Z-W/VICE-main.

authors.name: Jinqian Yang
authors.institution: Jiangsu Key Laboratory of Construction Materials

papers.title: Identifying level-$k$ reasoning in repeated games: Strategies, beliefs, and cognitive ability
papers.abstract: In this paper, we identify level-$k$ reasoning in repeated games that operates at the level of a supergame strategy. First, we develop a model of level-$k$ reasoning that incorporates choices over strategies as well as beliefs about the strategies chosen by others. Then, jointly using elicited strategies and beliefs about strategies from the indefinitely repeated Prisoner's Dilemma, and applying a new notion of balance-optimal error tolerance, we classify a substantial fraction of subjects as level-1 or level-2. Moreover, we show that when level-$k$ reasoning operates at the level of a repeated-game strategy, cognitive ability and experience predict higher level reasoning.

papers.title: Ordinary algebras of complex-valued functions
papers.abstract: A classical theorem due to Gleason, Kahane, and Zelazko states that every complex unital Banach algebra is ordinary, meaning that any linear functional mapping elements into their spectrum is a character. While Roitman and Sternfeld extended this property to algebras with bounded spectra-showing in particular that the algebra C(X) of continuous functions is ordinary when X is pseudocompact-the general case of C(X) for arbitrary topological spaces X appears to be open, as we could not locate any reference in this direction. In this paper, we show that the pseudocompactness condition is unnecessary, that is, C(X) is ordinary for every topological space X. This fact is obtained as a consequence of a more general result characterizing positive characters on a purely algebraic generalization of unital C*-algebras, which we introduce under the name of AC*-algebras. As applications, we obtain two necessary and sufficient conditions for a Tychonoff space X to be realcompact in terms of 1-evaluating linear functionals on C(X) and their continuity with respect to the compact-open topology. Finally, we establish a Banach--Stone type theorem showing that two realcompact spaces X and Y are homeomorphic if and only if C(X) and C(Y) are linearly isomorphic via a map that preserves invertibility.

papers.title: Spectrally optimized implicit neural representations mitigate acquisition-related image quality trade-offs in intracranial 4D Flow MRI
papers.abstract: 4D Flow MRI promises opportunities for non-invasive mapping of neurovascular hemodynamics, but its clinical utility faces trade-offs between resolution, acquisition time, and noise. Deep learning-based super-resolution offers a post-scan solution, but supervised approaches require paired or domain-specific data, while patient-specific physics-informed models can be computationally demanding. This creates a need for unsupervised reconstruction models that can adapt to individual acquisitions without paired high-resolution training data, while remaining robust across anatomy, disease severity, and acquisition quality. To address this, we introduce a spectrally tuned implicit neural representation (INR) framework for intracranial 4D Flow MRI, representing the velocity field as a continuous coordinate-based neural field using WIRE activation functions with tunable spectral bias. Data-driven and physics-informed variants were evaluated in nine cerebrovascular cases spanning healthy controls and moderate-to-severe intracranial atherosclerotic disease, using CFD-derived high-resolution reference fields, MR-realistic synthetic low-resolution inputs, and direct fitting to acquired in-vivo data. Cohort-optimal spectral-bias settings generalized across subjects with only small increases in relative error compared with subject-specific optima, reducing the need for case-specific hyperparameter tuning. Physics-informed regularization provided modest additional accuracy but required substantially longer optimization, whereas the data-driven INR achieved near-comparable reconstruction performance within minutes. The framework also remained robust to acquisition-realistic noise and moderate VENC-dependent aliasing. These findings establish spectrally optimized INRs as a flexible unsupervised approach for mitigating acquisition-related trade-offs in intracranial 4D Flow MRI.

authors.name: Patrick Winter
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Dallas

papers.title: Toward Clinical Translation of Deep Learning-Based Intracranial Super-Resolution 4D Flow MRI Using Multi-Cohort Transfer Learning
papers.abstract: We evaluated synthetic pretraining and multi-cohort transfer learning for deep learning-based super-resolution of intracranial 4D Flow MRI across heterogeneous neurologic cohorts. This mixed prospective-retrospective study analyzed 18 participants (12 healthy participants, 3 with moyamoya disease, and 3 with multiple sclerosis) with paired 1.2-mm and 0.6-mm 4D Flow MRI scans. A convolutional neural network pretrained on synthetic cerebrovascular data was fine-tuned using cohort-specific or pooled multi-cohort in vivo data. High-resolution-derived inputs enabled voxel-wise evaluation; native standard-resolution scans were used for angiographic and hemodynamic analyses. Synthetic pretraining reduced mean artery-wise velocity-normalized root mean square error (vNRMSE) versus interpolation (0.147 vs 0.166). Pooled transfer learning yielded the lowest mean vNRMSE (0.119 vs 0.127 for cohort-specific models and 0.147 for synthetic pretraining), with narrower 95% limits-of-agreement widths than synthetic pretraining across all test cases (0.109-0.222 vs 0.154-0.278 m/s). Super-resolved phase-contrast angiography achieved higher precision-recall area under the curve than native standard-resolution imaging in all cohorts (0.848-0.896 vs 0.486-0.805). These results indicate that pooled transfer learning improves cross-cohort reconstruction agreement and that super-resolution can improve vessel depiction, supporting further multi-center validation for cerebrovascular imaging.

authors.name: Patrick Winter
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Dallas

papers.title: From Hype to ROI: An Economic Model for LLM Adoption in Information Systems and Security Operations
papers.abstract:
Large Language Models (LLMs) promise significant efficiency gains across information-intensive operations by automating repetitive language-based tasks. However, adoption decisions remain largely opportunistic, as organizations struggle to move from pilots to sustainable industrialization. Without systematic economic frameworks, practitioners cannot assess whether LLM investments create value in a given context.
  This paper develops a general economic model to support informed LLM adoption decisions in operational information systems. Facing high uncertainty, we represent parameters as random variables centered on authoritative benchmarks, and evaluate the model by Monte Carlo simulation across pessimistic-to-optimistic assumptions on LLM efficiency. The ROI distributions show the probability of profitability and the Value at Risk for each configuration, together with a sensitivity analysis of its main drivers.
  As a first instantiation, we apply the model to Security Operations Centers (SOCs), mapping workflows onto established standards to identify tasks suited to LLM augmentation. The model balances productivity gains, driven by alert volume, analyst effort, and LLM efficiency, against operational costs, including inference, infrastructure, and error remediation, covering both cloud API and self-hosted deployments.
  Results show that adoption economics are context-dependent, and that automation is an exploitable lever, gated by accuracy, while the cost of errors and the model's price are secondary. Across the analyzed models and prices, most configurations are unprofitable, with profitability limited to high-accuracy, low-uncertainty deployments.
  The model gives organizations a quantitative basis for evidence-based adoption decisions, by locating the boundary between profit and loss, and the loss risked beyond it.

authors.name: Rosario Patan\`e
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Liouville Theorems for the Stationary Fractional Hall-Magnetohydrodynamic Equations
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove Liouville-type theorems for the stationary fractional Hall-magnetohydrodynamic equations in $\mathbb R^3$. Smooth solutions vanishing at infinity, with $u\in\dot H^{\alpha/2}$ and $b\in\dot H^{\beta/2}$, are trivial for $1\le\alpha\le\frac53$, $1\le\beta<2$ and $\alpha+2\beta\le5$, with no additional integrability assumption. The key step is to estimate the Hall boundary term through the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension of $b$.

authors.name: Gaston Vergara-Hermosilla
authors.institution: Laboratoire de Mathématiques et Modélisation d'Évry

papers.title: On AI and Progress in Mathematics: Dreaming a Mathematical Universal Machine
papers.abstract: In the autumn of 2026, mathematics is facing what may be the deepest crisis in its history. The entire ecosystem through which mathematical knowledge is produced, validated, communicated, and assessed is beginning to break down. Mathematics departments, those usually quiet and civilized places, are suddenly in turmoil -- the unlikely theaters of a new Battle of the Ancients and the Moderns. The source of the crisis is clear: AI systems have become better than even the best human mathematicians at proving and validating mathematical results. This document proposes a metaphor for mathematical activity: we once thought of ourselves as mountain climbers; soon, we may become miners digging in the mathematical mine, either collaborating or competing with mathematical AI machines. Publications would then be seen primarily as a means of helping humans understand mathematics, while the measurement of mathematical progress would be entrusted to a Mathematical Universal Machine. In nontechnical terms, we explore what this brave new world of mathematics might look like and how we might collectively shape its future.

authors.name: Vincent Runge
authors.institution: Laboratoire de Mathématiques et Modélisation d'Évry

papers.title: Congruence lattices of $2$-valued unary algebras
papers.abstract: We study congruence lattices of finite algebras whose basic operations are unary and have exactly two values. We prove that the class of finite lattices representable in this way is closed under taking filters, glued sums and ordinal sums, and direct products with finite distributive lattices, but it is not closed under taking ideals or arbitrary direct products. A classification of lattices with at most seven elements with respect to representability is also presented.

papers.title: Hydrodynamics for hypersingular interactions by $\Gamma$-convergence of gradient flows
papers.abstract: We consider the dynamics of $N$ particles with Riesz repulsive interaction in one dimension, focusing in particular on the hypersingular case (i.e. inverse power with power larger than or equal to the dimension). We prove convergence of the empirical measure to the solution of a porous medium equation by the method of $\Gamma$-convergence of gradient flows introduced by Sandier and the second author. This improves on the prior convergence result by Oelschl\"ager obtained under more stringent assumptions. The method also works for the case where the power is smaller than the dimension, as well as for a class of convex short-range interactions. The proof highlights the crucial role played by the convexity of the interaction, which allows one to show that no excess energy can arise along the flow, implying the needed "slope inequality".

papers.title: PinGER: Token-Efficient Generative Retrieval with Semantic IDs
papers.abstract: Generative retrieval replaces nearest-neighbor search with token-by-token decoding of an item's semantic ID (SID). But existing SID-based methods primarily use L levels of tokens sequentially to represent each item in the input history. As a result, a fixed context window holds L times fewer items than it would with one embedding per item. We present PinGER, a generative retriever deployed at Pinterest that retains SID outputs while making input histories compact, built on three ideas. (1) An asymmetric attention mask over interleaved SID and dense tokens lets later items attend only to the dense ones, so the model is supervised at every SID position in training yet serves one token per item while computing the same function. (2) Generation is controllable through goal-conditioned outputs, reinforcement learning, and a prefix-diversity penalty, which together steer retrieval toward surface-specific goals and diverse candidates. (3) A serving stack built for efficient wide-beam generation is paired with decoding constrained to valid identifiers and candidate resolution from a host-local index. Deployed in Related Pins, PinGER lifts saves of fresh Pins by 3.60% and overall saves by 0.62%, while reducing the surface's end-to-end latency by 0.7% and eliminating the cost of the nearest-neighbor search it replaces.

authors.name: Charles Rosenberg
authors.institution: Institut National de la Recherche Agronomique

papers.title: Grounded Exploration for Open-Ended Image Editing
papers.abstract: Open-ended image-editing requests, such as ``decorate this room,'' admit multiple valid realizations. Direct sampling may produce ungrounded variation, whereas explicit diversity prompting often produces superficial differences. We study how to ground these requests without prematurely eliminating their legitimate ambiguity. We introduce a two-stage framework that first identifies diverse, feasible edit scopes and then realizes them as executable edit instructions. Across 300 open-ended image-editing tasks, our approach achieves 24.6% higher mean semantic dispersion and 17.1% higher mean groundedness than direct diversity prompting, while producing more valid and distinct realizations. These results show that structuring feasible edit directions before realization supports more useful grounded exploration.

authors.name: Charles Rosenberg
authors.institution: Institut National de la Recherche Agronomique

papers.title: Remarks on the Brascamp--Lieb inequality
papers.abstract: We prove several variants of the Brascamp--Lieb inequality which are adapted to additional symmetries, weights, and non-Euclidean radial structures. First, an improved Brascamp--Lieb inequality for even functions yields a strengthened Pr\'ekopa--Leindler theorem for even strongly log-concave functions. We also record a Legendre-transform proof of a generalized log-Sobolev inequality for log-concave functions. Further results include a Brascamp--Lieb inequality with a concave weight, an unconditional second-order Poincar\'e inequality, a rotation-trick improvement for arbitrary even log-concave measures, and a Poincar\'e-type inequality associated with smooth norms.

papers.title: Factual Yet One-Sided: Stance Poisoning and Evidence Balancing in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.abstract:
The stance expressed in responses from retrieval-augmented generation systems is significantly influenced by the stance distribution of the retrieved materials. Existing research on knowledge poisoning has primarily targeted factual errors. In contrast, this study focuses on injection attacks in which the facts are correct but the stance on a controversial issue is one-sided. At a mean topic-level poisoning share of 18.9% within the post-injection ProCon documents, all four generation models from different vendors exhibited stance shifts aligned with the poisoning direction; across four concentration levels, the shifts increased monotonically.
  This paper proposes a Stance-Balancing Middleware positioned between the retriever and the generator. It consists of stance detection, fixed balancing (2 supporting + 2 opposing + 1 neutral), and a debiasing prompt, without introducing additional large language model calls. Across all eight concentration-direction settings, the complete method reduced the magnitude of stance deviation by an estimated 0.106 to 0.350; the six settings at poisoning shares of 11.9%-18.9% remained significant after Holm adjustment (adjusted p <= 0.009). In the cross-model experiment, all eight model-direction combinations moved along the stance axis in the corrective direction, and seven of eight showed a clearly detected reduction in absolute distance from 0. In the concentration sweep, the post-defense intervals included 0 in all eight settings, while the cross-model pro-poisoning results retained small positive residual point estimates of +0.045 to +0.063. For 20 candidate documents, stance detection took approximately 1.5% of the median generation time on a single GPU and approximately 16% on CPU.

papers.title: The Target Agent Is Its Own Best Critic but a Poor Proposer: Self-Improved Red Teaming
papers.abstract: Automatic red teaming increasingly relies on large language models (LLMs) to iteratively diagnose failed attacks and propose improved adversarial prompts or injections. Although prior work strengthens this loop through prompt engineering and search-harness design, the mechanisms underlying its two core roles, criticism and attack proposal, has not been explored. To further investigate the core roles and therefore improve red teaming effectiveness, we disentangle two design choices: whether criticism is generated by the target session itself (self-criticism) or by a separately instantiated critic (external criticism), and whether that criticism is translated into the next attack by the target session (self-proposal) or by a separate attacker (external proposal). Through our analysis, we find that self-criticism is more effective because it is grounded in the target's live execution context, including observations, constraints, and available reasoning; removing reasoning reduces downstream attack success by 6%-17%. In contrast, self-proposal is substantially less effective because awareness of the adversarial objective induces explicit refusal and non-refusal sandbagging. These findings motivate a role-separated red-teaming approach: the target session diagnoses why an attack failed, while a separately instantiated attacker generates the next proposal. On DTAP-BENCH, spanning Telecom, Workflow, CRM, and Code domains, under both direct misuse and indirect threat models, as well as multiple agent frameworks, this configuration achieves 63.2% overall attack success rate (ASR), much higher than baselines. Our results show that effective automatic red teaming depends not only on model capability and search strategy, but also on how execution context and adversarial responsibility are distributed across model sessions.

authors.name: Melissa Kazemi Rad
authors.institution: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

papers.title: Quasi locally free sheaves on primitive double schemes
papers.abstract: Let $X_2$ be a complex primitive double scheme, $X=(X_2)_{red}$. The ideal sheaf of $X$ is a line bundle on $X$. Let $E$ be a coherent sheaf on $X_2$. Then there exists a nonempty open subset $U$ of $X_2$ and integers $m_1$, $m_2$, uniquely determined by $E$, such that $E_{|U}$ is locally isomorphic to $(O_X\otimes C^{m_1})\oplus(O_{X_2}\otimes C^{m_2})$. If we can take $U=X_2$, we say the $E$ is quasi locally free. If $m_1=1$ we say that $E$ is rigid. In this case, we show that deformations of $E$ are of the same type. So locally free sheaves and rigid quasi locally free sheaves on $X_2$ play the same role on $X_2$ as locally free sheaves do on smooth schemes. In this paper we study the existence and description of quasi locally free sheaves, and flat families of such sheaves.

papers.title: Probing the phon* representations of the Mimi codebooks
papers.abstract: Neural audio codecs are increasingly used to encode speech for integration with large language models. This paper investigates the phonetic representations in the first codebook (CB0) of the Mimi codec. ABX style evaluation is poorly suited to Mimi fixed 80 ms tokenization window, which often spans multiple phonemes; we instead use forced alignment, entropy analysis, and Phone-Normalized Mutual Information (PNMI). Using TIMIT speech (58/55 speakers, SA1/SA2), individual tokens are strongly associated with specific phonemes (PNMI = 0.84, above random), yet phonemes are realized by multiple competing tokens rather than a one-to-one mapping.

papers.title: Closing the Modality Gap via Simplex-Constrained Representations
papers.abstract: While multimodal contrastive models like CLIP and CLAP successfully learn shared representations, their embeddings typically exhibit a persistent \emph{modality gap}. We propose addressing this separation through a purely geometric approach: changing the embedding domain from the unit sphere, $S^{d-1}$, to the probability simplex, $\Delta^{d-1}$. Although both manifolds share the same intrinsic dimension, the simplex acts as a structural prior; its nonnegative, unit-mass constraints serve as a cross-modal calibration that forces both modalities to ground themselves in the same coordinate system. By attaching lightweight softmax adapters and using Total Variation similarity, we reduce the centroid $\ell_2$ gap by 97--99\% across five multimodal retrieval benchmarks. This confirms that simplicial geometry induces genuine semantic alignment, matching or exceeding the retrieval performance of standard unconstrained models.

papers.title: Do bioacoustic foundation models hear through the noise ? SNR and generalization in underwater detection
papers.abstract: Bioacoustic foundation models are claimed to generalize across taxa and recording conditions, but are trained mainly on terrestrial archives of focal, high-quality recordings and evaluated on benchmarks emphasizing architecture over data conditions. We evaluate four such models as frozen encoders on an underwater detection task, using linear probing on continuously recorded data from the Kerguelen Plateau. Four datasets of identical size were built to differ only in the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of their positive segments, and probes were trained and evaluated across all combinations. Evaluation SNR accounts for more variation in average precision (AP) than model choice, and performance peaks when training and evaluation share a noise regime --- the configuration least representative of a continuous deployment. Training on mixed SNR redistributes performance toward low-SNR conditions without improving it overall, and AP remains low throughout. In light of these results, we call for evaluation standards grounded in realistic noise and deployment conditions rather than curated, high-quality recordings.

papers.title: Empirical Brightening Model for Distant Long-Period Comets
papers.abstract: Recent studies have shown the traditional comet brightening model, $Hn$, with a constant activity index $n$ (i.e., single slope in $\log_{10}(r_{\rm h})$), fails to accurately describe heliocentric lightcurves at large distances, where water-ice sublimation is inefficient. We present a new empirical model, $Hab$, for distant comet brightening in which the effective brightening slope varies with heliocentric distance, $r_{\rm h}$. Using a multi-year pre-perihelion dataset from uniform instrumentation for 23 comets, we found that $Hab$ provides the best match to long inbound arcs spanning a wide range in $r_{\rm h}$. The best-fit coefficients $a$ and $b$ cluster tightly for our best-observed comets, suggesting a common brightening behavior; we therefore also tested one- and two-parameter $Hab$ variants in which $a$ and/or $b$ are fixed to anchor values derived from these comets ($A_1 = 0.40 \pm 0.09$, $B_1 = -1.78 \pm 0.68$), either individually, jointly, or via a linear relation. The three-parameter $Hab$ model is strongly favored by the Bayesian information criterion (BIC) for the full lightcurve, justifying its added complexity for characterization. We also tested predictive performance against $Hn$. For brightness forecasting from limited initial data ($\Delta r_{\rm h} \lesssim 2.5$ au, the heliocentric distance range spanned by observations), $Hab$ itself predicts poorly, whereas a one-parameter reduction, with both coefficients fixed, predicts more reliably, including outperforming $Hn$ with a fixed $n \sim 2-4$. Two-parameter reductions with only one coefficient fixed typically reach predictions within 1 mag of the observed brightness after only $\Delta r_{\rm h} \sim 1.0$ au of inbound coverage.

papers.title: Cooperation of itinerant and localized physics in the magnetic phase diagram of 214 Ruddlesden-Popper iridates
papers.abstract: The $5d^5$ Ruddlesden-Popper iridates Sr$_2$IrO$_4$ and Ba$_2$IrO$_4$ have attracted considerable attention as spin-orbit entangled analogues of the cuprates, yet the origin of their antiferromagnetic insulating state, of Slater or of Mott-Heisenberg type, remains debated. We find that both materials sit in an intermediate regime in which itinerant and localized electrons cooperate in stabilizing the antiferromagnetic order, with Ba$_2$IrO$_4$ slightly more correlated than Sr$_2$IrO$_4$. We obtain this by computing, within dynamical mean-field theory, the interaction-temperature phase diagram of a realistic three-orbital $t_{2g}$ Hubbard model with spin-orbit coupling. Our study shows that neither the behavior of the gap across the N\'eel temperature nor the spin-polaron features of the spectral function unambiguously identify the cooperative regime, whereas the two-peak structure of the optical conductivity is reproduced only there and therefore constitutes a reliable fingerprint. By placing both compounds in a common phase diagram, our results reconcile seemingly contradictory experimental and theoretical reports, and provide a unified framework for future studies of the 214 iridates and of other spin-orbit coupled correlated materials.

papers.title: Dephasing-powered open quantum-dot battery
papers.abstract: We propose a simple realization of an open quantum battery powered by local dephasing. The setup consists of a triple-quantum-dot chain coupled at one end to a thermal reservoir, with the dot at the opposite end strongly detuned to form a high-energy storage element. Local dephasing populates this highly excited state and autonomously drives the system into a nonequilibrium steady state with high ergotropic efficiency. We find a limit where the ergotropic efficiency approaches unity, while the ergotropy itself approaches one-third of the energy detuning. We characterize the battery through its energy-storage performance, charging time, and stability, showing that the charged state remains long-lived after the dephasing source is switched off. We then demonstrate two complementary protocols for extracting the stored energy. First, nearly all the available ergotropy can be recovered through a simple cyclic unitary protocol involving only modulation of the detuned-dot gate. Second, coupling the detuned dot to an electronic load allows the extraction of electrochemical work exceeding the initial ergotropy, thereby accessing part of the battery's passive energy. Our results establish local dephasing as an autonomous resource for charging open quantum batteries and demonstrate simple routes for extracting the resulting stored energy in experimentally accessible mesoscopic platforms.

papers.title: Linear statistics in the Coulomb gas: cumulants beyond rotational invariance
papers.abstract: We consider a classical Coulomb gas of $N$ particles in dimension $d\geq2$, confined by a general external potential $U$ in the large-$N$ limit. In that limit the density of particles has a compact support called the droplet. We study smooth linear statistics ${\mathcal L}_N=\sum_{i=1}^N f({\bf x}_i)$ at large $N$. While the leading variance of ${\mathcal L}_N$ is by now well understood in many settings, much less is known about higher cumulants. When $f({\bf x})=f(|{\bf x}|)$ and the potential is rotationally invariant, these cumulants were computed recently at leading order. We derive explicit formulas for the leading third and fourth cumulants for general smooth droplets, without assuming that either the potential or the test function is radial. The answers are expressed as intrinsic boundary integrals over the equilibrium droplet. The third cumulant depends on the cube of the jump of the normal derivative of the harmonic extension of $f$, while the fourth cumulant also involves the exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator, the mean curvature of the boundary, and normal derivatives of the background density. Our derivation uses the tilted potential $U_s=U+s f/\beta$, the associated deformation of the droplet, and shape derivatives of the Dirichlet energy. This deformation has a natural interpretation as the infinitesimal motion of the free boundary in the obstacle-problem formulation of the equilibrium measure. Our formulas extend previous studies by Wiegmann and Zabrodin in two dimensions for $\beta=2$. In their setting, we provide a rigorous proof of the limiting third and fourth cumulants, supporting the proposed formulas for general Coulomb gases. We specialize the general formulas to the disk, the half-plane and the sphere, and check them against exactly solvable non-radial deformations, including translated elliptic droplets in $d=2$ and spheroidal deformations in $d=3$.

papers.title: Pseudospectral phenomena preventing the analyticity sector of a Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroup to be ruled by the spectral angle of its generator
papers.abstract: We study elliptic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck operators in $L^2$ spaces with respect to invariant measures. These operators have discrete spectra and generate analytic semigroups. The angle defining the analyticity sector of a Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroup is not always equal to the complementary angle of the spectral angle of its generator. In this work, we study the link between these two angles. More specifically, we provide a necessary and sufficient criterion ensuring that they are complementary, and explain how pseudospectral phenomena account for these two angles to fail to be complementary.

authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Polarized X-rays from table-top free-electron-driven van der Waals crystals
papers.abstract: Polarized X-rays are essential for polarization-sensitive techniques such as X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy, magnetic microscopy, and fluorescence imaging. These techniques are crucial in the study of molecular and material dynamics, which are in turn central to driving the global transition to clean energy and sustainability through research in photovoltaics, catalysis and optoelectronics. Currently, polarized X-rays with tunable polarization and photon energy are available only in large facilities like synchrotrons. Here, we theoretically predict and experimentally demonstrate the generation of linearly polarized X-rays from free electron-driven van der Waals crystals, without the need for additional optical stages like polarizers. We show that precise, real-time control over the polarization can be achieved by simply re-orienting the van der Waals crystal. Furthermore, we show that a high degree of polarization can be achieved across all polarization angles - from perpendicular to in-plane - with intensities exceeding 10^9 photons s^(-1) sr^(-1) mA^(-1). Using our findings, we present a scheme for table-top XANES, achieving performance comparable to that of synchrotron facilities. In the process, we develop a new methodology for performing XANES using high-quality polarized X-rays with larger spectral linewidths, named ORIXANES (Orientation-controlled XANES). Our findings pave the way to greater accessibility and smaller carbon footprint for advanced X-ray modalities.

papers.title: Recovery of a source of anomalous diffusion from space-time sparse data
papers.abstract: We study an inverse source problem for a time-fractional sub- and super-diffusive anomalous diffusion equation on the unit disk with sparse boundary observations. We prove the recovery of a general class of $L^2$ sources for anomalous diffusion, with separated variables, from boundary measurements that are sparse in both space and time, using observations at two carefully chosen boundary points on a discrete set of times arbitrarily close to the final time. The analysis relies heavily on the memory effect of the model, properties of complex analysis and the representation of solutions.

authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Berezin Transform Commutators
papers.abstract: We study commutators of Berezin transforms $\mathcal B_\alpha$ associated with radial weighted Fock spaces with exponential weights $e^{-\alpha |z|^{m}}$ on the complex plane. We prove that when $m>2$, the commutator $[\mathcal B_\alpha,\mathcal B_\beta]$ is compact on the space $L^{2}(\mathbb C, dA)$ whenever $\alpha,\beta>0$. We further show that if $m>2$ and $\alpha\neq\beta$, then the commutator is never of finite rank.

papers.title: Designing sustainability under Earth-system rate constraints
papers.abstract: Sustainability debates are monopolized by quantities: total energy use, material stocks, or recycling volumes. These metrics are informative, but they obscure a more fundamental constraint. On a materially closed but energetically open Earth, long-term viability is governed by rates: power density, areal power density, and the rate at which dispersed materials can be repurified under dif- fuse solar fluxes. We develop a physical framework that links technological metabolism, material dilution, and recycling limits through these rate con- straints. This perspective clarifies why many contemporary technologies remain viable only through stock drawdown and high-power buffering, and why green growth strategies often shift rather than resolve the underlying mismatch between industrial activity and Earth-system dynamics. We argue that long-term sustain- ability requires both quantitative reduction in aggregate industrial throughput toward rate-bounded regimes and the development of technologies qualitatively compatible with biospheric operating conditions.

papers.title: Tuning from intrinsic to disorder-dominated quantum states in a kagome antiferromagnet
papers.abstract: The spin-1/2 kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet (AFM) provides a paradigmatic platform for realizing quantum spin-liquid (QSL) and magnetization-plateau states. Experimental progress, however, has been hindered by structural disorder, whose effects on these quantum states remain elusive. A key experimental challenge is therefore to connect intrinsic and disorder-dominated regimes through controlled disorder and identify emergent degrees of freedom associated with disorder. Here we introduce controlled point defects through electron irradiation into the spin-1/2 kagome AFM YCu3(OH)6.5Br2.5 (YCOB) and track the resulting evolution of its low-energy magnetic states. High-field magnetic torque measurements reveal that the 1/9 and 1/3 magnetization plateaus are strongly suppressed by only ~0.05% irradiation-induced defects, demonstrating that these delicate quantum many-body states are extraordinarily fragile against dilute disorder. Moreover, the irradiation induces a sign reversal of the magnetic torque only at low temperatures and low fields, indicating the emergence of correlated defect-induced moments rather than isolated free spins. Remarkably, the characteristic scaling of the magnetic specific heat, absent in pristine YCOB, progressively emerges with increasing disorder. These findings establish dilute disorder as an effective tuning parameter that drives the kagome AFM from intrinsic quantum states toward a disorder-dominated regime. The contrasting responses further identify pristine YCOB as an exceptionally clean kagome AFM for accessing intrinsic quantum states.

papers.title: Weighted Fairness in Multi-User Earth Observation Satellite Scheduling
papers.abstract: As constellations of satellite grow in size, and become more costly, they are increasingly funded by multiple stakeholders who expect access to the constellation's resources that is commensurate with their investment. Such cooperation raises significant challenges for constellation operation, in particular regarding the fairness of the computed schedules among stakeholders. While several existing works deal with fairness in the Earth Observation Satellite Scheduling Problem (EOSSP), most of them assume that users (e.g. space agencies, research labs, countries) have the same weights, i.e. contributed equally to the project and therefore have equal access to the constellation. However, in practice, users' contributions often differ significantly. Hence, in this paper, we study a weighted variant of the EOSSP where users are assigned weights reflecting their respective contributions to the constellation. We propose several solution concepts with varying focus on efficiency and fairness, namely weighted utilitarianism, weighted egalitarianism, weighted leximin, and weighted ordered weighed averaging (WOWA). We formulate the related optimization problems as Mixed-Integer Linear Programs (MILPs), and compare them against two natural heuristics: weighted greedy and weighted round robin. All methods are evaluated on scenarios drawn from the literature, under strict runtime constraints, in order to assess the performance of each approach with respect to both efficiency and fairness metrics.

papers.title: EditDistill: Is It Possible to Guide Video Editing with Image Editing?
papers.abstract: Recent advances in image editing have enabled fine-grained and highly controllable visual modifications. However, achieving similar levels of controllability in video editing remains an open challenge, particularly for precise local edits, dynamic temporal effects, and consistent lighting across frames.In this paper, we propose EditDistill, a framework that distills image-level visual transformations from edits to guide video editing.Specifically, given a source video and an edit prompt, we first generate an edited version of the initial video frame using an off-the-shelf image editing model. We then distill the visual transformation of this original-edited image pair into a compact representation termed an edit descriptor.This descriptor is injected into a video diffusion model through our lightweight fusion module, which steers the denoising process toward the desired edit. To align the video trajectory with the demonstrated image edit while preserving motion and layout, we train with edit-descriptor alignment and DINO structural consistency losses, and derive an equivalent inference-time guidance formulation under flow matching.Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves strong performance on standard benchmarks and produces high-quality video editing results across diverse scenarios. For more details and videos, please refer to the anonymous webpage: https://yu-shaonian.github.io/EditDistill-Web/.

authors.name: Lixue Gong
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: 6G Reasoning Agent Societies: Composition, Scaling, and Consistency-Time Laws
papers.abstract: Emerging 6G control planes would compose Large Language Model (LLM) agents that exchange interpreted conclusions, so hallucinations can propagate even over error-free transport. Recent architectures audit each message locally against the sender's observation mask, but isolated audits miss collective behavior. Modeling the agent society as a cellular sheaf, we establish three laws valid on arbitrary topologies. First, the \emph{composition law}: network-wide divergence exceeds the sum of per-agent audit scores by exactly their hidden total correlation. This blind spot masks up to 23\% of joint divergence and, because the declared signal cancels in the cognitive signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), overstates it by $1.14$\,dB purely through topology; the resulting trust inflation preserves valid consensus states but slows convergence. Second, the \emph{scaling law}: reconciliation decouples across metric counters, so the worst-connected dimension sets the pace. Consistency time grows for a society size $n$ as $\Omega(n^{2/d})$ on polynomial-growth topologies of degree $d$, and paths breach a $1$\,s near-real-time budget at $n^\ast=13$ agents, whereas expanders ($\Theta(1)$) and radius-3 local audits ($O(1)$, $\approx300$\,ms) stay bounded. Third, the \emph{consistency-time law}: the timing error from omitted correlations is one-sided and capped by the worst-measured link. These laws, validated on simulated topologies and deployed LLM societies, give provable worst-case latency ceilings for near-real-time operation.

authors.name: Mustapha Benjillali
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Maximum-Likelihood Decoding of Gabidulin Codes Is NP-Hard Even in Dimension One
papers.abstract: Fix a prime power q. We prove that deciding whether a received word y in Fnqm lies at rank distance at most n-2 from the one-dimensional Gabidulin code {{\lambda.g : {\lambda} in Fqm } is NP-complete. Thus maximum-likelihood decoding of Gabidulin codes is NP-hard even for k = 1, an analogue of the Guruswami-Vardy theorem for Reed-Solomon codes. In the Hamming metric, by contrast, hardness at this radius requires the dimension to grow with the length, as in the Guruswami-Vardy theorem. The reduction is deterministic; consequently Rank Syndrome Decoding (RSD) and Rank Minimum Distance (RMD) for Fqm -linear codes are NP-complete under deterministic polynomial reductions, whereas the previously known reduction was randomized. The proof goes through a pivot problem that we introduce, Twisted Square Membership (TSM): given Fq-subspaces U, W in FqN , decide whether some non-zero a in U satisfies a^(q+1) in W . Quadratic systems in d unknowns are encoded into TSM, then TSM into Gabidulin decoding. The last step views the received word as an Fq-linear map and decoding at radius n - 2 as the search for an Fq-plane on which it acts as a scalar. With support U + {\tau} W in a cubic extension and map a + {\tau} b to a^(q^2) + {\tau} bq^q , two Frobenius twists force solution planes to encode the relation a^(q+1) in W . All constructions are explicit and polynomial, with N = O(qd^2 ), n less than N + d, and m = 3N .

authors.name: Philippe Gaborit
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Correlations between Dynamical Dark Energy and Neutrino Parameters
papers.abstract: Recent Baryon Acoustic Oscillation (BAO) data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), fitted jointly with Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) and Type Ia Supernovae (SNe) data, favor dynamical dark energy (DDE) over the standard $\Lambda$CDM model. In this work, we investigate whether the mass and degeneracy of relic neutrinos are degenerate with DDE parameters and can also account for this statistical deviation from $\Lambda$CDM. Using a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis of a joint Planck CMB temperature, DESI BAO, and Pantheon+ dataset, we show a robust parameter degeneracy between the DDE equation of state and neutrino physics. We supplement this with a semi-analytical framework that recovers the numerical correlation, showing that the tight constraint on the CMB acoustic scale drives this degeneracy. Our results highlight the clear correlation between DDE and neutrino parameters, underscoring the critical need to jointly constrain the neutrino sector and the dark sector in next-generation cosmological surveys.

authors.name: WangZheng Zhang
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Ming-Chung Chu
authors.institution: Centre de physique des particules de Marseille

papers.title: A Multi-Domain Study on the Effectiveness of LLMs at Writing Property-Based Tests
papers.abstract: A property-based test (PBT) checks a property of a program on many generated inputs, but writing one takes a property, a generator of valid inputs, and an oracle. LLM-based PBT writers produce all three, yet they have been evaluated only on Python libraries. We study how two of them, Proptest-AI and Agentic-PBT, generalize to ten programs in five domains: deep learning libraries, databases, system software, compilers, and LLM serving engines. Most of these programs take text in their own language, such as queries, configurations, and programs. Agentic-PBT covers more branches than Proptest-AI on seven of the ten programs with Opus 5 and on all ten with GLM-5.3-Flash. Domain-specific fuzzers cover more of the compilers and of PostgreSQL and less of PyTorch than Agentic-PBT. We filed 180 bug reports, 44 of which duplicate reports that others filed after the models' knowledge cutoffs; maintainers have confirmed 65 of the others, in all five domains, and fixed 23. We draw lessons for building and evaluating such writers: low observability hurts them, and mature fuzzers paired with LLM-written properties could check that each feature behaves as documented.

authors.name: Marcelo d'Amorim
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Magnetic switchback development from the evolution of torsional Alfv\'en waves
papers.abstract: Magnetic switchbacks are mostly Alfv\'enic local deflections, or even reversals, of the ambient magnetic field of the solar wind. Despite intense research their origin remains unclear and is highly debated. Here we describe a new simulation study demonstrating how torsional Alfv\'en waves can evolve into switchbacks. We use surface rotational motions to launch torsional Alfv\'en waves into the super-radially expanding magnetic field of a coronal hole. The simulations demonstrate that in such an expanding wind, the waves initially steepen as they propagate while also inducing a cylindrical parallel plasma jet. A combination of shear from the jet and wave evolution under the constraint of approximate spherical polarisation ($|\mathbf{B}|\approx const.$) then leads to the formation of switchbacks in a ring configuration. We explore the 3D nature of the switchbacks, how and where they from, and present scalings for their peak deflection and parallel and perpendicular length scales. We also derive an expression for switchback deflection in the linear regime which we contrast against our results. The results are discussed in relation to recent observations and previous switchback formation studies.

authors.name: Etienne Pariat
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Multi-view Semantic-aware Resource Allocation for Edge AI
papers.abstract: Semantic communication is emerging as a pivotal paradigm to overcome wireless resource scarcity in 6G networks. This paper proposes a novel end-to-end framework for semantics-aware resource allocation in multi-user Edge AI. We extend the Opportunistic Information Bottleneck (OIB) to a multi-view setting, termed the Multi-view Gaussian Information Bottleneck (MGIB), by fusing complementary source views without variational approximation or network retraining. A resource allocation framework is then formulated for joint compression-level selection, transmission mode selection (i.e., the number of active sources per group), and PRB assignment. The problem is formulated as a Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP), solved efficiently via a proposed Lagrangian Relaxation (LR) algorithm, and benchmarked against the NP-hard optimal solution. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed LR scheme achieves near-optimal utility, and doubles PRB efficiency versus average allocation.

authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Concentration of Exponential Tilts Implies Curvature
papers.abstract: We show, under a smoothness assumption, that probability measures whose exponential tilts have a uniformly bounded variance are given by a strongly convex potential, up to a bounded perturbation, yielding a partial converse to the Bakry-\'Emery theorem combined with Holley-Stroock's perturbation principle. A stronger version enforcing uniform convexity of the potential is obtained by considering the low-temperature regime.

authors.name: Aziz Ben Nejma
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: High-speed laser speckle contrast imaging of the human retina
papers.abstract: We demonstrate real-time laser speckle contrast imaging of the human retina using a Phantom S980 streaming camera at $3840\times2160$ pixels, 8-bit depth, and 1000 frames per second, with a $988\,\mu\mathrm{s}$ exposure. We report four recordings of the peripapillary retina around the optic disc in the right eye of one healthy 25-year-old emmetropic man, acquired without pharmacological pupil dilation, using 852-nm diffuse Maxwellian illumination at an entering optical power of 5.0 mW. Each recording contained 4096 frames (4.10 s), and all 16384 frames in the reported recordings were retained. Open-source Holoflow software on an NVIDIA RTX 5090 computes $K=\sigma/\mu$ over $5\times5$ spatial pixels and nonoverlapping blocks of 16 frames, producing 62.5 contrast maps/s with 60-frame/s rendering and no additional averaging. The nominal raw-input throughput is 8.29 Gpixel/s. Main retinal arterial and venous branches and smaller peripapillary vessels were visualized. Variations during the cardiac cycle were visible in the principal retinal arteries and veins, as illustrated in the Supplementary Videos. Regional inverse-contrast traces show an arterial dicrotic notch and spontaneous venous pulsation. This single-volunteer demonstration establishes an operating point for high-throughput retinal speckle-contrast visualization. Physiological observations are descriptive; contrast is an instrument-dependent observable rather than a calibrated blood-flow velocity.
