papers.title: Simulation-Efficient Double-Flow Neural Posterior Estimation for Agent-Based Models
papers.abstract: Neural posterior estimation (NPE) enables Bayesian inference of the posterior parameter in agent-based models (ABMs) with intractable likelihoods, but simulating training data can be computationally expensive. We propose Double-Flow Neural Posterior Estimation (DF-NPE), which combines learned time-series summaries with two conditional normalizing flows for synthetic-data generation and posterior estimation. The framework supplements direct simulations with synthetic training pairs and supports both pooled and ordered training strategies. Experiments in two settings of the Brock-Hommes asset-pricing model show that DF-NPE can reduce direct simulations by 90 percent while achieving lower mean posterior discrepancies and runtime than standard NPE. Performance varies with the allocation of directly simulated and synthetic data and the training strategy. These results establish learned summary augmentation as a practical approach to reducing simulation costs for Bayesian posterior inference of parameters in ABMs.

papers.title: Of Chains and Gains: What Reinforcement Learning changes on Reasoning-based Image Quality Assessment
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has improved the performance of large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) on image quality assessment (IQA). Existing approaches often attribute these gains to improved reasoning before scoring, supported by increasingly plausible Chain-of-Thought (CoT). However, whether these gains exceed sampling effects and how they depend on explicit reasoning remain unclear. We rigorously investigate these questions through sampling-aware evaluation, controlled reasoning interventions, and shortcut experiments. We find that RL-trained models outperform base models under large-budget $\operatorname{max}_g@k$ evaluation, while improvements beyond averaging are concentrated in-distribution. RLVR produces chains that raise base-model performance when transplanted and improves scoring with the chain held fixed. Yet scoring becomes less dependent on the chain during inference, more clearly at 7B than at 32B. Steering the probed quality direction in thinking tokens also has little effect on scoring. Finally, RL can improve scoring accuracy by exploiting textual cues correlated with mean opinion scores (MOSs), which could inflate benchmark performance. Together, these findings show that RLVR raises quality scoring and produces more useful chains, but that better scoring does not imply a stronger reliance on explicit reasoning, while score-based rewards can also encourage reliance on quality-irrelevant shortcuts. We hope this preliminary study can enlighten more and more concrete reasoning schemes in IQA.

papers.title: VISTA: Active Exploration for Self-Improvement in Embodied Agents
papers.abstract: Agentic embodied intelligence plays a foundational role in open-ended, dynamic physical environments. Rather than treating policy learning as an end-to-end mapping from instructions to actions, recent studies reveal that embodied systems depend not only on pre-trained foundation models, but also on harness. Prior approaches largely treat rollouts as static logs for post-hoc reflection, producing harness updates without autonomously testing and refining them through subsequent embodied interaction. To address this challenge, we propose VISTA, a meta-agent framework that transforms post-hoc rollout reflection into active self-exploration for embodied harness improvement. Specifically, VISTA maintains a harness graph that records the lineage of proposed harnesses, which enables the meta-agent to retrieve prior hypotheses, build on effective mechanisms, and avoid repeatedly exploring failed directions. Each iteration begins from a retained harness version and its execution evidence. Rather than directly committing an update from these historical trajectories, the meta-agent actively explores in the environment. It autonomously generates new rollouts, probes execution failures and recovery behaviors, and iteratively modifies the harness based on the resulting evidence. The refined harness is then evaluated afresh and added to the harness graph. We evaluate VISTA on the LIBERO-Pro, RoboCasa, and RoboTwin benchmarks. Experimental results demonstrate that VISTA progressively improves task success and is more rollout-efficient than static reflection, achieving higher success rates with fewer simulator rollouts.

papers.title: Uniform Large Deviations, Barrier Identity and the N\'eel--Arrhenius Law for the One-Dimensional Stochastic Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert Equation
papers.abstract:
We study the one-dimensional stochastic Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation with a regularised, multiplicative, degenerate trace-class noise of strength sqrt(eps), the regularisation being Q_delta^{1/2} = (I + delta A^{beta/2})^{-1}, A = -d^2/dx^2, beta > 3/2, and determine the exponential rate of thermally induced magnetisation reversal.
  (i) Uniform large deviations at fixed delta: for every delta > 0 the solution satisfies a large deviation principle on C([0,T];H), with a good rate function, uniformly in the initial datum over a V-bounded set with compact H-closure; no non-degeneracy of the noise is assumed.
  (ii) Removal of the regularisation: as delta tends to 0 the noise tends to space-time white noise. With U_delta the state-space quasi-potential and U_0 that of the limiting control problem (Q_0^{1/2} = I), U_delta converges to U_0 in the Gamma-sense, and the barrier is delta-independent: the infimum of U_delta over the boundary of D equals that of U_0 and equals c_* times the infimum of the micromagnetic energy E over that boundary, c_* = 2 lambda_2/(lambda_1^2 + lambda_2^2), under two structural assumptions only and with no geometric or transversality input. Pointwise convergence fails, so the Gamma-limit is the sharp form of the statement.
  (iii) Neel-Arrhenius law: combining (i) and (ii) with the classical exit-time theorem, the escape time tau from D = {E < r} satisfies both levels of the law - for every fixed delta > 0, eps log E[tau] converges, uniformly on compact subsets of the initial set, to the barrier, and lim_{delta->0} lim_{eps->0} eps log E[tau] = c_* times the infimum of E over the boundary of D. The Arrhenius exponent is therefore stable under the regularisation of the noise and is determined by the micromagnetic energy alone.

papers.title: The Evolution and 'Chineseness' of Urban Screens in China: From Propaganda Posters to Smart City Interfaces
papers.abstract: Urban screens have become a global feature of the media city, yet their developmental paths are not universal. This paper argues that the evolution of urban screens in China constitutes a distinct paradigm of media urbanism, termed Chineseness, understood here not as cultural essence but as a relational, historically situated configuration of three linked elements: deep-rooted lineages of public communication; state-steered technological leapfrogging driven by industrial policy and mega-events; and a regulatory paradox that enables spectacular scale while tightening operational control. Drawing on a five-stage genealogy (1990-present), a chronology of representative screens, and five paradigmatic cases, the study shows how this configuration produces temporal-spatial compression, the coexistence of multiple technological generations, and privileges collective witnessing over device-centric interactivity. The paper contributes a documented genealogy of Chinese urban screens, develops temporal-spatial compression and collective witnessing as analytical tools for non-Western media ecologies, and positions Chineseness as a globally relevant alternative to market-led models of media architecture.

papers.intro:
Urban screens have become a defining feature of the global media city, but their paths of development are not universal. China offers a distinctive, accelerated trajectory. Rapid, state-led urbanisation and targeted industrial policy, exemplified by the ‘Hundreds of Cities, Thousands of Screens’ UHD initiative11 1 A national digital display initiative launched as a five-year plan (2019–2023), reissued in 2021 following pandemic disruptions, to promote ultra-high-definition (UHD) infrastructure and smart-city screen networks across China. Referred to hereafter as the UHD initiative., have supported a nationwide network of landmark displays and a domestic LED sector with a significant global share(Wang and Samuseva, 2023; Hu et al., 2015; Sanderson and Simons, 2014; Ye et al., 2018; COEMA LED Display Panel Committee, 2001; CCTV News, 2023). Despite this scale, academic discourse remains skewed toward Western cases and single-site studies in China, leaving the broader history and governance logics undertheorised (McQuire, 2006; Colangelo, 2015; Berry, 2013; Schielke and Ma, 2021). This paper addresses that gap by proposing Chineseness as a situated configuration that shapes the evolution of urban screens. This study argues that the evolution of urban screens in China forms a distinct paradigm of media urbanism, Chineseness, defined by three linked elements: lineages of public communication (from dazibao and open-air cinema to architectural illumination)(Huhtamo, 2009; Turnock, 2015; Berry, 2013); state-driven technological leapfrogging driven by industrial policy and mega-events(Butollo and Ten Brink, 2018; Lauermann, 2019); and a durable enable-and-constrain regime that scales spectacle while tightening day-to-day control. Using a five-stage genealogy (1990–present) and paradigmatic cases, this paper shows how this configuration yields temporal–spatial compression and privileges collective witnessing over individualized interactivity. This research contributes a compact genealogy, two operational concepts, and a specification of Chineseness as a globally relevant alternative to market-led models.

papers.title: Initialization Stability and Convergence of Projected Langevin Dynamics
papers.abstract: The entropic regularized optimal transport (EOT) plays a fundamental role in the computation of optimal transport. In \cite{CLP}, the authors proposed a gradient flow approach to EOT, and derived a projected Langevin diffusion that converges in distribution to the solution of EOT when initialized with a coupling between the two given marginals. In this paper, motivated by samplings of optimal couplings for EOT, we analyze the projected Langevin dynamics with arbitrary initial distribution, and prove that its long time behavior is the same as if it was initialized from a coupling.

papers.title: Does LeWorldModel Preserve Local Action Geometry?
papers.abstract: We examine how closely pretrained LeWorldModel (LeWM) reproduces the effects of small action changes. Using matched simulator and model responses, we measure action sensitivity with Gram matrices at three perturbation scales. Across nearly a thousand states from Reacher and OGBench Cube, the most sensitive action directions differ by median angles of about $36^\circ$ and $42^\circ$, respectively, at the smallest scale. Increasing the perturbation tenfold reduces median normalized Gram discrepancy by roughly 70\% on Reacher and 47\% on Cube. Geometry measured in pixels and embeddings varies more across scales than the chosen physical-state geometry. On held-out directions, environment Grams achieve median embedding response errors of 17\% and 28\%, compared with 26\% and 38\% for an isotropic reference with the same trace. LeWM's errors are higher at this scale. These findings support scale-specific evaluation of action sensitivity; its effect on control remains an open question.

papers.title: Near-Optimal List Replicability from Littlestone Dimension
papers.abstract:
We study the list replicability number in the realizable PAC learning framework and prove that every concept class $H$ over a countable domain with Littlestone dimension $d$ and dual VC dimension $v^*$ satisfies \[ \mathrm{LR}(H)\leq 2^{O(d\min\{\log d,v^*\})}. \] This matches the worst-case lower bound of $2^{\Omega(d)}$ up to a logarithmic factor in the exponent and exponentially improves the previous best upper bound $\mathrm{LR}(H)\le 2^{2^{O(d)}}$ of Bun, Livni, and Moran [FOCS 2020]. Unlike earlier bounds of $2^{O_\epsilon(d^2)}$ for fixed accuracy $\epsilon>0$ implied by the work of Ghazi, Golowich, Kumar, and Manurangsi [STOC 2021] and Lyu [STOC 2026], our bound is independent of $\epsilon$.
  The $2^{O(d\log d)}$ bound follows from a new inductive framework for bounding list replicability that builds on the recent notion of irreducibility from differentially private learning. The $2^{O(dv^*)}$ bound follows from a simple globally stable learner that takes the majority vote of multiple empirical risk minimizers, with stability established using tools from stable regularity.

papers.title: Flow Mesh: A Velocity-Regularized Flow Matching Framework for Stable Distributional Modeling of Physical Fields on Unstructured Meshes
papers.abstract: Thermal-fluid field distributions underpin the analysis and operation of energy infrastructure, from nuclear-reactor cooling channels to industrial heat exchangers, but resolving these distributions through computational fluid dynamics requires prohibitively large simulation ensembles. Their complex geometries also demand unstructured meshes that are poorly accommodated by generative models developed for regular grids. Here we introduce FlowMesh, a generative framework that combines permutation-invariant mesh encoding with deterministic latent flow matching and an l1 penalty on the learned transport velocity. FlowMesh generates full-field realizations directly on fixed unstructured meshes without auxiliary grid interpolation or a stochastic denoising chain. Across lid-driven-cavity, pressurized-water-reactor subchannel and heat-exchanger datasets, evaluated over six matched training seeds, FlowMesh achieves macro-averaged probability-density-function coverage of 91.7%-97.0%, exceeding an architecture-controlled latent diffusion model by $11.6$--$45.4$ percentage points. Latent-velocity regularization increases coverage by $3.8$ percentage points for reactor flows and 1.1 points for heat-exchanger flows, while reducing temperature-field Kullback--Leibler divergence by 1.7-2.4-fold. Each full-field realization requires 1.23 \pm 0.15 s, providing a 585--1902-fold wall-clock acceleration over computational fluid dynamics. FlowMesh therefore makes large-scale generative characterization of thermal-fluid states computationally feasible, providing a foundation for data-driven analysis and digital-twin development in fixed-geometry energy systems.

papers.title: Accretion Geometry and Variability in QS Telescopii from multi-epoch Observations
papers.abstract: We present phase-resolved photometry, spectroscopy, photopolarimetry, and circular spectropolarimetry of the polar QS Telescopii, obtained between 2017 and 2025 using the South African Astronomical Observatory (SAAO) 1.0-m and 1.9-m telescopes, the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS), Asteroid Terrestrial-impact Last Alert System (ATLAS) and the Southern African Large Telescope (SALT). From ground-based photometry, we report the first detection of quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in QS Tel, with timescales ranging between 2 and 11 minutes. This makes QS Tel one of only seven polars to show QPOs. The average spectra of QS Tel show broad and strong Balmer ($\rm H\delta$, $\rm H\gamma$, $\rm H\beta$ and $\rm H\alpha$) and He\textsc{ii} 4686 \AA\ emission lines, along with weaker emission from He\textsc{i} at (6678\,\AA, 5017\,\AA, 4921\,\AA, 4712\,\AA, 4471\,\AA, and 4387\,\AA) and the Bowen fluorescence complex C\textsc{iii}/N\textsc{iii} at 4650\,\AA. For the first time detailed Doppler tomography of the $\rm H\alpha$ and He\textsc{ii}\,4686\,\AA\, lines are presented which reveal emission from the irradiated face of the secondary star, the ballistic stream, the threading region and complex magnetically confined flows. The magnetically confined accretion stream splits into two distinct components coming from the same stream. One component appears near the threading region and the other component is seen along the high velocity in the magnetically confined accretion stream closer to the White Dwarf. Broad band photopolarimetry reveals circular polarisation reaching levels of $+8\%$, however more detailed circular spectropolarimetry shows polarisation ranging from $-10\%$ to $+25\%$, associated with two broad, phase-dependent cyclotron humps centred at $\sim$4800 \AA\ and $\sim$6300 \AA, consistent with a magnetic field strength of $\sim$53 MG.

papers.title: How Does Post-Training Shape LLM Value Preferences?
papers.abstract: During post-training, large language models (LLMs) learn value preferences from corpora that may contain imbalanced proportions of opinions associated with different demographic groups. Amplifying these imbalances may further underrepresent some groups' opinions. However, how opinion mixtures shape value preferences across post-training paths remains unclear. To answer this question, we conduct controlled experiments using post-training corpora with different opinion mixtures and five post-training paths based on SFT, DPO, and GRPO. We find that post-training amplifies opinion imbalances differently across post-training paths. Once value preferences are amplified, whether further post-training can remove them depends on both the post-training method and the opinion mixture in the corpus. More concerningly, a model's stability under interventions depends on whether further post-training changes its value preference. Moreover, these value preferences are transferred to student models even when distillation uses corpora with no explicit opinion questions. These findings suggest that both the opinion mixture in post-training corpora and the choice of post-training method should be considered when developing, evaluating, and reusing LLMs. Our code and data are available at https://github.com/ku-nlp/llm-value-preferences.

papers.title: HuGe: Scaling Humanoid Generalist Vision-Language-Action Models with Egocentric Experience
papers.abstract: Extending Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) to humanoid robots requires coordinated whole-body control and diverse demonstrations that are costly to collect in real-world scenarios. Although egocentric human demonstrations provide a complementary source of task experience, differences in visual embodiment and missing robot proprioception complicate transfer to humanoid policies. To address these challenges, we introduce HuGe, a family of Humanoid Generalist VLAs pre-trained on over 2,000 hours of egocentric human and robot data. Specifically, HuGe employs three existing representative VLA architectures to predict latent motion tokens for a pretrained whole-body controller, together with hand-control signals. Based on this, we introduce a three-stage training pipeline that combines egocentric pre-training, humanoid adaptation, and downstream fine-tuning. To facilitate transfer across embodiments, we construct pseudo-proprioceptive states through simulation playback during pre-training and modify arm appearance in egocentric observations through re-rendering during downstream fine-tuning. With this pipeline, HuGe achieves the state-of-the-art on simulation benchmark HumanoidArena. Furthermore, real-world experiments on the Unitree G1 indicate that augmenting robot demonstrations with visually adapted egocentric demonstrations significantly increases success on a pick-and-drop task.

papers.title: Synergizing Wireless Foundation Models and LLMs: A Multi-Task Framework for MA Systems
papers.abstract: While movable antennas (MAs) provide enhanced spatial flexibility through dynamic repositioning, they confront critical challenges in acquiring complete channel state information (CSI) and efficiently optimizing antenna positions. Encouragingly, wireless foundation models (WFMs) capture generalizable channel priors for high-quality CSI extrapolation, while large language models (LLMs) enable parameter-efficient, token-level optimization for wireless tasks. In this paper, we synergistically integrate a WFM and an LLM into a multi-task framework for MA systems. First, to address the mismatch between existing WFM pre-training and MA channel characteristics, we develop an MA-oriented ``ExtLWM'' based on the large wireless model (LWM) architecture. Second, we design a unified ExtLWM-Connector-LLM architecture that flexibly adapts to different MA configurations without structural redesign. Third, we reformulate discrete MA positioning as a sequential decision-making problem, where candidate positions are represented by numerical tokens and optimized using group relative policy optimization (GRPO) to exploit the serial generation capability of the LLM. Finally, a multi-stage training strategy is developed to maintain multi-task performance under limited training samples while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. Simulation results show that ExtLWM can produce high-quality channel embeddings while outperforming various benchmarks in CSI extrapolation. Meanwhile, the proposed LLM-based approach achieves a favorable trade-off between performance and computational complexity.

papers.title: Lifting $\tau$-exceptional sequences
papers.abstract: We study the behaviour of $\tau$-exceptional sequences under passage from a finite-dimensional algebra $\Lambda$ to a factor algebra $\Lambda/I$. Assuming that $\Lambda$ is $\tau$-tilting finite and that $I\subseteq \operatorname{rad}\Lambda$, we construct, for every $r$ less than or equal to the number of simple $\Lambda$-modules, an injective map from the $\tau$-exceptional sequences of length $r$ over $\Lambda/I$ to those over $\Lambda$. The construction is recursive and is based on lifting indecomposable $\tau$-rigid modules and comparing their associated $\tau$-perpendicular categories. At each stage, we construct a right exact functor between the relevant $\tau$-perpendicular categories which, after identifying them with module categories, is naturally isomorphic to extension of scalars along a quotient $\Gamma\to\Gamma/J$, where $J\subseteq \operatorname{rad}\Gamma$. These functors send each lifted term to an object in the additive closure of the corresponding original term. Finally, we conjecture connections with known bijections for representations of quivers over local algebras and for Nakayama algebras.

authors.name: Aslak B. Buan
authors.institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Positivity of simplicial volume and uniqueness for the twelve-vertex flag three-spheres
papers.abstract: We study the twelve-vertex flag triangulation $T_{12}$ of $S^3$ and the Davis $4$-manifold $M(T_{12})$ associated with it. We prove that $T_{12}$ is, up to isomorphism, the unique flag triangulation of $S^3$ with twelve vertices in which every edge is contained in a square; this proves Milizia's Conjecture~6.31. We also prove a general criterion for the tangent Euler class of a Davis $4$-manifold to be bounded, and we verify it for $T_{12}$ by means of an explicit symmetric form. Since the Euler class takes the value $256$ on the fundamental class of $M(T_{12})$, the duality between bounded cohomology and simplicial volume gives $\|M(T_{12})\|>0$. This answers Milizia's Question~1.7.

papers.title: Learning Direct Control from Optimization for Dynamic Target Tracking
papers.abstract: Dynamic target tracking requires a mobile robot to maintain target visibility while navigating obstacles with smooth, feasible controls. Online trajectory optimization explicitly encodes these objectives but requires repeated numerical solving, whereas waypoint-based neural policies separate geometric prediction from control execution. We introduce LECO, a framework that transfers tracking optimization into offline learning of a direct-control policy. LECO predicts control sequences and maps them to trajectories through a differentiable kinematic model, allowing trajectory-level objectives to directly guide control learning. A decaying expert-guidance curriculum initializes effective tracking behavior and progressively shifts learning toward these task objectives. At deployment, a predictive safety lock checks short-horizon obstacle clearance and invokes a classical planning and control fallback when the predicted motion is unsafe or the target prediction is invalid. Across three simulated obstacle densities, LECO reduces root-mean-square linear jerk by 14.1--31.2\% relative to the best competing method for this metric and achieves the highest tracking success rate, with per-cycle computation times of 4.25--5.63\,ms. Experiments on two robot platforms further demonstrate tracking through indoor narrow passages and outdoor forest environments. These results demonstrate that learning direct control from optimization enables smooth and robust dynamic target tracking.

papers.title: Ellipsoid Separation in Data-Dependent Time via Infimal Displacement Vectors
papers.abstract: The infimal displacement vector of the nonexpansive operator underlying the primal-dual hybrid gradient algorithm (PDHG) is known to encode useful information for infeasible optimization problems. In particular, for the ellipsoid separation problem (ESP), where the goal is to find a separating hyperplane between two collections of ellipsoids, the infimal displacement vector corresponding to an infeasible second-order cone program (SOCP) encodes a separating hyperplane. We show FISTA computes a sequence of approximations to the dual component of the infimal displacement vector and establish that a solution to the ESP can be obtained in $\mathcal{O}(\delta_{\mathcal{A}}^{-2})$ iterations. Here $\delta_{\mathcal{A}}$ denotes the distance between the convex hulls of the two ellipsoid collections.

papers.title: Financial Context-Rich Strategy for Actor-Critic based Agents: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Stock Trading
papers.abstract: In modern financial markets, more than 3/4th of the large volume trade is executed by algorithmic trading based on advanced trading strategies to attain higher precision and speed than traditional human traders. The conventional strategies focused on price-based indicators are inadequate in capturing the market dynamism arising from real-world events such as social sentiments, political instability, or sudden economic shifts. With the rise of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) and data availability, there is a requirement for more efficient algorithms that can incorporate these external factors in trading strategies. DRL has shown potential in simulating real-world scenarios and in simplifying complex decision-making since DRL agents can automate the trading process i.e. executing trades in a manner comparable to human traders. They have shown reliable performance since they can update their policies based on risk and quantitative factors. In this paper, we propose a DRL approach based on partial and deep-infusion of sentimental analysis. It features distinct policy designs of actor-critic-based agents: only policy optimization (A2C & PPO) and policy optimization along with Q-learning principles (DDPG, TD3 & SAC). Our findings reveal, that the agents based on policy optimization combined with Q-learning, significantly and consistently demonstrate improved performance upon sentiment deep-infusion in profit maximization as well as risk-averse trading.

papers.title: TeQCo: Temporal Quota Consistency for Training-Free Video Token Compression
papers.abstract: Video token compression must control both temporal coverage and task relevance, but sequential stages can conflict: a content-driven allocation stage may be overwritten by a global ranking that removes entire temporal positions. We identify this as an allocation conflict and propose TeQCo, a training-free framework that resolves it through temporal quota consistency. TeQCo allocates candidate capacity from first-order changes in normalized frame representations and aggregates all tokens within each frame into a compact candidate set. Candidates are then scored by prior-corrected task attention and selected within integer frame quotas inherited from the first-stage counts. Content variation determines temporal capacity; question relevance determines which candidates fill it. This design guarantees an exact token budget and a per-frame coverage floor whenever feasible. On the 2,700-question Video-MME benchmark with Qwen3-VL-8B, TeQCo achieves 68.52% accuracy at 510 ms TTFT, a 32.9% TTFT reduction with a 1.00-percentage-point accuracy decrease.

authors.name: Xianglong Wang
authors.institution: Wuhan University of Science and Technology

papers.title: ContextTom: Training-Free Video VLM Acceleration with Early Spatial Context
papers.abstract: Video vision-language models process thousands of visual tokens before producing an answer. Reducing these tokens early saves computation, but also determines which evidence reaches the language model. We introduce ContextTom, a training-free framework that separates the timing of temporal and spatial compression. Its central idea is to compress time before vision encoding while preserving spatial coverage through early multimodal processing. A fixed-budget temporal partition produces representative medoid anchors, supplemented with bounded local detail from neighboring observations. The anchors retain their complete spatial grids through a short decoder prefix, allowing question tokens to access the visual evidence and completing Qwen3-VL's multi-level visual injections. ContextTom then selects spatial representatives using query attention and agreement across visual feature levels, and continues directly from their computed states. This schedule reduces vision computation and later decoder workload while reusing the prefix. On Qwen3-VL-8B, ContextTom achieves 76.22% accuracy on Video-MME Short with a mean time-to-first-token (TTFT) of 123.5 ms, yielding a 2.77x speedup over full-input inference. It matches the full-input accuracy of 72.20% on EgoSchema with a 2.82x speedup and achieves a 5.54x speedup on LongVideoBench at 59.24% accuracy.

authors.name: Xianglong Wang
authors.institution: Wuhan University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Weekend Crypto Volatility and Monday Market Risk
papers.abstract: Cryptocurrencies trade continuously while major traditional markets close over the weekend. We examine whether weekend cryptocurrency volatility predicts Monday variance in equity, commodity and fixed-income markets. Using daily range-based variance measures for Bitcoin, Ether, XRP, the S&P 500, gold and a US Treasury ETF over 2017-2026, we augment heterogeneous autoregressive models with a common weekend cryptocurrency factor. Predictive content is weak before 2024 but significant thereafter. In the post-2024 sample, a one-standard-deviation increase in the factor is associated with 27-54% higher fitted Monday variance. Adding the factor reduces out-of-sample QLIKE losses by 11-22%, although statistical evidence varies across markets. Friday cryptocurrency volatility does not reproduce the result, and coin-specific variation adds no significant predictive information beyond the common factor. An endogenous procedure estimates a break in late 2023, during growing anticipation of US spot-Bitcoin ETF approval. However, ETF-flow interactions provide no evidence of amplification through greater measured Monday flow activity, leaving the mechanism unresolved. The findings suggest that calendar-specific volatility measures reveal predictive information that aggregate connectedness measures may obscure.

papers.title: From Writing Advice to Manuscript Governance: A Constrained-Transformation Framework for Academic Revision
papers.abstract: Academic revision presents a governance problem when legitimate writing objectives conflict. Writing-process and social-science research show that revision is recursive and that wording carries epistemic and disciplinary commitments. Those literatures identify important constraints but do not settle which objective should prevail when concision, outlet form or stylistic variation conflicts with evidence and claim boundaries. This paper models revision as an admissibility problem under ordered constraints. Task-relative invariants, contextual constraints and mutable presentation choices define the admissible space; a claim-preservation contract links evidence and judgement to an authorised claim boundary. Four governance propositions specify preservation, precedence, context and sufficiency. The Academic Writing Filter implements the model by screening candidate revisions; it is not a universal definition or classifier of good academic writing. The contribution is a technology-independent mechanism for changing presentation without silently changing the research argument.

papers.title: On the Doppler Effect in Static Materials: Vortices and Black, White and Worm-Hole Like Wave Trajectories
papers.abstract: We demonstrate the Doppler effect in a static material. The effect is achieved with a network of thin waveguides whose lengths depend on the direction of travel, chosen to simulate the compression and expansion of the wave experienced by a source travelling with velocity $v$. Each edge of length $\ell$ becomes a pair of waveguides of lengths $\ell/(1\mp v/c)$, one for each direction of travel. On a lattice this gives the field pattern of a moving source. To demonstrate the effect, we design a vortex, an analogue black hole and wormhole.

papers.title: Position Matters More Than Channel: Talking a Language Model Out of a Correct Answer
papers.abstract: Language models now answer questions alongside other claims: a note in the system prompt, a message from another agent, their own earlier answer. We ask what it takes to talk a model out of an answer it gets right on its own, and separate three factors that earlier studies vary together: where the advice sits in the prompt, who is said to have written it, and what the model has already written. On Qwen3.5-27B and four-option MMLU-Pro items, with the rest of the advice held fixed in each comparison, we find three things. First, position matters far more than the API channel, in opposite directions for a bare claim and an argument: a bare "the answer is X" does most harm just before the model answers, while the same claim with a false rationale does most harm before the question, where it raises error on items the model otherwise almost never misses from 1% to 67%; moving the claim between the system message and the user message at the same position changes error by a few points. Second, attributing the note to an authority rather than to another participant, and phrasing it assertively, each raise error by 10-27 points, while the two authorities we tested differ by under two. Third, replaying a correct worked answer before the advice protects it whether the text is shown as the model's own or as someone else's, and the same replay keeps wrong answers from being corrected by a bare correct note. The position result replicates under an independently written prompt. Code, items and all result tables are released at https://github.com/coolkillercat/safety.

papers.title: High-efficiency solid-state electrochemical thermal switching through phonon engineering of 2D materials
papers.abstract: Reversible solid-state thermal switches with large thermal contrasts remain rare, yet are essential for advanced thermal management. Using universal machine-learned interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) and density functional theory (DFT), we screen 57 transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), spanning the 1T and 2H phases with Li and Mg intercalation. Among the candidates, Li$_a$ZrS$_2$ combines exceptional thermal conductivity switching with low heat capacity. Lithiation to Li$_{0.125}$ZrS$_2$ reduces the cross-plane thermal conductivity from approximately 3.7 to 0.05 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$. The switching behaviour exceeds that of previously reported solid-state electrochemical thermal switches. Device-level modelling further demonstrates the potential for waste-heat recovery, with a pulsed system capturing 86\% of the energy recovered by an ideal switch. We attribute the switching behaviour to substantial softening of the Zr--Zr framework, with the mean force constant decreasing from approximately 4.2 to 1.2 eV $\mathrm{\mathring{A}}^{-2}$, alongside enhanced scattering of heat-carrying acoustic phonons. These findings establish electrochemical intercalation as a promising route to engineering thermal transport in layered materials.

papers.title: Useful Diversity or Hallucinated Variety? Persona-Conditioned Synthetic Query Generation for E-Commerce Search
papers.abstract: Synthetic supervision can bootstrap semantic parsers in new search domains, but prompt-induced diversity is useful only when generations are faithful to the structured intent. We explore this for cold-start e-commerce search: 118,098 synthetic pairs produced by 6 LLMs with 9 persona-conditioned prompt families on a 47-field UK automotive schema, against 1,214 human-annotated and 15,304 production queries. We show that the IPIP personality bundle improves parser F1 in all four matched contrasts (Holm-corrected $p<.001$), and all three bundles have a positive main effect over the complete $2^3$ grid. Syntax conditioning is the axis that moves generations towards real traffic. It also induces lexical diversity. Alignment sKL, the divergence between von Mises-Fisher distributions fitted to synthetic and human-annotated queries, is an unlabelled proxy for parser F1 ($\rho=-0.917$ against human queries written for simulated shopper scenarios, lower is closer). An LLM committee, checked against a blinded author pass, triages the 927 queries missed by every parser and labels 37% as hallucinated. Dropped constraints dominate. The four syntax-bearing families have the largest hallucinated shares, 38 to 42%, while IPIP alone has the lowest at 28%.

papers.title: Emission line stacking on cosmological scales: equivalence to two-point statistics and modelling of the observational effects
papers.abstract: Emission line stacking measurement for cosmological line intensity mapping (LIM) contains not only the average emission line profile of the stacked sources, but usually also the clustering signal, due to the limited angular resolution of the observations. We provide an explicit derivation of the equivalence between the emission line stacking, the two-point cross-correlation function in configuration space and the power spectrum in Fourier space, similar to the case between the angular stacking signal for the kinematic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect and the angular power spectrum in harmonic space (arXiv:2512.14625, arXiv:2605.15947). Using the quadratic estimator formalism, we establish that the emission line stacking signal measurement is equivalent to a quadratic estimator for the cross-correlation function. The formalism allows for the explicit modelling of the stacked signal, including the clustering statistics as well as observational effects such as the galaxy selection function and the LIM survey footprint. In particular, using mock HI intensity mapping data, we show that we can accurately model the effects of foreground removal on the stacked signal. The correlation function estimator provides significant speed-up for the stacking measurement and enables modelling of the signal and its covariance for large LIM datasets with MeerKLASS and future SKAO.

authors.name: Jos\'e Luis Bernal
authors.institution: Fundación Instituto para la Mejora de la Asistencia Sanitaria

papers.title: AdaDexTrack: Dynamic Modulation for Adaptive and Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation Tracking
papers.abstract: Language is a natural way to command robots, but converting a single instruction into a long-horizon, contact-rich hand-object interaction remains challenging: synthesized references are noisy, human-to-robot retargeting introduces embodiment bias, and fixed-reference tracking lets small errors snowball. We address this with AdaDexTrack, a modulator-in-the-loop framework for language-conditioned manipulation tracking. A distilled generalist tracker serves as the skill carrier, while a tightly aligned modulator performs three feedback corrections: reference modulation (continual adjustment of what to track), object-latent modulation (online adaptation of the object representation to recruit suitable skills), and positional-target modulation (small state-dependent refinements for execution). The tracker is learned via large-scale specialist to generalist distillation on a corpus of language-conditioned hand-object trajectories; the modulator is trained with RL under the same task objective, ensuring tight coupling. Across large-scale evaluations, AdaDexTrack consistently outperforms prior SOTA on unseen-trajectory and unseen-object sets in both average tracking error and success rate, demonstrating robustness and generalization. We further show zero-shot sim-to-real transfer on real hardware, where adding the modulator yields substantial gains over a tracker-only variant. AdaDexTrack reframes language-conditioned dexterous manipulation as modulated tracking, replacing the open-loop, fixed-reference tracking with in-loop modulation that adjusts the reference, object latent, and positional target, yielding drift-resistant execution from noisy text references.

authors.name: Qianwei Han
authors.institution: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

papers.title: HumanoidNDM: Closing the Training-Deployment Gap of Motion Tracking via Humanoid Neural Dynamics Model
papers.abstract: Humanoid robots have recently achieved remarkable success in motion tracking. However, during real-world deployment, robots inevitably encounter dynamics gaps arising from either extra physical disturbances or inaccurate simulation modeling, resulting in a significant training-deployment gap. Therefore, effectively leveraging real-world data to fine-tune policies represents the crucial last mile for robust deployment. To bridge this gap, we propose HumanoidNDM, an online fine-tuning framework for humanoid motion tracking driven by a real-world-trained neural dynamics model. First, in the data collection stage, we introduce a low-frequency reference perturbation method with an adaptive intensity mechanism, balancing deployment feasibility and exploration efficiency. Second, for the model training stage, we train a robust history-based, proprioceptive neural dynamics model in Euclidean space by incorporating differentiable forward kinematics, eliminating the reliance on costly motion capture systems. Finally, in the policy fine-tuning stage, we directly fine-tune the policy via backpropagated model gradients, achieving high data efficiency. Through physical validation on the Unitree G1 robot, we demonstrate that HumanoidNDM enables rapid real-world adaptation to various perturbations, representing the first online, MoCap-free fine-tuning framework for humanoid tracking policies.

papers.title: Bug Severity Classification with Fine-Tuned Open LLMs: A Paired Comparison with TF-IDF and CodeBERT Baselines on Eclipse Reports
papers.abstract: Open large language models (LLMs) small enough to run on a laptop are an obvious candidate for automatic bug severity prediction. We measure what they add over cheaper classifiers on one task: assigning one of four Bugzilla severity levels (Critical, Major, Minor, Trivial) to Eclipse bug reports. From a public dump of 361,006 unique Eclipse reports we draw a class-balanced sample of 20,000 rows and compare eleven configurations of nine model types: six TF-IDF classifiers, a fine-tuned CodeBERT encoder, and Llama 3 8B and Qwen 2.5 7B, each run zero-shot and after QLoRA fine-tuning. All eleven are scored on the same 2,000 held-out reports, with bootstrap intervals and McNemar tests. The zero-shot runs reach macro-F1 0.305 and 0.321, below every TF-IDF model (0.430-0.489). The fine-tuned runs reach 0.526 and 0.485, but the zero-shot and fine-tuned setups also differ in checkpoint, serving runtime and decoding, so this gap cannot be credited to fine-tuning alone. Fine-tuned Llama 3 shows no detectable difference from CodeBERT (0.518; difference +0.007, 95% CI -0.017 to +0.032), and fine-tuned Qwen 2.5 is below it on macro-F1. The models differ more by class than in aggregate: fine-tuned Llama 3 finds 36% of Critical reports, Qwen 2.5 finds 69% but only 21% of Minor ones. The dump repeats 60,000 rows, and 8% of the test reports duplicate a training report; removing them lowers TF-IDF scores by up to 0.031 and leaves the LLMs almost unchanged. We release split identifiers, per-report predictions and the analysis script at https://github.com/tbayan/bug_finetuning_llm_artifacts, together with CyberTriage, a tool that serves the fine-tuned classifier locally.

papers.title: Almost global existence for quadratic Schr\"odinger equations in two dimensions
papers.abstract: We study the two-dimensional quadratic Schr\"odinger equation $(i\partial_t+\Delta)u=\lambda_1u^2+\lambda_2\overline u^{\,2}$ with initial data of size $\varepsilon$ in a weighted $H^2$ space. We prove almost global existence, with a lifespan of at least $\exp(c/\varepsilon)$ and decay at the optimal linear dispersive rate $t^{-1}$. Our proof is based on the space--time resonance method introduced by Germain, Masmoudi, and Shatah. The main new ingredient is a Besov-type profile norm $\mathcal Z$, which allows us to close the bootstrap argument without controlling the global second spatial momentof the free profile, thereby avoiding the substantial time-dependent losses arising from direct second-moment estimates.

papers.title: From Speech Tokens to Stolen Voices: Attacker-Chosen-Text Speaker Impersonation via Representation Inversion
papers.abstract: Speech interaction systems have gradually evolved from traditional cascaded systems that use text as intermediate information to end-to-end speech language models that directly process speech representations. In some applications, the speech frontend runs on the user's device and sends speech representations to a remote server for inference, while the original audio remains local. However, these representations may still contain speaker identity information. If an attacker obtains them, it may use this information to imitate the user's voice, threatening their voice privacy. To investigate this risk, we propose \stia, a Speech Token Inversion Attack that generates speech with attacker-specified text in a victim's voice using a single short leaked representation, without access to the original audio or its transcript. Specifically, \stia converts discrete, continuous, or mixed speech representations into conditioning sequences and trains a conditional flow-matching speech generation model using pairs of different utterances from the same speaker in public speech datasets. The model combines speaker characteristics contained in the leaked representation with the specified text to generate speech in the victim's voice. Experiments show that, with a Moshi representation leak corresponding to 3 seconds of speech, \stia achieves an average CAM++ speaker cosine similarity of 0.78 and a target-text word error rate of 3.80\%. These results show that speech frontend representations reveal reusable speaker identity information and highlight the need to consider privacy risks when designing speech frontend representation methods.

papers.title: Sharp effective Nullstellensatz for projective Cohen-Macaulay schemes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove a sharp effective Nullstellensatz for projective Cohen-Macaulay schemes of pure dimension over an arbitrary field. In particular, if L is an ample line bundle on a smooth complex projective variety X and J is a coherent ideal sheaf with J\otimes L globally generated, then (\sqrt{J})^{\deg_L X}\subseteq J. This establishes the sharp bound conjectured by Ein and Lazarsfeld. More generally, we obtain sharp bounds in terms of mixed intersection numbers and a refinement involving products of powers of prime ideal sheaves associated to the irreducible components of the base locus. We also establish sharp radical power bounds for homogeneous ideals in finitely generated standard graded Cohen-Macaulay domains, extending Koll\'ar's sharp effective Nullstellensatz for polynomial rings. The proofs combine purity and cycle preservation for leading Ext sheaves with Koszul evaluation maps compatible with successive divisor cuts.

papers.title: Space Electric and Magnetic Sensor (SEAMS) Phase I: A Pathfinder Mission for Low-Frequency Radio Astronomy
papers.abstract: In this paper, the Space Electric and Magnetic Sensor (SEAMS), a space based mission dedicated to very low frequency (below 16 MHz) observations of the radio sky is proposed. The SEAMS mission is planned in two phases. The first phase is specifically designed for radio frequency interference (RFI) mapping from the low earth orbit (LEO). The low frequency region of the electromagnetic spectrum is filled with a variety of artificial as well as natural RFI. Previous observations have confirmed the effect of this terrestrial interference on astronomical observations. Thus, a map of terrestrial RFI as observed from space would give valuable information to groups working in the low-frequency regime. For the first phase, the payload will be mounted on to the fourth stage of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)'s third generation Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV), which will stay in LEO for several weeks. The payload consists of a pair of orthogonal active monopoles, a simple baseband sampling receiver optimized for recording power spectra from each antenna. The design also aims to detect strong signals of astronomical origin despite RFI. In the second phase, we intend to send a more sophisticated space payload to orbit the moon and subsequently land on its surface.

papers.title: On the asymptotic behaviour of $\alpha$-divergence generalized posteriors
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the solutions to the unconstrained generalized variational inference problem regularized by an $\alpha$-divergence. Under mild conditions, the minimizer is explicit up to a scalar normalizing constant, and we show that it admits a rescaling under which it converges in $L^1$ to a fixed non-Gaussian law, at a concentration scale around the empirical loss minimizer that departs from the typical $n^{-1/2}$ in the classical Bernstein--von Mises theorem. For $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and $d<2/(1-\alpha)$ the limit is a Student-$t$ distribution and the posterior width shrinks faster than the sampling error of the empirical minimizer. Conversely, for $\alpha>1$ the limiting distribution is a compactly supported Pearson type-II distribution, and the posterior width shrinks more slowly than the sampling error. The KL divergence ($\alpha=1$) is the unique member of the $\alpha$-divergence family whose posterior width matches the sampling scale and whose limit is Gaussian. We discuss the implications of these qualitatively different regimes for the frequentist coverage of credible regions, and a toy example on intercept-only logistic regression illustrates the theoretical claims.

papers.title: Understanding Python Linters through a Comprehensive and Systematic Empirical Study
papers.abstract: Code linters, tools that automatically detect code issues, help developers accelerate development and improve code quality by identifying errors early. Unlike previous studies that focused mainly on single linters or informal comparisons, this paper presents the first large-scale empirical study of five widely used Python linters: Ruff, Pylint, Flake8, Mypy and Black, through four key user concerns: linting rule checks, speed, configuration methods, and linter preferences. We analyze 1,551 linting rules, categorize them into five types, and construct rule mappings, finding that more than 40% are shared between multiple linters, with Ruff and Pylint together covering over 80% of all rules. Pylint has the most rules in the first two categories, and Ruff leads in the last three. Next, we measure their running times on 1,000 GitHub projects under three setups (single-rule, default, all-rules), finding a consistent speed ranking from fastest to slowest: Ruff, Mypy, Flake8, Black, and Pylint. Ruff is extremely fast, with runtimes typically within one second. Then, we summarize four configuration methods and four types of configuration options from 443 available options across the five linters. While all linters support the four configuration methods, they differ in project configuration formats and flexibility in their configuration options. Finally, an analysis of 3,094 GitHub projects using the five linters reveals that over 50% use multiple linters, share strong consensus on option selections and rule suppressions, but exhibit project-specific variations in enabled-rule configurations. Our findings provide actionable insights for linter users and establish a benchmark dataset and taxonomy to support future research, such as cross-linter rule mapping, performance modeling, and automated configuration.

papers.title: Towards a Unified Framework of Optimal Input-Side Dimensional Configuration for Deep CTR Prediction
papers.abstract: Deep click-through rate (CTR) prediction has achieved substantial success through increasingly expressive feature interaction architectures. However, predictive performance also depends on how input-side information is configured before interaction modeling. Existing studies have shown that selecting informative samples, features, or embedding units can improve prediction accuracy. Nevertheless, they primarily optimize these selection mechanisms independently along a single input-side dimension, overlooking their shared basic form and the inherent dependencies across input levels, thereby limiting the effectiveness of input-side dimensional configuration. To address this issue, we propose OptIDC, a unified framework for Optimal Input-side Dimensional Configuration in deep CTR prediction. OptIDC jointly learns sample, feature, and embedding-unit level configurations within a unified framework by integrating their corresponding selection mechanisms. To explicitly coordinate selection decisions across different levels, OptIDC further introduces a selection-weighted Optimal Transport mechanism that aligns coarse- and fine-grained selections via transport over finite measures, thereby alleviating cross-level selection conflicts while preserving the semantics of each input level. Moreover, OptIDC is model-agnostic and can be seamlessly integrated into existing CTR models. Extensive experiments on four real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate that OptIDC consistently achieves higher AUC than existing input-side selection methods, validating the effectiveness of unified input-side dimensional configuration.

authors.name: Chaohua Yang
authors.institution: Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University

papers.title: From Representations to Computational Trajectories: Intrinsic Fingerprinting for Large Language Model Provenance Verification
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are valuable digital assets, yet their weights can be easily modified after unauthorized acquisition, making model provenance difficult to verify. Model fingerprinting provides a promising solution for model ownership protection without modifying the model or embedding ownership information. However, parameter-based fingerprints can be sensitive to model transformations, limiting their robustness, while representation-based fingerprints may assign high similarity to unrelated models, limiting their uniqueness. To address these limitations, we propose TrFP, an intrinsic fingerprinting method based on computational trajectories. Instead of comparing model parameters or representations, TrFP captures how representations evolve across network depth and constructs compact fingerprints using permutation-invariant trajectory descriptors. Experiments across multiple LLM families show that TrFP reliably distinguishes related and unrelated models. It also remains robust under fine-tuning, pruning, quantization, model merging, parameter permutation, and adaptive attacks, while requiring less than 0.3 MiB of fingerprint storage. Overall, TrFP provides stronger provenance discrimination than several existing state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating the effectiveness of computational trajectories for reliable LLM provenance verification.

papers.title: A Computationally Efficient Non-Interpolation Virtual Trellis Approach for Mammogram Gradient-based Patterns Analysis
papers.abstract: Feature analysis is a crucial step in medical image analysis, particularly in breast cancer classification. Traditional image analysis methods often struggle with optimal patterns along the diagonal axis, computational efficiency and feature buffer storage. Different classical operators require high-efficiency hardware for the complex operations, such as image convolution and gradient analysis, which are used for processing complex machine learning models for training and test operations. Here, in this research, we introduce a non-interpolation virtual trellis-based (NVHT) operator that utilizes a filter kernel over the same square image without transformation to a hexagonal trellis. This proposed method is very efficient in reducing computational and storage costs. The proposed operator is used for improved feature extraction efficiency and accuracy in disease classification. This method outperforms conventional approaches by leveraging a hexagonal pixel representation while maintaining high sensitivity in different directions with less storage.

papers.title: Elmendorf's Theorem for $\infty$-categories
papers.abstract: Motivated by Teleman's study of gauged topological quantum field theories, our main result is an analog of Elmendorf's theorem in the setting of simplicial group actions on $\infty$-categories. In particular, we prove that if $G$ is a simplicial group, there is a Quillen equivalence between the homotopy category of $\infty$-categories with $G$-action and the homotopy category of $\infty$-category-valued presheaves on the orbit category of $G$. We also show an analog of Whitehead's theorem in this setting.

papers.title: Non-discrete complex hyperbolic $(p_1,p_2,p_3;p_4)$-triangle groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study complex hyperbolic triangle groups of type $(p_1,p_2,p_3;p_4)$ with $3\le p_1\le p_2\le p_3\le p_4\le \infty$. We show that if the element $R_1R_2R_3$ is elliptic, then the group is either non-discrete or it belongs to a short list of known discrete groups.

papers.title: Periodic measures for time-inhomogeneous stochastic differential equations driven by multiplicative $\alpha$-stable processes: Existence, uniqueness and numerical approximation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the periodic measures within the context of time-inhomogeneous Markov processes. By extending the Hairer--Mattingly method to the time-inhomogeneous case, we first establish the existence, uniqueness and exponential ergodicity of periodic measures for general time-periodic Markov processes. These results are subsequently applied to time-inhomogeneous stochastic differential equations under the assumption that the drift is weakly dissipative and locally Lipschitz. We further employ the truncated Euler--Maruyama scheme to study numerical approximations of the periodic measures and derive the convergence rate between the exact and discrete periodic measures. These numerical results are new even in the time-homogeneous case under the assumptions considered in this paper.

papers.title: Polarization-resolved haze in transparent wood - towards wooden glass
papers.abstract: Transparent wood (TW) composites possess residual haze that limits image clarity despite their high light transmission, yet the physical origin of this scattering has not been established. Here, polarization-resolved measurements reveal a pronounced polarization dependence of scattering by a wood-polymer composite with improved refractive index matching. Polarization- and spectrally-resolved haze as low as 21% (40-45% at 550 nm for unpolarized light) with transmittance of approximately 92% for polarization perpendicular to the fibers was detected. It is found that the low-haze spectrum closely follows an inverse-square relation over the 400-800 nm range, well described by a weak-index-contrast Rayleigh-Gans-Debye (RGD) model invoking subwavelength birefringent heterogeneities within the cell wall. This physical mechanism was previously obscured by haze-limiting strong scattering from debonding gaps or refraction at the lumen-cell wall interface. Scanning electron diffraction independently reveals spatially distinct domains with markedly different cellulose diffraction responses within the infiltrated cell walls. The observed polarization-dependent refractive-index mismatch is attributed to inherent cellulose birefringence. Time-resolved measurements further support nearly scattering-free quasi-ballistic transport of the sampled transmitted light. It is demonstrated that selecting only a preferential polarization markedly improves image visibility through TW without further material modification. These findings connect polarization-dependent haze to the internal structure of transparent wood and identify ways to engineer a refractive-index match in hierarchical anisotropic composites towards glass-like clarity.

papers.title: Data-Driven LQR with Uncertainty Refinement and Domain Randomization---Part~I: Certified Uncertainty Refinement
papers.abstract: Learning controllers from trajectories corrupted by process and measurement noise is difficult when the system matrices and the noise covariances are unknown: noisy regressors bias least squares, and model uncertainty cannot be quantified without the noise covariance, which can only be estimated from residuals of the uncertain model. This paper, Part~I of a two-part study, resolves both obstacles with a finite-sample framework that certifies, and iteratively refines, uncertainty sets for the model, the noise in the collected data, and the noise covariance. A closed-loop parametrization based on delayed instrumental variables (IVs) removes the bias and assigns to every candidate model exactly one noise sequence that reproduces the data. Learning this noise breaks the circular dependence: the noise sequences give the covariance estimate directly, models whose noise violates the prior or the statistical certificates are discarded, and the surviving models yield a tighter covariance certificate. Several delayed instruments further tighten the model set and give a certified test of data consistency. We prove finite-sample containment of the true model, noise, and covariance, recursive nesting, and convergence at the IV rate. Part~II uses these certificates for domain-randomized linear quadratic regulator synthesis.

papers.title: Data-Driven LQR with Uncertainty Refinement and Domain Randomization---Part~II: Fisher-Majorized Certified Policy Iteration
papers.abstract: Building on the uncertainty description developed in Part~I, this paper introduces a Fisher-majorized domain-randomized generalized policy iteration framework for data-driven linear quadratic regulator (LQR) synthesis. At each iteration, partial Bellman evaluation over a fixed batch of uncertainty realizations produces a structured Sylvester policy-improvement step. A residual-weighted Fisher curvature controls the policy-induced variation in the stationary covariance and converts the Sylvester model into a certified upper bound on the cost change, thereby guaranteeing descent for every accepted step. A check-and-correct mechanism then certifies stability over the entire uncertainty support, rather than only over the sampled realizations. Consequently, every iterate is robustly stabilizing and monotonically decreases the fixed-batch objective. The Fisher truncation and stability correction become inactive after finitely many times. The objective gap then contracts linearly to a floor determined by the dispersion of the realization-wise Riccati targets and by measurement noise. In the absence of measurement noise, this floor vanishes when the realization-wise targets coincide.

papers.title: Core-Collapse Supernovae from Single and Binary-Stripped Massive Stars - I. Explodability and Nucleosynthesis
papers.abstract: Binary interaction can substantially alter massive-star evolution and pre-supernova structure, changing core-collapse outcomes and nucleosynthetic yields. We compare explodability and nucleosynthesis in 66 non-rotating, solar-metallicity single-star and binary-stripped progenitors spanning zero-age main-sequence (ZAMS) masses of $11$-$45\,{\rm M}_\odot$, using the spherically symmetric PUSH framework and nucleosynthesis post-processing. Both populations explode up to $22\,{\rm M}_\odot$, with binary stripping altering explodability at higher ZAMS masses. Successful explosions span similar energies ($\sim$0.4-1.3$\,$B) and remnant masses ($\sim$1.4-2.0$\,{\rm M}_\odot$). The largest nucleosynthetic differences occur at low ZAMS masses, particularly for material undergoing explosive O and Si burning. The $^{56}$Ni yields and iron-group abundances broadly agree with observations of core-collapse supernovae and the metal-poor star HD 84937. When compared with calculations using time-dependent mixing-length theory and a two-parameter explodability criterion for the same progenitors, our results reveal substantial differences in explodability, with agreement on successful explosions for only 5 cases across all three approaches. Nevertheless, elemental yield patterns can remain broadly similar for models that explode successfully across treatments. Salpeter initial-mass-function-weighted yields of most elements differ by $\sim$20% between populations, with K enhanced by a factor of $\sim$3.4 in the binary-stripped population, driven by increased production in the lowest-mass progenitors. Binary-stripped models show closer agreement with empirical core-collapse S, K, and Ca abundance ratios relative to Mg inferred from APOGEE, while Na remains overproduced in both populations. Together, our results highlight the need to account for binarity when interpreting supernova abundance patterns.

authors.name: C. Fr\"ohlich
authors.institution: University of Texas Institute for Geophysics

papers.title: The Ising lattice gas and the surface diffusion of CO on Cu(001) at finite coverage
papers.abstract: The memory equation of the coherent intermediate scattering function (ISF), derived previously for lattice gases, is applied to the Ising lattice gas under Kawasaki dynamics. The ISF follows the decay of a density wave of adparticles, a superposition of exponential relaxation modes: the decay starts at a rate fixed by a sum rule and is then slowed by a memory. The static structure factor and the effective hop rate are obtained in closed form, exactly along a one-dimensional channel; with the sum rule they give a single exponential, a lower bound on the ISF. Exact relaxation spectra show that this single exponential, built from equilibrium quantities alone, reproduces the correlation time only at weak coupling; only there can a measured dephasing rate be read through the statics. For strong attraction the slow dissolution of clusters lengthens the correlation time up to ninefold, whereas a repulsive layer relaxes nearly as a single mode at its structure peak. The dephasing rate, fitted over a time window where it is nearly constant, approaches the slowest relaxation rate, not the initial one; the sum rule reaches the data only through the area beneath the normalized decay, which defines the correlation time. For CO/Cu(001), the lattice gas reproduces the dephasing rates measured along two crystal directions and requires a nearest-neighbour repulsion of at least $35$--$50$~meV, whatever the jump rates; the measured rate is then close to the inverse correlation time, and the memory is predicted to grow with coverage.

papers.title: Pooling interval-monitored step-stress accelerated life tests for reliability prediction: A failure-rate-based meta-analysis for the proportional hazards family
papers.abstract: Reliability qualification often relies on several step-stress accelerated life tests conducted in separate campaigns, laboratories, or test rigs, each with its own stress profile, sample size, and inspection schedule, and with units inspected only periodically so that only failure counts between inspections are recorded. Existing meta-analysis methods combine several step-stress experiments but require exactly observed failure times. Methods for interval-inspected step-stress data, on the other hand, have been developed only for a single experiment. This paper develops a failure-rate-based meta-analysis framework for multiple interval-inspected step-stress experiments within the proportional hazards family, linking the experiments through a common underlying lifetime model and a log-linear stress-life relationship. Maximum likelihood estimators and confidence intervals are derived for the model parameters and for engineering quantities of interest at normal operating conditions, including mission reliability, mean time to failure, and lifetime quantiles such as the 0.10 quantile (B10 life). For the LED data, pooling the two tests reduced the RMSE of the estimated reliability at 5 hours by about 20% and that of the 0.10 quantile by about 66%, compared with the better single test. A misspecification study shows that the median is robust to the choice of lifetime distribution (relative bias below 6%), whereas tail quantiles can have a relative bias of up to 34% that does not vanish as the sample size increases, which is critical for warranty decisions. The methodology is illustrated with simulated data and with two step-stress tests of light-emitting diodes.

papers.title: Freeze What Is Settled, Cache What Is Smooth: Spatial Freezing Keeps Step Caching in Its Low-Error Regime
papers.abstract: Instruction-based image editors built on diffusion transformers run tens of denoising steps. Training-free acceleration either reuses features across steps (step caching) or stops computing the regions an edit leaves untouched (region freezing), and the two have been combined before. We ask how a high speed-up target should be split between them. On Qwen-Image-2.1, freezing does more than remove tokens: it lowers the cost of every step, so the step cache can reach the same overall speed-up with a conservative threshold that keeps its error small. A per-step cost model fitted on development runs predicts held-out latency with a median error of 4.0% and reproduces the speed ceilings of the region methods we re-implemented (2.73$\times$ predicted vs. 2.70$\times$ measured for RegionE). Driving frozen tokens to the model's one-step $x_0$ estimate beats returning them to the reference image on every development sample, and in 90% of measured cases the composed error stays below the sum of the two individual errors. The resulting method, FreezePlan, keeps five full steps and gives the rest of the budget to TaylorSeer. On a pre-registered test split it runs 5.05$\times$ faster end to end at 29.8 dB PSNR to the original output, with no significant drop in a VLM judge score; TaylorSeer at 5.02$\times$ reaches 23.5 dB. The curve extends to 5.99$\times$ at 28.0 dB. Swapping in the region selectors of prior methods under our schedule lowers median PSNR by only 0.5--0.6 dB, which places the gain in the schedule and budget split rather than in the selector.

papers.title: Poisson closures and Poisson $A$-algebras
papers.abstract: We study the interaction between the Lie and Poisson subalgebras of a Poisson algebra. Given a Lie subalgebra $U$ of the underlying Lie algebra $\mathcal P_L$, we consider the Poisson subalgebra generated by $U$, called its {Poisson closure}, and investigate when Lie-theoretic properties such as nilpotency and solvability are preserved under this construction. We also study the stability under Poisson closure of several distinguished Lie subalgebras, including maximal nilpotent and solvable subalgebras, Engel and Cartan subalgebras and the derived algebra. As an application, we investigate Poisson $A$-algebras, defined by the condition that every nilpotent subalgebra is a zero algebra. In the finite-dimensional case, we obtain structural results relating Poisson $A$-algebras to Lie $A$-algebras and to the associative structure of the algebra.

authors.name: Salvatore Siciliano
authors.institution: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro

papers.title: A-GE: Privacy-Preserving Age Assurance via Fine-Grained Motion
papers.abstract: Age assurance faces a fundamental privacy dilemma: meaningful assurance typically requires revealing identity or other sensitive information, whereas privacy-preserving alternatives often provide little assurance. Existing approaches either disclose sensitive information directly or shift the disclosure and trust requirement to an identity provider, while self-declared age provides little meaningful assurance. Thus, a fundamental gap remains between establishing an age property and revealing information beyond what is necessary to establish that property. We present \textit{A-GE} (Age-Grounded Evidence), a privacy-preserving age assurance system that derives age-related evidence from fine-grained motion captured by commodity inertial measurement units (IMUs). A-GE exploits subtle motion dynamics that we hypothesize reflect underlying neuromuscular and physiological processes during ordinary device interaction. It requires neither identity information nor government identification and operates across available sensor sampling rates, including the approximately 60~Hz limit of web-based sensing, with configurable minimum-age thresholds ranging from 14 to 21 years. We evaluate A-GE on more than 600 participants, with separate participant-disjoint cohorts for model development and final evaluation. At a 16-year minimum-age threshold, A-GE achieves up to 93.8\% accuracy with a comparable F1 score across the evaluated configurations. We further demonstrate client-side deployment on Android, iOS, and the web, and examine unintended attribute inference and residual privacy risks, characterizing both the privacy benefits and limitations of deriving age evidence from commodity motion.

papers.title: Optimal Connectivity of Random Boolean Networks for Reservoir Computing
papers.abstract: Reservoir computing shifts the focus from training a system's internal dynamics to designing dynamics that expose useful computational capabilities via linear projection. We study random Boolean networks as reservoirs: cellular automata with random recurrent wiring and a random rule at each node. Their main parameter is the connectivity, the mean number of edges into a node. Without input, these networks pass from ordered to chaotic dynamics at a connectivity of 2, where their dynamics are expected to facilitate computation. How the input is connected is itself a design factor: if the input shares the network's edges, the connectivity sets both the dynamics and how many nodes receive the input, the input fan-out. We set the input fan-out separately and compare 7,560 reservoir designs, all combinations of six design factors, each built as many random reservoirs, on recalling the majority or the parity of a few input bits seen several steps earlier. The optimal connectivity falls from 2.5 to 1.75-2 as more nodes receive the input, but hardly depends on the task or on the other design factors, except self-loops, which connect a node to itself and raise the optimal connectivity. A measure computed from the reservoir states without a trained readout peaks at a connectivity that also falls with the fan-out and rises with self-loops, but does not replace training a readout. Reservoirs of one design vary widely, so a design should be judged by its typical reservoir.

papers.title: False-Alarm Improvements and Detection Trade-Offs in QML Intrusion Detection: A Secondary Analysis of the Kaissar Corpus
papers.abstract: Published results in quantum machine learning for intrusion detection (QML-IDS) require joint interpretation of false-positive rate (FPR), attack true-positive rate (TPR), and evaluation provenance. We reconstruct operating points in the 25-entry frame selected by Kaissar and colleagues: 21 included articles, 20 identified documentary families, substantive methodological material consulted for 15, and 24 descriptive points from five. In one test-labelled comparison, a quantum support vector machine reduces FPR from 6.875% for random forest to 3.329%, while TPR decreases from 93.955% to 93.682%; both rates improve against three other comparators. In another study, a complete benign row identifies FPR as 12/6000 (0.200%), despite incomplete attack-side allocation that requires additional assumptions for TPR. Normalized matrices identify detection ranges rather than a unique aggregate rate. A uniform provenance rule separates training-described and test-adjusted results from six conditional illustrations whose independence remains unverified. The contribution is a reproducible interpretation of favorable comparisons and detection trade-offs, without converting descriptive results or hypothetical calculations into operational guarantees.

papers.title: Approximate Controllability of Neutral Integro-Differential Inclusions Associated with Hemivariational Inequalities in Banach Spaces with Uniformly Convex Dual
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the approximate controllability of neutral integro-differential inclusions driven by hemivariational inequalities with nonlocal inclusion conditions in a Banach space $\mathbb{V}$ whose dual $\mathbb{V}^*$ is uniformly convex, using resolvent operator theory. We first establish an equivalence between the original problem and an associated differential inclusion involving the Clarke subdifferential. Under suitable assumptions, we then prove the existence of mild solutions corresponding to admissible controls in $\mathrm{L}^2(I,\mathbb{U})$. A key contribution of this work lies in the analysis of the control construction in Banach spaces, where the duality mapping $\mathcal{J} = \partial\big(\tfrac{1}{2}\|\cdot\|_{\mathbb{V}}^2\big)$ is generally nonlinear, in contrast to the Hilbert space setting, while such nonlinearity has been viewed as a technical obstruction in earlier studies. Based on this framework, we prove approximate controllability of the original system by relating it to the controllability of the associated linearized inclusion and constructing appropriate controls involving the duality mapping. Finally, we present applications to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

papers.title: Optimal Control of the 2D Boussinesq Equations with Finite Codimension Constraints
papers.abstract: We study an optimal control problem (OCP) governed by the two-dimensional (2D) Boussinesq equations, where the right-hand sides of the velocity and temperature equations are projected onto the corresponding tangent spaces of the manifolds $\mathcal{M}_1:=\{y\in\mathbb{H}:\|y\|_{\mathbb{H}}=1\}$ and $\mathcal{M}_2:=\{\theta\in H:\|\theta\|_H=1\}$, respectively.
