papers.title: Zeros of Melnikov functions for periodically perturbed Hamiltonian systems with random coefficients
papers.abstract: Introducing a probabilistic perspective on a classical theme within the study of chaotic dynamics, we investigate the zeros of the Melnikov distance function associated to a periodically perturbed Hamiltonian system when the perturbation has random coefficients. We provide asymptotic estimates (as the period of the perturbation becomes large or small) for the average number of zeros and for the probability of no zeros.

papers.title: The $\rm{v}$-number of $t$-closed neighborhood ideals
papers.abstract: We give a combinatorial characterization of the $\rm{v}$-number of a $t$-closed neighborhood ideal associated to a graph $G$, and investigate its relation with other invariants such as the $t$-domination number and the smallest size of a ball of radius $t$ in the graph $G$. We present several new cases where it is satisfied that the $\rm{v}$-number is bounded above by the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity. We analyze the behavior of the $\rm{v}$-number of a $t$-closed neighborhood ideal with respect to the parameter $t$. Lastly, we compute explicit formulas for the $\rm{v}$-number in the case of paths, cycles, and caterpillars, and analyze the case of Hamming graphs.

papers.title: Counting transversals in Latin squares over groups of even order
papers.abstract: The number of transversals in a Latin square $L(G)$ whose rows and columns are indexed by a finite group $G$ has been determined computationally for all $G$ of order at most $23$ and for $C_{25}$. However, computation of the number of transversals of $L(G)$ has until now been considered intractable for all non-cyclic groups $G$ of order $32$. We show, for a group $G$ containing an order $2$ normal subgroup $N$, that the image of a transversal in $L(G)$ under the quotient mapping from $G$ to $G/N$ is a $2$-plex in $L(G/N)$. We then derive linear algebraic conditions that determine the number of transversals in $L(G)$ whose image under the quotient mapping is a given $2$-plex in $L(G/N)$. This allows us to count transversals in $L(G)$ by examining all $2$-plexes in $L(G/N)$. Although we can simplify the counting of $2$-plexes in $L(G/N)$ by taking advantage of their symmetry group, the linear algebraic conditions can vary over a symmetry class of $2$-plexes. However, in the case that $G$ takes the splitting form $C_2 \times H$, the linear algebraic conditions become invariant over each symmetry class and so the counting of transversals in $L(C_2 \times H)$ reduces to counting the $2$-plexes in $L(H)$ under the action of their symmetry group. We illustrate the power of these techniques by computing the exact number of transversals in $L(C_2^5)$.

papers.title: Self-thresholding angular-radial models of extremal dependence
papers.abstract: Assessing compound risks requires a model for routine and extreme joint behaviour together, and a principled answer to where the joint tail begins. We propose the self-thresholding angular-radial (STAR) model: after marginal standardization, the radius given the angle follows a spliced distribution, with a flexible body below an angle-dependent threshold curve and a generalized Pareto tail above it. The threshold curve is estimated with all other parameters, so its uncertainty propagates to every summary, and the joint density is in closed form because the splice normalizes in one dimension for every angle. The tail scale function is the reciprocal gauge of the implied limit set, and the coefficient of extremal association is an explicit parameter, so a prior with atoms at tail independence and at the asymptotic dependence boundary yields posterior probabilities of the dependence class. At that boundary the copula of the model is asymptotically dependent, while its margins and joint tail are both lighter than exponential by a factor inversely proportional to the level. Simulations show accurate recovery of finite-level dependence summaries within and beyond the model class, and the slow separation of asymptotic dependence from strong asymptotic independence that the theory predicts. For warm-season daily maxima of fine particulate matter and ozone at a Beijing station, the pair is asymptotically independent with posterior probability 0.96 and both pollutants exceed their 0.9 quantiles on about two and a half days per season; the model gives summaries comparable to those of existing approaches without requiring the arbitrary choice of a threshold. The construction extends to d dimensions through pairwise deficits of the gauge, illustrated by adding coarse particulate matter as a third pollutant.

authors.name: Dani Gamerman
authors.institution: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro

papers.title: Learning-Accelerated Joint AP/RIS Optimization for Low-Latency Indoor mmWave XR Networks
papers.abstract: This paper studies a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted indoor architecture for extended reality (XR) applications, where multiple access points (APs) simultaneously serve multiple users over a shared frequency channel under a centralized AP controller. We formulate a non-convex sum-rate maximization problem with coupled AP precoders and RIS phase shifts, and develop a centralized alternating optimization (AO) framework for joint design. We rigorously prove that the proposed AO guarantees monotonic improvement of the sum rate that converges to a coordinate-wise stationary point, despite the non-convexity of the resulting subproblems. Although AO provides reliable performance, its iterative nature limits real-time applicability as the system dimension grows. To overcome this limitation, we propose a supervised learning-assisted approach that leverages AO-generated solutions to significantly accelerate convergence. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves near-optimal performance with substantially fewer AO iterations, which makes it well-suited for latency-critical RIS-assisted XR deployments.

authors.institution: King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals

papers.title: On the types of quasiperiodic potentials and level surfaces of quasiperiodic functions
papers.abstract: We examine the similarities and differences between two types of quasiperiodic functions: those obtained by restricting smooth periodic functions in $\mathbb{R}^N$ to lower-dimensional subspaces $\mathbb{R}^n \subset \mathbb{R}^N$, and those that arise as physical fields or potentials in quasicrystalline structures. Our analysis reveals that functions in these two classes share a number of common features while also exhibiting significant differences. As a key tool for investigating both classes of functions, we employ the Novikov problem - specifically, the problem of describing the global geometry of the level sets of quasiperiodic functions.

papers.title: The kernel mean embedding of a random probability distribution and its principal components
papers.abstract: Given a random probability distribution \(F\), whose realizations are defined on \(\mathbb R^d\), and a kernel \(k\), our aim is to analyze the properties of the kernel mean embedding, \(\mu_F\), of \(F\) as a random element of the corresponding reproducing kernel Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\). This establishes a rigorous framework in which kernel statistical techniques for distributional data can be stated both in the sample and population settings and, thus, the asymptotic properties of sample procedures can be properly established. As an illustration of this approach we focus on the principal components of \(F\). We obtain a general convergence result and the explicit expression of the spectral decomposition for the uncentered covariance operator of a normal probability distribution with a Gaussian distributed expectation. The performance of this kernel principal components procedure is illustrated with simulations and the analysis of the intensity distribution in synthetic aperture radar images.

papers.title: Automated screening of Parkinson's Disease using Smooth Pursuit Eye Movements
papers.abstract: Smooth pursuit eye movements are frequently altered in Parkinson's disease, but previous studies have relied mainly on conventional parameters that describe the relationship between gaze and target. This study investigates whether complexity and nonlinear dynamics measures of the gaze position sequences can support the automatic screening of Parkinson's disease. Gaze position sequences were recorded with a video eye tracker in 41 participants with early Parkinson's disease and 47 healthy controls during 12 smooth pursuit tasks. Four experimental frameworks and four embedding delay strategies were compared. The selected experimental setting combined baseline wander removal with a fixed embedding delay. After feature selection, a support vector machine was trained for each task and axis and their outputs were combined in a mixture of experts. The pipeline was developed in 70 participants and evaluated on an external test set of 18 participants. On the external test set, the pipeline obtained an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.86. The most informative features described less persistent and more irregular gaze position sequences in Parkinson's disease, mainly along the horizontal axis. These results support complexity and nonlinear dynamics measures of smooth pursuit as candidate markers for Parkinson's disease screening, pending validation in larger independent cohorts.

papers.title: Novel or Not? PatEx-Gym: Agentic Prior-Art Search for Novelty Assessment in Patent Examination
papers.abstract: Patent examination is a challenging real-world task that requires agents to discover sparse prior art, iteratively refine queries, inspect technical evidence, and produce novelty assessments documented in Office Actions (OAs) across heterogeneous scientific and technical domains. However, existing benchmarks largely focus on static and limited candidate sets, leaving the full search--reasoning--assessment process underexplored. We present PatEx-Gym, the first framework for developing and evaluating agents for patent examination, which integrates three components. First, PatEx-Bench provides 1K realistic examination tasks, two large-scale retrieval corpora containing over 1M patents and 52K scientific papers, and a harness runtime supporting iterative search, document visits, reasoning, and OA generation. Second, we introduce PASS, an annotation-free Prior-Art Agentic Search Trajectory Synthesis framework. Specifically, it exploits document visits as implicit relevance signals and evidence-acquisition anchors to model intra-turn query behavior, inter-turn search progression, and trajectory-level evidence and outcome quality, yielding PatEx-SynData. Third, we train PatEx-Agent at the 4B scale via supervised fine-tuning on the curated trajectories, establishing a lightweight baseline. Extensive experiments show that final decision accuracy alone does not fully reflect examination quality, while prior-art discovery remains difficult even for strong frontier models. Our PatEx-Agent achieves competitive performance against substantially larger general-purpose agents. These results show that training on PatEx-SynData enables a compact 4B model to serve as a competitive baseline for prior-art search and patent examination. We view patent examination as a demanding testbed for agentic search and deep research agents.

authors.name: Min Yang
authors.institution: Southwest University of Science and Technology

papers.title: The $C_p$ conjecture of Muckenhoupt
papers.abstract: We give an affirmative answer to Muckenhoupt's $C_p$ conjecture: for $1<p<\infty$, the $C_p$ condition is necessary and sufficient for the weighted $L^p(w)$ norm inequality relating the Hilbert transform and the Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator. We also show that the $C_p$ condition is necessary and sufficient for the weighted Fefferman--Stein inequality.

papers.title: Analysis of Biomarkers from Visual Explorations in Individuals Suspected to Be in the Prodromal Phase of Parkinson's Disease
papers.abstract: Identifying prodromal Parkinson's Disease is a precondition for any future treatment that modifies the course of the disease, since such therapies would ideally act on the initial pathogenic events, early enough to delay the clinical onset of the disease rather than only slow its progression. In this work, a visual exploration model is retrained on an expanded corpus. Without any further training or threshold recalibration, it is then tested on an enriched cohort of patients with high risk of being in the prodromal phase of Parkinson's Disease, testing whether the learned signal follows a continuum of disease rather than only separating patients from controls. The resulting score distribution is analysed as an external evaluation of the hypothesis that the oculomotor signature targeted by the model is already partly present before clinical diagnosis. With every subject scored on data not used to train the model, the scores are ordered as controls < high-risk patients < Parkinson's Disease, with 42% of the high-risk patients exceeding the decision threshold. A SHAP decomposition of the scores into classifiers and gaze features shows that high scores in this cohort are driven mainly by reduced saccadic excursion, fewer fixations and longer fixations, the hypokinetic oculomotor profile that characterises Parkinson's Disease. The model score is also compared against the prodromal markers used for recruitment. The score is not correlated with hyposmia, constipation, depression or REM sleep behaviour disorder; these results, interpreted in the context of the selection induced by the recruitment criteria, are discussed as evidence that within the high-risk cohort the score is largely not explained by the available ancillary clinical variables. The results suggest that the visual biomarkers analysed are a complementary indicator to identify patients at risk of being in the prodromal stage.

papers.title: Beyond Vision-Language Models: Visual-Semantic Affect Graphs for Emotion Recognition in Artworks
papers.abstract: Emotion recognition in artworks remains challenging because affective meaning is often subjective, implicit, and shaped by relationships between visual form and semantic associations. While vision-language models provide strong multimodal representations, direct image-to-emotion prediction may overlook explicit relations among formal, semantic, and affective cues that support emotional interpretation. This paper proposes Visual-Semantic Affect Graphs (VSAG), a graph-based framework that represents artworks through interpretable feature nodes, including color, brushstroke, composition, light-shadow, line quality, and extracted visual entities. The graph learns feature-emotion associations for dominant emotion prediction, with valence-arousal structure modeled through an optional hierarchical auxiliary affect module. We evaluate VSAG and VSAG-TopK against direct VLM inference using Qwen3-VL and InternVL3.5 on EmoArt-5k. Results show that direct VLMs provide useful but modest baselines, while graph-based models improve dominant emotion prediction. In particular, the hierarchical valence-arousal variant of VSAG achieves the best overall performance, improving accuracy, macro-F1, and weighted-F1 over both direct VLM inference and the emotion-only VSAG baseline. Per-class results indicate that graph-based models and VLMs capture partly complementary signals, while valence-arousal structure is most useful when integrated as a coarse-to-fine affect hierarchy rather than as a simple post-hoc correction. These findings suggest that explicit visual-semantic structure can support both prediction and interpretation in artwork emotion recognition.

papers.title: From Language to Drives: A Multimodal Framework for Aligning Autonomous Robots with Human Purposes
papers.abstract: This work explores a multimodal approach to the alignment of the behavior of open-ended learning autonomous robots with human purposes through the use of large language models as cultural enablers. While autonomous robots can generate their own skills and goals through interaction with the environment, they often lack mechanisms to ensure that these remain relevant and aligned to those of human users. The proposed approach makes use of the general and cultural knowledge contained in LLMs and VLMs to establish a multimodal interactive alignment process in which human purposes, expressed in natural language, are transformed into motivational components of a robot architecture in the form of robot missions and drives that guide the behavior of the robot. The system is structured into three layers for semantic alignment, mission generation, and drive modeling. This design enables a bidirectional interaction loop: human inputs define high-level purposes, robots expand them into executable missions making use of multimodal information relayed by LLMs and VLMs, and feedback maintains alignment with human intent. Experiments in simulation and with a physical robot demonstrate that the process produces valid missions and behaviors, supporting effective human-agent alignment in interactive scenarios with autonomous robots.

papers.title: Third harmonic generation in the transition metal trichalcogenides
papers.abstract: The transition metal trichalcogenides (TMTs) are an interesting class of layered 2D materials that have strong anisotropic electrical and optical properties. We report on the polarization-dependent nonlinear optical response of exfoliated crystals at the third harmonic using non-resonant excitation with a 1560 nm femtosecond laser. All members of the TMT crystal family explored (ZrS3, HfS3, TiS3, and NbS3) display large anisotropy in their polarized third harmonic generation signal, with anisotropy ratios as large as chi_11/chi_22 ~ 6.5. From the expected nonlinear dependence of these monoclinic and triclinic crystals we extract the relative nonlinear susceptibility coefficients. We find that the anisotropy ratio is largest for ZrS3 and decreases across the family, a trend we associate with the proximity of the third harmonic energy to the strongly b-polarized absorption edge of each material. NbS3, the only triclinic crystal, displays a pronounced anisotropy in thick flakes that is strongly reduced in the thinnest flakes, which we attribute to a partial relaxation of the Peierls-type Nb-Nb dimerization that underlies the triclinic distortion. The large anisotropic nonlinear response in this crystal family sets it apart from other 2D materials and makes it particularly attractive for further investigation.

papers.title: U-NeXt: General-purpose event detection for neonatal EEG
papers.abstract: We developed U-NeXt, a general framework for neonatal electroencephalography (EEG) event detection based on semantic segmentation. Its convolutional encoder-decoder directly segments individual channels using long input segments to preserve temporal context. A shared architecture and training framework were developed using low-voltage interval, artefact, and seizure datasets containing 51, 98, and 278 neonates, respectively, comprising over 11,000 hours of EEG and 82,000 annotated events. Performance was compared with task-specific ConvNeXt classifiers. For seizure detection, we also evaluated U-NeXt+, trained on an expanded dataset. Both U-NeXt variants and the ConvNeXt baseline were evaluated on two independent held-out seizure datasets, Helsinki and Cork, comprising 130 neonates, with recordings annotated by three experts. U-NeXt improved detection across all three event types, with particular gains in sensitivity for short events. U-NeXt+ achieved Matthews correlation coefficients of 0.862 and 0.891 on Helsinki and Cork, respectively, and improved hourly seizure burden correlations by 30-40% relative to ConvNeXt. U-NeXt+ met the criterion for expert-level performance on both datasets (p < 0.001). In separate computational benchmarks, U-NeXt reduced batch inference time relative to ConvNeXt by 254-fold on a central processing unit and 200-fold on a graphics processing unit. A common segmentation framework improves detection across diverse neonatal EEG event types while substantially reducing inference time. Accurate seizure burden estimates and performance comparable to expert reviewers support its potential use in continuous monitoring and clinical decision support.

papers.title: Omni-representations of Leibniz conformal algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notion of an omni-representation of a Leibniz conformal algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ on a $\mathbb{C}[\partial]$-module $M$ as a Leibniz conformal algebra homomorphism from $\mathfrak{g}$ to the conformal omni-Lie algebra $\mathfrak{gc}(M)\oplus M$. We show that the right $\lambda$-action of a representation induces a Maurer--Cartan element. When $M$ is a free $\mathbb{C}[\partial]$-module of finite rank, it also defines, via the conformal dual $M_c^*$, a $1$-cocycle with values in $M_c^*\otimes M\cong\mathfrak{gc}(M)$. Consequently, every such representation gives rise to an omni-representation on $M_c^*\otimes M$. We characterize omni-representations with values in the graph of a conformal embedding tensor. Finally, we introduce the omni-cohomology theory of Leibniz conformal algebras and establish the relation between omni-cohomology groups and the usual cohomology groups.

papers.title: Follow the Regularized Leader Does Not Converge in Constrained Optimization
papers.abstract: Follow the regularized leader (FTRL) is a foundational algorithm in online learning whose regret properties have been extensively studied for decades. However, in stark contrast to mirror descent---and gradient descent in particular---the convergence of FTRL to first-order stationary points in constrained nonconvex optimization was not well understood. In this paper, we show that continuous-time FTRL can fail to converge even asymptotically in infinitely smooth constrained optimization problems: its Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) gap can remain bounded away from zero indefinitely. This is especially surprising in light of the fact that continuous-time FTRL guarantees a monotonic improvement of the objective value. As a result, we establish that non-convergent behavior of no-regret dynamics---which besets general variational inequality problems---can occur even in potential systems. From a technical standpoint, our construction relies on an infinitely differentiable function where the gradient flow dynamics exhibit decelerating oscillations without ever converging pointwise, which we in turn embed into higher-dimensional FTRL dynamics that sustain a perpetually large KKT gap. We complement our negative result by showing that FTRL with Euclidean regularization does converge when the objective function is analytic. This shows that the analytic property plays a more fundamental role for FTRL than for gradient flow: it governs not only pointwise convergence, but convergence to first-order stationarity itself.

authors.name: Ioannis Panageas
authors.institution: Athena Research and Innovation Center In Information Communication & Knowledge Technologies

papers.title: Exploring the Tractability Frontier of Hylland-Zeckhauser Models
papers.abstract:
The Hylland-Zeckhauser (HZ) mechanism provides a market-based approach to one-sided matching, making efficient equilibrium computation central to its implementation. Bi-valued utilities admit a strongly polynomial-time algorithm [VY], whereas with four values per buyer, the problem is PPAD-hard under inverse polynomial approximation [CCPY]. To understand the tractability boundary, we study two extensions of the bi-valued case: a third linear utility value and separable concave utilities with two common marginal slopes.
  For every fixed rational $a\in(0,1)$, we prove that computing a normalized additive $\varepsilon_{*}(a)/N$-equilibrium in an $N$-buyer HZ market is PPAD-hard for some constant $\varepsilon_{*}(a)>0$, even when all utilities belong to the same prescribed set $\{0,a,1\}$. This resolves the main question left open by [VY, CCPY]: whether three utility values already suffice for PPAD-hardness. Using the same market gadgets, we show that hardness at a specified constant accuracy on the recognizable family generated by our construction is equivalent to the PCP-for-PPAD conjecture. Consequently, assuming that conjecture, general markets over $\{0,a,1\}$ admit no PTAS unless $\mathrm{PPAD}\subseteq\mathrm{P}$.
  For the concave extension, we compute an exact equilibrium in polynomial time with two marginal slopes common across goods for each buyer and arbitrary rational buyer--good breakpoints. The algorithm selects a cheapest utility-maximizing bundle for each buyer. With three common marginal slopes, suitable breakpoints encode the three valued linear case, yielding PPAD-hardness.
  Thus, our paper identifies two thresholds separating tractable and intractable cases of HZ models with utility functions specified by utility values or marginal slopes. In both cases, the tractability threshold lies between two and three.

authors.name: Ioannis Panageas
authors.institution: Athena Research and Innovation Center In Information Communication & Knowledge Technologies

papers.title: Online Continual Learning in Edge-Cloud Applications
papers.abstract: Deployed machine learning models in real-world IoT and edge/cloud systems face a critical reliability bottleneck: the requirement for online adaptation to non-stationary data streams while operating without access to the full original training dataset. Performance is severely degraded when models encounter Out-of-Distribution (OOD) inputs or suffer from catastrophic forgetting. Addressing these challenges requires adaptation mechanisms capable of learning from evolving data streams while preserving previously acquired knowledge. This paper proposes an edge-cloud methodology for integrating Continual Learning (CL) with Out-of-Distribution (OOD) Detection and Concept Drift Detection in IoT applications. The methodology incorporates ODIN and ECDD as alternative mechanisms for identifying informative samples for annotation and triggering rehearsal-based model updates. Experimental results across automotive, healthcare, and agricultural datasets demonstrate the applicability of the proposed methodology and its potential to support model adaptation while mitigating catastrophic forgetting.

papers.title: Making the Telemetry Pipeline Measurable: An Edge IoT Testbed and Dataset for End-to-End Latency, Provenance, and Energy-Aware Benchmarking
papers.abstract: Edge-centric IoT systems are increasingly evaluated through sensor values or platform features, yet the telemetry pipeline itself, the sequence of sensing, serialization, message mediation, ingestion, and persistence, is rarely released as a measurable object. This limits reproducible benchmarking of timeliness, provenance, and operational cost, especially in early-stage IoT design where real deployments and high-quality open data are often unavailable. I present a measurement-first edge IoT testbed and dataset that elevate timeliness, provenance, and energy to first-class telemetry dimensions. The testbed operationalizes a role-based event-driven architecture with explicit Source-Broker-Aggregator responsibilities and a schema-governed TelemetryMessage envelope (Avro) that embeds correlation identifiers and a uniform, cross-role vocabulary of stage-level timestamps. To trace mediation effects, I extend an MQTT broker (Eclipse Mosquitto) with a plugin that annotates messages with high-precision ingress/egress timestamps. I release the dataset in a dual representation: (i) replayable raw events as compressed Avro streams and (ii) analysis-ready long-format Parquet tables partitioned for efficient query and benchmarking, generated by a deterministic raw-to-tabular transformation pipeline. The contribution is an integrated engineering artifact and dataset built from established components. The demonstration describes one deployment through latency summaries, measurement-context distributions, and energy aggregates; it does not establish a new attribution method or a controlled performance benchmark. By co-releasing heterogeneous telemetry with pipeline timing and energy signals in both replayable and queryable forms, the artifact provides a basis for reproducible exploratory analysis and subsequent benchmarking studies.

papers.title: PastaLean: Deterministic transpilation from Python to Lean for Verification
papers.abstract: We present PastaLean, an extensible system for deterministic translation from Python to Lean via the Abstract Syntax Tree of Python. This allows for verification of Python code, especially auxiliary code used by AI. Every program is translated into a provable twin written in the form Lean's verification tooling can reason about, and a runnable twin that gives a fast and correct computation support. We also introduce our Type Inference engine TypeInfer which provides static typing support for untyped Python code. Our tool provides coverage of more than 92\% for LeetCode and HumanEval\textsuperscript{+} and more than 98\% for LiveCodeBench ground truth Python files. Further, at least 97\% of each dataset's (numerical) test cases pass, with 100\% on HumanEval\textsuperscript{+} and LiveCodeBench. The TypeInfer engine is the best-scoring tool on the TypeEvalPy static leaderboard, and on a repository-level TypyBench benchmark it scores above every competing repository-level inference tool.

papers.title: Learning Discriminative Prototypes via Boundary Repulsion MixUp for Object Re-Identification
papers.abstract: Object re-identification requires embeddings that are robust to intra-class variation in viewpoint, illumination, and occlusion, yet preserve sharp separation between visually similar identities. The hardest errors arise precisely where confusable identities meet, a region that pairwise losses shape only implicitly. We present PBR-ReID, a prototype-based framework that makes this inter-class geometry an explicit learning target. Each identity is represented by a learnable prototype jointly optimized with a DiNOv3 backbone and the resulting prototype similarity matrix reveals, at every training step, which identities are most confusable. On this signal we build Boundary Repulsion MixUp (BRM), a geometry-aware regularizer that converts standard MixUp's weakness into a discriminative signal. Rather than interpolating samples across confusable identities, which blurs the boundaries that matter most, BRM constructs an explicit boundary proxy between each confusable pair and repels their features away from it, converting boundary ambiguity into a discriminative signal. We adopt a two-stage training protocol consisting of a prototype warmup phase followed by EMA-stabilized joint fine-tuning. Extensive experiments on person and vehicle ReID benchmarks demonstrate strong performance, with thorough ablations confirming each component's contribution. Code is available at https://github.com/psaltaath/pbr-reid.

papers.title: Mixed-norm Herz-type Triebel-Lizorkin spaces
papers.abstract: Based on mixed-norm Herz spaces, we introduce a new class of mixed-norm Herz-type Triebel-Lizorkin spaces. We establish their $\varphi$-transform characterization in the sense of Frazier and Jawerth and prove Sobolev embedding theorems for these spaces. The resulting embedding theorems extend and improve several known results for mixed-norm Triebel-Lizorkin spaces.

papers.title: Optimal Experimental Design for the Polynomial Maximization Method: a Higher-Order Reserve Beyond Second-Order Design Theory
papers.abstract: Optimal designs for regression with asymmetric errors build on the second-order least squares estimator (SLSE) of Wang and Leblanc (2008), whose gain over ordinary least squares (OLS) comes from the error skewness. With i.i.d. errors the optimally weighted SLSE solves the same estimating equation as the degree-two Polynomial Maximization Method (PMM), a family whose degree-$S$ location estimator has asymptotic variance $g_S\le1$ times that of the sample mean. We derive optimal designs for this family when the errors are independent with constant variance but have standardised cumulants of order three and higher that vary with the regressor (cumulant heteroscedasticity). For a known reduction field $g_S(x)$, the $g_S$-weighted information matrix $M_{g_S}$ obeys the Kiefer-Wolfowitz equivalence theorem. A constant field leaves the OLS-optimal design unchanged; a non-constant field can change it but need not. For symmetric errors with varying kurtosis, the PMM$_2$ and conditional-SLSE designs cannot depart from the OLS-optimal one, whereas a degree-three design can. A stratify-and-pool PMM$_S$ estimator attains $N\mathrm{Cov}(\hat\theta)\to\sigma^2M_{g_S}^{-1}$ at every degree as all strata grow; its per-stratum reduction is below one only for symmetric errors with the symmetry imposed. For a quadratic model on $[0,1]$ with symmetric Beta errors of unit variance and dose-varying shape, the third-order design for the known field has $A$-efficiency $1.047$ relative to the OLS-optimal design, and $1.001$ under the $D$-criterion. A two-stage procedure that estimates the field from a one-third pilot builds designs of $A$-efficiency $1.014$-$1.020$ at $N=600$-$2400$; its realised mean-squared-error ratio against the OLS-optimal design ranges from $0.89$ (a loss) to $1.08$.

authors.name: Serhii Zabolotnii
authors.institution: State Scientific Research Institute of Armament and Military Equipment Testing and Certification

papers.title: On Detection Reliability for Small Object Segmentation
papers.abstract: This study investigates whether predicted bounding boxes are reliable for determining where small-object segmentation should be performed without risking false negatives outside those boxes. The investigation leverages adenovirus particles as small objects, YOLO26x for detection, YO-LO26x-Sem for segmentation, and Mask R-CNN for both detection and segmentation. Segmenta-tion-model predictions were matched to ground-truth adenovirus masks or reference objects using their centroids, with ground-truth mask centroids preferred over ground-truth bounding-box centroids as references for matching. Matched predicted-mask centroids were considered as inside at least one detector-predicted bounding box or outside all such boxes, while ground-truth masks without matched predictions were recorded as having no matched segmentation. For the YOLO26 models, 34 reference objects (47.89%) had matched segmentation centroids inside at least one pre-dicted box, 8 (11.27%) had centroids outside all predicted boxes, and 29 (40.85%) had no matched predicted segmentation. For the Mask R-CNN model, the corresponding counts were 69 (97.18%), 0 (0.00%), and 2 (2.82%). These preliminary experiments demonstrated that restricting segmentation to detector-predicted bounding boxes risks excluding matched segmentation predictions outside those boxes, potentially introducing false negatives.

papers.title: Automatic indexing of wide-band quasi-Laue neutron diffraction patterns of large unit cells
papers.abstract: With a continuous spectrum of incident neutron wavelengths, quasi-Laue diffraction records many Bragg reflections from a stationary crystal, each satisfying the diffraction condition at a particular wavelength. Because the wavelength of each reflection is not measured, the crystal orientation must be determined from the scattering directions alone. At the new IMAGINE-X instrument, instant-readout detectors and many short exposures per experiment require this indexing to run automatically, yet for a protein crystal at the full 2-10 Angstrom band a single peak can have approximately $10^4$ candidate reflections, and a random orientation indexes a large fraction of the observed peaks. We describe an algorithm that indexes such patterns for a known unit cell and wavelength band. Differential evolution searches uniformly sampled rotations, matching observed directions to band-limited shells of candidate directions, and each solution is tested against the indexing expected for a random orientation. In a benchmark search, a k-d tree and a persistent pool of 32 worker processes reduce the wall time 270-fold relative to a serial scan of all candidates. The algorithm is first validated on the time-of-flight diffractometer MANDI, where the measured wavelengths give a reference solution by standard indexing. With the wavelengths discarded, every indexed reflection from 93 rare-earth garnet patterns agrees up to harmonic order. The algorithm then reliably indexes the natural mineral mesolite, measured on the original image plate at IMAGINE before the upgrade, and the protein T4 lysozyme, measured on the new IMAGINE-X instrument over the full band.

papers.title: Solid-Resolving Sets on Directed Graphs
papers.abstract: A set $S \subseteq V(G)$ is a solid-resolving set of an undirected graph $G$ if each vertex can be distinguished from any vertex subset by their distances from the set $S$. Solid-resolving sets are a generalization of resolving sets, which have been studied extensively in the literature. We extend this concept to oriented graphs and directed graphs. In this setting, we first define solid-resolving sets for digraphs and then consider vertices that must be included in any solid-resolving set. We also study the solid-metric dimension, which is the minimum cardinality of a solid-resolving set of a given digraph. We determine the possible values of the solid-metric dimension for several common graph classes, including tournaments, directed trees, oriented cycles, complete bipartite graphs, as well as for Cartesian products of oriented paths and cycles. We also show via some examples that there is no trivial relation between the solid-metric dimension of a digraph and the solid-metric dimension of its underlying undirected graph. Furthermore, we show that the solid-metric dimension can increase or decrease by an arbitrary $k$ when one vertex is removed. Similarly, removing a single arc can decrease the solid-metric dimension by an arbitrary $k$; however, it can increase by at most 1. The arbitrary changes in solid-metric dimension indicate that the solid-metric dimension is a global, rather than a local, property.

papers.title: Geometric Consistency Based Label-Free Validation for Checkpoint Selection in Audio Active Learning
papers.abstract: Audio active learning (AL) trains a classifier at low annotation cost by labeling only an informative fraction of an unlabeled collection over successive rounds. Each round picks one of the checkpoints saved during training. Mainstream AL protocols do so with an assumed validation set, but in practice its labels also count toward the annotation cost, shrinking the advantage of an already small annotation budget. We propose geometric consistency, a label-free validation rule for checkpoint selection. Both classifiers, nearest-class-mean and k-nearest-neighbor, are built from the labeled set in a frozen pretrained embedding space. They then predict the unlabeled data to model its geometry. The rule scores each checkpoint by its agreement with these pseudo-labels and its cross-entropy on the labeled set. It works with any query strategy, has one hyperparameter, insensitive in practice, and adds only one batched forward pass over the unlabeled data per round. At matched label budgets across datasets, encoders, and query strategies, it attains the best mean rank in area under the labeling curve (AULC) among methods without extra labels and is on par with an out-of-budget validation set. To our knowledge, this is the first systematic study of label-free validation for checkpoint selection in audio AL.

papers.title: Tapering to Enhance the Performance of Nanowire-Based Fluorescent Biosensors
papers.abstract: High-refractive-index nanowires are of interest for signal enhancement in fluorescence-based biosensing. Here, through electromagnetic modelling, we demonstrate substantial fluorescence signal enhancement by incorporating a tapered section into a cylindrical nanowire and investigate two complementary tapering configurations to address practical implementation challenges. Under near-normal excitation, the excitation enhancement increases approximately linearly with taper length, reaching more than three times that of the corresponding non-tapered nanowire at a taper length of 8000 nm. In a non-imaging signal detection scheme using a low numerical aperture (NA), the proposed tapered nanowire achieves more than three orders of magnitude enhancement in fluorescence signal compared with a planar biosensor. Thus, the tapered nanowire should enable efficient fluorescence detection using compact, low-NA optical configuration. In imaging mode, similarly as for non-tapered nanowires, imaging sharpness beyond conventional microscopy limitations is obtained when imaging from the non-tapered nanowire end, while strongly increased excitation enhancement is simultaneously obtained when exciting from the opposite, tapered end.

papers.title: End-to-End Differentiable Diffusion Conditioning for Physics-Informed Optimization
papers.abstract: Optimizing high-dimensional physical systems under expensive evaluations and complex constraints is a central challenge in science and engineering. In offline model-based optimization (MBO), methods must improve designs using only a fixed dataset and no test-time access to the true objective. However, existing methods typically suffer from conservatism, unconstrained surrogate exploitation, or function as static inference-time samplers that cannot refine candidates against precise physical objectives. In this paper, we propose Differentiable Diffusion Conditioning (D2C) for offline MBO, which leverages the fact that deterministic sampling makes the reverse denoising chain differentiable with respect to the conditioning signal. D2C turns a frozen conditional diffusion model into an end-to-end gradient-based optimizer by directly optimizing conditioning variables at test time via gradients from frozen surrogate objectives and physics-informed penalties backpropagated through the reverse chain. We implement this idea in a composed proposer-evaluator framework and evaluate it on laser pulse optimization for inertial confinement fusion, sustainable data-center workload scheduling, and four Design-Bench tasks. Our method achieves the strongest results on the two real-world tasks and the best average rank across four Design-Bench tasks.

papers.title: Identifying Cosmic Ray Over-Flagging in STIS CCD Spectroscopic Observations
papers.abstract: The standard method for rejecting cosmic rays in CCD data taken by the Hubble Space Telescope's Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph (STIS) instrument relies on combining multiple sub-exposures while flagging outliers. A known caveat of this method is that when the sub-exposures are not well registered, large portions of valid spectroscopic data can be flagged as cosmic rays. In this work we discuss the new ocrreject_exam() task in the stistools Python package designed to quickly identify datasets impacted by this misregistration-induced over-flagging. We demonstrate its effectiveness on known cases of over-flagged data, introduce a new monitoring website which automatically runs the tool on STIS CCD spectroscopic data, and analyze the tool's output on STIS CCD spectroscopic data from 1997 through 2025. From this analysis we estimate that ~31% of datasets will exhibit cosmic ray over-flagging. Lastly, we discuss various methods of recalibrating impacted data to mitigate the effects of over-flagging.

authors.name: Matthew M. Dallas
authors.institution: Ollscoil na Gaillimhe – University of Galway

papers.title: Contact-Free Nuclear and Cytoplasmic Mechanophenotyping by Amplitude-Modulated Ultrasound and Phase-Locked Optical Diffraction Tomography: Computational Feasibility and Initial Experimental Readouts
papers.abstract: We investigate whether acoustic stimulation combined with phase-locked optical diffraction tomography (ODT) could measure the mechanical responses of the nucleus and cytoplasm separately in adherent cells. A megahertz ultrasound carrier is amplitude-modulated at low frequencies, while angle-scanned holography provides a route to reconstruct the first-harmonic refractive-index response in three dimensions. We built a computational model connecting viscoelastic finite-element simulations of MDA-MB-231 cells with a refractive-index phantom, hologram formation, camera noise and ODT reconstruction. Under an assumed 0.1 Pa harmonic shear traction at 10 Hz, the model predicts 3.6 to 9.2 nm of nuclear shear and 6.6 to 15.1 nm of apical motion. The nuclear-to-cytoplasmic amplitude ratio (R_A) is primarily sensitive to stiffness contrast in the tested scenarios, while the relative phase (Delta phi) responds to differences in dissipation. A simulated protocol using 100 illumination angles and 16 phase visits per angle recovered an imposed stiffening and recovery trajectory after averaging four acquisitions. We also obtained initial 3D tomograms of adherent MDA-MB-231 cells and report preliminary regional measurements from five cells. Their mean amplitude ratio was 0.616 plus or minus 0.098, and their mean relative phase was -1.91 plus or minus 0.58 degrees (mean and between-cell sample standard deviation). All five amplitude ratios were below unity, and all phase differences were negative, consistent with the qualitative directions of selected model scenarios. The small cohort and the absence of independently quantified experimental phase noise prevent a claim of quantitative mechanical validation. Together, these results support further evaluation of phase-locked acoustic ODT and identify experimental requirements for a controlled validation study.

papers.title: Synchronization-Oriented Multi-Radius BMOCZ for Non-Coherent Short-Packet Communications
papers.abstract: Modulation on conjugate-reciprocal zeros (MOCZ) is a promising candidate for blind short-packet communication (SPC) in future wireless systems; however, its performance is sensitive to timing and frequency synchronization errors. In this paper, we propose a novel scheme named multi-radius binary MOCZ (MR-BMOCZ). This method introduces a new root placement strategy that enhances diversity in the autocorrelation domain. The resulting structure enhances the autocorrelation properties of the transmitted waveform, leading to improved timing offset (TO) estimation. Moreover, the multi-radius construction distributes the signal energy over a larger set of radii, hence reducing the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR). The resulting waveform also exhibits a distinctive spectral structure that is exploited for carrier frequency offset (CFO) estimation and correction, yielding lower normalized mean square error (NMSE) compared with BMOCZ-based schemes. Simulation results over additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and fading channels demonstrate that MR-BMOCZ achieves superior synchronization performance while maintaining comparable bit error rate (BER) and block error rate (BLER) performance. Consequently, the proposed scheme offers a synchronization oriented extension of BMOCZ for robust non-coherent SPC.

papers.title: Cross-Platform Application Migration to HarmonyOS: An Agentic Pipeline with Artifact-Derived Verification
papers.abstract: The migration of applications written for a different platforms like Android or iOS to HarmonyOS NEXT requires a complete rewrite in ArkTS. Although LLMs automate the translation of source constructs into ArkTS, syntactic compilation is not enough and functional assurance is a critical open challenge in HarmonyOS NEXT migration. We present HMOS~Migrator, an agentic pipeline that reads an application's source code, generates an ArkTS project, and validates the result by replaying recorded interactions on a real device. We cast the scoring problem as quality estimation without a reference implementation; we score a migration using only the source application's recorded behaviour and the artifacts produced by the pipeline. We define seven weighted metrics, each constructed so that reduced measurement cannot artificially raise the score. Over twelve runs across six open-source applications, the pipeline's structural reproduction is high (completeness \pct{83.3}--\pct{100.0}), while on-device behaviour (\pct{4.3}--\pct{63.1}) and UI fidelity (\pct{21.1}--\pct{63.2}) remain the primary limits. Scores improve steadily over time: $+0.45$~points per day overall ($R^2=0.44$, $p=0.019$) and $+0.47$ over the model-free subset ($R^2=0.39$, $p=0.029$), with corresponding to fit angles of $+8.4^{\circ}$ and $+11.7^{\circ}$ respectively.

papers.title: Lie symmetry analysis of the Saint--Venant equations with variable bottom
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to apply Lie-symmetry methods to the one-dimensional Saint--Venant shallow-water equations over variable bottom topography. We classify the bottom profiles that admit symmetry extensions, derive similarity reductions to ordinary differential equations, and analyze selected reduced systems. In particular, heteroclinic trajectories yield physically meaningful self-similar solutions describing the draining and filling of water over a quadratic bottom with a fixed shoreline.

papers.title: Autonomous Structural Discovery Of Bioprocess Dynamics And Kinetics Via LLM-Driven Agents
papers.abstract: High-fidelity digital twins in continuous biomanufacturing are often bottlenecked by incomplete kinetic models, while standard data-driven algorithms (e.g., SINDy, PINNs) lack interpretability or impose rigid physical assumptions. This paper introduces a hybrid closed-loop architecture for autonomous kinetic state-space discovery driven by a Large Language Model (LLM) agent. The framework employs a sequential "isolation-peeling" methodology across orthogonal operational regimes. This algorithmic peeling mathematically decouples entangled multiplicative (inhibitory) and additive (catalytic) biological rate law. Grounded in a Two-Level Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) library, the framework utilizes Moving Horizon Estimation (MHE) and logarithmic decomposition to decouple complex cell growth kinetics into orthogonal multiplicative (inhibitory) and additive (regulatory) residual channels. When statistical degeneracy occurs an Active Design of Experiments (DoE) controller dynamically triggers targeted perturbations to decorrelate competing model hypotheses. Evaluated on a continuous stirred-tank reactor exhibiting unmodeled Haldane inhibition, Luong product toxicity, and secondary metabolite autocatalysis, the framework autonomously expanded the state space and recovered ground-truth parameters with under 6% error without a priori kinetic knowledge.

papers.title: Sharp Norm Approximation of Covering Markov Operators
papers.abstract:
We study the operator-norm approximation of Markov operators associated with finite graph coverings. Let $q:Y\to X$ be a connected covering of degree $d\geq 2$ between finite connected graphs, and let $A_q:C(Y)\to C(X)$ be its fiber-averaging operator. We show that $A_q$ is not a finite convex combination of extreme Markov operators, although such combinations approximate $A_q$ arbitrarily well in operator norm.
  We determine the exact distances from $A_q$ to convex combinations of at most $m$ extreme Markov operators, with arbitrary or equal convex weights. If $m=kd+r$, where $k\geq 0$ and $1\leq r\leq d$, these distances are
  $2(d-r+1)/[d(k(d-r+1)+1)]$
  and
  $2r(d-r+1)/(dm)$,
  respectively. Both distances are attained and depend only on the covering degree $d$ and the number of terms $m$. We also determine when equal weights are optimal and quantify the additional approximation error when they are not. Our proofs use total-variation estimates and continuous rearrangements of labelled weighted atoms. In particular, the unrestricted errors have a common scaled limit, while the equal-weight errors exhibit residue-dependent asymptotic behavior.

papers.title: Permission to Retry: A Study of Authorization and Recovery in AI Agent Workflows
papers.abstract: A durable agent can resume a consequential action while its authority changes and the action's external outcome remains uncertain. We study execution-time reliability of tool-using AI agents, isolating recovery decisions from language-model behavior. Checkpoint state, permission to dispatch, evidence of an external effect and permission to reconcile are distinct obligations. We present a finite conformance study that checks these obligations through histories scored against a provider effect ledger hidden from the recovering application. A prospectively frozen campaign executes 336 histories on native LangGraph and Temporal hosts, crossing 14 schedules, three provider contracts and four matched application policies. All 168 paired host cells have identical checked outcomes. Per host, retained-ledger reconciliation passes all 42 histories: 21 checked completions, 15 denials and six unknown outcomes with reservations retained. Cached retry, revalidation before retry and stable-key retry pass 30, 36 and 31 histories respectively. A separate 16-case component study of InfinityOS, an enterprise AI platform developed by Arya.ai, exercises exported authority, worker, recovery and settlement code over repository fakes. The results isolate the roles of current authority, provider contracts and retained observations in recovery, with safety, completion and unresolved obligations reported separately for the declared application profile.

papers.title: Beyond On-Policy vs. Off-Policy: At What Level Should LLM Agent Distillation Follow the Student?
papers.abstract: Distilling interactive LLM agents requires choosing between teacher-generated demonstrations and student-generated experience, corresponding broadly to off-policy and on-policy distillation. While both have proven effective, we argue that this distinction is inherently hierarchical: the policy that induces an interaction history need not be the same as the policy that generates the token prefix of the current action. We introduce a hierarchical agent distillation framework that formalizes these two levels of on-policiness and enables explicit control over their pairing, mixture proportions, and training schedule. We study this problem through self-distillation, where a frozen teacher has access to task guidance unavailable to the student, and conduct a three-stage controlled study across three models and four interactive environments. We find that student-induced histories paired with teacher-generated action prefixes generally provide the strongest standalone training signal, whereas following the student at both levels generally performs worst. Nevertheless, fully on-policy data becomes beneficial when incorporated into a mixture with other configurations. Moreover, mixtures with identical teacher/student proportions at each level can yield substantially different performance, showing that how the two levels are paired matters beyond the overall amount of on-policy data. Finally, front-loading fully teacher-generated contexts and delaying fully on-policy contexts improves over a static mixture. These findings provide practical principles for deciding where, how much, and when agent distillation should follow the student.

authors.name: Ya Gao
authors.institution: Xi’an University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Learning Representative Port Subsets for Efficient Fluid Antenna Systems
papers.abstract: Fluid antenna systems (FASs) provide many candidate ports, but probing all ports for each channel realization incurs substantial online overhead. We study a complementary offline problem: compress the candidate-port space once and reuse the compressed set across future channel realizations. The method collects optimal ports from sampled training realizations, requiring only one scan of the candidate ports per realization. On a DeepMIMO 7-by-7 FAS with 49 candidate ports, 120 training realizations yield 27 representative ports on average while retaining 99.995% of the channel power gain achieved by exhaustive port selection.

papers.title: Networked Humanoid Intelligence: Communication, Coordination, Collaboration, and Social Interaction
papers.abstract: Humanoid robots are moving from laboratory platforms toward connected fleets that share workspaces, infrastructure, tasks, and knowledge with other robots and humans. As deployments grow, the operation and improvement of each humanoid depend on information exchanged across the network. However, existing research has largely studied humanoids as individual systems. This survey examines networked humanoid intelligence through four functions of information exchange: communication, coordination, collaboration, and social intelligence with human interaction. We first establish the foundations of networked humanoid systems, define the question addressed by each function, and connect them through a common factory scenario. We review the literature along six dimensions: interaction architecture, exchanged information, physical coupling, operating timescale, system scale, and embodiment. We separate results obtained with physical and simulated humanoids from those based on other robotic platforms or disembodied agents, because the latter do not fully capture humanoid-specific constraints such as balance, whole-body motion, contact, and physical interaction. We examine hardware, datasets, and benchmarks, and distinguish risks handled locally from those networking introduces, such as stale information or unsafe knowledge propagation. Finally, we identify open problems in control-aware networking, compact body-centric messages, physically grounded coordination, network- and embodiment-aware knowledge sharing, fleet-level social consistency, and accountable human oversight.

papers.title: Optical Speckle Patterns as Nonlinear Feature Maps for Photonic Machine Learning
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) has increased the demand for energy-efficient hardware, and optical computing has emerged as a promising alternative to conventional electronic processors owing to its high parallelism and potentially lower power consumption. In this work, we investigate an optical computing architecture based on an integrated photonic circular multipass cell, focusing on its suitability for machine learning and pattern recognition tasks. The properties of the system are evaluated through measures of nonlinearity and cosine similarity, which characterize the system's information-processing capacity and the dimensionality of the generated feature representations. Numerical results demonstrate that the reservoir mirror reflectance, the size of the encoded figure, and the refractive-index contrast between the reservoir and the encoded figure modify the nonlinearity of the system, as verified via pairwise similarity estimates. These results indicate that the features generated by the circular multipass cell can be tailored by adjusting the system parameters, providing a means to control the reservoir transformation of the input data. The resulting representations were applied to classification tasks involving texture images and thyroid collagen images, achieving classification accuracies ranging from 69% to 93%. These findings suggest that photonic computing systems could provide a basis for more energy-efficient machine-learning hardware.

papers.title: RynnVLA-Latent: Scaling Robotic Manipulation Foundation Models with 3D-Grounded Latent Actions
papers.abstract: Scaling vision-language-action (VLA) models is constrained by scarce action-labeled demonstrations and incompatible control spaces across robot embodiments. We present RynnVLA-Latent, a framework that turns heterogeneous interaction videos into scalable supervision for robot policy pretraining. At its core, RynnLAM learns continuous, 3D-grounded latent actions from visual transitions without requiring native robot controls. By combining residual future-feature prediction, camera-compensated 3D-flow supervision, and camera-motion decoupling, RynnLAM encourages representations that capture control-relevant motion rather than appearance changes alone. We apply RynnLAM to 30.1K hours of human, robot, and simulation videos, producing 745.52M latent-action descriptors. RynnVLA-Latent then learns to predict latent-action chunks from visual observations and language through flow matching, before adapting its pretrained backbone and action expert to embodiment-specific robot actions. The resulting 4B policy achieves 98.8% success on LIBERO, 84.7% on LIBERO-Plus without benchmark-specific adaptation, 51.9% average success across five VLABench tracks, and 88.6% average success on the RoboTwin 2.0 bimanual benchmark. It also achieves the highest observed success rates among the compared methods on six real-world manipulation tasks across dexterous-hand and mobile-gripper platforms. Together with representation ablations and data-scaling results, these findings demonstrate the potential of latent-action supervision for scaling robot policy learning beyond native action-labeled data.

authors.name: Xingyue Zhao
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Kehan Li
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Mechanical Transmission

authors.name: Yuming Jiang
authors.institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Deli Zhao
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: RSKD: Grounding Semantic Consistency in Driving VLMs via Distillation
papers.abstract: Knowledge distillation can transfer large multimodal models to compact models for autonomous driving, but uniform token-level matching can dilute planning-relevant semantics and amplify teacher errors. We propose RSKD, a semantic-consistency-guided distillation framework that routes supervision according to both the task importance of an answer phrase and its semantic consistency with the teacher prediction. Task-critical semantic phrases are localized in the ground-truth answer, and a phrase-level consistency score controls the balance between Jensen--Shannon divergence (JSD) distillation and ground-truth supervision. Teacher information is emphasized only where it is semantically consistent, while semantically inconsistent phrases receive stronger ground-truth supervision. We evaluate RSKD on DrivingVQA, LingoQA, and MapLMv2. RSKD improves over the compared student-based baselines on DrivingVQA and LingoQA and remains competitive on MapLMv2.

authors.name: Hao Ye
authors.institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Governing Artificial Intelligence as a Macro Socio-Technical Regime: The F-I-C-P Framework for Regime-Level AI Infrastructure and Governance
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is often analysed through technical, organisational, or regulatory perspectives that treat capability, adoption, and governance as separate issues. This article conceptualises AI instead as an emerging macro socio-technical regime generated through the interaction of finance, infrastructure, capability, and productivity. It develops the F-I-C-P framework to explain how finance enables infrastructure, infrastructure conditions capability, and capability creates the possibility--but not the guarantee--of productivity and value realisation. The article also introduces the concept of regime-level AI infrastructure to identify concrete configurations, such as AI Gigafactories, foundation-model platforms, national compute infrastructures, public AI platforms, sectoral AI ecosystems, and corporate AI infrastructures, through which the macro-regime becomes observable and evaluable. The central analytical problem is structural misalignment: the risk that financial expectations, infrastructural expansion, technical capability, organisational absorption, productivity realisation, governance capacity, and societal outcomes evolve at different speeds or under unequal conditions of power. Governance is therefore conceptualised not as a final stage after technological deployment, but as a transversal and anticipatory steering capacity. Briefly illustrated through Spain and Chile as non-frontier configurations, the article argues that AI governance should be understood as regime alignment: the task of anticipating, evaluating, and correcting structural misalignments before they become embedded in infrastructural dependencies, organisational routines, market structures, and international asymmetries.

papers.title: The norm reveals projections in the positive unit sphere of an arbitrary C*-algebra
papers.abstract: We show how a simple metric condition in terms of the C$^*$-norm of an arbitrary C$^*$-algebra $A$ can be employed to determine those norm-one positive elements which are projections. Concretely, if we write $S_{A^+}$ for the intersection of the positive cone and the unit sphere of $A$, we establish that an element $a \in S_{A^+}$ is a projection if, and only if, $$\{a\} = \left\{x\in S_{A^+}: \|x-z\| = 1 \hbox{ for all } z\in S_{A^+}\hbox{ with } \|a-z\|=1 \right\}.$$ This proves a conjecture which has been previously confirmed for von Neumann algebras and unital C$^*$-algebras. In the setting of not necessarily unital JB$^*$-algebras, the Shirshov--Cohn theorem is invoked to obtain a similar metric characterisation of projections. In the wider setting of JB$^*$-triples, we show how a metric characterisation in terms of inner ideals can be established to determine non-zero tripotents.

authors.name: Pedro Saavedra
authors.institution: Universidad de Las Palmas de Gran Canaria

papers.title: An eight-dimensional nilpotent Leibniz algebra without outer derivations
papers.abstract: Jacobson's classical theorem asserts that every nilpotent Lie algebra admits a non-inner derivation. This result, however, does not extend to Leibniz algebras: there exists an eight-dimensional complex nilpotent Leibniz algebra whose every derivation is inner. In this paper, we present a systematic investigation of this algebra, with particular emphasis on the absence of outer derivations and its structural properties. We describe its lower central series, annihilators, center, and Leibniz kernel, and prove that its derivation algebra is a six-dimensional nilpotent Lie algebra isomorphic to the quotient of the algebra by its Leibniz kernel. We further show that its automorphism group is a connected six-dimensional unipotent group obtained by exponentiating inner derivations; in particular, it contains no nontrivial elements of finite order. In addition, we provide a complete classification of the quasiderivation, generalized derivation, and $\sigma$-derivation of the algebra. Finally, we show that, among the four linearly independent infinitesimal deformations, exactly one is integrable, giving rise to a one-parameter family of pairwise non-isomorphic algebras which, with a single exception, also admit only inner derivations.

authors.name: Jobir Adashev
authors.institution: Academy of Sciences Republic of Uzbekistan

papers.title: Printed and Scanned: Exposing the Fragility of Single-Image Morphing Attack Detectors under Print-Scan Degradation
papers.abstract: Face morphing attacks, in which the biometric traits of two or more identities are blended into a single face image, pose a severe threat to identity document issuance and automated border control. Consequently, a large body of work has proposed Single-image Morphing Attack Detection (S-MAD) algorithms and benchmarked them on datasets such as SYN-MAD22. However, the majority of these benchmarks operate exclusively in the digital domain, which contrasts with the real-world passport issuance pipeline in some countries, which still requires an applicant-supplied photograph to be printed and subsequently re-scanned before it is embedded in the identity document or fed into an automated verification system. This print-scan step introduces halftoning, resampling, color-space, and sensor noise that are absent from digital pipelines, and may mask the high-frequency artifacts that S-MAD models rely on. In this work, we introduce a print-scan version of the SYN-MAD22 dataset, obtained by printing and re-scanning all bona fide and morphed images at 300 and 600 DPI, and we use it to evaluate eight state-of-the-art S-MAD models trained exclusively on digital data. We additionally repeat the acquisition with a second scanner to assess cross-device robustness. Our results show that detectors that achieve near state-of-the-art performance in the digital domain suffer a more than threefold increase in average equal error rate, with the same qualitative degradation observed across both scanning devices, exposing a critical, previously under-reported gap between digital-benchmark performance and robustness to print-scan degradation.

papers.title: Cross-Lingual Information Retrieval in Tetun for Ad-Hoc Search
papers.abstract: Developing information retrieval (IR) systems that enable access across multiple languages is crucial in multilingual contexts. In Timor-Leste, where Tetun, Portuguese, English, and Indonesian are official and working languages, no cross-lingual information retrieval (CLIR) solutions currently exist to support information access across these languages. This study addresses that gap by investigating CLIR approaches tailored to the linguistic landscape of Timor-Leste. Leveraging an existing monolingual Tetun document collection and ad-hoc text retrieval baselines, we explore the feasibility of CLIR for Tetun. Queries were manually translated into Portuguese, English, and Indonesian to create a multilingual query set. These were then automatically translated back into Tetun using Google Translate and several large language models, and used to retrieve documents in Tetun. Results show that Google Translate is the most reliable tool for Tetun CLIR overall, and the Hiemstra LM consistently outperforms BM25 and DFR BM25 in cross-lingual retrieval performance. However, overall effectiveness remains up to 26.95 percentage points lower than that of the monolingual baseline, underscoring the limitations of current translation tools and the challenges of developing an effective CLIR for Tetun. Despite these challenges, this work establishes the first CLIR baseline for Tetun ad-hoc text retrieval, providing a foundation for future research in this under-resourced setting.

papers.title: Agreement rather than normalisation keeps depth reusable in looped language models
papers.abstract: Looped language models apply one block of layers repeatedly, and the design pays off only if depth is reusable: loop steps beyond the trained budget must remain usable at inference. We ask whether that rests on normalising the state between loop steps, as the released Ouro models do, or on agreement between the loop a model is trained with and the loop it is run with. On released weights this loop-boundary normalisation can be removed without adding parameters and with the readout path bit-identical, and the operation is an identity at one loop step, which serves as an implementation check. Removing it takes Ouro-1.4B and Ouro-2.6B to zero accuracy by the trained budget on a balanced binary task (chance 0.500). State-norm growth, the failure that prior accounts predict, is not the cause: the norm stays within a factor of 2.021 while the head commits to a single wrong token. Yet in 19M-parameter models trained from scratch on two synthetic tasks, 16 seeds per configuration, training without the normalisation is never worse than training with it and extrapolates better: the two are closest at the trained depth and separate on both sides of it (Cliff's delta up to 0.867 beyond the budget). Both results follow if agreement, and not the normalisation itself, is what keeps depth reusable. The damage sits in the readout together with the last layer of the block: in the models trained from scratch, refitting the head over the frozen modified loop recovers a third of the lost accuracy and plateaus, while refitting the last block layer with it recovers all of it. Finally, comparing looped with stacked depth at an equal inference loop count is confounded by unequal overshoot of the trained budget; at matched overshoot the advantage of looping vanishes on one task and shrinks on the other.

authors.name: Maxim Abramov
authors.institution: St. Petersburg Research Center of the Russian Academy of Sciences

authors.name: Grach Mkrtchian
authors.institution: Moscow Technical University of Communication and Informatics

papers.title: Development of an FPGA-Based Readout System and Functional Characterization of a Custom NSX1 ASIC for X-ray instrumentation
papers.abstract: We developed an FPGA-based readout system for a front-end ASIC (NSX1) with 64 channels to read out a large- area silicon drift detector used in X-ray detection instruments such as the Wide Field Monitor module for the STROBE-X mission concept. The FPGA acts as a central controller for the NSX1 configuration, implementing trigger handling and event sequencing, precise event timestamping, control of an external ADC for digitization, and data transfer to the host PC. The system enables comprehensive ASIC characterization; here, we demonstrate preliminary ASIC functionality and characterization tests using a calibrated pulser for two programmable linear gain responses of 375 mV/fC and 750 mV/fC. These preliminary results validate the low-noise performance of the NSX1 ASIC and demonstrate successful integration of the DAQ system.

papers.title: Cross-Domain Sequential Recommendation with Representation-Level User Transfer
papers.abstract: Cross-domain sequential recommendation aims to improve next-item prediction in a target domain by leveraging user behavior from auxiliary source domains. However, real-world deployment faces two critical challenges: business constraints that isolate interaction data across domains, and user heterogeneity, where many users lack cross-domain activity. This makes existing cross-domain methods difficult to apply. In this paper, we propose a simple and practical framework for cross-domain sequential recommendations that transfers information exclusively through learned user representations, without sharing raw interaction data or item embeddings across domains. We introduce a lightweight adapter that projects the source-domain user representation into the target-domain embedding space and integrates it with the target interaction sequence. Importantly, when source data is unavailable (i.e., the user observed only in the target domain), the model seamlessly defaults to a robust target-only sequential recommender, retaining benefits from joint training across all users. Extensive experiments were conducted under two setups; one targets benchmarking against previous baselines, while the other focuses on realistic and scalable conditions. Both sets of experiments demonstrate consistent performance gains for shared and unshared users.

authors.name: Evgeny Frolov
authors.institution: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Sharp Bounds on the Winner's Bias under Independent and Nonnegatively Correlated Noise
papers.abstract: Reporting the best of $M$ noisy, unbiased scores overstates the winner's value by up to $c\sqrt{V}$, where $V$ is the total noise variance and the sharp constant $c$ depends on how the noise is dependent. It was known only at the two extremes, arbitrary dependence ($\sqrt{(M-1)/M}$) and i.i.d. noise. We determine it for two classes in between: for independent, not identically distributed noise it is $\sqrt{(M-1)/(2M)}$, and for pairwise nonnegatively correlated noise it is $(M-1)/M$; for uncorrelated noise this answers the maximum version of an open question about the expected range. Explicit finite constructions attain both. As a corollary, the bias of the cross-validation estimator is bounded sharply within each class. All theorems are formally verified in Lean 4. Across 448 language-model and classifier selection pipelines, designs with per-candidate items realize a median 0.75 of the independent-class ceiling. At a fixed item budget, scoring all candidates on shared items is markedly less optimistic than giving each candidate its own items.

authors.name: Grach Mkrtchian
authors.institution: Moscow Technical University of Communication and Informatics

papers.title: Sages and Their Anonymous Slips
papers.abstract: Before the game, the sages agree on a finite set of symbols and on a rule for choosing one of them. They are then seated in an unknown order, either in a row or around a circle with a common clockwise direction. Each sage sees only the adjacent sage or sages and secretly writes one symbol. The slips are then mixed, so nobody learns who wrote which symbol; everyone learns only how many times each symbol occurred. The aim is that every sage should be able to independently reconstruct the entire seating. We ask for the smallest number of distinct symbols that makes this possible. We also consider a version in which the seats have fixed public labels, and each sage is told the label of their own seat. For large numbers of sages, the minimum number of symbols is proportional to the square of the number of sages, up to a constant factor. Several small cases can be settled exactly. Four sages in a row need exactly two symbols, and so do five sages on a circle. Six sages on a circle need exactly three symbols, both with and without labeled seats; we give a short explicit rule. Five sages in a row with labeled seats also need exactly three symbols. Without seat labels, two symbols are impossible, and four are sufficient; whether three symbols suffice remains open.

papers.title: Tau creates spatially moving hotspots of amyloid-$\beta$ secondary nucleation: a reaction-diffusion model
papers.abstract: Tau-amyloid-$\beta$ cross-seeding creates a spatial paradox. Bioavailable tau can promote A$\beta$42 nucleation, thereby increasing local fibril number and catalytic-site burden; yet the same fibrils consume the free A$\beta$ monomer required for homotypic secondary nucleation. The region containing the most tau or fibrillar material therefore need not be the region with the highest secondary-nucleation rate. We test this idea with a reaction-diffusion model that tracks a propagating effective tau catalyst, free A$\beta$ monomer, elongation-competent fibrils, fibril mass, and the catalytic sites exposed to monomer. The model reduces the spatial competition to two quantities: accessible catalytic sites and free monomer. Their balance yields an exact condition for an interior kinetic maximum: the logarithmic decrease in accessible catalytic sites must equal twice the logarithmic increase in free monomer. Two Damkohler numbers then separate the relevant competitions-elongation versus clearance, and elongation versus diffusive redistribution-while a monomer screening length sets the physical scale over which depletion can persist. Independent transport and turnover estimates place this length near 0.44-0.54 mm.
