This paper investigates how the algebraic and analytic properties of ordinary length generating functions constrain the grammatical and computational complexity of formal languages. We review the Chomsky-Schutzenberger representation, DSV translations for unambiguous context-free grammars, and their stack-indexed extensions, distinguishing finite algebraic systems from more general constructions. Examples and a diagonal argument demonstrate that even a rational generating function need not determine a language's grammatical class.
  Our central computability result establishes that, for a recursively enumerable language, computability of its length-counting sequence is equivalent to decidability of membership. Consequently, if a recursively enumerable language has a D-finite length generating function over Q(z), it is decidable; equivalently, undecidable recursively enumerable languages cannot have D-finite length generating functions.
  We then examine coefficient growth and singularities through Pringsheim's theorem, the Polya-Carlson dichotomy, Hadamard gaps, and Siegel G-functions. The resulting picture is asymmetric: analytic properties provide useful one-way constraints on language computability, but length enumeration loses too much information to determine grammatical or computational complexity without additional assumptions.

papers.title: Matching Particle-Arrival Rates for Low-Count Image Denoising
papers.abstract: Low-count imaging arises when limited illumination or dose yields only a few detected particles in microscopy, such as photons or electrons, causing measurements to be dominated by signal-dependent Poisson shot noise. Supervised denoisers typically require paired clean and noisy observations, whereas many self-supervised approaches exploit spatial or temporal redundancy without directly estimating the underlying particle-arrival process. We introduce PARM, a self-supervised denoising framework based on particle-arrival-rate matching. By modeling particle accumulation over exposure as a Poisson counting process, PARM identifies the conditional particle-arrival-rate field with the posterior mean of the latent clean rate. Poisson thinning then splits each observation into complementary lower-exposure views that provide self-supervised rate targets for one another. In implementation, the network estimates the normalized spatial allocation of the conditional rate, while the observed total count determines its global particle mass. Experiments on synthetic data, natural-video sequences corrupted with Poisson noise, and real low-dose electron microscopy demonstrate leading or competitive performance while effectively preserving fine structures. PARM therefore provides a statistically grounded approach to low-count image denoising when clean references are unavailable.

authors.name: Huazhen Liu
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Jizhou Li
authors.institution: City University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen Research Institute

papers.title: The Locality Trade-off in Masked Patch Self-Distillation
papers.abstract: Masked patch self-distillation is a key component of modern vision foundation models, including DINOv2 and DINOv3, yet its implications for local visual information remain unclear. We show that its semantic benefits can coexist with a scale-dependent locality cost. Using two annotation-free diagnostics, we distinguish recoverable local appearance from spatial correspondence. In smaller models, adding iBOT substantially weakens patch correspondence while largely preserving appearance decodability. In larger models, correspondence improves, but pixel and texture evidence becomes less linearly accessible in deep features. Thus, scaling changes the form of the locality cost rather than uniformly eliminating it. Our analysis of Gram anchoring further shows that preserving patch relations does not guarantee simultaneous improvements in both properties. These findings motivate evaluating and designing visual representations around the complementary demands of semantic abstraction, appearance preservation, and spatial correspondence. Our code is available at https://github.com/winci-ai/jea.

papers.title: Weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for noncommutative maximal truncated rough singular integrals
papers.abstract: We prove a weak type $(1,1)$ estimate for maximal truncations of noncommutative rough singular integrals whose angular kernels satisfy the classical $L\log L$ integrability and cancellation conditions. The main ingredient of the proof is a new linearization method for handling the maximal truncations acting on the bad functions arising from the noncommutative Calder\'on--Zygmund decomposition.

authors.name: Junming Cao
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory on Integrated Optoelectronics

papers.title: Stability of certain elements in the Bernstein center
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a split connected reductive algebraic group over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. The stable center conjecture asserts that the subspace of stable elements in the Bernstein center of $G(F)$ is a sub-algebra, and this subring is conjecturally isomorphic to the regular functions on the moduli of semi-simple Langlands parameters. Bezrukavnikov-Kazhdan-Varshavsky suggested an approach towards the stable center conjecture by explicitly constructing elements and proving their stability directly without assuming LLC, and proved the stability of the depth-$r$ projectors. Following the idea, the first author and Tsao-Hsien Chen produced a family of elements in the center which are conjecturally stable using Deligne-Lusztig parameters attached to irreducible representations. This paper proves the stability of the projectors corresponding to strongly regular Deligne-Lusztig parameters in depth-zero, and for all the positive depth elements with some restrictions on the residue characteristic.

papers.title: Real Time Motion Detection in Video Inspired by Photonic Time Stretch
papers.abstract: Motion perception is fundamental to computer vision and physical AI, and plays a central role in robotics, autonomous vehicles, human-computer interaction, and video compression. Traditional approaches such as background subtraction, frame-differencing and optical flow algorithms often struggle in complex or dynamic scenes, typically sacrificing spatial resolution for computational tractability. Here we introduce MoViD (Motion estimation via Virtual dispersion and phase Detection), a physics-inspired algorithm grounded in the principles that govern photonic time stretch - a highly successful ultrafast realtime data acquisition platform. Drawing inspiration from the optical physics therein, MoViD treats video as a collection of optical time series waveforms associated with pixels. Motion of an object through a pixel broadens the time series spectrum and, after group delay dispersion, induces a temporal phase that exists only if there is motion. Spatiotemporal group delay dispersion templates, corresponding to dielectric functions, classify specific motion trajectories. Unlike conventional empirical phase-based motion-analysis pipelines that require narrow-band spatial channelization and pyramid reconstruction, the physics-based MoViD operates directly on the broadband video signal, vastly increasing its computational speed. The resulting algorithm achieves unprecedented performance in both motion characterization and motion magnification, providing full-resolution motion mapping in real time at nearly 200 frames per second at 4K resolution and 70 frames per second for 8K video - orders of magnitude faster than classical optical flow approaches or learning-based methods. Notably, such extreme performance enables real time motion analysis at ultrahigh resolution for motion detection and compensation in robotics and other autonomous devices.

authors.name: Bahram Jalali
authors.institution: National Institute of Information and Communications Technology

papers.title: Fast Instinct, Slow Reason: A Dual-Speed Agentic Framework for Self-Configuring Multi-Object Tracking in Satellite Video
papers.abstract: Multi-object tracking in satellite video underpins persistent monitoring, yet offline-tuned trackers lack the onboard intelligence and efficiency to adapt within an observation of tens of seconds. The root is that adaptation still means relabelling and retraining the detector, which cannot run on board in time. Tuning the tracker configuration strongly controls accuracy without touching the network, yet search needs labelled or proxy evaluations, and a language agent costs seconds and tokens per decision. We propose a dual-speed agentic framework pairing a fast instinct compiled offline with a slow reason serving the mission. Its algorithm, Arbitration of Unlabelled Shortlists from Prior Experience, or AUSPEX, learns a covering shortlist and a label-free ranker from labelled source tasks and commits one configuration per sequence. Its system, a Cascaded Onboard Runtime with Verified Uplinked Skills, or CORVUS, cascades reflex, skill, and agent layers, so that a verified skill commits 2.5 s into each observation while a language agent serves natural- language missions. On SatMTB and SatVideoDT with three recent detectors, AUSPEX raises IDF1 by 2.84 to 2.94 points and MOTA by 3.21 to 3.29 points on average without target labels, balances accuracy and labels best among sixteen methods, and loses at most 0.28 IDF1 points at 1.25 tracking passes. CORVUS executes four missions with execution accuracy up to 0.99 and target recall at the perception ceiling, spends no token on the routine decision, runs on Jetson Xavier NX, and hosts fifteen language models from six families without altering any commitment, demonstrating its extensibility and generalization.

authors.name: Fan He
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Yan Li
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: Volume of area-bounded PGL3-Hitchin moduli space
papers.abstract: For the $\mathrm{PGL}_3$-Hitchin moduli space of unmarked convex $\mathbb{RP}^2$ structures on the surface $S_{g,m}$ with fixed boundary data $\mathbf L$ when $m>0$, we investigate the subset whose canonical Hilbert--Busemann area is bounded above by $t$. We show that the Goldman symplectic volume of this subset is at most $C_{g,m}(t+\lambda^2)^{8g-8+3m}$, where $\lambda$ is the largest total-root boundary length for $m>0$ and is set to $0$ for $m=0$. As a consequence, We obtain the explicit upper bound for the $e^{-s\cdot\mathrm{Area}}$-weighted volume.

papers.title: Incremental Predictive Value of LLM Tutoring Interactions for Student Performance
papers.abstract: We evaluate whether semester-level interaction features from a large language model tutor improve assignment-score prediction beyond constant baselines. StudyChat provides 16,851 student-assistant exchanges from two offerings of an undergraduate artificial intelligence course, with outcomes matched to 175 of 203 student-semester records. Six fitted estimators and training-fold mean and median baselines share repeated nested cross-validation. After averaging each student's held-out predictions across ten repeats, Gradient Boosting achieves mean absolute error of 3.023 grade points, versus 3.138 for the median baseline. The paired difference is -0.114, with a conditional 95% bootstrap interval of [-0.245,0.013]. Representation changes and a semester-specific median yield similarly small gains. In the lowest observed-score quartile, however, boosting's error is 7.30 points, versus 8.07 for the median and 6.67 for the mean; Ridge has the lowest fitted-model error at 6.37 despite its worse overall error of 3.331. Scores concentrate near the ceiling: 160 students (91.4%) score above 90, and the lowest quartile contributes 62.1% of boosting's total absolute error. This retrospective comparison shows how baseline choice and error distribution affect predictive value, informing evaluation of student-support tools without establishing a learning effect.

papers.title: From Instructions to Exploits: Applying Program Analysis to Malicious Agent Skills Across Natural Language and Code
papers.abstract: LLM-powered agents increasingly rely on third-party skills that combine natural-language instructions with executable code, creating supply-chain risks that may span both artifacts. Existing skill scanners often rely on rule matching or direct LLM judgments and provide limited support for tracing such cross-domain behavior. We present the Supply-Chain Scanner for Agent Skills (SCS), a static analysis framework that unifies instructions and code for security analysis. SCS compiles natural-language instructions into a constrained Python-style intermediate representation using a limited set of security-oriented APIs. It then constructs program dependence graphs for instructions and bundled code and connects them into a cross-domain graph (xPDG). A Trust-Sensitivity-Capability (TSC) model propagates security properties over the graph to support structured, largely deterministic risk detection. On a manually verified benchmark of 117 malicious and 117 benign skills, SCS achieves the highest average accuracy (85.6%), recall (95.2%), and F1-score (86.9%) among evaluated methods across five LLMs, with 80.2% precision and average token consumption of 13.7 million. Its NL-to-IR compiler achieves 92.5%-94.5% step-level correctness on 400 human-annotated instruction steps. Finally, analyzing 66,157 real-world ClawHub skills yields 2,473 candidates, of which 627 are confirmed malicious through auxiliary dynamic validation and manual review.

authors.name: Xuezhang Liu
authors.institution: Jiangxi Science and Technology Normal University

papers.title: Parabolic filtrations of Soergel bimodules
papers.abstract: Given a Coxeter system $(W,S)$ and a subset $I\subset S$. Let $W_I=\langle I\rangle$ be the standard parabolic subgroup of a Coxeter group $W$, and ${}^IW$ be the set of representatives of minimal length in the coset $W_I\backslash W$. We construct a parabolic version of Soergel's standard filtration, and show that, given any Soergel bimodule, each subquotient of its parabolic filtration is a direct sum of grading shifts of $B_x^I\otimes_R R_y$ with $x\in W_I$ and $y\in {}^IW$. By applying the character theorem of Elias and Williamson, we deduce the positivity of coefficients in the expansion of $C_w$ with respect to the hybrid basis $\{C_xT_y:x\in W_I,y\in {}^IW\}$. This generalizes Grojnowski and Haiman's result to any Coxeter group.

papers.title: Causal Inference in Metric Spaces via Distance Profiles
papers.abstract: Modern interventions increasingly produce object-valued outcomes, such as distributions, covariance matrices, networks, and trees. Existing causal frameworks often exploit special geometry such as one-dimensional Wasserstein quantiles or geodesic Fr\'echet means, whereas metric statistics studies random objects without confounding adjustment. We propose the profile causal effect $\Delta(\omega,t)$, which describes where and at what scale a treatment shifts probability mass, including changes in dispersion, tails, or structure that leave mean-level summaries unchanged. Formally, $\Delta(\omega,t)=\Pr\{d(\omega,Y(1))\le t\}-\Pr\{d(\omega,Y(0))\le t\}$ contrasts the potential-outcome probabilities of the same anchor-centered metric ball and requires no structure beyond the metric. On grids fixed by a deterministic or auxiliary design, we combine cross-fitted doubly robust scores with high-dimensional Gaussian approximation and the multiplier bootstrap to obtain simultaneous confidence bands and a global test under regularity conditions. The bands bound treatment-induced changes in ball and shell probabilities simultaneously and, at fixed anchors, extend to all radii. A protocol guides the choice of anchors and radii. Across the experiments, the global test detects concentration effects that mean-quantile and Fr\'echet-mean summaries miss. Its empirical size is near or below the nominal level, even under confounding, where naive metric tests are substantially oversized.

papers.title: FreqPKC: Frequency-Aware PeakConv for Radar Semantic Segmentation
papers.abstract: Automotive millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar has attracted increasing attention for semantic segmentation in autonomous driving, owing to its robustness under adverse weather and lighting conditions. Recent works have introduced radar-specific neural operators such as PeakConv (PKC), inspired by constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detection, to better model the peak-dominated characteristics of radar images. However, existing methods typically treat the guard bandwidth as learnable parameters, without explicitly characterizing the frequency response of the PKC operator. In this work, we revisit PKC from a frequency-domain perspective and propose Frequency-Aware PeakConv (FreqPKC), which explicitly models and exploits its underlying spectral characteristics. By analyzing the frequency response of PKC, FreqPKC enables the network to capture a broader range of frequency components and adaptively adjust its effective bandwidth. With the proposed Frequency-Aware (FA) module, the network can infer appropriate guard bandwidths to balance high- and low-frequency information: it enhances high-frequency components in target regions for more precise segmentation while suppressing noise through low-frequency filtering in background areas. Building on FreqPKC, we further develop FreqPKC-Net, a radar semantic segmentation (RSS) framework that integrates frequency-guided adaptive modulation with cross-view fusion for multi-view inputs, and can also be adapted to single-view data. Experiments on the public datasets CARRADA, CARRADA-RAC, and a self-built dataset named RS-SAR demonstrate that FreqPKC-Net consistently outperforms existing SoTA methods on both range-Doppler and range-angle views.

authors.name: Jian Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Communication Complexity of Integer Matrix Singularity
papers.abstract:
Alice and Bob hold complementary halves of the columns of an $n\times n$ matrix of $k$-bit integers and decide whether it is singular over $\mathbb Q$. Up to constant-factor dimension growth, this partitioned problem is equivalent to additive singularity, where Alice and Bob hold $n\times n$ matrices $A,B$ of $k$-bit integers and test the singularity of $A+B$ over $\mathbb Q$. We prove a bounded-error quantum lower bound $\Omega(\min\{n^{3/2}\sqrt{k\log n},n^2\log(nk)\})$ and a randomized upper bound $O(n^2\min\{k,\log(k+\log n)\})$. The bounds match at $\Theta(n^2\log(nk))$ for $k\ge n\log n$. The lower bound holds even under the promise of rank $n-1$ versus $n$. Its proof combines an integer witness with a local digit encoding, while the upper-bound protocol lifts modular kernel relations using short messages.
  Bitwise sharing changes how the communication complexity depends on the entry bit length $k$. If Alice and Bob instead hold $n\times n$ matrices $A,B$ of $k$-bit integers and test whether their entrywise bitwise XOR $A\oplus B$ is singular over $\mathbb Q$, we prove a quantum lower bound $\Omega(n^2k)$, matching the trivial upper bound. This lower bound holds even under the promise of rank $n-1$ versus $n$. Our proof uses a dense weighted equation and a signed Fourier witness whose exceptional dyadic frequencies can be removed at small variation cost.

papers.title: Mass concentration and ground states of Fermi systems in Hartree--Fock model with potentials
papers.abstract: Understanding the onset and mechanism of collapse at critical attractive interaction is a fundamental problem in the variational theory of finite fermionic systems. In this paper, we study this problem within the Hartree--Fock framework under various trapping potentials. By establishing a finite-rank Hartree-type Gagliardo--Nirenberg--Sobolev inequality, we identify a critical threshold $\mathcal{K}^{(N)}$ governing the existence of ground states. We then determine the concentration behavior of ground states as the interaction parameter approaches $\mathcal{K}^{(N)}$. To reveal how the geometry of the trap influences this critical phenomenon, we consider three representative classes of potentials: polynomial-type potentials, ring-shaped potentials, and potentials whose zero set has nonempty interior. For each class, we derive the concentration scale and sharp asymptotics of the least energy. The resulting regimes are qualitatively different, showing that both the location and the rate of concentration are selected by the local geometry of the potential near its minimum set. In contrast to scalar Hartree problems, the nonlocal interaction is coupled here with pairwise $L^2$-orthogonality constraints, and their interplay creates substantial difficulties in the compactness and blow-up analysis.

authors.name: Zhuocheng Li
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Distilling Dense Trajectory Teachers For Large-Motion Video World Models
papers.abstract: Video world models are expected to generate videos that accurately follow specified camera trajectories while maintaining consistent 3D structures. However, existing models are predominantly trained on densely sampled videos with small inter-frame camera motions. When applied to sparse, large step trajectories, they often produce frozen frames, inaccurate camera motion, and severe geometric drift. We attribute this degradation to a mismatch between the gradual viewpoint transitions seen during training and the large viewpoint changes required at inference time. To address this problem, we propose Dense Trajectory Teacher Distillation (DTTD), a post-training framework that transfers a model's generation capability from dense trajectories to large camera motions. Given a sparse trajectory, DTTD interpolates additional camera poses to construct a dense trajectory covering the same path. The frozen base model then generates reliable teacher videos along this familiar dense trajectory, and pose aligned teacher observations are used to evaluate candidate videos generated under the original sparse trajectory. In this way, the model serves as its own generation teacher, requiring neither additional video data nor a stronger external video generator. We further combine dense teacher supervision with geometry aware rewards that assess cross frame consistency and camera trajectory following, and use the resulting preferences for offline preference optimization. To stably expand the model's motion range, we introduce a cumulative curriculum that progressively incorporates larger motion steps while retaining simpler trajectories to reduce capability forgetting.

authors.name: Shuofeng Sun
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Haibin Yan
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: When the Weakest Language Keeps Moving: ARMOR-DP for Multilingual BabyLM
papers.abstract: Multilingual BabyLM systems usually fix language sampling proportions even though the weakest language can change during training. We present ARMOR-DP, a modular framework that diagnoses imbalance arising from representation, exposure, capacity, and objective pressure, and uses per-language validation loss to update sampling. Controlled experiments show that equal character budgets create a severe representation artifact for Chinese; byte-level encoding removes much of it, while static Chinese protection can subsequently make English the weakest language. The dynamic controller tracks these transitions and achieves a better score--balance tradeoff than fixed protection. On official evaluation, curriculum-dynamic checkpoints outperform a matched static Chinese-protective baseline while using fewer Chinese epochs; scaling capacity yields the strongest internal ARMOR-DP system. These results support a simple conclusion: multilingual weakness is a training-time state rather than a fixed property of a language. ARMOR-DP therefore separates diagnosis from intervention, allowing protection to follow the current bottleneck instead of a predetermined language label.

authors.name: Yijing Chen
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A Global Magnetohydrodynamic Simulation of the Birth and Cannibalism of Homologous Coronal Mass Ejections
papers.abstract: Homologous coronal mass ejections (CMEs) are sequential eruptions from the same active region. They are of particular space weather interest because they can interact and coalesce into compound ejecta, potentially amplifying their geomagnetic impact. Yet the full chain from recurrent initiation to magnetic merging has not been captured self-consistently in a single global simulation. We present a three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic model that generates three homologous CMEs from a bipolar active region by recurrent photospheric shearing. All three eruptions follow the same initiation mechanism by tether-cutting reconnection within a recurrently formed sigmoid, while the later CMEs propagate significantly faster than the first. We demonstrate that this speed hierarchy arises from progressive coronal preconditioning; preceding eruptions evacuate the overlying corona, reducing both mass loading and ambient drag. The faster later CMEs catch up with their predecessors, and the compression between them forms inter-CME current sheets. Reconnection within these current sheets then progressively merges the interacting flux systems, completing the cannibalistic process. Synthetic coronagraph images reproduce the apparent coalescence of multiple white-light fronts. This simulation provides the first self-consistent global view of the birth, preconditioning, and cannibalistic interaction of homologous CMEs, bridging recurrent eruption initiation and inter-CME magnetic merging in the near-Sun corona.

papers.title: PreView: Enhancing GUI Grounding with Preprocessed Views and Cues
papers.abstract: GUI grounding requires locating small controls in cluttered screenshots and identifying which control a natural-language instruction refers to. Cropping and enlargement can expose local detail, but the resulting image may still leave ambiguity about the intended target. We propose PreView, an auxiliary preprocessor that improves the inputs to an existing grounding model without further training that model. PreView prepares two complementary types of input features: task-relevant views for localization and candidate-specific cues for target understanding. A trained lightweight auxiliary model predicts and refines a center, crops the screenshot into a local view, and enlarges that view for zoomed-in grounding. It also prepares a visual cue (i.e., a red-circle marker with a location hint) and a textual cue describing the candidate's identity or function. The frozen grounding model uses the prepared inputs to predict the final click. Across five benchmarks, PreView improves the average grounding accuracy of Qwen3-VL-2B, OS-Atlas-4B, and Qwen3-VL-4B without further training these grounding models. Extensive analyses examine the contributions of views and cues, center refinement, and visual input budgets.

authors.name: Wenjun Hou
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Kaishuai Xu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Beijing

papers.title: Approximation algorithms for identical parallel machine scheduling with assignment costs
papers.abstract: We study non-preemptive scheduling on identical parallel machines in which assigning job $j$ to machine $M_i$ incurs the cost $c_{ij}=a_iw_j+b_j$. The processing times $p_j$ and the cost weights $w_j$ are independent, and the number of machines is part of the input. For every fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$ and every deadline $T$ for which a schedule with makespan at most $T$ exists, we give a polynomial-time algorithm that computes a schedule with makespan at most $(1+\varepsilon)T$ whose total assignment cost does not exceed the minimum under the deadline $T$. Using this algorithm as a subroutine, we obtain a polynomial-time approximation scheme for minimizing the makespan under a total cost budget whose schedules always satisfy the budget; this answers an open question for costs $c_{ij}=l_ic_j$ with $c_j$ independent of $p_j$. For the lexicographic problem, in which the total assignment cost is minimized among all schedules of minimum makespan, we obtain in polynomial time a schedule with makespan at most $1+\varepsilon$ times the minimum and total assignment cost at most that of a lexicographically optimal schedule; this improves the makespan guarantees of earlier algorithms for additive and multiplicative costs. For costs $c_{ij}=s_i+a_iw_j$, where $s_i$ is charged for each job processed on $M_i$, the same guarantees are obtained in quasi-polynomial time.

papers.title: Which posets are spectra of Noetherian rings? The case of height at most one
papers.abstract: A finite poset is the prime spectrum of a Noetherian ring exactly when it has no chain of three elements, that is, it is the poset of a finite bipartite graph. This answers Conjecture 5.3 of Alkass. The substance is a construction: minimal elements become curves y=g_i(x), maximal elements points, edges the incidences, arranged by interpolation. The coordinate ring of the union of the curves, localized at the chosen points, is essentially of finite type over Q and of dimension at most one. Dropping finiteness costs two conditions, both isolated by Colbert: a poset with no chain of three elements is a Noetherian spectrum exactly when it has finitely many minimal elements and any two distinct ones have finitely many common upper bounds. A variant keeping the shape of the ideals of Alkass but changing their exponents shows why that construction produces only nested neighborhoods. Constraining the ring destroys most of this freedom: normal rings leave finite disjoint unions of stars, domains a single star, local rings a point or a finite co-star. In height two the question is open in general, but the conditions conjectured by Wiegand and Wiegand are not sufficient

papers.title: EXE: Egocentric Cross-Embodiment Pretraining via Factorized Latent Actions for VLA Models
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are bottlenecked by the scarcity of robot data. Egocentric human manipulation videos offer an abundant, diverse, and semantically-rich alternative that inherently captures manipulation intent. However, the embodiment gap makes it difficult to extract action-relevant representations from these videos. From the perspective of action execution, human hands and robots share analogous manipulation primitives---reaching, grasping, placing---yet exhibit distinct kinematics tied to their embodiments. This might motivate our key approach: egocentric video pretraining can yield shared action representations capturing transferable manipulation skills, while human-specific motion patterns should be disentangled to avoid interfering with robot policy learning. To this end, we propose EXE, an Egocentric Cross(X)-Embodiment pretraining framework that learns a factorized latent action representation from egocentric human videos, separating shared manipulation priors from embodiment-specific signals. By leveraging the shared action space, the robot policy acquires generalizable manipulation semantics from diverse human demonstrations without being biased by human-specific kinematics. This shared knowledge transfers across embodiments with different kinematic structures, enabling the same pretraining to benefit both parallel grippers and dexterous hands. EXE yields consistent gains over baseline without pretraining on RoboTwin 2.0, RoboCasa GR1, and real-world manipulation tasks.

authors.name: Jianyu Chen
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Effects of Synchrotron Self-Absorption on Polarization Diagnostics of MHD Turbulence
papers.abstract: Synchrotron polarization is a powerful tool for diagnosing magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence, yet prior analyses are confined to the optically thin regime, neglecting the effects of synchrotron self-absorption (SSA). Here, we incorporate SSA into the radiative transfer of polarized synchrotron emission and employ 3D MHD turbulence simulations to investigate its impacts on polarization statistics. We show that SSA strongly modulates polarized intensity by suppressing its emission amplitude, steepening its low-frequency power-law slopes, and reducing scale-dependent anisotropy. Notably, SSA does not impede the recovery of the scaling slope of the magnetic turbulence. Our results extend the applicability of synchrotron polarization diagnostics to optically thick astrophysical environments, providing a theoretical foundation for interpreting multi-frequency radio polarization observations. This confirms that polarization statistical techniques remain effective for diagnosing MHD turbulence properties in astrophysical environments where SSA is present.

authors.name: Jian-Fu Zhang
authors.institution: China Iron and Steel Research Institute Group

papers.title: A Necessary and Sufficient Condition for the Existence of Global Smooth Solutions to the One-Dimensional Inviscid Burgers-Vlasov System
papers.abstract: We investigate global smooth solvability for the one-dimensional inviscid Burgers-Vlasov system. For a smooth initial fluid velocity and a nonnegative, compactly supported particle distribution, we establish a sharp necessary and sufficient threshold expressed through the sum of the initial velocity gradient and the initial particle density. The principal difficulty is to control simultaneously the nonlinear steepening of the fluid velocity, the drag coupling, the particle velocity support, and the full hierarchy of derivatives. To overcome it, we introduce a combined gradient-density quantity whose evolution closes along fluid characteristics. Its sign invariance, together with characteristic support estimates and fixed-order derivative bounds, yields global continuation whenever the initial threshold is nonnegative. If the threshold fails at one point, a Riccati comparison gives an explicit finite upper bound for the maximal smooth lifespan and identifies negative velocity-gradient blow-up when this bound is attained. We also use nonnegative regularization and compactness to extend the threshold result to initial data of any fixed finite regularity.

papers.title: Compactness of composition operators on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present a complete characterization of the compactness of arbitrary finite linear combinations of composition operators acting on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees. In particular, we obtain a characterization of compactness for linear combinations satisfying the CNC. As an application, we give an affirmative answer to a conjecture raised by Choe et al. [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. Ser. B 9(2022), 733--756] concerning such Hardy spaces. Furthermore, we establish the phenomenon of (double) difference cancellation for linear combinations of composition operators by constructing explicit examples.

papers.title: Multi-marginal optimal transport on sub-Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study multi-marginal optimal transport on ideal sub-Riemannian manifolds. We establish a sub-Riemannian barycentric balance condition and prove the existence of a solution to the Monge problem under an additional assumption. We also investigate the absolute continuity of Wasserstein barycenters. Our results extend and improve upon those of Pass, Pinamonti, and Vedovato (Methods Appl. Anal. 28 (2021), 61-76) on the Heisenberg group, answering two open questions raised in their work.

papers.title: CVE-to-ATT&CK Mapping via Evidence-Constrained Ranking
papers.abstract:
Mapping CVEs to MITRE ATT&CK techniques helps defenders translate vulnerability information into hypotheses about adversary behavior. Automating this mapping is challenging because relevant evidence is fragmented across heterogeneous security sources. In addition, ATT&CK techniques can be semantically similar, and existing annotations cover a highly long-tailed subset of the technique space. Existing supervised, retrieval-based, and LLM-based approaches therefore face limitations from closed-set supervision, semantic ambiguity, or unconstrained prediction.
  We formulate CVE-to-ATT&CK mapping as multi-evidence constrained ranking. Our framework TRACE first integrates complementary structural and semantic evidence from multiple sources to construct a bounded, high-coverage candidate pool over the complete ATT&CK technique space. It then reranks the retained candidates by combining their accumulated evidence with CVE--technique textual interactions and frequency-aware scoring. We evaluate the framework across six public datasets with different annotation processes and vulnerability distributions. Candidate construction reduces the 201-technique ATT&CK search space by approximately 60% while retaining at least one ground-truth technique for 95.11%-100% of CVEs. These results show that combining heterogeneous security evidence with constrained ranking provides a more controlled and generalizable bridge from vulnerability information to adversary behavior.

papers.title: On 2-Arc-Transitive Cayley Graphs of Nonabelian Characteristically Simple Groups
papers.abstract: The classification of symmetric Cayley graphs has attracted considerable attention. Results have been obtained for finite abelian groups and nonabelian simple groups. However, the problem remains open for finite nonabelian characteristically simple groups, although some results on normality for small valencies are known. In this paper, we determine the possible structures of automorphism groups $X$ of connected 2-arc-transitive Cayley graphs $\Gamma$ of $G\cong T^k$, where $T$ is a finite nonabelian simple group and $k\geqslant2$. In the quasiprimitive case, we prove that $G\unlhd X$, $\Gamma$ is complete, or $X$ is of product action type with restricted parameters. For the non-quasiprimitive case, we determine the possible structures of the quasiprimitive normal quotients of $\Gamma$.

papers.title: The Golomb--Welch conjecture for lattice tilings
papers.abstract: We prove the Golomb--Welch conjecture for lattice tilings: for every $n\ge3$ and $r\ge2$, the integer lattice $\Z^n$ admits no lattice tiling by Lee balls $B_n(r)$ of radius $r$. Together with the classical constructions for $n\le2$ and for $r=1$, this determines all parameters for which a lattice Lee tiling exists. Equivalently, we show that every abelian Cayley graph of even degree $2n\ge6$ and diameter $r\ge2$ has strictly fewer than $|B_n(r)|$ vertices.

authors.name: Gaojun Luo
authors.institution: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology

papers.title: Detecting and Understanding Ambiguity in Visualizations with Role-Playing Vision Language Model Interpretations
papers.abstract: Communicative visualizations can support multiple chart-grounded takeaways, including divergent or conflicting ones; we refer to this variation as interpretive ambiguity. Such ambiguity can undermine a visualization's communicative goal when the supported takeaways diverge from its intended message. Evaluating visualizations with target audiences can surface this variation, but such evaluations can be costly and difficult to scale. In this work, we explore persona-conditioned Vision Language Models (VLMs) as a complementary evaluation tool for interpretive ambiguity. For a given visualization, our pipeline uses topic-relevant personas to elicit candidate contextual takeaways supported by interpretations of perceived visual patterns, such as trends and clusters. We derive a Target--Pattern--Scope framework for comparing these interpretations, use LLM judges to assign Compatible, Disjoint, or Opposing ambiguity labels to statement pairs, and summarize their distribution in an ambiguity profile. To improve chart grounding, we benchmark candidate VLMs on chart comprehension and select the highest-performing model for each chart type. We evaluate statement-pair labeling against human-authored annotations and apply the approach to real-world, public-facing visualizations curated from established datasets. Through case studies, we examine how perceived visual patterns relate to contextual takeaways and how a visualization redesign changes the sampled interpretations. Our findings show how persona-conditioned VLMs can complement human feedback by generating candidate contextual takeaways and surfacing potential ambiguity for further inspection.

papers.title: Integrable distortion II: the p-Weil-Petersson variational problem
papers.abstract:
We study the hyperbolically weighted distortion energies \[
  \mathcal{I}_p(f)=\int_\mathbb{D}
  \frac{|\mu_f|^p}{(1-|\mu_f|^2)^{\max\{2,p\}/2}}\,dA_\eta \] for finite-distortion disk homeomorphisms with prescribed boundary values, together with the associated inverse problem in the monotone Sobolev class. For $1<p\leq2$, the inverse density is polyconvex precisely when $p\geq p_{\mathrm c}=1+1/\sqrt2$. In this range, quasisymmetric data with finite-energy monotone barriers yield minimisers with holomorphic Ahlfors--Hopf differentials and strong local Sobolev convergence of minimising subsequences.
  For $p_{\mathrm c}<p<2$, a finite-energy finite-distortion barrier yields a unique absolute monotone minimiser, which is a quasiconformal diffeomorphism and is asymptotically conformal. Together with the boundary-class theorem of Part~I, this characterises the admissible boundary data as $T^p$. The proof combines a selected barrier approximation, uniform scalar gradient estimates and a weighted Reich--Strebel comparison.
  For $1<p<p_{\mathrm c}$, finite rank-one comparisons bound distortion on the positive-Jacobian set by a cutoff strictly below the ellipticity cutoff. An attained monotone minimum is either a quasiconformal diffeomorphism or has nonzero rank-one derivatives on a set of positive area. For $0<p\leq1$, minimisers with finite distortion, or homeomorphic minimisers with a locally Sobolev inverse, are M\"obius maps. We also obtain energy-dependent quasiconformal bounds for regular minimisers when $p>2$. \

authors.name: Gaven Martin
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: Uniqueness of radial bound states for an equation with an odd cubic-like nonlinearity
papers.abstract:
We investigate radial bound states with prescribed nodes for the odd cubic equation \[
  \Delta u+u(\abs{u}-b)(c-\abs{u})=0
  \quad\text{in }\R^n,\qquad n\ge2,\quad 0<b<c. \] Writing $a=b/c$, we prove that a radial bound state with exactly $k\ge1$ simple zeros and positive central value exists if and only if $0<a<1/2$. For each $k$, this solution is unique for all $0<a<1/2$ in dimension two, for $a\ge(7-3\sqrt5)/2$ in dimension three, and for $a\ge(43-5\sqrt{33})/32$ in dimension four. For one node, we identify exact ranges obtained from a tangent comparison and a quotient inequality in every dimension $n\ge3$; the threshold is dimension-independent for $3\le n\le23$ and is characterized implicitly for $n\ge24$. These results address the natural odd counterpart of the cubic nonlinearity highlighted in Tang's prescribed-node uniqueness conjecture [M. Tang, \emph{Invent. Math.}, 2026]. The main challenges are the second positive zero of the cubic source, the lack of a global comparison inequality, and supercritical cubic growth in higher dimensions. We overcome them by an amplitude confinement argument, controlled extensions preserving sharp comparison estimates, and a subcritical truncation for existence. A complementary small-$a$ uniqueness range in dimensions three to five follows from a recent massive double-power result.

papers.title: Distributional Counterfactual Dependence in the Special Sciences
papers.abstract: Special-science explanations often concern distributions rather than individual outcomes. Since higher-level states depend on lower-level processes, what would make a higher-level explanation redundant? I argue that redundancy requires replacement without loss, not merely a reconstruction of individual outcomes. Distributional counterfactual dependence (DCD) identifies how changes in higher-level conditions alter an outcome distribution or a relevant feature of it. Against the background of stochastic supervenience, I distinguish this explanatory role from the dependence of higher-level states on lower-level bases. A replacement must be specified independently of the distribution to be explained and preserve the same counterfactual pattern at the grain and across the conditions relevant to the question. Applications to wage distributions, cognitive load, and selection clarify this requirement. A hypothetical comparison shows how a lower-level model can preserve the explanation and why matching selected outcome statistics may not suffice. DCD thus describes one form of non-reductive explanation that depends on counterfactual organization rather than additional higher-level productive powers.

papers.title: LegoOcc++: Towards Consistent Open-Vocabulary 3D Occupancy Prediction
papers.abstract: Open-vocabulary 3D occupancy prediction is important for embodied agents operating in complex environments whose semantic categories extend beyond fixed taxonomies. While recent studies have explored open-vocabulary occupancy in outdoor driving scenarios, indoor environments remain challenging due to dense occlusions, complex geometry, and fine-grained long-tailed semantics. To reduce the need for expensive voxel-level semantic annotations, we study a geometry-only supervision setting requiring only binary occupancy labels. We build upon Language-Embedded Gaussians as a unified representation coupling 3D geometry with language-aligned semantics. For geometry learning, we introduce an opacity-aware Poisson-based Gaussian-to-Occupancy formulation that enables stable volumetric aggregation under binary occupancy supervision. For semantic learning, we render Gaussian features into images and align them with a frozen open-vocabulary model, together with Progressive Temperature Decay to reduce feature mixing during Gaussian splatting. Building on this framework, we further introduce Instance-Level Semantic Consistency to alleviate fragmented object predictions, and Covisibility-Aware Support-View Selection to provide informative and less redundant multi-view semantic supervision. We also extend our framework to outdoor driving scenarios to evaluate its generality across substantially different environments. Extensive experiments on indoor and outdoor benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves strong open-vocabulary occupancy performance, validating the effectiveness and generality of our framework. Code will be available at https://github.com/JuIvyy/LegoOcc.

authors.name: Yueru Luo
authors.institution: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

papers.title: T2D: Target-to-Draft Model Pruning & Adaptation for Efficient Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Speculative decoding significantly accelerates autoregressive text generation in Large Language Models (LLMs), but its efficacy depends largely on two key factors: the distributional alignment between the draft and the target model, and the draft model's latency during inference. However, existing approaches typically utilize independently pretrained small draft models or seek to prune the target model to a manually chosen architecture, thereby failing to explicitly balance the trade-off between draft model alignment and token generation efficiency. To address this gap, we formulate draft model design as an optimization problem and propose T2D, a framework that constructs draft models directly from the target model using latency-aware structured pruning and knowledge distillation. In this manner, T2D obtains draft models that are jointly optimized for both measured inference latency and cross-entropy loss on the target model's responses, resulting in superlative speculative decoding performance. Through extensive experiments on multi-domain speculative decoding benchmarks and across several target model families of differing scale, we demonstrate how T2D prunes up to 92\% of the target model to obtain highly performant draft models compared to competitive baselines. Moreover, draft models obtained via T2D can also be utilized by other speculative decoding token-alignment and knowledge distillation methods in a plug-and-play fashion, leading to further gains. Our findings underscore the importance of jointly navigating the draft model architecture-alignment frontier to unlock the full potential of speculative decoding for LLMs.

papers.title: Functional Superoscillations in a Wave Processor
papers.abstract: Physical wave processors are constrained by diffraction, but the bandwidth of the mathematical functions they implement need not be set by it. Here, we demonstrate continuous and multiplexed optical processing of superoscillatory functions, in which a scalar argument is encoded onto a wavefront and a fixed diffractive wave processor synthesizes optical responses that approximate the corresponding function outputs in parallel. Unlike conventional superoscillatory optics that generates predetermined fields, superoscillation here is expressed in the input-output dependence on the encoded argument. Its frequencies are therefore distinct from the transverse spatial frequencies of propagating light and are not subject to the same diffraction-imposed cutoff. We demonstrate complex-valued superoscillatory function synthesis and introduce a multiplexed architecture that simultaneously evaluates distinct target superoscillatory functions whose harmonic content exceeds that of the optical input encoding. Visible-light experiments further validate this beyond-encoding superoscillatory regime. Together, these results establish functional superoscillation as a design principle for wave-based computation and show how interference, diffractive depth and spatial channel allocation extend the functional reach of passive wave processors. More broadly, these analyses establish a separation between functional bandwidth and physical wave bandwidth in analog optical computation.

papers.title: Rethinking Retrieval in the Long-Context Era: Training-Free Semantic Trees for Adaptive Context Construction
papers.abstract: Long-context language models can increasingly process entire documents, making full-context prompting a practical alternative to passage retrieval. However, greater capacity determines how much information a model can receive, but not which information best supports a query. This distinction motivates rethinking retrieval: when the full document already fits, can selecting and organizing its evidence improve answering? The challenge is to retain supporting facts and relations while keeping the context focused on the question. To reconcile these goals, we introduce \ours, a training-free framework that uses semantic abstraction to guide selection while retaining original text for answering. \ours constructs a reusable semantic hierarchy from the full document in a single generation, linking node descriptions to source spans. Given a query, structural--semantic scoring and fine-grained lexical attribution nominate shared source nodes; their union with ancestor context preserves structural relations and complete local text. Across four frontier answer models, \ours improves average QA-F1 by 1.72 points over full-context prompting on three LongBench tasks, surpassing the evaluated baselines on the four-model average while reducing answer-context length by 58.55\%. Our code is available at the $\href{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/treefuse-ECFE}{repository}$.

papers.title: Asymptotic behavior of solutions of the compressible MHD equations on the half space
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the global well-posedness and large-time asymptotic behavior of strong solutions to the $n$-dimensional ($n\ge 2$) compressible viscous resistive magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) equations in the upper half-space $\mathbb{R}_+^n$. We impose the standard no-slip boundary condition on the velocity field and two types of physically relevant boundary conditions on the magnetic field: the insulating boundary condition and the perfectly conducting boundary condition. Under the assumption that the initial data are small perturbations of the constant equilibrium state $(\bar{\rho}, \mathbf{0}, \mathbf{0})$, we first establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions in Sobolev spaces by deriving uniform energy estimates and using a bootstrapping argument. Then, by combining the sharp decay estimates of solutions to the corresponding linearized system with Duhamel's principle, we obtain the decay rates of solutions to the nonlinear problem. Specifically, we prove that the solutions decay at the rate $t^{-\frac{n}{2}\left(1-\frac{1}{p}\right)}$ in $L^p$ norm for $2\le p\le\infty$, and we also establish the decay rates of their first-order derivatives. Furthermore, we show that the global solutions converge to the linearized solutions with an improved decay rate as time goes to infinity. Our results extend the classical results of Kagei and Kobayashi \cite{Kagei-Kobayashi2002, Kagei-Kobayashi2005} for the compressible Navier--Stokes equations on the half space to the compressible MHD system with both insulating and perfectly conducting boundary conditions.

papers.title: Timing Matters Twice: When to Query and When to Skip in Flow-Matching On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract:
On-policy distillation (OPD) enables flow-matching models to acquire complementary capabilities from specialized teachers through supervision on student-generated trajectories. However, different evaluation dimensions, such as aesthetics and OCR accuracy, and different tasks, such as image generation and editing, emphasize different aspects of the denoising process, suggesting that their effective supervision may occur at different stages. Existing methods typically select supervision states from predefined timestep distributions, which may overlook these phase-dependent differences and incur unnecessary computational overhead. This motivates two critical timing decisions: when to adaptively query teachers for effective supervision based on the evolving generative process, and when to skip the remaining rollout to avoid redundant computation.
  In this paper, we introduce PhaseOPD, a phase-aware query-and-skip framework that identifies generative phases online from revisions of predicted-clean latents, using existing student velocity predictions without additional model evaluations. For each task-assigned teacher, PhaseOPD selects a supervision state based on its phase preference and skips the unused rollout suffix once all query decisions are finalized, preserving the single-query velocity-distillation objective. On SD3.5-M, PhaseOPD executes only 5.56 of 16 rollout positions per local batch, reducing training time by 41.3% relative to DanceOPD while improving Aesthetic, GenEval, and OCR scores.

papers.title: Crossed modularity of twisted VOA modules
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a strongly rational vertex operator algebra and $G\leq\operatorname{Aut}(V)$ a finite group. Using the $G$-crossed braided fusion structure of twisted modules constructed in \cite{Crossed}, we prove that the conformal twist $e^{2\pi iL(0)}$ gives a crossed ribbon structure and that the crossed category is modular in Kirillov's sense. Consequently, its equivariantization is a modular tensor category. We also obtain dimension and simple-object counting formulas for the twisted sectors.

papers.title: Numerical Construction of Quasi-Periodic Solutions for Nonlinear PDEs: II. Unbounded Perturbation
papers.abstract: Many nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) arising in physical models involve unbounded perturbations, where nonlinear terms contain spatial derivatives. Such perturbations can be expressed as compositions of unbounded operators with bounded nonlinear maps. In this paper, we propose alternating numerical schemes for constructing quasi-periodic solutions to this class of PDEs, including the nonlinear acoustic wave (NLAW) equation and the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation. To render the nonlinear perturbations bounded, we apply inverse differential operators as a preconditioning; this, however, also rescales the linear part by polynomial factors in the spatial mode $n$. Two main difficulties arise. The first is to control the measure of the resulting ``bad'' frequencies, since the bounds on the measures of the excluded frequency sets are enlarged by polynomial factors in $n$; we show that this measure nevertheless remains small. The second concerns resonances involving the perturbed eigenvalues of the linearized operator at large scales. Our key observation is that, when the dispersive frequencies grow polynomially in $n$ with degree greater than one, such resonances cannot occur if the magnitude of the temporal index lies below a threshold proportional to $|n|$ raised to one less than that degree. It therefore suffices to consider the complementary regime, in which the growth induced by the unbounded perturbation can be controlled in terms of the temporal index. At large scales, an additional complication arises: for a given spatial index $n$, all temporal indices in a box may be ``bad''. We show, however, that at each scale there is at most one such spatial index. Consequently, the resulting counting loss is only polynomial and can be absorbed into the exponential-logarithmic threshold, allowing us once again to retain control over the measures of the excluded frequency sets.

authors.name: Mingwei Fu
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Axion Quasibound States in the Continuum and Their Enhanced Axion Nonlinearity
papers.abstract: Dynamical axion quasiparticles (DAQs) in condensed-matter systmes have emerged as a fascinating platform for exploring axion physics and nonlinear optical phenomena. However, the amplitude of the coherent oscillating $\theta$ field is even smaller than that of the static counterpart, making the experimental observation of DAQs particularly challenging. Here, we introduce symmetry-sensitive bound states in the continuum (BICs) physics to enable the all-optical detection of DAQs and enhance DAQ-mediated second-harmonic generation (SHG). Specifically, we uncover that DAQs induce optical shear that breaks the $C_{2z}$ symmetry of metagratings without geometric engineering, thereby converting symmetry-protected BICs into axion quasi-BICs (qBICs). In this context, the evolution of the quality factor and topological charge in momentum space, together with the appearance of optical resonances in far field associated with axion qBICs, offers achiral optical signatures for DAQ detection beyond the widely used Kerr and Faraday effects. Furthermore, by exploiting axion qBICs in the critical coupling regime to enhance fundamental optical field, we show that the SHG efficiency can be enhanced more than $10^5$-fold compared to bulk axion materials, achieving a conversion efficiency exceeding $10^{-6}~W^{-1}$. The SHG is governed by the magnetoelectric coupling, which differs from that in conventional SHG materials. Our findings establish a new approach for probing DAQs via achiral optical effects, while providing a versatile route for reconfigurable photonics and terahertz nonlinear optics.

papers.title: Necessary and Sufficient Conditions for Adaptive Stabilizability of Continuous-Time Markov Jump Linear Stochastic Systems
papers.abstract: The purpose of this paper is to provide a mathematically rigorous solution to a well-known problem in stochastic adaptive control, i.e., to find the weakest possible structural condition for global stabilizability of continuous-time Markov jump linear stochastic systems with known candidate modes but with an unobservable Markov parameter process. Under some regularity assumptions, it is shown that the necessary and sufficient condition for global adaptive stabilizability hinges on the solvability of the same coupled Riccati equations as in the non-adaptive case. This result highlights a fundamental difference between the continuous-time case considered here and the discrete-time case studied earlier by Xue and Guo (2001), in which the coupled Riccati equations for adaptive and non-adaptive stabilizability are different.

authors.name: Ziwei Guo
authors.institution: China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences

papers.title: Sharp gradient comparison and rigidity for semilinear equations on manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove sharp amplitude and gradient comparisons for positive solutions of a class of semilinear elliptic equations on complete manifolds under a Ricci lower bound. Equality at one point characterizes hyperbolic space and the corresponding radial solution. The local estimates are uniform in the mixing coefficients and number of terms for positive mixtures of subcritical powers. For a class of conformal compactifications defined by a source equation, we obtain sharp boundary scalar-curvature bounds and hyperbolic rigidity. We also construct non-Einstein examples whose normalization persists under small compactly supported metric perturbations.

papers.title: Quasicircularity of the Zakeri Curve and Capture Component Boundaries
papers.abstract: For a fixed irrational rotation number of bounded type, we prove that the locus of critically marked cubic polynomials whose two critical points lie on the boundary of the fixed Siegel disk is a quasicircle. This locus is known as the Zakeri curve. The main step is a boundary correspondence lemma for holomorphic families of disks with uniformly quasiconformal extensions. We further prove that every capture component in this family is a quasidisk, including components attached to the Zakeri curve.

papers.title: ESPC-Transolver: An Equivalent-Surface Physics-Guided Coupling-Aware Transolver for 3D Multiple Scattering
papers.abstract: Cross-geometry generalization is particularly challenging because geometry-conditioned multiple-scattering surrogates must infer unseen objects' scattering properties from geometric features while accurately capturing complex, phase-sensitive interactions arising from repeated wave exchange. We introduce ESPC-Transolver, an equivalent-surface physics-guided, coupling-aware Transolver that separates local scattering-response representations from inter-object interaction modeling. For each sound-hard scatterer, canonical scattered-pressure responses are constructed under a shared set of spherical-wave excitations. A local Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) map and modal scattering conversion express these responses on an enclosing sphere, providing physically consistent input channels across geometries. Shared object-local Transolver blocks encode these responses and incident-field traces, while relative-position-aware slice attention models inter-object coupling. Predicted interface pressure and normal flux recovered from the local operator define equivalent sources for reconstructing exterior near- and far-field scattering. We evaluate the method on three-dimensional acoustic multiple-scattering problems at a fixed frequency, comparing it with geometry-conditioned predictors and alternative neural network backbones. ESPC-Transolver achieves lower scattered-field prediction errors on held-out instances of familiar geometry families and generalizes effectively to previously unseen Peanut and Torus geometries. Exterior-field reconstructions reproduce multiple-scattering interference patterns, linking cross-geometry interface prediction to near-field pressure and far-field scattering recovery.

papers.title: Clifford-weighted residues, partial spectral curvature, and torsion
papers.abstract: We study Clifford-weighted noncommutative residues associated with Dirac operators and connections. On closed spin manifolds a double commutator of the square of the Dirac operator, paired with a Clifford commutator, recovers the localized Riemann curvature tensor. We prove presentation independence for its extension to arbitrary classical one-forms, recompute four-Clifford functionals, and give explicit Weyl, Schouten and Einstein curvature combinations. For spectral triples with an admissible residue calculus we define a partial spectral curvature functional on two arbitrary represented one-forms and two exact represented one-forms. Its well-definedness is distinguished from module tensoriality: explicit flat noncommutative-torus computations exhibit both a failure of general presentation descent and nonzero partial pairings. A connection-based curvature pairing provides a separate construction, including noncentral pure Clifford-degree-two examples. We also derive ordered first- and second-derivative torsion residues on free torus modules and prove an obstruction to ordinary alternation for unrestricted noncentral inputs. All constants, coefficient orders and hypotheses are kept explicit.

papers.title: Asymptotic Rank of Complete Graph Tensors
papers.abstract:
Graph tensors extend the matrix multiplication tensor by placing a two-party identity tensor on every edge of a graph and keeping one tensor leg at every vertex. We study the asymptotic rank of the tensor associated with the complete graph. For every integer $n\geq 2$, over the complex numbers, we prove
  \[
  \left\lfloor\frac{n^2}{4}\right\rfloor
  \leq \log_2\widetilde R\bigl(\mathsf{GT}_2(K_n)\bigr)
  \leq \frac{n^2}{4}.
  \] The upper bound matches the maximum-cut lower bound for every even $n$ and differs from it by only $1/4$ for every odd $n$. In particular, the exponent per edge is below $2/3$ for every $n\geq5$, answering a question of Christandl, Vrana, and Zuiddam.
  Our proof extends the polynomial multiplication approach underlying OpenAI's bound $\omega\leq9/4$. The main step separates any fixed number of shared tensor legs simultaneously, using only linearly many direct-sum copies in the number of blocks. This yields an entropy inequality for higher-order tensors. We apply it to the tensor for multiplying $n-1$ polynomials, whose rank is linear in the input length. Discrete concavity and a shifted tripling inequality then force a lower bound on a symmetrized spectral profile. Comparing this growth with polynomial interpolation gives the stated upper bound while preserving all $n$ tensor legs.
  We also prove an operational barrier for these higher-order polynomial constructions. For $n\geq3$, the specified formal reduction rules cannot certify an exponent below $n^2/4$ for $\mathsf{GT}_2(K_n)$, even after taking tensor powers and allowing subexponential overhead and common auxiliary factors. This extends the symmetric three-leg barrier of Amanov, van den Berg, and Zuiddam and explains the remaining gap for odd complete graphs within this method.

papers.title: RIS-Assisted Downlink Pinching-Antenna Systems With NLOS Environments
papers.abstract: This paper investigates a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted downlink pinching-antenna system (PASS) in the presence of non-line-of-sight (NLOS) users caused by unavoidable obstacles. An RIS is deployed to extend the coverage of the physically constrained PASS by establishing virtual line-of-sight (LOS) links. To improve system performance, we propose a zero-forcing (ZF) beamforming-based alternating optimization (AO) framework that minimizes the transmit power by jointly optimizing the RIS reflection coefficients and pinching-antenna (PA) activation positions. Specifically, the RIS reflection coefficients are optimized using the Riemannian conjugate gradient (RCG) method, while a novel projected gradient-based method is developed to efficiently optimize the PA activation positions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed AO framework outperforms baseline schemes in terms of both transmit power and computational efficiency under different system configurations including the rate requirements and RIS sizes.

authors.name: Yue Geng
authors.institution: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology

papers.title: The Golomb--Welch conjecture for arbitrary centre sets
papers.abstract:
We prove that for all $n\ge3$ and $r\ge2$, the Lee ball $B_n(r)$ does not
  tile $\Z^n$ by translations, resolving the Golomb--Welch conjecture for
  arbitrary centre sets and completing the existence classification of
  perfect Lee codes in $\Z^n$.
  The proof combines translation-invariant averaging, boundary contact
  identities, and integer moment inequalities with coefficient comparisons
  in stable symmetric functions.
  Consequently, we obtain finite local obstructions, strict Banach density
  gaps for packings and coverings, and the nonexistence of exact measurable
  Lee-ball towers.
  In the lattice specialization, our result classifies the attainability of
  the Lee bound for even-degree abelian Cayley graphs, excludes normal
  topological coverings and Galois graph coverings for Lee-ball completions,
  and gives a strict node bound for lattice cubature as well as the
  nonexistence of subgroup-indexed orthogonal exponential bases on $B_n(r)$.

authors.name: Gaojun Luo
authors.institution: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology

papers.title: Universal Scaling of the Little-Parks Oscillation Amplitude
papers.abstract: The Little-Parks effect played a pivotal role in establishing fluxoid quantization in doubly connected superconductors and providing early evidence for electron pairing, central to BCS theory. More recently, it has emerged as an important phase-sensitive probe of superconducting order. Yet the amplitude of the Little-Parks oscillation has never been fully understood theoretically, as the conventional mean-field Ginzburg-Landau description does not account for its pronounced temperature dependence. Here, we develop a universal theoretical framework incorporating thermal fluctuations in reduced-dimensional superconducting rings. By analyzing Little-Parks measurements across multiple superconductors, we show that the resulting scaling quantitatively captures the temperature-dependent oscillation amplitudes over a broad range of materials and device geometries, resolving the long-standing discrepancy between theory and experiment.

authors.name: Yufan Li
authors.institution: National Health and Family Planning Commission

papers.title: A geometric construction of supercuspidal representations
papers.abstract: We extend the framework of deep level Deligne-Lusztig varieties to the case of arbitrary residue characteristics $p > 0$. As an application, we provide a construction of a large class of (new) supercuspidal representations for unramified $p$-adic groups with arbitrary residue fields, in a purely geometric way.

papers.title: Fermionic superfluid transition and pairing scale separation in the kagome flat band
papers.abstract: Flat-band systems provide a promising platform for exploring exotic correlated phases owing to quenched kinetic energy and enhanced interaction effects. In this work, we investigate the flat-band superfluid transition in the attractive kagome Hubbard model using large-scale determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations accelerated by fast Fourier transforms and delay updates. Through systematic calculations of the transition temperature, spin susceptibility, and density compressibility, we establish the finite-temperature phase diagram at the flat-band filling $\rho=5/3$ and find a clear linear scaling of the superfluid transition temperature with the interaction strength, $T_{\mathrm{c}}=0.0314|U|$. Our results reveal a wide separation of temperature scales between local pair formation and global phase coherence, which stabilizes a broad intermediate supercompressible bosonic fluid region of preformed pairs that bridges the normal Fermi gas and the flat-band superfluid. We further demonstrate that both the transition temperature and density compressibility are significantly enhanced in the flat band compared to van Hove fillings. Our findings highlight the essential role of flat-band-enhanced pair-density fluctuations in separating the pairing and phase-coherence scales, offering clear experimental signatures for probing flat-band superfluidity and superconductivity in cold-atom and kagome-material platforms.

papers.title: Lie Symmetry-Guided Adaptive Sampling for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have emerged as a promising mesh-free framework for solving partial differential equations (PDEs), with broad applications in physics, engineering, and medicine. However, their performance is highly sensitive to the sampling strategy for training points. Conventional uniform sampling often fails to adequately resolve regions with complex solution features, leading to low efficiency and limited accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose a Lie symmetry-driven adaptive sampling framework for PINNs, termed Lie-AS-ISC. For PDEs admitting Lie symmetry groups, symmetry transformations are exploited to derive intrinsic functional relationships between the solution and its variables, enabling the construction of basis points with exact solutions that span the solution domain. Building on this, an adaptive sampling strategy is developed by jointly considering absolute error and invariant surface conditions, while a dual-index loss is introduced to enhance training constraints. The proposed method significantly improves prediction accuracy. The experimental results show that this method consistently outperforms existing methods in accuracy.

papers.title: Tight Coreset Bounds for Euclidean $(k,z)$-Clustering
papers.abstract: We study the optimal coreset size for Euclidean $(k,z)$-clustering, where $z\ge1$ is fixed. Huang, Li, and Wu (STOC 2024) proved a lower bound of $\Omega_z(k\varepsilon^{-z-2})$ for $\varepsilon\gtrsim_z k^{-1/(z+2)}$, matching the known upper bound up to polylogarithmic factors. For $0<\varepsilon<k^{-1/(z+2)}$, the upper bound $\widetilde O_z(k^{(2z+2)/(z+2)}\varepsilon^{-2})$ remained unmatched. The previous lower bounds gave only $\Omega_z(\max\{k\varepsilon^{-2},k^{(2z+3)/(z+2)}\varepsilon^{-1}\})$. We close this gap by proving a matching lower bound throughout $0<\varepsilon<k^{-1/(z+2)}$, including arbitrarily small $\varepsilon$. Together with known bounds, this determines the optimal worst-case coreset size as $$ \widetilde\Theta_z\!\left(\min\left\{k^{(2z+2)/(z+2)}\varepsilon^{-2},\,k\varepsilon^{-z-2}\right\}\right) $$ for every integer $k\ge1$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$. In particular, the bounds are $\widetilde\Theta(k^{4/3}\varepsilon^{-2})$ for $k$-median when $\varepsilon<k^{-1/3}$, and $\widetilde\Theta(k^{3/2}\varepsilon^{-2})$ for $k$-means when $\varepsilon<k^{-1/4}$. Our construction uses projection levels to encode four-wise independent signs, allowing $k$ centers to detect omissions regardless of how the retained points are reweighted.

authors.name: Jian Li
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: The ascending chain condition for radical well-mixed difference ideals
papers.abstract: We establish a finite-basis theorem for radical well-mixed difference ideals in a difference polynomial ring with one endomorphism over an arbitrary difference field. The result extends to every finitely difference-generated difference algebra over such a field and is equivalent to the ascending chain condition for radical well-mixed difference ideals, hence resolving a long-standing open problem in difference algebra. The proof proceeds in two stages. Over an inversive difference coefficient field, we establish a uniform inverse-transform bound relating the perfect closure of a finite system to its radical well-mixed closure. This uses Noetherian induction in a fixed truncated polynomial ring, together with generic freeness and going-down for flat ring homomorphisms. We then prove that the radical well-mixed closure of a system over a difference field $K$ is the contraction of its radical well-mixed closure over the inversive closure of $K$. This contraction result follows from successive prime lifting along flat extensions and removes the inversiveness assumption without requiring the coefficient-field extension to be finitely generated.

papers.title: A Levi-form criterion for Oka complements
papers.abstract: We prove that if $M$ is a connected Stein manifold of complex dimension at least three with the density property, then $M\setminus K$ is a connected Oka manifold for every nonempty compact $K\Subset M$ with smooth boundary whose Levi form has at least two nonnegative eigenvalues at every boundary point for local defining functions negative on $\operatorname{int}K$. For compact sets in $\mathbb{C}^n$ with smooth boundary, this settles both implications between pseudoconvexity of $\partial K$ and the Oka property of $\mathbb{C}^n\setminus K$: pseudoconvexity is sufficient but not necessary for $n\geq3$, and necessary but not sufficient for $n=2$. In dimension two, we give an explicit compact set in $\mathbb{C}^2$ with strongly pseudoconvex boundary and non-Oka complement.

papers.title: Spectra, Growth, and Localization in Half-Bounded Tensor Triangular Geometry
papers.abstract: Over a noetherian scheme, classical cohomological support determines thick tensor ideals of perfect complexes. In half-bounded derived categories, complexes with the same support can generate different radical thick tensor ideals. We study how these distinctions affect the Balmer spectrum and localization. For a commutative noetherian ring $R$, we prove that $\operatorname{Spc}(\mathbf D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(R))$ is noetherian if and only if $R$ is artinian. For a nonempty noetherian scheme $X$, the corresponding condition is $\dim X=0$. For such a ring $R$ and a finite group $G$, $\operatorname{Spc}(\mathbf D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(RG))$ is noetherian if and only if $R$ is artinian and $|G|$ is invertible in $R$. Using the Sanders--Zhang classification over a discrete valuation ring, we compare objects whose annihilator exponents grow at different rates in different degrees. We lift the relevant generation relations before changing coefficients and obtain spectral retractions. These comparisons persist after thick quotients and algebraic localization under explicit uniform annihilation and nonvanishing conditions. A second argument uses nonnilpotent classes of positive degree and passes from cyclic subgroups to finite groups. Applications include relative results for schemes and bounded-below spectra with degreewise finitely generated homotopy. We also describe the cohomological information shared by the resulting ideals. The localization comparisons for bounded-below complexes of finitely generated modules and for bounded-below derived objects with finitely generated cohomology are established separately.

papers.title: The Price of Scale in Proactive Memory Recall
papers.abstract: A long-lived assistant that brings up memories without being asked must decide at every turn whether anything in its store is worth an interruption.
