We show that this decision is a multiple-testing problem whose difficulty grows with the store size $N$. On streaming replays of LongMemEval and LoCoMo, a similarity threshold tuned to 5% false alarms at $N=8$ reaches 87-100% at $N=2048$, across embedding models and for explicit and implicit cues; LLM judges show the same growth from a lower base. We prove that a gate with false-alarm rate $\alpha$ operates at a per-item false-positive rate of about $-\ln(1-\alpha)/N$, which pins its hit rate to the far left of the single-comparison ROC curve and, under regular variation, makes it decay as a power of $N$ with an explicit constant. The resulting prediction matches the hit rate of a per-$N$ oracle threshold to within one percentage point. The analysis explains why lexical and semantic channels need thresholds growing like $\ln N$ and $\sqrt{\ln N}$, and why per-cue normalisation roughly doubles the hit rate at matched false alarms. A cue-swap conformal gate, which compares the current cue with the user's other cues on the same store, needs no labels and has a finite-sample false-alarm guarantee under exchangeability; on LongMemEval it holds false alarms near 5% at the hit rate of a label-tuned threshold. Three annotators (Fleiss' $\kappa=0.63$) find that about nine in ten false alarms are genuine interruptions. Code and data: https://github.com/RiverChenStillCompiling/price-of-scale

papers.title: A 1.932 Guarantee for (r,Q) Policies in Continuous-Review Lost-Sales Inventory Systems
papers.abstract: We provide a uniform guarantee for a continuous-review lost-sales inventory system with unit Poisson demand, deterministic lead time, and fixed ordering costs: a simple algorithm computes an $(r,Q)$ policy and chooses between that policy and no replenishment, with cost at most $(\sqrt2+\sqrt6)/2<1.932$ times the unrestricted nonanticipative optimum. The algorithm starts by generating an optimal integer base-stock policy, which at zero setup cost achieves the tight worst-case factor $\sqrt2$ relative to the optimal system cost. For positive setup costs, it uses the reorder point of this integer base-stock policy and an integer lot at the economic order quantity scale. The inclusion of ordinary base stock in the continuous-review capped base-stock family also improves that family's earlier asymptotic $1.79$ upper guarantee to a uniform $\sqrt2$ guarantee valid at every finite parameter vector. To establish these guarantees, we construct a computable lower bound on the zero-setup optimal cost by tracking units already on hand or committed for delivery. We then combine it with a bound on holding and setup costs required by batching to obtain the general-setup guarantee and instance-specific performance bounds for any admissible replenishment policy. In our numerical study, the largest estimated policy-cost-to-lower-bound ratios are about $1.59$ for our heuristic $(r, Q)$ policy and $1.47$ after joint optimization of $r$ and $Q$. The heuristic also performs well against the optimized policy: over the sampled instances, its median extra cost ranges from $2.33\%$ to $3.91\%$, depending on the setup cost.

papers.title: Finiteness theorems for trace Euclidean quadratic lattices over totally real number fields
papers.abstract: Motivated by Clark's work on Euclidean quadratic forms, we introduce trace Euclidean and house Euclidean quadratic lattices over totally real number fields, and relate these concepts through the $p$-norm Euclidean property. We prove that, as $F$ varies over all totally real number fields of arbitrary degree, there are only finitely many positive definite trace Euclidean $\mathcal{O}_{F}$-lattices of arbitrary rank $n\ge1$, up to isometry. For every $p\in[1,\infty]$, the same finiteness holds for positive definite $p$-norm Euclidean lattices. We also classify all positive definite trace Euclidean lattices of rank one over real quadratic fields: there are exactly six isometry classes, and every such lattice is free. As a corollary, the trace Euclidean real quadratic fields are precisely $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2})$, $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$, and $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{13})$.

papers.title: A proof of the Grothendieck join-meet positivity

authors.name: Mingyang Kang
authors.institution: Second Affiliated Hospital of Jilin University

papers.title: Abelian quotients and orbit sizes for subgroups of linear groups
papers.abstract: Keller and Yang formulated two conjectures relating abelian quotients of subgroups of finite linear groups to largest orbit sizes. After counterexamples were found to the original conjectures, two revised versions were proposed. We prove both revised conjectures for every finite group $G$ satisfying $F(G)=F^*(G)$. We also extend a regular-orbit theorem for nilpotent subgroups to completely reducible modules of mixed characteristic under the same hypothesis.

papers.title: Local Reflexivity and Exactness for Reduced $C^*$-Algebras of Wreath Products
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every countable non-exact discrete group $H$ and every nontrivial countable discrete group $K$, the reduced group $C^*$-algebra $C_r^*(K\wr H)$ is not locally reflexive. These provide the first known examples of non-locally reflexive reduced group $C^*$-algebras, settling a longstanding existence question. Moreover, for every nontrivial countable exact discrete group $K$, we establish that local reflexivity of $C_r^*(K\wr H)$ is equivalent to exactness of $H$, and hence to exactness of $C_r^*(K\wr H)$. This gives a partial affirmative answer to Kirchberg's question of whether local reflexivity implies exactness for $C^*$-algebras. As applications, we construct finitely generated groups with the Haagerup property, as well as finitely generated residually finite groups, whose reduced group $C^*$-algebras are not locally reflexive. In particular, neither the Haagerup property nor coarse embeddability into Hilbert space guarantees local reflexivity of the associated reduced group $C^*$-algebra.

papers.title: Unconditional uniqueness for the cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation in $H^{1/2}(\Bbb T^3)$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish unconditional uniqueness for the cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation (NLS) in the scaling-critical class $H^{1/2}(\mathbb{T}^3)$. Unlike approaches based on the GP-hierarchy or normal form reductions, which typically involve higher-order expansions, our proof works directly with the original cubic NLS, where we also make use of several new a priori Euclidean-like Strichartz estimates. More precisely, we show that every distributional solution in $C_tH_x^{1/2}$ belongs a priori to the class $L^2_{t,\mathrm{loc}}L_x^6$. The key ingredients are a suitable high-low modulation decomposition and the compactness of solution trajectories on bounded time intervals. We also exploit the preservation of the canonical symplectic form under the truncated NLS flow, in order to obtain necessary stability estimates in the rough Sobolev space $H^{-1/2}(\mathbb{T}^3)$.

papers.title: Learning by Confusion Locates a Parametrization-Dependent Fisher Information Maximum
papers.abstract: Learning by confusion (LBC) is a machine-learning method for locating phase transitions without assuming a known order parameter. Its characteristic accuracy curve contains a central maximum that is interpreted as the transition point, but what determines the location and finite-size scaling of this maximum has remained unclear. We derive an exact balance condition for the Bayes-optimal confusion peak and show that, for equilibrium systems with a single swept parameter, the peak closely follows the maximum of the corresponding Fisher information. This immediately gives its finite-size scaling and reveals an unexpected dependence on how the data are sampled: the same configurations arranged on grids uniform in $T$, $\ln T$, or $\beta=1/T$ can yield different finite-size pseudocritical trajectories. Tests on the Ising, Blume-Capel, Potts, and Baxter-Wu models confirm the prediction across continuous, tricritical, and first-order transitions. Our results identify the statistical quantity measured by LBC and show that finite-size machine-learning estimates can depend on the parametrization of the training data as well as on the underlying physics.

papers.title: Performance Guarantees for Permissionless Lending
papers.abstract: We propose a lending protocol with far fewer risks than existing pool-based lending protocols (e.g., Aave, Compound). In our protocol, lenders and borrowers embody the spirit of decentralization by making competing interest-rate offers, resulting in the discovery of the prevailing interest rate through t\^atonnement-like dynamics as opposed to taking rates partly determined by a central authority (e.g., Aave, Federal Reserve). We eliminate the risk of manipulation by creating loans with a fixed interest rate throughout the loan---like US Treasury bills. In particular, we further derive performance guarantees probabilities of repayment shortfall and liquidation by modeling the value of the collateral as a random walk, thus allowing participants to more efficiently manage their risk. To do so, we use characteristic functions and Fourier inversion to derive exact integral representations of the liquidation and repayment shortfall probabilities under the most general assumptions. We illustrate empirically this method by using Bitcoin as collateral and fitting its historical prices to Gaussian, Student-$t$, and symmetric stable Paretian distributions.

papers.title: Liouville theorems for the stationary Navier-Stokes equations under partial component conditions
papers.abstract: We prove Liouville theorems for smooth stationary incompressible Navier-Stokes flows in $R^3$ with finite Dirichlet integral and velocity vanishing uniformly at infinity. If the partial components of velocity $(u_1,u_2)$ belong to $L^{4,\infty}$, then we show that $u$ must vanish. The second result only requires that one component $u_1$ belongs to $L^{3/2,\infty}$. The proofs are based on the head-pressure sign and a localized energy identity, combined with different pressure estimates for the two cases.

papers.title: Text Is the Bottleneck: A Small-Scale Replication of LLM Game Playing in Riichi Mahjong
papers.abstract: We replicate the riichi-mahjong track of "Can Large Language Models Master Complex Card Games?" (arXiv:2509.01328) under a drastically smaller budget: models of at most 2B parameters, one 16 GB consumer GPU, about five GPU-days. (1) With matched data and labels, text is the bottleneck: on the same 100k-decision training set, a 2.6M-parameter convolutional board encoder agrees with the strong AI Mortal on 80.6% of test decisions, above every text-prompt LLM we train (best 77.8%), and places better at the table (2.85 over 1,000 games vs. ~3.0 for the LLMs; paired difference at n=100 not significant). Scaled to 1.71M decisions, a 4.9M-parameter Transformer reaches 94.7% agreement, beats the 0.8B LLMs on identical seeds (-0.45 ranks, sign test p=0.005), and is statistically equivalent to parity against three Mortal champions (TOST within 0.10 ranks, p=6e-4); parity against a teacher-opponent is roughly the ceiling of pure imitation. (2) Training toward the teacher raises teacher agreement more than a 2.5x parameter increase does (+2.5 vs. +1.5 points); on human-record agreement both effects are +1.0, and neither is visible at the table. (3) Few-point agreement differences do not resolve into playing strength within a family: +2.5 agreement points coincide with a paired placement difference of +0.02 +/- 0.12 ranks (p=1.0), and +2.0 points at 2B with -0.06 (p=0.37) - both below the ~0.25-rank resolution of 100 paired games. We also document a paper-code mismatch in the original winner filter, reconstruct its two private engine patches, and show that a divide-and-conquer pipeline makes template-generated Japanese rationales 93% sentence-exact (43% without facts). Per Tenhou's terms we release no trained weights - only code, configurations, and evaluation protocols.

papers.title: The anomalously large transiting planet around Boyajian's star: evidence for a circumplanetary ring
papers.abstract: A recent study reported a transiting giant-planet candidate with a mass of $9.4^{+4.9}_{-4.1}\,M_{\rm J}$ and a radius of $1.7\pm0.1\,R_{\rm J}$ on a wide orbit around Boyajian's star (KIC 8462852, also called Tabby's star), which is well known for its irregular, deep flux dips. The reported radius is puzzling, because cool giant planets of $\sim$10\,$M_{\rm Jup}$ are expected to have radii close to Jupiter's, so the companion appears $\sim$60--70\% larger than standard models allow. Here we explore the solution that the planet is actually ringed. We develop a fast and accurate code to compute the transit light curve due to a ringed planet, and apply it to the TESS light curve. The ring model is marginally favoured by the data by $\Delta \chi^2>10$ and a difference in Bayesian information criterion (BIC) of $<2$. The preferred configuration is a Jupiter-sized ($1.1\,R_{\rm J}$) planet surrounded by an opaque, highly flattened ring extending to $3.1$--$4.4$ planetary radii with a nearly polar obliquity. While the ring geometry is uncertain, simple estimates suggest that a debris annulus extending out to the planet's Roche limit is needed to explain the large transit depth. The ring thus removes the radius anomaly altogether and is qualitatively consistent with the dusty, comet-shepherding environment inferred from the star's historic dimmings.

papers.intro:
KIC 8462852, better known as Boyajian’s star or Tabby’s star, is an otherwise ordinary F3 V main-sequence star that has become one of the most enigmatic objects in the Kepler field. During the four years of Kepler monitoring it exhibited a series of abrupt, aperiodic flux dips, reaching depths of 15% and 22% in events near days 792 and 1519 of the mission, which were far deeper than any planetary transit and had no detectable periodicity [4]. A series of dipping events have also been observed after the Kepler era [5, 3, e.g.,]. The dips are chromatic, with stronger attenuation at shorter wavelengths, indicating occulting material of dust-sized grains rather than a solid body [9]. A wide range of mechanisms has been proposed to explain the variability of Boyajian’s star, including disintegrating exocomets or comet swarms [4, 14], a family of Trojan bodies sharing the orbit of a massive perturber [2], debris from a recently consumed planet [21], a warped or clumpy circumstellar dust disk, and, after all, non-natural “megastructure” scenarios [30]. None of these has gained universal acceptance, and the leading class of models still requires an unseen massive companion whose gravity shepherds the dust-producing bodies onto star-grazing orbits. A stellar companion to Boyajian’s star was discovered later [23], but with a separation ∼880\sim 880\,au it is unlikely to be responsible for the mysterious light curve variation of Boyajian’s star.

None of these has gained universal acceptance, and the leading class of models still requires an unseen massive companion whose gravity shepherds the dust-producing bodies onto star-grazing orbits. Recently, Madurga-Favieres et al. [19] reported a single, isolated transit event in the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite [26, TESS,] photometry. The event is strikingly different from the irregular dips that have been seen before: it is symmetric to within the photometric precision, with a depth of ∼\sim1.1% and a duration of ∼\sim21 hours, exactly the morphology expected for a solid, roughly spherical body crossing the stellar disk. Combining the transit data with a re-analysis of archival radial velocities, Madurga-Favieres et al. [19] obtained a companion mass of 9.4−4.1+4.9​MJ9.4^{+4.9}_{-4.1}\,M_{\rm J} and a radius of 1.7±0.1​RJ1.7\pm 0.1\,R_{\rm J} on an orbit with a period of at least ∼\sim1030 days, with only five discrete period windows surviving the Kepler archival constraints. If confirmed, this companion would both constitute the first transiting giant planet/brown dwarf around Boyajian’s star and may be the long-sought perturber capable of driving the exocomet population responsible for the historic dimmings.

There is, however, a physical puzzle hidden in the numbers. Gas-giant planets more massive than Jupiter are supported largely by electron degeneracy pressure, and their radii are expected to be nearly mass-independent at cool temperatures. As shown in Figure 1, both planetary evolution models [11, e.g.,] and the empirical mass-radius relation for cool giants [28] predict Rp≃1.0R_{\rm p}\simeq 1.0–1.1​RJ1.1\,R_{\rm J} across ∼\sim2–12 MJM_{\rm J}, with an intrinsic dispersion of only ∼\sim0.1 RJR_{\rm J}. Inflation by stellar irradiation, which applies to close-in hot Jupiters, is negligible at the companion’s equilibrium temperature of ∼\sim270 K. At an age of ∼1.2\sim 1.2\,Gyr [23], the star is no longer young for the residual heat of formation to keep the planet substantially puffed up either. The reported radius of 1.7​RJup1.7\,R_{\rm Jup} is therefore surprisingly large by ∼\sim60–70%.

There is, however, a physical puzzle hidden in the numbers. Gas-giant planets more massive than Jupiter are supported largely by electron degeneracy pressure, and their radii are expected to be nearly mass-independent at cool temperatures. As shown in Figure 1, both planetary evolution models [11, e.g.,] and the empirical mass-radius relation for cool giants [28] predict Rp≃1.0R_{\rm p}\simeq 1.0–1.1​RJ1.1\,R_{\rm J} across ∼\sim2–12 MJM_{\rm J}, with an intrinsic dispersion of only ∼\sim0.1 RJR_{\rm J}. Inflation by stellar irradiation, which applies to close-in hot Jupiters, is negligible at the companion’s equilibrium temperature of ∼\sim270 K. At an age of ∼1.2\sim 1.2\,Gyr [23], the star is no longer young for the residual heat of formation to keep the planet substantially puffed up either. The reported radius of 1.7​RJup1.7\,R_{\rm Jup} is therefore surprisingly large by ∼\sim60–70%.

In this paper we propose and quantify a geometric solution to the puzzle by adding a ring to the planetary companion. An opaque ring surrounding a much smaller planet blocks additional starlight, mimicking an anomalously large planetary radius. Similar ideas have been proposed to explain other planets. In particular, Piro and Vissapragada [24] showed that several of the lowest-density “super-puff” planets could in principle be explained by small rocky planets with opaque rings, and ringed configurations have also been invoked for individual ambiguous systems [1, e.g.]. In the case of Boyajian’s star, a qualitatively similar idea was advanced by Ballesteros et al. [2], who interpreted the historic, asymmetric 15% dip at D792 as the grazing transit of a Saturn-like ringed giant, with the later dimmings caused by a swarm of Trojan bodies sharing its orbit. The ring model in Ballesteros et al. [2] is only schematic, because no ring parameters were fitted, the light-curve reproduction was qualitative, and the predicted repeating events, with Trojan passages in 2021 and a new transit in 2023, have not been reported.

papers.title: Electro-optic comb-driven massive data transmission on monolithically integrated lithium niobate photonic circuits
papers.abstract: Driven by large AI models, the demand for datacenter interconnects is outstripping traditional scaling laws. This necessitates a transition toward dense multiplexing techniques, such as wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM), for datacenter environments, transferring long-haul spectral efficiency to short-reach, high-bandwidth applications. Integrated optical frequency combs offer compact, low-cost light sources for future datacenter WDM interconnects. However, existing Kerr comb and mode-locked laser implementations suffer from drawbacks in power efficiency, spectral flatness and phase noise. Their fixed, device-specific channel spacings often conflict with standard WDM grids, and co-integration with high-speed modulators remains challenging. Here, we overcome these limitations by demonstrating high-capacity data transmission using flat-top electro-optic combs on thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN), a platform featuring flat spectra, tunable wavelengths and comb spacing, alongside native compatibility with (de-)multiplexers and high-speed modulators. Using 46 wavelength channels from two lasers and a 50-GHz on-chip electro-optic comb, we realize 16.56 Tb/s coherent transmission over a 98.84-km deployed fiber link between two universities and two datacenters in Hong Kong, verifying its suitability for inter-datacenter connections. To highlight grid reconfigurability, we reconfigure the comb to 100-GHz spacing via an on-chip demultiplexer and demonstrate 10-channel, 80-GBaud coherent transmission at 6.4 Tb/s. We further report a proof-of-concept monolithic WDM transmitter integrating the comb and high-speed modulator, achieving 19-channel, 45-GBaud IM/DD transmission at 1.71 Tb/s. Our work validates TFLN electro-optic combs as flexible, compact and scalable WDM engines for both coherent and IM/DD datacenter links to satisfy rapidly rising bandwidth requirements.

papers.title: A Variational Geometric Approach to Exact Recovery by $\ell_1/\ell_2$ Minimization
papers.abstract: For affine-constrained $\ell_1/\ell_2$ minimization with nonzero data, a variational geometric approach is developed to characterize exact recovery. Necessary and sufficient conditions for local and global exact recovery are established in terms of directional derivatives and cones associated with sublevel sets of the ratio objective. The local analysis further reveals that local minimality, first-order growth, and tilt stability are equivalent. These pointwise characterizations lead to improved sufficient conditions for uniform recovery of sparse signals. The sufficient condition for uniform local recovery has coefficient $c_s=\max\{1,(\sqrt{s}-1)/2\}$ for $s\ge2$. For each fixed $s$, the coefficient $c_s$ is optimal within the considered family of local null-space conditions. Projection estimates yield a scalar bound for uniform global recovery with coefficient two, improving the earlier coefficient three. The coefficient two is optimal within the considered family of global null-space bounds when both $s$ and $n$ may vary. A positive margin in the local null-space condition provides explicit growth moduli, localization radii, and bounds on linear objective perturbations that leave the localized minimizer fixed. Examples show that uniform local recovery does not imply uniform global recovery.

papers.title: Cross-vehicle injury spillovers of ADAS functions in two-vehicle rear-end and same-direction sideswipe crashes
papers.abstract: Advanced driver assistance system (ADAS) functions are evaluated mainly by the crashes they prevent, and little is known about how they relate to the injuries sustained in the crashes that would still occur. Because two colliding vehicles share one impact, a function on one vehicle may also be associated with the other driver's injury. This study examines whether an ADAS function on either vehicle in such two-vehicle crashes is associated with either driver's injury. It focuses on rear-end (n = 2,273) and same-direction sideswipe crashes (n = 1,216) from Texas police reports across 2023 to 2025. Striking and struck roles were assigned within each crash, and the ADAS functions of each vehicle were identified from vehicle identification numbers. For each crash type, a bivariate probit model, with random parameters for rear-end crashes, jointly estimates whether each driver was injured. Significant cross-equation correlations (0.559 and 0.375) support the joint specification. Electronic stability control on the striking vehicle is associated with a lower struck-driver injury probability in both crash types, by 0.036 to 0.073 in rear-end and 0.102 in sideswipe crashes. Lane departure warning on the striking vehicle shows a similar association in sideswipe crashes (about 0.078). Traction control with anti-lock braking on the struck vehicle shows the largest association among the ADAS functions with its own driver's injury probability (0.097 and 0.103 lower). No struck-vehicle function is associated with the striking driver's injury, and forward-looking functions show no association with either driver's injury, consistent with their benefit lying mainly in crash prevention. The findings suggest that the protective benefits of stability and lane departure functions may reach beyond the equipped vehicle to the other driver, strengthening the case for their wider fleet adoption.

papers.title: Equivalent Pseudo-angular Momentum Governs Selective Magnon-Phonon Hybridization
papers.abstract: Magnon-phonon hybridization provides a powerful route to couple spin and lattice excitations, yet the symmetry principle governing mode selectivity remains unclear. Here, we show that crystalline pseudoangular momentum provides a general criterion for selective magnon-phonon hybridization in noncollinear multisublattice magnetic systems. The rotation eigenvalue associated with pseudoangular momentum encodes polarization transformations, sublattice permutations, and Bloch phases, requiring magnetoelastic coupling between modes belonging to the same rotation sector. We illustrate this principle in a stacked kagome model with noncollinear spin order. An out-of-plane magnetic field tunes one magnon sector into resonance with a degenerate phonon doublet, yet only the pseudoangular-momentum-matched phonon develops a pronounced avoided crossing while the other remains nearly unmixed. Field reversal switches the selected rotation sector and reverses the rotational polarization of the hybridized phonon component without changing the hybrid-mode energies. Our results reveal pseudoangular-momentum matching as a general framework for understanding and controlling mode-selective spin-lattice hybridization.

papers.title: SGDB: Semantic-Geometric Decoupling and Evidence Binding for Logical Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Logical anomaly detection requires recognizing scene components and measuring whether their configuration satisfies task constraints. Correct identities can coexist with inaccurate geometry; clean mask fragments can yield misleading lengths. We propose Semantic-Geometric Decoupling and Evidence Binding (SGDB). A semantic decoder learns object identities from component-annotated normal sources and factual edits; a separate reader supplies final measurements. Partial one-to-one association binds geometric witnesses to identities while retaining unmatched objects in the count. A support-certified reader selects mask-derived axes using line quality and complete component ownership. Explicit task requirements and normal-data references define executable checks, with decision thresholds fixed by independent normal calibration. Execution-grounded explanation traces rule contributions to source objects and measurements, extracting compact sufficient alarm certificates. A frozen language model expresses selected outcomes as cited claims, with numeric evidence retained by the executor. Reports preserve observed deviations and unavailable evidence. SGDB achieves 98.19% AUROC and 94.52% fixed-threshold F1 on five MVTec LOCO logical categories, and 93.56% AUROC and 92.76% F1 across all 50 VID-AD tasks. Frozen-output controls evaluate geometric readout and explanatory sufficiency and compactness.

papers.title: DiffAuction: An Auction-Driven Framework for Generative Image Advertising
papers.abstract: Diffusion models enable multiple advertisers to compete for exposure within a shared generated image. Yet existing approaches are computationally costly when generating images under varying target-share configurations, and it remains unclear how the resulting outcomes should be evaluated and priced. To address these gaps, we propose DiffAuction, a framework integrating controllable generation, click-intent evaluation, and auction design. First, our training-free Residual Share Calibration (RSC) decomposes joint-attention updates into product-specific residuals and rescales them according to target shares. We further introduce Share-Conditioned Prompting (SCP) to adapt the viewpoint to each desired allocation. Second, we develop an evaluator that uses a VLM to extract visual evidence and an LLM to assess Click-Through Intent (CTI), a proxy for click propensity, along four dimensions: Product Prominence, Brand Recognizability, Scene Integration, and Contextual Value Communication. We validate its assessments against judgments from 10 trained annotators on 1000 images. Third, we formulate this advertising setting as an auction over jointly feasible generation configurations. Each configuration has a public expected CTI vector, while advertisers hold configuration-specific private values per unit of CTI that map click intent into commercial value. We adopt a learnable affine maximizer auction (AMA), which jointly selects a shared generation configuration and determines advertiser-specific payments to maximize expected platform revenue. The resulting allocation and payment rules guarantee dominant-strategy incentive compatibility (DSIC) and individual rationality (IR). Experiments show that our generation method strengthens the monotonic relationship between target shares and CTI relative to baselines, while the learned AMA achieves higher platform revenue in the resulting auction setting.

papers.title: An explicit third-order low-regularity integrator for the cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose an explicit third-order low-regularity integrator for the cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on the one-dimensional torus $\mathbb{T}$. By carefully designing numerical approximations for the integrals in Fourier space, we construct a third-order scheme and provide a rigorous global error analysis. More precisely, we prove that the scheme achieves third-order convergence in $H^{r}(\mathbb{T})$ for the initial data in $H^{r+4}(\mathbb{T})$ with $r>1/2$. Furthermore, the third-order convergence in $L^{2}(\mathbb{T})$ is established for the initial data in $H^{4}(\mathbb{T})$. Numerical experiments are presented to confirm the theoretical convergence results.

papers.title: Reasoning Patterns for Efficient AI Coding: An Empirical Study
papers.abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) generate long reasoning traces that expose intermediate inference behavior, offering opportunities to study and control reasoning in AI coding. However, the underlying patterns in these traces and their potential for analyzing and guiding coding models remain poorly understood, limiting systematic characterization and inference-time control of LRM reasoning. We conduct an empirical study of reasoning patterns across four representative coding tasks. We transform reasoning traces into structured action sequences and mine recurring fragments using within-task support, cross-task contrasts, and valid--invalid support contrasts. We characterize four general reasoning patterns by coding agents: design-to-implementation for code generation, state tracing for execution reasoning, evidence--fix--recheck for debugging, and semantic mapping for translation. We further identify positive and negative patterns associated with valid and invalid reasoning traces, respectively. Positive patterns reflect verification-driven convergence, whereas negative patterns reflect repeated design revision, reflection, and knowledge recall without closure. To demonstrate their practical utility, we evaluate three pattern-based applications: task identification, pattern-guided prompting, and pattern-aware early stopping. Features capturing general reasoning patterns enable accurate task identification from reasoning traces without accessing task descriptions or final answers. Prompting guided by positive and negative patterns improves the overall accuracy of downstream tasks, while negative pattern-aware early stopping substantially reduces API-reported token usage with only a modest decrease in pass@1. All three applications also generalize to previously unseen models, showing that reasoning patterns can support both the analysis and control of LRM behavior in AI coding.

papers.title: On the product of nontrivial cross-intersecting families
papers.abstract: Let $n\geq2\ell\geq2k\geq6$ and $n>k+\ell$. We determine the maximum of $|\mathcal A||\mathcal B|$ over all nonempty, nontrivial cross-intersecting families $\mathcal A\subseteq\binom{[n]}k$ and $\mathcal B\subseteq\binom{[n]}\ell$. The exact bound is $|\mathcal A||\mathcal B|\leq\max\{M_1,M_2\}$, where \[ \begin{aligned} M_1 &=\left(\binom{n-1}{k-1}-\binom{n-\ell-1}{k-1}+1\right) \left(\binom{n-1}{\ell-1}-\binom{n-k-1}{\ell-1}+1\right),\\ M_2 &=\left(\binom{n-2}{\ell-2}+1\right) \sum_{i=1}^{2} \left(\binom{n-i}{k-1}-\binom{n-\ell-i}{k-1}\right). \end{aligned} \] Both terms are attained by explicit constructions: a Hilton--Milner-type pair and a two-point construction, respectively. We classify all equality cases, including the additional cross-triangle pairs when $k=\ell=3$. Two structural results underlie the proof. First, we establish a restricted-lex comparison theorem showing that restricted lexicographic initial segments minimize disjointness neighborhoods, and characterize equality at the first nontrivial threshold. Second, a decomposition of critically shifted families into two parts with disjoint cores leads to a sharp product theorem, with equality characterized, for all cross-intersecting pairs admitting this decomposition, without additional nontriviality assumptions. Endpoint comparisons and reverse shifting complete the proof for unequal as well as equal uniformities.

papers.title: On Brezis' open problem 2.4
papers.abstract: We show the existence of a ``nonradial" smooth entire solution of the Ginzburg--Landau equation with degree $q\in\{8,9\}$ and modulus tending to one at infinity. This answers Brezis' Open Problem 2.4 negatively. To construct the counterexample, we vary a cone parameter $q \in [8, 9]$ and keeping the degree on the cone equal to one. Several key ingredients are needed. First, we need to compute the Morse index of radial vortex solutions at $q\in \{8, 9\}$. Second, we need to show compactness. Finally, Leray-Schauder degree theory and a homotopy argument yield the desired existence result.

papers.title: Reinforcement learning for constrained stochastic linear--quadratic control in continuous time
papers.abstract: We study continuous-time stochastic linear--quadratic control with a scalar state and nonnegative control constraints. With quadratic running costs, randomized exploration can change the optimal mean feedback. We introduce an auxiliary problem without entropy in which the conditional policy mean is nonnegative and the covariance is prescribed in proportion to the squared state. Moment reduction and state separation yield two regional Riccati equations and characterize the finite-horizon value function and optimal conditional mean. We give a sufficient control--cost compatibility condition under which this mean coincides with the optimal feedback of the original constrained problem. For time-invariant coefficients, we characterize the undiscounted infinite-horizon optimum and establish mean square asymptotic stability under the stated assumptions. For unknown dynamics, we develop model-free actor--critic schemes for finite and infinite horizons. Numerical experiments compare the learned policies with their analytical targets and examine the effect of exploration on the optimal mean.

papers.title: Inverse heat source problem from terminal data on a set of low Hausdorff dimension
papers.abstract: We study the recovery of a spatial source in the heat equation from terminal observations on a compact interior set $E$ with positive $\beta$ dimensional Hausdorff content for some $\beta>d-1$. The prescribed temporal forcing vanishes on a nontrivial interval immediately preceding the observation time. Under a spectral Sobolev prior and a quantitative noncancellation condition on the terminal spectral multipliers, we establish conditional logarithmic stability. For scattered observations on such sets, we derive a sampling inequality under a quasi uniformity assumption. Under explicit sampling and independent noise assumptions, we prove a logarithmic convergence rate in probability for the corresponding Tikhonov reconstructions with a data driven parameter choice. Two numerical experiments using a finite candidate approximation of a fixed Hausdorff set assess discrete spectral sampling stability and illustrate the effects of the waiting interval and measurement noise on reconstruction.

papers.title: SimPOTrans: Self-Adaptation for Offline-to-Simultaneous Speech Translation via Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Simultaneous speech translation (SimulST) aims to translate ongoing speech with low latency while preserving translation quality. Recent studies have adopted large language models (LLMs) for SimulST and formulated it as a multi-turn dialogue task for efficient generation, achieving state-of-the-art performance. However, existing dialogue-style SimulST approaches typically rely on specialized training schemes to acquire simultaneous translation behavior, either using synthesized read/write trajectories, which may provide suboptimal training signals, or jointly optimizing translation quality and latency, whose competing objectives may cause optimization instability. In this paper, we introduce SimPOTrans, a reinforcement learning (RL) framework that enables offline speech translation models to self-adapt to dialogue-style SimulST. Through a simple two-stage RL post-training pipeline, SimPOTrans rewards an offline model for exhibiting translation behaviors beneficial to simultaneous scenarios when given partial speech inputs, thereby enabling offline-to-simultaneous self-adaptation without synthesized read/write trajectories or explicit latency optimization. At inference time, SimPOTrans requires no external decision policy and enables flexible quality--latency control by simply adjusting the chunk size of speech input. Experiments on the ACL 60/60 and MCIF benchmarks across three language directions (En$\rightarrow$De, En$\rightarrow$Zh, and En$\rightarrow$Ja) demonstrate that SimPOTrans outperforms several strong baselines, achieving a superior quality--latency trade-off.

papers.title: Hallucination-Aware Multi-Agent RAG via Internal Attention Rewards
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounds language models in retrieved evidence, but its outputs often contain claims unsupported by that evidence. Recent multi-agent RAG systems decompose the pipeline into cooperative decisions, yet they typically optimize all agents under a shared task reward such as EM or F1, which measures answer overlap rather than faithfulness to evidence. We propose a hallucination-aware multi-agent RAG framework that combines the task reward with an internal hallucination-risk signal computed from the generator's attention-head norms. Three role-specific LoRA adapters, a query planner, an evidence selector, and an answer generator, share a frozen backbone. A lightweight critic is trained once on TruthfulQA truthful/false pairs and then kept frozen, providing a complementary risk score that is added to the shared reward during cooperative PPO training. Across three backbones (Qwen3-8B, Llama3-8B, Llama2-13B) and three benchmarks (RAGTruth, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA), our method improves task performance and reduces hallucination rates over the strongest multi-agent baseline. Ablations and critic diagnostics show that the TruthfulQA-calibrated signal provides useful reward shaping that transfers across RAG tasks.

papers.title: MemVLN: Streaming Episodic Memory for Vision-Language Navigation
papers.abstract: Vision-language navigation (VLN) requires an embodied agent to follow language instructions through 3D environments. Maintaining persistent episodic memory remains a challenge for VLM-based streaming agents in long-horizon navigation. We present MEMVLN, a streaming episodic memory framework that maintains a bounded bank of compressed perceptual features annotated with timesteps and action-derived relative poses, and produces compact memory tokens via cross-attention. We pair the proposed memory with a frozen pretrained geometry encoder. To learn the memory module, we design a masking-based trajectory summarization task with multi-granularity sub-trajectory decomposition, encouraging route reconstruction exclusively from episodic memory. Under navigation training restricted to the official R2R/RxR trajectories, MEMVLN achieves state-of-the-art performance on most reported metrics on standard VLN-CE benchmarks. Long-horizon analyses further characterize when episodic memory is useful. For physical evaluation, we collect 30 instruction-conditioned episodes in one physical scene, use 24 as demonstrations for post-training, and hold out six for testing. On the held-out episodes, MEMVLN improves success over the VLM baseline from 17% to 40%, and post-training further raises it to 47%.
