papers.title: Learning to Remember: Advances in Memory Mechanisms for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Memory has become a central mechanism for extending large language models (LLMs) beyond fixed context windows, stateless interaction, and static parametric knowledge. This survey organizes the literature around three complementary dimensions: the life cycle of memory, the storage substrate, and the system role that memory plays in LLM-based agents, while using cognitive-science-inspired memory concepts as a lightweight conceptual motivation rather than as a separate technical contribution or implementation family. On this basis, we distinguish three mechanism families: nonparametric memory, where information is stored outside model parameters in text, graph, multimodal, or database-like structures; parametric memory, where information is stored or accessed through activations, key-value caches, learned modules, adapter-based parameterizations, or model weights; and memory for agent evolution, where stored experiences support reinforcement learning, continual learning, procedural reuse, context engineering, and agent harness design. Evaluation is treated as a separate cross-cutting component rather than as a memory mechanism. Unlike surveys that focus primarily on retrieval-augmented generation or long-context modeling, this paper emphasizes the full memory life cycle: construction, maintenance, retrieval, consolidation, forgetting, governance, and evaluation. By aligning conceptual motivations, computational memory mechanisms, benchmarks, and deployment concerns, the survey provides a structured roadmap for designing memory-augmented LLM agents that are persistent, adaptive, auditable, and safe to update over time.

papers.title: New families of additive non-RS MDS codes and ACD codes from twisted Reed-Solomon codes
papers.abstract: Additive codes generalize linear codes and play an important role in the construc?tion of quantum codes. As generalizations of linear MDS codes, additive MDS codes have received much research attention. As an important subclass of additive codes, ACD codes are widely used for quantum error correction. In this paper, we study single-twist additive generalized twisted Reed-Solomon (GTRS) codes over finite fields. We derive necessary and sufficient conditions for these codes to be MDS for arbitrary hook and twist parameters. Then we employ Schur squares to prove that such additive MDS codes are not monomially equivalent to additive Reed-Solomon codes. We also identify a class of additive GTRS codes whose duals remain additive GTRS codes, and show that, for all sufficiently large prime powers q whose characteristic avoids a finite set, such GTRS codes yield ACD codes.

authors.name: Yansheng Wu
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: On a family of stably handle-slide trivial R-links
papers.abstract: An R-link is an n-component link L in S^3 such that Dehn surgery on L yields #^nS1 \times S2. Adapting work of Gompf, Scharlemann and Thompson, Meier and Zupan produced a family of R-links L(p, q; c/d), where the pairs (p, q) and (c, d) are relatively prime and c is even. For most of link in this family, whether it is handle-slide trivial remains open. In this work, we show one subfamily, L(3, 2; 4/d), are stably handle-slide trivial for all d.

papers.title: Theoretical progress on regularized lattice Boltzmann collision models on weakly incompressible and compressible thermal flows
papers.abstract: Numerical stability has long constrained the application of lattice Boltzmann methods to high-Reynolds-number and high-Mach-number flows. Improving the stability and accuracy of collision models has therefore remained a major challenge for nearly three decades. Regularized collision models constitute an important class of lattice Boltzmann collision models and have recently undergone substantial theoretical development. They are now widely used for high-Reynolds-number turbulence, high-Mach-number compressible flow and aeroacoustics. This article systematically reviews their development and establishes a unified theoretical framework that clarifies the relationships among the principal formulations. The analysis identifies the underlying principle of the regularized multiple-relaxation collision model: higher-order kinetic moments that cannot be represented by the discrete lattice are rapidly relaxed in a coordinate-independent, self-similar moment space, thereby preventing spurious modes from contaminating the hydrodynamic equations.

papers.title: RetroNav: Scene-Grounded Retrospection and Retry for Self-Evolving Lifelong Navigation
papers.abstract: Existing robot navigation methods primarily focus on isolated tasks, overlooking the need to accumulate knowledge and experience across repeated navigation episodes. Although recent lifelong navigation methods have explored cross-task knowledge accumulation, they mainly focus on scene knowledge while neglecting historical navigation experience and its connection to scene evidence, limiting the ability to reflect on past mistakes and improve future decisions. To address this limitation, this paper presents RetroNav, a training-free self-evolving navigation framework that integrates navigation, memory accumulation, and failure reflection. Specifically, we develop a unified memory system that connects geometric and semantic scene knowledge with historical navigation experience, distinguishing objective observations from task-dependent interpretations. After each navigation attempt, an independent evaluator determines whether a retry is necessary. If so, a Retrospection Agent revisits historical decisions using accumulated scene knowledge and navigation records, generating an evidence-grounded retry brief to guide the next attempt. RetroNav achieves state-of-the-art performance across five navigation benchmarks. Our method will be open-sourced at https://github.com/3dv-casia/RetroNav .

papers.title: Orbital-selective correlations in kagome flat bands of Co$_3$Sn$_2$S$_2$
papers.abstract: Geometrical flat bands provide an ideal platform for studying electronic correlations and quantum-geometric effects. Although the ferromagnetic Weyl semimetal \CoSnS is generally considered a moderately correlated system, recent spectroscopy experiments have revealed a flat-band feature near the Fermi level ($\EF$) that is absent in conventional density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Using DFT plus dynamical mean-field theory and a minimal kagome model, we show that this feature arises not from heavy-fermion-like dynamical band renormalization, but from the shifting of a $d_{x^2-y^2}$ dominated geometrical kagome flat band toward $\EF$ driven by orbital- and spin-dependent self-energies. The relocated flat band enhances the local Berry curvature near $\EF$, resulting in a strongly energy-dependent anomalous Hall conductivity and a giant anomalous Nernst effect. Our findings establish an orbital-selective correlation mechanism for positioning geometrical flat bands at $\EF$, and propose anomalous thermoelectric transport as a sensitive probe of flat band induced topology.

papers.title: Further Study of p-Ary Self-Orthogonal Codes From Square Functions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate a family of trace codes over finite fields of odd characteristic defined by two quadratic trace conditions. By analyzing the quadratic forms associated with these trace conditions and evaluating the corresponding character sums, we obtain the parameters and complete weight distributions of the codes. We further exploit the natural multiplicative orbit structure of the defining sets to obtain punctured codes and determine their parameters, weight distributions and dual distances. Moreover, we establish self?orthogonality criteria and investigate divisibility and projectivity of the constructed codes. These results give a unified treatment for arbitrary odd prime fields and for extension degrees of both parities.

papers.title: Minimality of Binary Codes From Weight Layers and Graph Cut Spaces
papers.abstract: Minimal binary linear codes play an important role in secret-sharing schemes and in the structural study of linear codes. We study the minimality of three classes of known constructions: codes from a single complete Hamming-weight layer, codes from arbitrary unions of such layers and graph cut-space codes. For the previously studied single-layer codes C, we give a complete minimality classification: C is minimal if and only if t is even. For t = 4, we determine the minimum and maximum weights, and show that the family strictly violates the binary Ashikhmin Barg sufficient condition for every k. We also calculate the minimum distance of the dual code. For arbitrary unions of complete Hamming-weight layers, we obtain an if-and-only-if classification of minimality and uniform criteria for evenness, self-orthogonality, the doubly even property and hull dimension. We further analyze the family for odd k. Finally, using the classical bond characterization of cuts, we translate minimality of graph cut space codes into a graph-theoretic condition: a nonempty simple graph has a minimal cut code precisely when it has one edge-containing component and that component is complete. We also give a graph-function realization of the known binary tetrahedron code and explicitly identify the resulting code equivalence.

authors.name: Mengni Wang
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: The quermassintegral inequalities for k-convex spiral-star-shaped domains
papers.abstract:
We extend the quermassintegral inequalities of our earlier work \cite{GuanLi2009} from star-shaped domains to a substantially broader class of domains in Euclidean space, which we call spiral-star-shaped. A smooth domain is spiral-star-shaped if its boundary satisfies \[
  \langle X+A X,\nu\rangle>0 \] for some fixed skew-symmetric linear map $ A$, where $X$ is the position vector and $\nu$ is the outward unit normal. The vector field $X+A X$ is conformal Killing, with dilation component $X$ and rotational component $A X$; its trajectories combine expansion and rotation, giving rise to the spiral terminology. When $A=0$, it reduces to ordinary star-shapedness, while nonzero $A$ allows domains that are not star-shaped in the usual radial sense.
  For smooth $k$-convex spiral-star-shaped domains, we prove long-time existence and exponential convergence to a round sphere for a locally constrained inverse curvature flow. The positive spiral support function provides the geometric control needed to treat initial hypersurfaces that need not be star-shaped in the usual sense. Monotonicity of the quermassintegrals along the flow yields sharp quermassintegral inequalities in this enlarged class, with equality if and only if the domain is a ball.

papers.title: Finite determinacy and rigidity of quiver potentials
papers.abstract: We prove that a quiver potential over a field of characteristic zero is finitely determined if and only if the trace space of its Jacobian algebra is finite dimensional. In particular, Jacobi-finite potentials are finitely determined. We further prove that rigid potentials are finitely determined and, over an algebraically closed field, unique up to right equivalence on a fixed quiver. For finitely determined weighted-homogeneous potentials, we give an explicit bound on the jet order sufficient for finite determinacy in terms of the arrow weights, the weight of the potential, and the highest nonzero weight of the trace space of its Jacobian algebra. We also establish new invariance results for weighted-homogeneous potentials under right equivalence.

papers.title: Extremal Perfect Monotone Equilibria in Bayesian Games with Strategic Complementarities
papers.abstract: We study sharp bounds on equilibrium behavior in Bayesian games when players may make mistakes. Under strategic complementarities, the set of behavioral perfect equilibria has a largest and a smallest element, both in pure strategies. We ask when these bounds are monotone and how they depend on the way mistakes are made. For monotone supermodular games, we consider limits of equilibria under increasing perturbations, in the sense that conditional tremble distributions have full support and increase stochastically with type. We show that the largest and smallest perfect equilibria exist, which are pure and monotone. Under the general perfection notion, the extremal perfect equilibria continue to be monotone in the setting with finite actions. With infinite actions, the extremal perfect equilibria can be nonmonotone, and the set of perfect monotone equilibria can even lack extrema.

papers.title: JANUS: Synthesizing Cross-Layer Defenses Against Web Deserialization Attacks
papers.abstract:
Unsafe deserialization turns untrusted data into attacker-controlled execution, and a single vulnerability can admit diverse exploit variants that evade defenses tailored to a known exploit. Existing defenses typically operate at a single enforcement point with limited visibility into the full attack. Combining controls across layers offers complementary protection, but coordinating them to preserve legitimate functionality and adapting them to new variants requires substantial expert effort.
  We propose JANUS, a red-blue adversarial framework for automated cross-layer defense synthesis. Starting from a known exploit, \sys iteratively refines deployment-specific policies in an isolated offline environment. A black-box attacker probes the current policy for exploit variants using only externally observable feedback. The defender summarizes each verified variant into its security-relevant effects, uses counterfactual replay to separate complementary coverage from redundant enforcement, and jointly selects and scopes controls across layers. Each candidate policy is validated against accumulated exploits and benign workflows.
  We evaluate JANUS on sixteen vulnerability deployments across six Java and PHP applications against gateway, application, system, and cross-layer defenses. JANUS reduces held-out attack success to 6.2%, compared with 18.8-55.0% for the baselines, fully mitigates 13 of 16 deployments, and preserves 98.4% of benign functionality tests at a 6.9% targeted P95 latency increase.

authors.name: Xiaofei Xie
authors.institution: Xiangyang Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: The Agent in the Middle: How AI-Mediated Access Reshapes Web Vulnerability Exploitation
papers.abstract: Web services increasingly expose backend interfaces that let users delegate tasks to AI agents, which invoke service operations directly without navigating websites. This shift changes how existing Web vulnerabilities can be exploited. We investigate these changes through VELA, an executable benchmark covering 44 vulnerabilities across twelve Web application families. The benchmark preserves vulnerable backends and derives agent-facing interfaces from legitimate workflows. We evaluate three commercial agents across multiple interface configurations, using controlled comparisons to separate interface effects from agent behavior and independent oracles to verify attack outcomes. Our results show that the agent realizes every attack that direct interface invocation realizes in the reference configuration, so exploitability is set mainly by the interface: 91% of vulnerabilities remain exploitable under the reference design. Interface restrictions prevent some attacks by removing required operations or limiting input control, while retention remains high across vulnerability classes. No case-level loss in the reference configuration is attributed to agent refusal or input normalization, and in one case the agent completed an attack by supplying calls the attacker omitted. Across the tested configurations, interface design affects exploitability more than agent choice, moving retention from 39% to 95% against at most 4.5 points across agents, but some restrictive interfaces also limit legitimate workflows. Our study provides a systematic empirical account of how agent-mediated access reshapes existing Web vulnerabilities, grounding future Web architecture design in measured security outcomes and trade-offs between reducing attack exposure and preserving legitimate functionality in agent-facing services.

authors.name: Xiaofei Xie
authors.institution: Xiangyang Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Positivity of Relative Pluricanonical Direct Images via Fixed-Point Metrics
papers.abstract: We develop a direct analytic approach to positivity of relative pluricanonical direct images through a fixed-point Hermitian metric by direct differential curvature calculations. The curvature resolvent formula from fixed-point equation leads to two-sided estimates of entire Nakano curvature by determinant curvature. In this way, we identify generic rank of determinant curvature with birational variation dimension for a projective algebraic fibration between smooth connected projective varieties with general fiber of general type and maximal birational variation, assuming $mK_F$ is globally generated or the $m$-canonical map is birational for general fiber $F$. In the global generation case, Green--Griffiths Conjecture asks for the tautological bigness of the ordinary symmetric powers $\operatorname{Sym}^{\ell}f_*\omega_{X/Y}^{\otimes m}$, without passing to reflexive hulls, for $\ell\geq P_m(F)=h^0(F,mK_F)$ whenever $m\geq 1$. We prove it for all $\ell\geq1$ at levels $m\geq 2$, also in the case of birational $m$-canonical map, but construct a counterexample at level $m=1$. Over curves, curvature and boundary estimates give a direct analytic proof of Viehweg's ampleness theorem requested by Fujino. For smooth projective families, we also establish numerical dimension and vanishing results related to the birational variation dimension.

authors.name: Yunyang Xiao
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Beijing

papers.title: Provably Efficient Q-learning for Robust Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Standard reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms based on Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) are vulnerable to sim-to-real gaps. To address this issue, distributionally robust RL algorithms based on robust MDPs (RMDPs) have been proposed, for ensuring that agents can perform reliably to unpredictable conditions in real-world environments. Despite of the rich literature, \revision{an efficient model-free method is still lacking} for robust RL, particularly for Markovian data, which is more relevant in practical applications. In this work, we take a step towards settling this problem by proposing a sample efficient (asynchronous Q-learning) algorithm for robust RL. In particular, consider a $\gamma$-discounted infinite-horizon RMDP with state space $\mathcal{S}$ and action space $\mathcal{A}$, where the uncertainty set is specified by the total variation (TV) distance with uncertainty level $\sigma$. Assuming access to a single trajectory of Markovian samples induced by a behavior policy and the nominal transition kernel, the sample complexity of the proposed Q-learning algorithm --- to achieve an entrywise $\varepsilon$-approximation of the optimal Q-function --- is bounded by $$ \frac{1}{\mu_{\mathsf{min}}\varepsilon^2(1-\gamma)^3\max\{1-\gamma,\sigma\}} + \frac{t_{\mathsf{mix}}}{\mu_{\mathsf{min}}(1-\gamma)} $$ up to logarithmic factors. Here, $t_{\mathsf{mix}}$ and $\mu_{\mathsf{min}}$ denote the mixing time and the minimum state-action occupancy probability of the sample trajectory, respectively. This result is nearly minimax optimal, with an additional factor of $\frac{1}{1-\gamma}$. Moreover, it achieves a significant improvement over existing bounds.

authors.name: Yuchen Jiao
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: FISRF: Flexible Instructional Scaffolding Reflection Framework for Robotics Task Planning with Large Language Model
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are widely adopted for reflective error correction in task planning; however, existing approaches primarily rely on autonomous exploration, rendering them prone to accumulating erroneous experiences during early interactions with new environments. To address this limitation, we propose the Flexible Instructional Scaffolding Reflection Framework (FISRF), an agent--mentor architecture that estimates the robot's Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD) in task planning and adaptively selects reflection strategies and mentor guidance, thereby facilitating the accumulation of effective error-correction experience. Experiments in ALFWorld and on real-world robotic platforms demonstrate that FISRF reduces the average number of error-correction rounds by 37% and redundant reasoning by 25.1%, while improving the overall task success rate by 8%. Project webpage : https://fisrfplanning.github.io/

authors.name: Qingmiao Liang
authors.institution: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

authors.name: Runxin Zou
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Number of left cells in the second lowest two-sided cell
papers.abstract: We prove Shi's conjecture that the number of left cells in the second lowest two-sided cell of the affine Weyl group attached to a simply connected simple complex group $G$ is exactly $|W_0|/2$, where $W_0$ is the corresponding finite Weyl group. The same formula holds for the corresponding extended affine Weyl group. The key step is to show that the reductive centralizer in $G$ of a minimal nilpotent element has identity component with simply connected derived subgroup and admits no nontrivial algebraic central extensions by $\mathbb G_m$. This gives an isomorphism of based rings between the asymptotic ring of the extended cell and a matrix ring over the representation ring of the centralizer, with matrix size equal to the Euler characteristic of the Springer fiber, namely $|W_0|/2$.

papers.title: On the Anderson Dual of $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$ and $H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we give complete classifications of the finite groups $G$ for which the constant Eilenberg--Mac Lane spectra $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$ and $H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ are Anderson self-dual up to a virtual representation shift, and we determine all such shifts. For both of these spectra, we determine the representation periodicity lattice for every finite group.
  As applications, we obtain $RO(G)$-graded universal coefficient theorems relating equivariant homology and cohomology, together with formulas for the Anderson duals of $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$-modules. In the $H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ self-dual cases, we identify the graded $\mathbb F_2$-linear dual of the coefficient ring $\pi_\star^G H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ with a representation shift of the ring as a module over itself. This gives perfect multiplication pairings and graded self-injectivity.

papers.title: Learning When to Commit: Schedule Distillation for Fast Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) can generate multiple tokens in parallel, but often require many decoding rounds to complete a response. Efficient generation depends not only on which tokens are easy to predict, but also on how committing to them helps predict the remaining positions. A highly predictable token may provide little useful context, while revealing a less predictable token can help several other positions become predictable sooner. We propose dSpark, a new schedule distillation-based framework for learning when to commit tokens for faster diffusion language generation. To achieve this, we construct unmasking schedules that prioritize tokens whose reveal makes other positions easier to predict, reducing uncertainty earlier in decoding. We then distill these schedules into the model to enable faster parallel sampling, with a KL-divergence regularizer to help preserve generation quality. We extensively evaluate our approach across mathematical reasoning and code generation tasks. On GSM8K, our method achieves remarkable 10.12$\times$ and 5.12$\times$ speedups over the various baselines on LLaDA-8B-Instruct and Dream-7B-Instruct, respectively, while maintaining superior task performance. Our code is available at https://github.com/VILA-Lab/dSpark.

papers.title: A secondary term in the first moment of cubic $L$-functions over function fields
papers.abstract: Let $q$ be a fixed odd prime power with $q\equiv2\pmod3$. We study the first moment of primitive cubic Dirichlet $L$-functions over $\Fq(T)$, ordered by their genus. By averaging the rational sieve variable in the double Dirichlet series of Hong and Fang, we obtain meromorphic continuation beyond the secondary polar divisor. Combining this continuation with the cubic Gauss-sum residues computed by David, Florea and Lal\'in gives an explicit term of order $q^{5g/6}$, with a real coefficient depending on $g$ modulo $6$, and an error $O_{q,\eps}(q^{(23/28+\eps)g})$. The periodic coefficient is not identically zero. The proof uses an exact first difference supplied by the functional equation, an Euler product for the sieve average, and Bochner's tube theorem in the Dirichlet variables.

papers.title: RoboDuo: Attempt, Check and Atomic Recovery through Code for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models map a language instruction and the current observation directly to actions, without checking whether the instruction has been completed. For long-horizon tasks, a single failed step therefore goes unnoticed and leaves the whole task unfinished. Such failed episodes, however, often end with the task partially complete. Moreover, the unfinished steps are reusable atomic skills that recur across demonstrations. A failed attempt can thus be recovered by composing with atomic skills. We propose RoboDuo, a closed-loop dual-system framework that uses code as the interface between a coding agent and two VLAs. The agent writes a program that lets a full-task VLA attempt the whole task and checks whether it is complete; on failure, an atomic VLA finishes the remaining steps. Since the agent emits no actions and only decides which VLA for execution, RoboDuo wraps an existing full-task VLA without updating its weights. To train the atomic VLA and the coding agent with the completion-checking ability, we build LIBERO-Atomic, LIBERO-Code, and LIBERO-Judge from a single set of LIBERO demonstrations. RoboDuo consistently improves X-VLA and $\pi_{0.5}$ on LIBERO and LIBERO-PRO, with the largest gains on long-horizon tasks, and recovers failed rollouts of a frozen full-task VLA on a real robot.

authors.name: Renzhi Lu
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Jianyu Chen
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Graham's rearrangement conjecture in finite abelian groups
papers.abstract:
Graham conjectured in 1971 that every subset of the nonzero elements of a prime cyclic group admits an ordering with pairwise distinct nonempty partial sums. Recently, the work of Pham and Sauermann, together with earlier results, settled this conjecture for all sufficiently large primes. In this paper, we prove that there is an absolute integer $n_0$ such that every subset $S\subseteq G\setminus\{0\}$ of a finite abelian group with $|S|\ge n_0$ admits such an ordering, which also solves a conjecture of Alspach and Liversidge for all sufficiently large sets.
  A key ingredient of our proof is a sufficient condition via additive dimension: If $|S|=n$ and $S$ contains a dissociated subset of size at least $\Omega((\log n)^2/\log\log n)$, then $S$ has an ordering in which no proper nonempty interval of consecutive terms sums to zero. This bound is within a factor of $O(\log n/\log\log n)$ of the smallest possible additive dimension of an $n$-element set.

papers.title: Endpoint well-posedness for the Boussinesq equation
papers.abstract: We prove small-data global well-posedness for the quadratic good Boussinesq equation on the real line and the circle at the endpoint $H^{-1/2}\times H^{-3/2}$. On each domain, a small invariant spectral set supports a continuous global group, with uniqueness in a fixed local integral class. In the periodic case, both components have zero mean and the flow is Lipschitz on bounded time intervals. The a priori bounds follow from a balanced perturbation determinant for the third-order Lax operator. Averaging two real spectral branches yields coercivity and frequency-tail control. On the line, we construct the endpoint flow by commuting Hamiltonians and Green-field estimates. On the circle, discrete spectral bounds and Kishimoto's endpoint local theory give global well-posedness.

papers.title: ACSAN: All-Convolutional Self-Attention Network Integrating Convolutional Operations with Vision Transformer
papers.abstract: In the past few years, Vision Transformer (ViT) has achieved excellent performance in the field of computer vision. However, there still some problems remain. For instance, ViTs heavily rely on large-scale training data since they simply contain a large number of trainable parameters, which slows down their learning efficiency and limits their applicability in resource-constrained scenarios. In this paper, we propose a novel deep learning model, namely All-Convolutional Self-Attention Network (ACSAN), which applies convolution operations to replace fully-connected matrices multiplications in the ViT framework. To implement ACSAN, we firstly design Dynamic Convolutional Self-Attention (DCSA) as the basic module, which employs multi-scale dilated convolutions to generate Query, Key, and Value. We defined spatial self-attention and channel self-attention to generate attention features respectively. The two attention features are finally merged as the output of the DCSA module. Based on DCSA, we then construct the basic ACSAN block. Comparing with ViT, we use DCSA to replace the regular self-attention operations, and use convolution layers to replace MLPs. To evaluate the performance of the proposed method, we train ACSAN on three widely-used image classification databases, i.e. CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-1k, from scratch. Experimental results show that ACSAN achieves excellent classification accuracy comparing with standard ViT with comparable or fewer parameters, as well as other state-of-the-art methods. Ablation studies verify that each component contributes positively to the final performance.

authors.name: Tianqi Zhang
authors.institution: Capital University of Economics and Business

papers.title: Gradient estimates and Liouville theorems for exponentially harmonic functions
papers.abstract: We study exponentially harmonic functions on complete Riemannian manifolds. Under a lower Ricci curvature bound \(\Ric_g\geq-Kg\), we first establish a local gradient estimate in terms of the oscillation. We then prove a pointwise gradient estimate for solutions bounded from one side. As an application, when \(\Ric_g\geq0\), we obtain a Liouville theorem under a one-sided sublinear growth condition. In particular, every exponentially harmonic function bounded above or below is constant.

papers.title: Projections in reduced group C*-algebras with prescribed trace values in (0,1)
papers.abstract: Building on OpenAI's preprint, we construct, for every real number $r\in(0,1)$, a finitely generated discrete group $G_r$ and a projection $e_r\in C_r^*(G_r)$ whose canonical trace is $r$. The construction encodes the geometry of expanders in the dynamics of a semidirect product of groups. For irrational $r$, the $K$-theory class $[e_r]$ is not in the image of the reduced Baum--Connes map. The groups $G_r$ have torsion and satisfy the maximal strong Novikov conjecture.

papers.title: Cavity Loss in QED Coupled-Cluster Theory: Polariton Linewidths, Driven Steady States, and the Rabi Splitting
papers.abstract: Molecular polariton experiments are performed in lossy cavities, whereas correlated ab initio polariton theory has been developed almost entirely for lossless cavities. In this work, cavity loss is added to real-time QED coupled-cluster theory (QED-CCSD-22) through a complex cavity frequency, which gives the non-Hermitian no-jump part of the Lindblad master equation. The resulting polariton linewidths and driven-dissipative steady states are, to our knowledge, the first from QED coupled-cluster theory. The linewidths obtained from the complex Jacobian and from real-time propagation agree and are partitioned by the biorthogonal photon numbers of the two polaritons. A closed-form continuous-wave drive of the cavity gives driven steady states and their lineshapes.

papers.title: Escaping cells dilute CRISPR screen responses unequally across cell types
papers.abstract: Single-cell CRISPR screens run in many cell types are used to compare how cell types respond to perturbation, to train models that transfer effects between them and to score such models. These uses assume that cells carrying a guide RNA had their target knocked down. Yet cells grow for days before sequencing: when an essential gene is knocked down, knocked-down cells are depleted or stop dividing while cells that escaped knockdown keep growing, and the measured response, an average over all cells carrying the guide, is diluted. We define the escape fraction of a perturbation as the share of its measured cells whose target was not effectively knocked down, and estimate it from each cell's counts of the targeted gene with a two-group mixture that recovers known fractions in simulated mixtures. In most cell types the escape fraction rises with how essential the gene is, it is higher in a later screen of the same cells, and it reaches about half of the measured cells in human embryonic stem cells (hESCs). It predicts how much each response is diluted: the response size falls to (1 - e)^2 of that of the knocked-down cells. Because the escape fraction differs between cell types, it changes all three uses: hESCs respond like K562 cells unless knockdown depletes them, the coefficient a simple transfer model learns is lowered by the dilution of the cell type it predicts, and a benchmark scored on all cells rewards predictions shrunk towards no change, partly because that ground truth is itself diluted. Where cells stop dividing instead, the response also contains expression differences between cell-cycle stages. Response sizes should be compared on knocked-down cells or corrected for the escape fraction.

papers.title: WiMoT: Replay-Free Continual Wi-Fi Sensing via Moment Transport
papers.abstract: Continual Wi-Fi sensing must balance plasticity, learning new rooms or users, against stability, keeping earlier ones, yet nodes often cannot retain channel state information (CSI) for privacy and storage reasons. We propose WiMoT (Wi-Fi Moment Transport), which stores the per-class feature mean and covariance of every earlier domain instead of samples. When the representation changes, stored statistics become stale. WiMoT restricts the change to an affine map on a frozen feature basis and applies the same map to the statistics, so they stay valid without old samples. Supervised contrastive learning learns the new domain, a closed-form loss on the stored statistics keeps earlier classes separable, and a Gaussian discriminant classifier, refitted from the transported statistics with equal weight per domain, predicts without domain identity. On 3DO, WiMANS, and Widar3.0, WiMoT's average final accuracies are 94.02%, 89.61%, and 95.16% with at most 0.58 percentage points (pp) of forgetting. On 3DO and Widar3.0, it also has the highest balance of new- and earlier-domain accuracy and is 3.77 and 13.11 pp ahead of the strongest of 21 baselines, which uses replay, staying ahead across domain orders and label budgets. On WiMANS, it matches the strongest replay baseline in accuracy (+0.41 pp) while reducing forgetting from 2.78 to 0.00 pp, and has the highest six-order average accuracy. Because full covariances dominate the memory, storing them as rank-32 factors shrinks the moment memory to 6.4%, losing at most 0.49 pp of accuracy, within edge-node storage budgets.

authors.name: Yang Cao
authors.institution: Hunan University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Ring-0 by Default: Agents as Operating Systems (AaOS)
papers.abstract:
LLM agents now read and write files, start processes and subagents, fetch network content, load third-party extensions, and save and resume state, which are the responsibilities of an operating system. They gained these functions within about three years, but not the protections that operating systems built over five decades: whatever the model outputs, whether it follows the user, a tool result, or a downloaded skill, runs with the full authority of the host user, in effect at ring 0. Prior work builds an operating system for agents (OS4A); we argue that a deployed agent already is like an operating system (AaOS) and analyze it as one. Taking the mechanisms of standard OS textbooks as a checklist, we map 116 mechanisms in 19 subsystems to their agent counterparts, from product documentation, source code, and the literature, and label each as isomorphic, degraded (function present, protection dependent on the model), missing, mutated, or novel. Only 11 are isomorphic and 65 are missing, most of them protections: privilege separation, resource quotas, transactions, and tamper-proof audit. Existing defenses confine the whole agent or review its extensions and leave this interior unprotected, and by Anderson's reference-monitor criteria (non-bypassable, tamper-proof, verifiable), rules written in the prompt satisfy none.
  We test the map with thirteen experiments on Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Gemini CLI, covering 25 mechanisms whose enforcement documentation cannot settle: 16 match the analysis, 7 gain a more precise description, and 2 change verdict. Checks sit in single tools, so the shell bypasses them; all three CLIs load forged transcript records on resume; and task control, sub-agent permissions, and model-based monitors are weak. We identify five problems for which no OS defense transfers and derive a prioritized list of open problems from the gaps of the map.

papers.title: Beyond "[at]": A Large-Scale Measurement of Email Address Presentation on Computer Science Scholars' Homepages
papers.abstract: Publishing an email address makes a scholar reachable, but also exposes it to automated collection. Yet how email addresses are presented on the Web has not been measured systematically across their content, form, and location. We measure it across 32,413 homepage records of computer-science scholars listed in CSRankings with MailScope, which preserves raw and rendered HTML, extracts addresses with a three-stage cascade (rules, then large language models, then a crawling agent), and labels each address. Among 19,517 reachable homepages, we find an address for 17,712 scholars (90.8%). Our measurement yields four main findings. (i) Presentation is diverse: only 53.8% publish plain content, the others spread over 23 subtypes of symbol substitution, code, and semantic description, and 5.5% of scholars' addresses appear only after rendering. (ii) Presentation follows hosts rather than individuals: scholars on one host share a content class in 67.9% of pairs, compared with 38.8% across hosts of one institution, whereas research output and institution rank are barely related to presentation. (iii) Content and form are coupled through code-based links, and 6.2% of scholars with non-plain selected presentations have plain-text copies of the same address elsewhere. (iv) Plain addresses are more common behind passed bot challenges, and 36.1% of redirecting homepages no longer lead to scholars. Human assessment yields 94.4% weighted exact-set agreement on 143 judgeable pages, complemented by three 500-page review rounds with human verification. Presentation is diverse but clusters by shared host, and by our label-based estimate plain-string matching misses nearly half of the addresses.

papers.title: Natural Jammers: When Non-Robust Features Become Antagonistic
papers.abstract: Deep neural networks are known to rely on non-robust features that align poorly with human perception. Prior work has largely framed these features as opportunistic shortcuts that help standard models on clean data. We show instead that non-robust cues can be antagonistic: they can act as Natural Jammers that actively mislead standard models on clean, unmodified images. Using disagreement between a standard model and robust models as an analysis lens, we identify a Jammed Set on which robust models outperform standard models. We provide causal evidence for Spectral-spatial Locking: jamming arises only when high-frequency components are precisely aligned with specific spatial structures. Disrupting this lock through spectral filtering or small geometric shifts can restore correct predictions. Crucially, we uncover a Substitution Paradox: while individual jammers are fragile to geometric shifts, the aggregate prevalence of jamming remains approximately stable and is redistributed rather than eliminated under such transformations. Our results reframe natural non-robustness as a failure field over the empirical model-data geometry: one that redistributes rather than disappears under small transformations.

papers.title: DualPace: Decoupled Scheduling and Cooperative GPU--CPU Decoding for LLM Serving
papers.abstract:
Large language model (LLM) serving relies on batching to improve inference throughput, but the key-value (KV) cache grows with sequence length and limits GPU-resident concurrency. CPU offloading can expand KV capacity using host memory, yet existing systems remain largely GPU-gated: CPU-resident requests make progress only when the GPU scheduler exposes suitable overlap opportunities. As a result, host memory and CPU compute cannot act as an independent serving resource, leading to bursty CPU-side progress and inflated tail inter-token latency (ITL) under load.
  We present DualPace, an LLM serving runtime that turns the host into an independently scheduled decode engine. DualPace separates scheduling authority across two engines: the GPU engine executes prefills and GPU-resident decodes, while an AMX-enabled CPU engine independently batches and advances CPU-resident decodes. The engines are decoupled in scheduling but cooperative in execution: the CPU can execute a complete decode iteration locally or selectively invoke GPU Dense Assist for dense stages, while offline profiles guide hardware-specific batching and routing.
  Our evaluations show that, in decode-oriented scenarios, DualPace improves serving throughput by 6.9--43.2\% over NEO, a state-of-the-art open-source CPU-offloading system, and by 11.5--90.6\% over vLLM, a widely used GPU serving system, while maintaining the same level of latency. DualPace also preserves NEO's P99 time-to-first-token (TTFT) advantage over vLLM while sustaining 7.3--50.5\% higher request rates than NEO at the same level of P99 ITL.

papers.title: Non-liftability of the field of norms of the $p$-adic false Tate curve extension
papers.abstract: Let $p\geq3$ be a prime number. We prove that the action of the Galois group on the field of norms of the $p$-adic false Tate curve extension $\mathbf{Q}_p\left(\zeta_{p^\infty},p^{1/p^\infty}\right)$ of $\mathbf{Q}_p$ is not liftable to its Cohen ring with respect to any admissible coefficient field.

papers.title: Fitting time-varying parameter models via partially noncentered parametrizations
papers.abstract: Time-varying parameter (TVP) models are widely used to capture evolving relationships but inference is often computationally demanding due to high-dimensional latent states. The efficiency of iterative algorithms depends critically on the choice of latent state augmentation, with centering preferred for genuinely time-varying coefficients and noncentering favored when coefficients are nearly constant. We propose a partially noncentered parametrization that bridges these extremes via dimension-specific working parameters for both location and scale. Optimal working parameters are derived by analyzing EM convergence rates, and an alternating expectation-conditional maximization algorithm is developed to implement the approach. As the convergence rate of mean-field variational Bayes (MFVB) is closely related to EM, we extend the approach to develop partially noncentered MFVB algorithms for the TVP model, placing triple gamma priors on baseline coefficients and process variances to induce shrinkage. Simulations and empirical applications show that the resulting MFVB algorithms yield posterior approximations closer to Markov chain Monte Carlo than conventional centered or noncentered parametrizations. We also develop an efficient solver for the block tridiagonal inverse matrices arising in the proposed algorithms.

authors.name: Lingjie Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Representation type of contraction algebras
papers.abstract: We classify the representation-finite, tame, and wild contraction algebras arising from 3-fold flopping contractions of isolated cDV singularities with at worst Gorenstein terminal sources. To achieve this, we first determine the representation type of all contracted preprojective algebras of Dynkin types $\mathsf{A}$, $\mathsf{D}$, and $\mathsf{E}$, and then use the representation type invariance under iterated flops and the radical structure of contraction algebras.

papers.title: MechGate: combining mechanism-derived measures of permeation and efflux to screen small molecule drugs targeting Escherichia coli
papers.abstract: Most antibiotic molecules must cross the cell membrane and escape efflux pumps before hitting their targets. For de novo antibiotic design, very few of the in-silico-generated drug molecules can successfully pass these two steps. Existing evaluations of generated molecules do not separate these steps. Therefore, we introduce MechGate, a mechanism-resolved screening tool evaluating small drug molecules against E. coli, measuring permeation, efflux and antibacterial activity. After SMILES input, five measures are reported side by side: two for permeation via porins, one for permeation via the phospholipid membrane, one for efflux and one for activity. Each measure is read on its own, so a molecule that fails can be traced to the step that stops it. All features are taken from papers that state their mechanism rather than selected by importance ranking. On an external set of marketed antibacterials the measures give a precision of 0.789 to 0.873 against baselines near 0.44, and combining them the way the mechanism predicts raises precision to 0.92. We also find that the four public source libraries are separable from one another using physicochemical features alone; every measure here therefore draws both classes from a single library. All code is open-source and requires no commercial software.

papers.title: Global Stability of the Kolmogorov--Zakharov Spectrum for the Wave Kinetic Equation
papers.abstract:
We prove global nonlinear stability near the mass Kolmogorov--Zakharov spectrum $f_M(\omega)=\omega^{-7/6}$ for the isotropic cubic wave kinetic equation, including small time-dependent external forces. For sufficiently small initial perturbations and forcing, the solution remains uniformly close to $f_M$ for all time in a weighted norm. This norm allows $f(t,\omega)\sim a_0(t)\omega^{-7/6}$ as $\omega\to0$ and $f(t,\omega)\sim a_\infty(t)\omega^{-7/6}$ as $\omega\to\infty$.
  When the external force $\phi$ is independent of time, the solution converges at an algebraic rate to a stationary solution in weaker weighted norms. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition on the initial perturbation for convergence in the original weighted norm. These results resolve, for small perturbations of the Kolmogorov--Zakharov spectrum, the question of convergence to a stationary solution under time-independent forcing raised by Collot, Dietert, and Germain (arXiv:2208.00947, Section 1.3).
  To establish this stability, the collision integral is expanded around $a_0(t)f_M$ at low frequencies and $a_\infty(t)f_M$ at high frequencies, separating it into a linear term with time-dependent coefficients and a nonlinear remainder. This decomposition yields improved control of the nonlinear remainder.
  The main difficulty is that $a_0(t)$ may vary in time, so the linear operator itself changes with time and its evolution cannot be represented by the semigroup of a single fixed operator. To address this difficulty, we use a parametrix construction to explicitly construct the evolution operator $U_{a_0,a_\infty}$ and establish the required uniform bounds. Moreover, our arguments provide a general framework for proving global stability that may also apply to other evolution equations.

authors.name: Jiajun Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Consequence-guided clarification: releasing minimum-compliance topology-optimized designs from incomplete specifications
papers.abstract: A converged topology optimization can solve the wrong problem when loads, supports, or the domain are underspecified. Assuming defaults, or asking the problem's author about every detail, ignores how much each answer changes the design. We propose consequence-guided clarification (CGC), which bases acceptance on computed mechanical consequences. CGC computes a reference design for each of a finite list of complete specifications, called readings. A design is accepted only if its compliance is at most 5% above the reference at every reading consistent with the answers. Otherwise, CGC asks the question whose worst answer leaves the smallest worst-case excess, and withholds acceptance at its question limit. To save optimizations, the screening variant CGC-S postpones some references until a candidate must be checked. We developed and evaluated both on 36 arXiv-derived tasks, treating each of 134 readings in turn as intended and simulating correct answers. In 26 tasks, the default-reading design failed another reading. Apart from always-asked questions on load direction, sign, and material budget, asking everything took 188 questions; CGC and CGC-S each took 105. The acceptance test supplied most of this saving: applying it to the default design alone took 117. Relative to asking everything, CGC-S requested 4.6 extra reference designs per avoided question, each from two optimization starts, counting optimization time only. References are not certified optima: better ones pushed three accepted cases above tolerance, and finer meshes changed some decisions. Within these limits, the test shows which readings a design covers and which details block acceptance.

papers.title: Periodic dynamics of transonic shocks in Euler-Poisson flows
papers.abstract: This paper studies the existence and dynamical stability of time-periodic transonic shock solutions to the one-dimensional Euler--Poisson equations under periodic boundary perturbations. The analysis relies on two key mechanisms: the structural dissipation induced by the transonic shock and the stabilization effect of the positive electric field on the shock position. Using a reformulation of the Rankine-Hugoniot conditions and uniform estimates on the flow and shock perturbations, we establish the existence of a time-periodic transonic shock solution. We further prove its dynamical stability under small perturbations of the initial data.

authors.name: Jiahui Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Adapting LLM-SC to Living Sacred Heritage: Domain-Specific Extraction, Semantic Networks and Human Evaluation on Pashupatinath Temple Reviews
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) pipelines can turn visitor reviews into structured data, but generic schemes may miss rituals, sacred spaces, cultural restrictions and emotionally mixed experiences at living sacred heritage sites. We adapted the LLM-Social Computing (LLM-SC) framework to Pashupatinath Temple, Nepal, by specifying a 12-type entity taxonomy (four original LLM-SC types plus eight sacred-heritage types), four relation types and nine aspect-sentiment dimensions in a GPT-4o extraction prompt, which was applied to a fixed random sample of 2,500 English-language Tripadvisor reviews from a processed corpus of 3,939. The exports contain 11,286 entity, 6,232 aspect-sentiment and 5,590 relation records, covering 2,485, 2,487 and 2,433 reviews, respectively; the eight added sacred-heritage types account for 64.8% of entity records. Against an adjudicated two-annotator reference for 200 reviews, exact normalized surface-and-type matching gave provisional entity scores of 41.0% precision, 21.8% recall and 28.4% micro-F1. Aspect-presence F1 was 53.6% and end-to-end aspect-plus-polarity F1 was 42.6%. Human adjudication supported 153 of 194 first-listed relation candidates (one per review; 78.9%), a candidate-level rate that does not estimate relation recall or whole-graph precision. The contribution is a culturally grounded, domain-specific adaptation with component-wise human evaluation and explicit reproducibility and generalization limitations.

papers.title: Sharp bounds for Duke--Erd\H{o}s--R\"odl problems on cycle-connected subgraphs
papers.abstract: For $k\ge2$, a graph is $C_{2k}$-connected if every two distinct edges lie together on an even cycle of length at most $2k$ in that graph. Let $f_k(n,m)$ be the largest number of edges in a $C_{2k}$-connected subgraph that every $n$-vertex graph with $m$ edges must contain. In this paper, we study two cycle-connected problems raised by Duke, Erd\H{o}s and R\"odl. First, Duke, Erd\H{o}s and R\"odl showed that $f_3(n,\lfloor n^{2-\beta}\rfloor)=\Theta(n^{2-3\beta})$ for every fixed $0< \beta<1/2$ and ask for the case of $\beta\ge 1/2$. We solve this problem in a stronger form by determining that the optimal range of $\beta$ is $(0,2/3]$. Second, we prove that $f_2(n,\binom n2-s)=(1/(2e)+o(1))n^3/s$ whenever $\frac{s}{n}\to\infty$ and $s=o(n^2)$, determining the leading constant in an estimate of Duke, Erd\H{o}s, and R\"odl. The first result uses a finite-field construction and a count of three-edge paths. The second uses the known structure of $C_4$-connected graphs and estimates for complete bipartite subgraphs in a random graph.

papers.title: SKG in Practice: OOD Generalization Cases Across FourDomains
papers.abstract: This paper presents the engineering implementation methods of the SKG inference framework and provides complete case studies across four domains. Case 1, 2D Dissipative Mechanical System: OOD MSE is 1.69 to 4.12 times lower than the best neural baseline; the state-dependent metric yields a 10^8-order improvement under controlled conditions. Case 2, Target Detection Sim-to-Real: Real-machine mAP increases from 0.2564 to 0.4964 (+24.00 points, single-run experiment, 32 images, point estimate), and AP75 increases from 0.1736 to 0.5765 (+40.29 points), with no real-machine retraining required. Case 3, Sequence Modeling sine to square: OOD MSE is 0.0296 versus Transformer 0.0641 (mean of 5 seeds, p=0.024). Case 4, Molecular Dynamics MD17: ID@100 ADE is 0.0285 versus ESTAG 0.1467; OOD@100 is 0.0316 versus 0.1411 (single seed). For each case, we present the objective, applied SKG theory, parameter settings, baseline comparison protocol, data results, and sources of advantage. Following the cases, we provide the complete methodology: pre-validation, task invariant construction, three-stage training, residual training, and the four theorems and one proposition supporting these methods. This paper not only demonstrates effective configurations of SKG across four domains but also honestly reports the variance of single-run experiments, limitations of single-seed results, negative updates caused by parameterization mismatch, and practical experience of using engineering thresholds as diagnostic signals rather than hard constraints.

papers.title: Equidistribution of mesh patterns of length 2 on involutions
papers.abstract: We classify all 1024 length-two mesh patterns on involutions into exactly 287 equidis- tribution classes, consisting of 262 trivial classes and 25 nontrivial classes. Since many bi- jections on arbitrary permutations do not preserve the involution condition, our proofs use several involution-preserving bijections, including conjugation and local adjacent-transposition operations, transposition of the RSK recording tableau, prefix-rank swap bijections and marked-occurrence bijections. In particular, we establish the equidistribution of INV-099, a nontrivial class closely related to the unrestricted Class 69, by adapting the marked- occurrence bijection of Zhang and Zhao through a symmetric closure of the marked set. We also obtain explicit distribution formulas and recurrences for several classes, including continued fractions obtained by specializing known labeled Motzkin-path formulas and rational expressions derived from paired skew decompositions of involutions.

papers.title: Fast Outflow Driven from the Magnetically Arrested Disc
papers.abstract: Fast outflows are commonly observed in accreting black hole systems, yet their launching mechanism remains debated, especially when the gas is highly ionized and radiation line driving becomes inefficient. We investigate magnetically driven outflows from magnetically arrested discs (MADs) using a steady, axisymmetric magnetocentrifugal outflow model. The outflow equations follow the classical trans-magnetosonic MHD framework, while the disc structural scalings and outflow-base conditions are motivated by general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics (GRMHD) simulations. We solve for the trans-magnetosonic outflow solutions along prescribed large-scale poloidal magnetic field lines. The outflows launched from the inner disc are strongly accelerated and the formal Newtonian solutions can enter the mildly relativistic regime. The outflow velocity decreases systematically with increasing footpoint radius, producing a radially stratified outflow in which inner streamlines reach UFO-like velocities while outer streamlines form slower components. We also find that the MAD solutions have a large magnetic lever arm $\tilde{l}=(R_{\rm A}/R)^2$ is typically several tens and can reach $\sim10^2$, which implies that the outflow can carry a large amount of the specific angular momentum of the disc material at its footpoint, and we find that about $55\%$ of the angular-momentum estimated between the outer and inner disc boundaries is removed by the magnetic outflow. The total mass-loss rate in the outflow is about $14\%$ of the disc mass-accretion rate in our fiducial model. These results suggest that the MADs provide a natural environment for producing both fast, radially stratified disc outflow and efficient disc angular-momentum removal. MAD-driven outflow may therefore provide a magnetic origin for ultra-fast absorbers in low-luminosity active galactic nuclei (AGNs) and X-ray binaries (XRBs).

papers.title: Some chromatic height computations for homotopy fixed points of iterated topological Hochschild homology
papers.abstract: For an $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-ring spectrum $R$ of chromatic height $k$, the trace method and the chromatic redshift imply that $T^n$-fixed point of $n$-fold iterated topological Hochschild homology of $R$ has chromatic height at most $k+n$. In this paper, we compute these heights for $H\mathbb{F}_p$, $H\mathbb{Z}$ and the $p$-complete connective image-of-$J$ spectrum $j_p$ for all primes and $n\geq1$, which are exactly $n-1$, $n$ and $n+1$, respectively. Our method is based on properties of Wilson spaces and relative topological Hochschild homology over $\mathrm{MU}$.

papers.title: Hausdorff and Packing Measures for $\beta$-L{\"u}roth Infinite Iterated Function Systems
papers.abstract: We study the Hausdorff and packing measures of attractors generated by infinite $\beta$-L\"uroth iterated function systems. Let $I\subset\mathbb N$ be infinite and let $\dim_H E_I=h$. For a regular system, we first give conditions for the positivity of $\mathcal H^h(E_I)$ and the finiteness of $\mathcal P^h(E_I)$ in terms of first-level L\"uroth intervals. We then introduce tail-regular partitions and the scale $R_n=\frac{B_n^\infty}{B_n}.$ Under tail-regularity, the Hausdorff and packing conditions reduce to counting conditions for $I$ on intervals of length comparable to $R_n$, together with a tail condition in the packing case. Finally, we apply these results to regularly varying partitions and stretched-exponential partitions.

papers.title: Finiteness of ergodic measures of maximal entropy for certain skew product systems
papers.abstract:
Consider a $C^{1+\beta}$ skew product $F$ over a topologically mixing Anosov diffeomorphism $f$, with fiber dynamics driven by a $C^{1+\beta}$ $\mathbb{R}^k$-action $\{\rho_{\bf t}\}$ on a closed manifold $Y$ through a $C^{1+\beta}$ cocycle $\tau$. Suppose that the fiber action preserves an ergodic smooth measure of maximal entropy $m_{\operatorname{MME}}$. Under a nondegeneracy condition called joint nontriviality, and assuming that each element $\rho_{\bf t}$ is either of class $C^\infty$ or hyperbolic, we prove that $F$ admits only finitely many ergodic measures of maximal entropy.
  Moreover, every such measure is of the form $\mu\times m_{\operatorname{MME}}$, where $\mu$ is an ergodic equilibrium state for a H\"older potential on the base. If, in addition, the fiber action is exponentially mixing of all orders, then every ergodic MME is Bernoulli, exponentially mixing of all orders, and satisfies the Central Limit Theorem.
  Our main novelties are entropy formulas for skew products, obtained through the cone property and $r$-neutralized entropy, and a relative Ledrappier--Young theorem that converts the fiber entropy contribution into absolute continuity of fiberwise conditional measures. Combined with nonlinear thermodynamic formalism, rotation theory and Yomdin theory, these yield the finiteness of the base projections and the product rigidity of ergodic MMEs.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds on Continuous Treatment Effects under Unobserved Confounding
papers.abstract: We study partial identification of conditional treatment effects with a continuous treatment under unobserved confounding. We target the conditional average potential outcome (CAPO) E[Y_x|z] and the conditional average treatment effect (CATE) between two treatment levels. We assume a bounded outcome and Lipschitz continuity of the response functions and of the propensity scores given the latent confounder, and show that these conditions imply the smooth treatment response and smooth treatment selection conditions of Kim et al. (2018). The combined bound of Kim et al. uses only two reference points on the identified diagonal and is generally loose. Bounding through every diagonal reference point instead gives explicit bounds whose average is the sharp identified set of the CAPO at every treatment, inside or outside the observational support. Capping the difference between the upper and lower bounds gives sharp causal bounds on the CATE. These bounds are informative without monotonicity or overlap assumptions.

authors.name: Junzhe Zhang
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Collaborative In-Context Learning for Indoor Radio Map Estimation
papers.abstract: Indoor radio map estimation (RME) is essential for wireless applications such as coverage planning, localization, and network deployment. However, most existing methods follow a supervised learning paradigm that requires costly labeled data and task-specific model training. Moreover, indoor environments involve privacy-sensitive information, such as building layouts and structures, that often cannot be centralized. To address these challenges, we make the first attempt to formulate indoor RME as a collaborative in-context learning (ICL) problem. We propose Poly-Ripple, a framework in which multiple clients perform ICL using large autoregressive vision models (LAVMs) without model updates. Each client is prompted by its private demonstrations and predicts the radio map for the same scene query. To capture the causal structure of wireless propagation outward from the transmitter (Tx), we adopt ripple-ordered autoregressive modeling. We further introduce importance-aware aggregation to exploit heterogeneous contextual knowledge distributed across clients under the context length constraint. We provide theoretical analysis and conduct extensive experiments on a public indoor RME benchmark. The experimental results show that Poly-Ripple consistently outperforms representative ICL baselines, while aligning with our theoretical analysis.

papers.title: Generalization of the Rosenbluth-Putvinski avalanche growth rate to the drift kinetic regime
papers.abstract: A new collisionless detrapping mechanism is shown to modify the rate of runaway electron (RE) generation by as much as a factor of two for strong inductive electric fields. This detrapping mechanism results from the magnetic well inherent to tokamak geometry being tilted by the strong inductive electric fields present during tokamak disruptions. The impact of this collisionless detrapping mechanism is found to be described by a single dimensionless parameter, whose identification enables the transition between distinct regimes of RE generation to be characterized. Using this composite parameter, it is shown that modifications to the avalanche growth rate by tokamak geometry across a broad range of plasma parameters collapse onto a one-dimensional curve that can be accurately fit with a two parameter function. The resulting analytical formula extends the classic Rosenbluth-Putvinski avalanche growth rate expression beyond the bounce-averaged limit into RE regimes where collisionless detrapping strongly modifies RE generation rates.

papers.title: The_Quadratic_Conjecture_and_p-groups_of_maximal_class
papers.abstract: The Quadratic Conjecture for finite p-groups, which is equivalent to the Strong Oliver Conjecture, asserts that if a finite p-group G acts faithfully on an F-module V, then the center Z(G) contains a quadratic element. In this paper, we investigate the structure of maximal class p-groups and establish that they satisfy the Quadratic Conjecture.
